subsections.label: Logistics operational turnaround
points: Strong focus on operational execution; significant action was white space reduction from 16 lakh sq ft (same period last year) to 2 lakh sq ft currently, expected to be sold by September.
None of the white space has been surrendered — all sold, so these are now revenue-generating assets.
Strong growth on manufacturing and e-commerce sites; three very large e-commerce sites started this month across the country.
After 11 straight quarters of losses, business achieved small profit in Q3 of last year, followed by strong Q4 and Q1.

RIVIGO (express logistics) turnaround: losses cut down significantly in last one year; still a drag but EBITDA positive is 'just around the corner', expected to lead to PAT positive at some point soon.

subsections.label: Trust and pricing power (Mahindra Way)
points: Lifespaces business can price 15% higher in market despite strong competitors because of trust.
Closed joint development partnership deals (e.g., ₹12,000 crore GDV opportunity) because partner chose to work exclusively with Mahindra regardless of other offers.
Underlying theme across businesses: strong execution driven by purpose, values (integrity, quality, care), talent, technology adoption, and startup-like behaviors (collaboration, agility, boldness).

subsections.label: Lifespaces strategy detail (Amit Sinha)
points: Strategy codified 3 years ago: focus on residential in Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore; exited affordable segment, focus on mid-premium and premium segments.
Locked in ~₹50,000 crore of land deal pipeline over last 3 years across greenfield, joint development, and society redevelopment, through rigorous process to ensure more upside than downside.
Focus on customer experience and premiumization so customers come for the brand and stay for the experience; 3,000 apartments covered by OCs, 1,500 delivered, 99% zero-snag apartments.

Execution discipline emphasized because pricing is locked upfront while costs are covered over next five years — prudence on cost escalation surprises; industrial/commercial (IC) business complements residential business.

subsections.label: EV pricing/profitability path
points: Management expects EV price sensitivity to reduce and inflection point likely after 20-25% EV penetration, enabling a reasonable premium of 5-7% versus ICE (today EVs priced near parity, e.g., XEV 9S vs 7XO).
As EV category adoption grows, word-of-mouth on tangible savings builds, reducing reliance on price parity.

Cost curve expected to improve via continued localization, scale benefits passed on by supply ecosystem (previously subscale given orders/VOBs awarded around 2022 with uncertain EV penetration), engineering optimization — expected over next 12-18 months.

Scale argument: company doing ~9x ICE volume vs EV; scaling up EV volume expected to improve profitability further; INGLO EV platform capex efficiency across multiple top-heads also supports profitability.
Consumers historically willing to pay more for diesel due to lower fuel cost/higher efficiency; EV value proposition includes similar fuel savings potential providing some pricing ability.

subsections.label: Lifespaces group strategy fit (Anish Shah)
points: Fit in group requires high quality products (aspiration: customers wait specifically for Mahindra Lifespaces property in their area), meaningful scale, and profitability standards (ROA maintenance) with some businesses given long-term view (5-15 years) to build profitability, similar to aerospace timeline.

Mahindra Lifespaces with ₹50,000 crore GDV positioned well versus large players, expected to continue growing faster than most competitors, described as a very profitable business under close monitoring.

key_figures.label: Aerostructures decade growth aspiration
key_figures.period: over a decade (Global Investor Day target)

subsections.label: SML Mahindra + Truck & Bus combination
points: Combination announced the day before the call, enhances competitiveness, creates synergies, doubles business size.

Truck and bus business trajectory validated over last 3-4 years after earlier questions about whether to retain it; management decided to let business prove execution before deciding to exit or continue — business executed well, giving confidence to proceed with SML combination.
Combination expected to be accretive to M&M with additional synergies from network/product and cost/value engineering already underway.

subsections.label: Aerostructures M&A
points: Business exploring potential acquisition globally based on strength of business and desire of OEM partner customers; acquisition would need to be underwritten to ensure appropriate returns.

Aspiration (from Global Investor Day) to grow business 30x over a decade organically and inorganically combined, with 10x organic component; management indicated confidence to grow faster than that target and will share more numbers closer to milestones.
Business moving up the aero value chain — from detailed parts player towards sub-assemblies and full fuselages (manufacturer of thousands of small parts moving toward hundreds of high-value parts).
Two large deals recently won with Airbus; company is single global source for fuselage of 2 helicopters, seen as testament to quality.

Industry dynamics: reliability/quality track record is central to reputation; parts industrialization takes 2-3 years; aircraft parts must last ~40 years (e.g., 747s still flying), so replacement/design cycles are long and quality bar very high.

subsections.label: Growth Gems / Federation model
points: Multiple growth engines (Growth Gems, Mahindra Finance, Tech Mahindra, Auto, Farm) delivering value simultaneously described as a 'federation' — every engine currently firing and contributing meaningfully to PAT growth.
Growth Gems (Real Estate, Logistics, Aerostructures, Truck & Bus) delivering profits up 3x, with format going forward to bring multiple business leaders on stage directly for analyst interaction.

key_figures.label: Kharif sowing shortfall vs last year

subsections.label: Rural demand risk / El Nino concerns
points: Positive enablers highlighted despite El Nino fears: farm labour shortage (accelerating trend as labour moves to industrial areas for better pay) driving mechanisation; healthy Rabi cash flows with wheat procurement up ~19%; rainfall deficit improved from very bad in June to 15% currently (varies by region); sentiment on ground is 'non-negative' despite data suggesting rainfall-driven negativity because rains have come in most parts of country; reservoir levels recovering though still 7% below LPA; Kharif sowing accelerated after rains started, shortfall vs last year only ~4%; government spending (including states) up 16% supporting rural cash flow.

Caveat: need to see what happens to rainfall and other factors over next two months; at the moment rural market reality assessed as reasonably okay based on last three months' volumes and early July signs.

subsections.label: Commodity inflation risk
points: Auto commodity price impact 400-500 bps in the quarter; escalated significantly after February.

Farm has completely unhedgeable steel and rubber inflation (steel +24%, rubber +30-53% since start of calendar year); price increases taken are insufficient given further escalation; temporary blip likely, duration dependent on how long price rally continues.
Commodity prices have started rising again even after price hike decisions were taken in Auto.
Auto hedging loss on aluminium/precious metals of 85 bps QoQ impact.

subsections.label: International farm business risk
points: Impairment taken on Erkunt Foundry and one more international subsidiary company, contributing to loss in international subs column.
International headwinds noted; company continues to have certain weak spots internationally that need fixing.

subsections.label: Production constraints
points: SUV and LCV volume growth impacted by production issues, especially in April and May.

subsections.label: Capacity constraint risk
points: Company is 'strapped for capacity right now' in Auto/EV; plan to double capacity from current level over several years to address this constraint, phased through FY31.

subsections.label: Season shift risk (tractors)
points: Festival (Navratri) has moved to 11th October this year vs Q2 last year when Navratri had already started and peak volume occurred in Q2; this season shift combined with operating leverage effects creates added complexity for Q2 tractor margins on top of commodity pressure.

subsections.label: PLI subsidy dependency
points: No specific timeline yet on whether PLI 2.0 continues beyond FY28; expectation is PLI should reduce as EV margins improve with scale, to avoid supernormal profits based on subsidies; more clarity expected in next 6-12 months.
Company confirmed EV business is EBITDA positive without PLI currently, though exact PLI contribution amount not disclosed.

subsections.label: Group outlook
points: ROE at 23% this quarter is higher than expected but management is not resetting target expectations, maintaining 18% ROE target going forward.
Growth continuing to outpace targets, EPS growth at 34% with ₹48 EPS this quarter, described as consistent delivery.
Cautiously optimistic overall outlook given challenges of last 3 months; team delivered better results than might have been expected 3-4 months ago.

subsections.label: Auto margin outlook
points: Expectation that Q1 was a low point for Auto margins and margins should improve from here absent further dramatic commodity moves.

Sequential expectation: maintain or slightly improve Operating Profit margin between Q1 and Q2, aided by conscious aggressive 2.7% average price increase taken to avoid disruptive incremental hikes; headroom from GST reduction retained since prices still below September-October last year levels; no significant demand impact observed so far from new prices.

subsections.label: Farm margin outlook
points: Farm situation more complex: unhedgeable steel/rubber inflation, season shift (festival moved to October vs Q2 last year) creating operating leverage headwind in Q2; hope for softening commodities plus season upcycle entering Q3 which should help tractors.

subsections.label: Tech Mahindra outlook
points: On track for 15% EBIT margin commitment by end of FY27; next phase of Tech Mahindra strategy to be outlined once this phase target is achieved.

subsections.label: Mahindra Finance outlook
points: Targeting 70% mobility / 30% non-wheels book mix by 2031 and ₹3 lakh crore book size by 2031.
ROA target range of 2.2%-2.5% (currently at 2.4%), intended to support Group ROE aspiration (~20% currently, Mahindra Finance's initial ROE target was 15%, currently close to that at present ROA).

subsections.label: Aerostructures outlook
points: Aspiration (from Global Investor Day) to grow 30x over a decade organic+inorganic combined, 10x organic; management indicated confidence to exceed that pace and will share more numbers as milestones approach.
Potential global acquisition being evaluated based on business strength and OEM partner requirements.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion outlook
points: Plan to double Auto/EV capacity between now and FY31 across multiple phases (details in MFG section): ICE and EV capacity ramps through September 2026, end of FY27, Chakan phase 2, and Nagpur phases through H1 CY2029 and beyond.

subsections.label: PLI outlook
points: No confirmed timeline on PLI 2.0 or extension beyond FY28; more clarity expected within 6-12 months; expectation that PLI will reduce as EV margins scale up.

guidance_ledger.statement: Our target is 18%, so we will go slightly up and above 18%. 23% is higher than what we expected as well, but we are not resetting expectations, we will stay with 18% as a target.
Tech Mahindra promise is to get to 15% EBIT margin by end of this fiscal year; on track for that.

guidance_ledger.horizon: over next few years to FY31
guidance_ledger.statement: Plan to double capacity from where we stand today, phased: total September capacity 68,000/month, end of FY27 82,000/month, then 92,000/month with Chakan phase 2, then 20,000/month added in Nagpur in two phases (first phase ready H1 calendar 2029, second a few months later), taking to 2x capacity increase between now and F31.
Sequentially if there is no further dramatic change in commodities, we should be able to maintain/slightly improve the Operating Profit margin between Q1 and Q2.
We are expecting that Q1 in Auto was a low point and it should improve from here.
Some temporary blip is likely in Farm and how long that extends will depend a lot on how long this rally in prices continues in steel and rubber.
As we get into Q3 we are hoping that there will be some softening on commodities plus we also get into season upcycle, which will help tractors.

Our expectation would be that as we start showing higher margins with scale, PLI should reduce. In terms of specific timelines, we don't have an answer on that as yet; we will have more clarity in the next maybe 6 to 12 months.
We would expect the cost curve to kick in on multiple technologies... I think both of these will kick in in the next 12 to 18 months.
The inflection point probably will be after 20-25% EV penetration... a reasonable premium of 5-7% is possible.
We are targeting a ₹3 lakh crore book by 2031.
By 2031, 70% of the book will still be mobility, 30% will be non-wheels.
First goal is to be between 2.2%-2.5% ROA.
Our first stated ROE target was 15%; with 2.4% ROA we are very close to 15% ROE.
We want to be a 10,000 crores company pre-sales by FY30, 14 times what we were in FY20.

Aspiration target that organic and inorganic put together we want to grow the business by almost 30 times in a decade, out of which organic was 10 times; I can assure you we will grow faster than that.
EBITDA positive is just around the corner... that should then lead us to a PAT positive number at some point in time very soon.
We have only 2 lakh square feet of white space available, and that also we should be able to sell it by September.
Tractor growth mid-single digit (~5%).
SUVs (M&M growth, not industry): mid-to-high teens.
<3.5T LCV: high single digits.
We’ll probably add this year 5 to 6,000 by July-August in ICE over what we have right now.

guidance_ledger.statement: Calendar year 2027, will see the addition of new capacity in Chakan for the new IQ platform.
The Nagpur facility, which will come up in calendar 2028, will have primarily the new IQ platform on the SUV side.

Rainfall deficit improved from very bad in June to 15% currently; reservoir levels 7% below LPA but recovering; sentiment non-negative on ground despite headline deficit data; still need to watch next two months.
Impairment taken on Erkunt Foundry and one more company; some international weak spots still being fixed.
SUV and LCV growth impacted by production issues in April and May.
Company 'strapped for capacity right now'; multi-year phased expansion plan underway to double capacity by FY31.

Very difficult but has not caused any disruption.

themes.label: Commodity cost inflation
themes.note: Auto faced 400-500 bps commodity pressure and Farm faced unhedgeable steel/rubber inflation (steel +24%, rubber +30-53%), partly offset by price hikes.

themes.label: Electric vehicle growth
themes.note: EV penetration at 12% for M&M vs 9% industry, EV-SUV growth of 77%, XEV 9S largest-selling EV, capacity being doubled to support acceleration.

themes.label: Capacity utilization
themes.note: Company currently capacity-constrained in Auto/EV; phased expansion plan to reach 92,000/month plus Nagpur additions taking total 2x by FY31.

themes.label: Market share expansion
themes.note: Farm machinery highest-ever quarter, Auto revenue market share steady at 24-25%, SML LCV bus segment moved to number two, Last Mile Mobility EV penetration jumped to 40%.

themes.label: Supply chain challenges
themes.note: Farm channel inventory discipline improved (30-40 days) reducing volatility, but unhedgeable steel/rubber costs and hedging losses on aluminium/precious metals persist.

themes.label: Growth Gems diversification
themes.note: Real Estate, Logistics and Aerostructures delivering profits up 3x collectively, contributing meaningfully to group PAT growth alongside Mahindra Finance and Tech Mahindra turnarounds.

themes.label: AI-driven productivity
themes.note: Company disclosed specific AI use cases across Auto (Paint.ai, Service.ai, Reach.ai, simulation) and Finance (Samurai, cross-sell, service requests) with quantified results and a 50-engineer, 19-model foundation.

key_takeaways: Consolidated profit up 34%, ROE at 23%.
Auto and Farm resilience in a strong quarter despite commodity price impact of 400 to 500 basis points. Auto profits up 21%, Farm up 15%.
Mahindra Finance and Tech Mahindra, on a very strong journey now... Mahindra Finance profits up 78%... Tech Mahindra up 28%.
Growth Gems, profits up 3x for Growth Gems.
Revenue up 28%, PAT is up 34%.
Tech Mahindra driven by margin expansion, EBIT margins up to 14.4% and the promise has been to get to 15% by the end of this fiscal year. On track for that.
SUV volume up 15% despite some challenges from a production standpoint. Penetration for electric is at 12% now.
SML and truck and bus division combination announced, enhancing competitiveness, creating synergies, business now double its size.
Aerostructures: $1.2 billion of cumulated contract wins, half of them in the last year alone at 600 million.
pressing_questions: On the battery electric vehicle business... what is the PLI in the current EBITDA/EBIT margin contribution from PLI, and is there any discussion around PLI 2.0 and whether this might be extended beyond FY28.

On the commodity part in Q2, how do you see the impact coming through in auto and farm, and would the price hikes taken be able to cover the commodity impact? Also, because of the price hikes, is there any thought process on how customers will accept it?

When I add up the comments, we are talking about 450 basis point of commodity headwind in Q1, we've taken 2.7% price hike and yet margin will be neutral-ish, which means almost 650-700 basis point of commodity headwind — is that understanding correct?

quarters.summary: Bajaj Auto achieved record performance in Q1 FY27 despite operational disruptions, with strong growth in exports and electric vehicles. The company plans to expand capacity and focus on premium and electric segments.

subsections.label: Cost & Margin Management
points: CFO called Q1 'hyperinflationary' with commodity inflation rising to ~4.5% of revenue.
Specific increases cited: steel +10%, aluminum/platinum +~40%, rhodium +~40%, plus ABS, copper, nickel, natural rubber.
Inflation broadened into electronics, proprietary components, energy, logistics, labor.
Pricing offset 'nearly about half' of inflation with pricing in Apr & Jun.
Additional offsets: rupee depreciation and discretionary cost rationalization.
Despite cost shock, EBITDA margin 20.9% (+10 bps QoQ, +110 bps YoY).

subsections.label: Capital Allocation, Balance Sheet, and Subsidiaries
points: Standalone FCF ~₹2,300cr (≈80% of PAT); surplus cash ₹21,000cr at quarter-end.
Shareholder returns: CFO clarified July outflows include dividend + recently concluded buyback.
Total payout aligned to prior commitment of 100% payout of FY26 profit (~₹9,825cr).
Cash expected to dip post-July and rebuild toward ~₹15,000cr by FY-end.
Consolidation: Q1 consolidated includes first full quarter of Bajaj Mobility AG, reducing YoY comparability.
Consolidated revenue ₹21,689cr (+65% YoY); consolidated PAT ₹3,226cr (+46% YoY).
Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL/BACM): income ₹1,100cr+, PAT ₹227cr (>2x YoY); AUM ~₹20,000cr (+70% YoY); CAR 19%; ROE >25% (as of Jun 2026).

subsections.label: Forward View
points: Export run-rate ambition: move beyond '250,000 per month' from Q2 onward (vs ~200k/month only a few quarters earlier).
Domestic 2W: portfolio 'turnaround program' and heavy launch calendar.

subsections.label: Segment Mix Shift
points: Management highlighted exports and EV as standout: 'Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double digit EBITDA percentage.'
EV profitability update (explicit): EV portfolio (2W+3W) remains 'double digit' EBITDA margin; Chetak moved from 'EBITDA neutral' to 'EBITDA positive.'
Exports: record volumes, broad-based share gains; aiming >250k/month.

subsections.label: Premium Exports
points: KTM exports from India recovered: +20% YoY; Triumph brand exports +40% YoY.

subsections.label: Domestic CV (3W incl. e‑rickshaws)

L3/e‑rickshaw: new product 'RICI' in ~150 cities; company frames L3 as upgrade opportunity via quality/reliability/ownership experience.
Noted: L3 segment highly disorganized and largely lead-acid; regulatory pressure is limiting lead-acid permits; this is expected to drive lead-acid → Li-ion migration and upgrading.

subsections.label: Near-term Launch Blitz

'an absolutely new 150cc under the Pulsar brand'
'10 facelifts in the 160 to 400cc range' with 'class-leading features,' more electronics, and improved engine performance
'an absolutely new 125cc' Pulsar + upgrades

Later in FY27: introduce 'two new brands in the 125cc segment' (new nameplates, not Pulsar), with differentiated propositions; strategic aim includes upgrading 100cc customers into 125cc where innovation headroom and profitability are better.

subsections.label: Capacity Management
points: Capacity is now the binding constraint; plan to expand ~25% from 7mn to ~9mn units/year focused on EV 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, and 3Ws.
Demand exceeds supply; capacity: currently ~50k/month, immediate unlock to ~60k/month via productivity/vendor actions; broader capacity expansion underway.

subsections.label: Africa
points: Industry grew ~50%; Bajaj grew ~2x that; retail 'doubled,' led by Boxer 125 Heavy Duty (upgrade).
Nigeria: pre-election institutional demand; Bajaj claims it captured disproportionate growth with ~60% retail market share; driven by Boxer equity and 'wide footprint of retail and service network.'

subsections.label: Latin America
points: Continued strong outperformance, especially Mexico (noted as 'amongst the top five markets of the world').
Drivers: success of NS / N250 models, 'well-organized supply chain in Mexico' and favorable tariffs (management cited 3%), plus distribution expansion (75 stores).
Region also positioned as a driver of 'corporate capital' (i.e., profitability/cash).

subsections.label: Asia

Philippines: multiple launches + exclusive motorcycle stores to build the premium/personal motorcycling category.

subsections.label: Supply Disruptions Quantified
points: Multiple concurrent shocks: industrial fuel supply curtailment, West Asia logistics force majeure impacting alloys/polymers, labor shortages due to cost-of-living + elections.
Estimated lost production opportunity: ~10% of volume.

subsections.label: Industry Context (Demand Shape)
points: Domestic 2W registrations +14% YoY (Q1), slower than Q4 (+25%); growth led by EV scooters and 150–400cc motorcycles.
100cc & 125cc segments were 'flattish,' resulting in ~7% industry motorcycle growth.

Management interpretation: stress is concentrated 'down the pyramid'; higher-income cohorts remain stronger. They explicitly linked sentiment drag to West Asia crisis and household fuel pressures ('LPG availability into every kitchen').

subsections.label: Bajaj Strategy: De-emphasize 100cc on Profitability Grounds

Rationale: 100cc structurally shrinking (management cited industry mix decline from ~55% to mid‑40s over 5–7 years) and low 'degrees of freedom' for innovation.

Continue scaling and performance in BACL.

quarters.summary: Bajaj Auto closed a record FY26 (revenue ~INR58,000+ crores, EBITDA >INR12,000 crores at 20.5% margin, PAT ~INR9,825 crores) and a standout Q4 (revenue >INR16,000 crores, EBITDA INR3,323 crores at 20.8% margin, volumes 13.7 lakh units, +24% YoY). Going into Q1 FY27, management flags a softened demand environment (motorcycle industry growth expected to moderate from ~20% in Q4 to 7-9% near term) driven by inflation, price hikes, LPG shortages and manpower migration, alongside a sharply inflationary commodity environment (~3.5-4% of revenue impact) partly offset by pricing (40% covered so far) and a favorable currency tailwind; company remains bullish on 150cc+ motorcycles, EVs (2W & 3W), exports (targeting 220K+ units/month) and expects growth to continue in Q1 despite these headwinds, while the Board approved a 100% FY26 profit payout via dividend and buyback.

subsections.label: Commodity & Currency Context
points: Q4 characterized by inflationary pressures across the basket; noble metals (rhodium, palladium, platinum) firmed 20-25%, broader inflation in copper, aluminium, lead.
Steel, ABS, nickel and natural rubber were relatively benign/stable for most of the quarter, though these started to inflate towards period-end, carrying steep inflation into next quarter.

Previous guidance was cost inflation of 50-60 bps, with plan to cover about half via pricing; commodities settled within that range due to good purchase team work, pushing out the impact so it did not hit Q4 results.

Net cost inflation of 40 bps came in after taking pricing, partly offset by absorption of the full quarter's impact of the PM E-DRIVE phase-out for electric 3-wheelers (budget outlay ran out end of Q3; absorbed to support competitive growth/market share).
Currency was distinctly favorable: rupee depreciated through Q4, providing sequential and YoY tailwind supporting margins amidst inflation.

subsections.label: Revenue Drivers Q4
points: Growth was broad-based: across 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers and exports, volumes grew 20% each and revenues 30% each.

Revenue supported by rich sales mix: rebound in KTM exports, higher contribution from commercial vehicles (domestic and international), continued traction in sports motorcycles — all structurally revenue accretive.
Favorable currency movements further aided revenue.
Spares revenue at steady INR1,700-1,800 crore range provided recurring support to revenue and profitability.
Exports revenue reached a new high of nearly $600 million in the quarter.

subsections.label: Margin Drivers Q4
points: Sequential margin held flat, supported by favorable currency, richer mix and operating leverage, which absorbed net commodity inflation and higher discretionary spends (notably marketing and R&D) plus full-quarter PM E-DRIVE absorption.
YoY margin expansion of 60 bps driven by operating leverage and currency tailwinds while managing cost inflation.

subsections.label: FY26 Full Year Recap
points: Highest ever annual volumes at over 5 million units — only second time achieved (last FY2019); achieved across both domestic and exports.
Domestic saw subdued H1 with acceleration in H2 aided by GST rate rationalization and buoyant festive season.
Commercial vehicles, 125cc+ segment, KTM, Triumph and Chetak all registered new highs in billing and retails; export volumes ex-Nigeria at all-time high; CV exports grew nearly 50% for the year.

Revenue growth was primarily volume-led with contribution from richer sales mix (higher share of sports motorcycles domestically, sharp step-up in KTM and CV within exports, growing electric contribution across 2W/3W); currency added further uplift.

EBITDA margin improvement driven by favorable currency, accretive mix and operating leverage on larger revenue base, more than offsetting commodity inflation (especially in H2) and pricing/investment actions.

Electric portfolio hit double-digit EBITDA margin in entirety for first time in the year, driven by rising scale of profitable electric 3-wheelers and improving Chetak unit economics (now EBITDA-neutral as a portfolio).

Two exceptional items in FY26 (Q3 charge of INR58 crore from Labor Code wage redefinition reassessment; Q4 gain of INR35 crore from sales tax deferral prepayment) largely offset each other for the full year.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 Commodity Outlook
points: Commodity environment has moved to being sharply, almost hyper, inflationary with tight material availability on aluminium alloys and polymers; company taking decisive actions to secure supplies.
Inflation now visible across almost entire basket including base metals (steel, aluminium), not just noble metals; largely event-driven (supply shock).
Quantum of increases stepped up materially vs previous quarter: steel ~15%, copper ~20%, aluminium and noble metals up 35-45%.
Estimated material cost inflation impact of ~3.5-4% of revenue at portfolio level (will vary by model/segment); situation described as volatile and dynamic, could change.

Judicious pricing actions taken to offset about 40% of this impact so far; company watching developments closely, acting dynamically — accelerating cost programs, being mindful/choiceful about discretionary spend, and considering further pricing only as a later recourse.
Currency continuing to emerge as a tailwind providing some cushion; realized rate moved from $90.6 (Q4) to hovering $94-95 currently.
Rate negotiations/locking now happening at shorter frequency (not quarterly) given dynamic environment; benefit of any settling down could translate into costs sooner rather than later.
Next round of pricing viewed as likely the last resource if required, to protect competitive growth, after exhausting cost savings and discretionary spend pullbacks and considering currency tailwind.

subsections.label: Capital Allocation & Cash
points: Closed year with cash surplus of over INR18,000 crore after deploying capital on multiple fronts, reflecting strong consistent cash generation.
Capex for the year ~INR500 crore, split equally between ICE and EV investments.
Invested over INR2,300 crore between BACL (to support scaling of lending book) and BAIH BV (in furtherance of KTM transaction).
Free cash flow >INR8,000 crore, reflecting robust cash conversion on profit.
Returned about INR5,900 crore to shareholders via dividends last year (July, pertaining to previous financial year).

Board approved payout of 100% of last year's profits (INR9,825 crore) in recognition of the Bajaj family's 100-year milestone: final dividend of INR150/share (aggregating INR4,192 crore) plus buyback under tender route (INR5,633 crore) at INR12,000/share.

Buyback in excess of 10% of free reserves (threshold ~INR3,500 crore) requires shareholder approval; process to run now, likely culminate by end of July with SEBI filing; payouts expected second week of July; dividend paid after AGM also in July.

subsections.label: Other Operating Income
points: Other operating income line driven by 3 factors: PLI scale-up from electric business as volumes move to higher slabs, export incentives from scale-up of exports, and robust growth in BGO/oils business royalty income.
No other material items sit in that line.

subsections.label: Exports Business Unit
points: Exports BU crossed 600,000 units mark for 2nd consecutive quarter, growing 25% YoY, resulting in highest ever quarterly export revenue.
FY26 was second-highest ever in volume terms but highest ever in revenue terms at USD2.2 billion — achieved despite Nigeria (largest volume market) operating at 50% of peak performance.
Nigeria reached stability in Q4, crossing 1 lakh units, delivering full-year performance equal to FY25; wide retail distribution footprint gives competitive edge with 50% retail market share.
Latam delivered sustained growth for 11 consecutive quarters, another all-time high, driven by strong growth across almost every country; remains key driver of export volume, revenue and EBITDA.
Asia recorded double-digit growth, particularly Sri Lanka, Philippines and Nepal, enabling Pulsar brand record export volume for the quarter.
Of top 30 markets (80% of emerging market industry), company grew at almost twice the industry rate in Q4.
KTM motorcycle exports from India revived after past quarters' disruption.

Brazil: supported by expanded manufacturing capacity (now 60,000 units/annum), new product introductions (400 NS) and wider market presence (~70 top-class stores); reached #5 position in April in share terms — youngest company (3 years old in Brazil vs Bajaj Group's 100 years) to break into top 5.
Company targeting export run-rate of 220,000 units/month this quarter, up from 200,000 level, despite loss of business in Gulf region due to geopolitical issues.

subsections.label: Domestic Motorcycles
points: Industry had split trajectory in FY26: muted H1, strong H2 recovery driven by festive season and GST rate cuts, resulting in ~11% full-year growth.
Growth driven by upper half of industry: 125cc+ growing faster than 100cc, with 150cc+ the fastest growing segment.
Clear turnaround in sports segment (150cc+) performance with sequential market share gains month-on-month, driven by refreshed Pulsar portfolio.
10 new Pulsar variants/upgrades introduced Oct-Mar now contribute 50% of sales, signaling good acceptance.
Share gains in H2 were secular across every state (J&K to Tamil Nadu, Northeast to Rajasthan), each growing faster than industry in their region.
Led by N and NS series of Pulsar, which grew at over twice industry rate in Q4.
Further upgrades/interventions planned across Pulsar portfolio in 125 and 150-plus segments in coming months to capture festive season surge.

subsections.label: Probiking (KTM & Triumph)
points: Continued steep growth trajectory; combined domestic volumes ~43,000 units in Q4, +43% YoY — highest ever quarterly performance.

KTM growth led by strong demand across Adventure and street portfolios, with Duke 250 leading street segment; Adventure portfolio strengthened with KTM 390 Adventure R launch in January (most off-road capable adventure motorcycle in India); more tax-friendly 350cc variants introduced.

Triumph delivered highest ever performance, driven by Speed 400; crossed 1 lakh unit milestone since inception within 2.5 years; portfolio expanded with 350cc platform (lower GST benefit) and Tracker 400 launch in Q4.
Continued investment in performance sports category via events: KTM Cup, Adventure Rally for KTM, Epic Rides, World of Triumph Expos.
Triumph Scrambler along with KTM and Triumph Adventure bikes achieved leadership share in the adventure segment in Q4.
Joint KTM/Triumph showroom rollout progressed with 80 showrooms operational, helping drive reach while maintaining differentiated brand presence.

subsections.label: Chetak (Electric Scooter)
points: Crossed 1 lakh retail mark for first time in a single quarter in Q4, highest ever quarterly retail; March'26 was largest month with 50,000+ retails.
Market share moved to ~23%, up 170 bps sequentially, amid strong consumer sentiment shift toward e-scooters (segment grew 40% in Q4, 60%+ in April, far outpacing ICE scooters).

Key contributor to Q4 sequential share gain was Chetak C25, new variant addressing youth needs for lighter, faster, easier last-mile mobility, combining everyday usability with Chetak's trusted durability/build quality.
FY26: crossed 5-lakh unit mark at INR4,000 crore revenue; reach at 500+ exclusive Chetak stores plus ~3,000+ shared motorcycle stores across 850+ cities.
Chetak commenced international exports in Q4 to Sri Lanka, Philippines and Nepal — seen as potentially significant opportunity in due course.

subsections.label: Commercial Vehicles / 3-Wheelers
points: Landmark year: first time CV business crossed 5-lakh unit mark for full year, reflecting ICE leadership and EV portfolio scale-up.
Q4 delivered highest ever quarterly CV volumes, +28% YoY; ICE franchise remains solid with ~90% share in CNG segment.

Maintained #1 position in electric 3-wheelers throughout Q4 and April in registrations; scale-up accompanied by healthy profitability, making E3-wheelers strong contributor to top line and bottom line.

Q4 highlight: launch of WEGO 9018, largest electric 3-wheeler in the industry, powered by 17.7 kWh battery with advanced PMS and regenerative braking, delivering max range of 296 km (highest in segment).

Riki (E-Rick) progressing steadily with presence in 100+ cities; segment itself has slowed due to enforcement of regulation, which is helping consolidate the industry in favor of larger/better OEMs; even so, ~30,000 units/month run-rate still offers large opportunity via quality/reliability upgrade.
Electric 2W+3W business is now the largest in the auto industry for the company, accounting for 20%+ of domestic revenues and contributing double-digit EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Spares Business
points: Sales of INR1,700+ crore, growth of 16%, delivering record EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: BACL (Bajaj Auto Credit) Business Update
points: Excellent year, scaled up rapidly; customer base ~1.8 million supported by ~6,200 outlets covering nearly entirety of Bajaj Auto retail network.
2-wheeler lending delivered robust growth with continued strength in core motorcycles and strong traction in EVs and premium segment (KTM, Triumph).
3-wheeler portfolio was a standout, recording ~49% volume growth, led by significant EV segment expansion and introduction of new business and refinancing models.
Total income crossed INR3,000 crore; PAT INR665 crore vs INR58 crore prior year, near 12x increase — business now hitting meaningful scale.
AUM reached ~INR19,000 crore, roughly doubling during the year; disbursements a tad under INR15,000 crore.
Onboarded over 1 million customers last year; asset quality remains healthy; capital adequacy ratio 19.5%; delivering industry-leading ROE of ~23%.
BACL now a material earnings contributor within the group within 2 years, positioned as strategic enabler within the Bajaj Auto ecosystem.

subsections.label: EV Revenue & Margin Detail (Q&A)
points: EV revenue (2W+3W combined) of INR8,000 crore delivers double-digit EBITDA margin, achieved despite Chetak (2-wheeler) being EBITDA neutral — driven by rising proportion of profitable electric 3-wheelers.

subsections.label: Upcoming Product Launches
points: New range planned in both 125cc and 150cc plus segments; new introductions expected to hit market as early as July under the Pulsar brand.
A 125cc affordable motorcycle is 'very much in the cards' though launch date undisclosed.

NS range introductions include NS 400 upgrades and variants that have been well accepted even in markets where the company doesn't enjoy a strong competitive ratio (e.g., UP), contributing to NS range growing at twice the sport segment growth rate.
Both the 125cc and 150cc plus new ranges expected to make their appearance in July.

subsections.label: WEGO 9018 Technology
points: Largest electric 3-wheeler in the industry, powered by a 17.7 kWh battery with advanced PMS (permanent magnet synchronous motor) and regenerative braking, delivering a max range of 296 km — highest in its segment.

subsections.label: Chetak Capacity Expansion
points: Demand for Chetak has not been fully met for various reasons; capacity now at 50,000 units/month, expected to be maxed out, contingent on labour issues and fuel availability at Tier 1/Tier 2 vendors not playing spoiler to reach 100% utilization.

Serious work underway to determine how/where to expand capacity in a quantum manner; company has reached a point where a substantive capacity increase is deemed needed; will share details once the exercise is complete.

subsections.label: Brazil Capacity Step Changes
points: Manufacturing capacity constrained by localization requirements which change at different volume thresholds (20,000, 50,000-60,000, and beyond 100,000 units — each threshold requiring different localization).
Current capacity closer to 60,000 (50,000 usable); company hopes to hit that level within next 12 months and will look at further capacity enhancement in FY27-28 by mid-year.

Approach in Brazil has been brand-forward rather than volume-forward, launching highest-end models first and investing in exclusive high-end stores to build the Pulsar and Dominar brand franchise, particularly in the first 5 years.

subsections.label: 3-Wheeler Capacity
points: Company is capacity limited in 3-wheelers and working to expand capacity, particularly for larger format 3-wheelers, given the shift in demand from small 3-wheelers toward larger 7 and 9 series 3-wheelers driven by ticketing/shared-ride markets rather than full-hire contracting markets.

Middle East/Gulf overall export base reference

subsections.label: Nigeria Outlook
points: Steady run-rate of 35,000+ units/month (2W) plus 5,000+ (3W) in last 2-3 months, healthy and expected to continue growing.

Watching Nigeria fuel prices which increased ~30%; higher oil prices help Nigeria as a net crude exporter, but lack of refining capacity means consumer fuel prices affecting common man have risen — two factors expected to balance out.
In readiness for season with stocks on ground and strong salesforce engagement with 800+ retailers; good advancements against 125cc bikes from Chinese and other sources.

subsections.label: Brazil Outlook
points: Still small in Brazil, viewed as a very large opportunity; top-down brand-forward approach; positioned with a plant with only 3% duty and ~300 stores (double any competitor including Japanese brands).
Expect strong growth in Mexico with hope that a US-Mexico FTA (June/July) gets signed; other Latam markets (Colombia, Argentina, Peru) recording highest ever sales.

subsections.label: Logistics & Container Availability
points: Container availability flagged as a market-wide issue ('big nightmare'), but years of logistics team experience and coordination between plant and logistics team managing it well.
Exporting one container every 10 minutes, catching 4 ships every day; out-of-the-box thinking used to find alternate routes and ensure container supply amid global disruptions.
No sale lost due to logistics in exports apart from the Middle East, where nothing is currently going to Gulf countries, costing about 5,000-6,000 units/month out of overall 200+ thousand.

subsections.label: Currency/Emerging Market Demand Context
points: Internationally, currency-devaluation-led inflation seen in India has not yet appeared in many emerging markets; demand remains healthy, particularly in Latam, where Bajaj's strong position and sports segment leadership drive rapid growth.
In Asia, Sri Lanka and Philippines continue to be good markets holding strong.

key_figures.label: Supply chain impairment to demand servicing

subsections.label: Supply Chain Constraints
points: Supply chain difficulties in terms of LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired ability to service demand by about 10-15%.
Hopeful these will resolve over time as manpower migration issues ease and people return to work; fuel availability alternates like PNG and vendor realignment underway.

April performance was impaired by 10-15%, largely due to vehicle availability constraints from vendor system facing manpower migration and fuel availability difficulties; if this impairment wasn't present, performance would have been better given spillover of unserviced demand from March/April.

subsections.label: Rate/Sourcing Negotiation Frequency
points: Negotiation and rate locking-in on commodity supplies has moved to shorter frequency rather than the quarterly rates that were the norm in the past, given the dynamic/volatile situation.

subsections.label: 3-Wheeler Structural Demand Drivers
points: 3-wheeler growth (best-performing auto category post-COVID) driven by exploding mobility requirements in non-metro locations and smaller towns.
Driven by huge spread of road network and people traveling between towns for work, choosing shared/commute options over renting homes near workplace.
Women coming out and traveling is exploding mobility requirements; insufficient public transport systems sustaining this phenomenon over several quarters.

Shift toward larger format 3-wheelers (7 and 9 series) as growth increasingly comes from ticketing/shared markets rather than full-hire contracting markets; some competitors remain only in small 3-wheelers.
Retail finance (via BACL) plays a key role enabling asset acquisition and enhancing income for 3-wheeler buyers.

subsections.label: Demand Environment Segmentation
points: Within the moderated 9% growth, upper half of the upper half of the industry is maintaining strong growth, indicating customers with stronger wallets continue to purchase, aided by good start to marriage season in northern India and evidence of upgrading behavior.
In 3-wheelers, ICE segment has come down while electric segment growth has strengthened (e.g., in April) due to LPG shortage, CNG issues and imminent petrol price hikes favoring EV adoption.

key_figures.label: BAIH BV acquisition of Bajaj Auto Holdings AG (formerly Pierer Bajaj AG) stake
Bajaj Auto Holdings AG stake in Bajaj Mobility AG (BMAG)

subsections.label: KTM/BMAG Acquisition Structure & Accounting
points: Bajaj Auto, through wholly-owned Netherlands subsidiary BAIH BV, completed acquisition of 100% stake in Bajaj Auto Holdings AG (formerly Pierer Bajaj AG), which held 75% stake in Bajaj Mobility AG (BMAG), the listed holding entity for KTM.
Transaction completed 18 November 2025; Bajaj moved from minority position to controlling stake; BMAG and KTM are now step-down subsidiaries of the group.
BAIH AG/BMAG/KTM AG Group publishes results on a half-yearly basis per European listing regulations, meaning quarterly financial information was not available in prior periods.

For quarter ended 31 March 2026, group accounted for its share of consolidated BMAG/KTM AG results for the period 1 July to 18 November 2025 (date of controlling-interest acquisition); prior accounting was last done in Q2 FY26 (published November) covering 1 Jan-30 June 2025.
Prior to acquisition, KTM (via BAIH AG) was accounted for as an associate under equity method; post-acquisition (from November onward), BMAG/KTM AG consolidated line-by-line through 31 December 2025.

Going forward, intention is to move BMAG/KTM AG to quarterly reporting (voluntary, aligning with Bajaj Auto's calendar) as a measure of good governance/transparency, consolidated with a 1-quarter lag.
Acquisition accounted for under Ind AS 103 (business combinations); excess of fair value over net assets and purchase consideration recognized as capital reserve in other equity line.
Detailed note on transaction structure and accounting treatment provided in press release; IR team available for offline clarity given the complexity.

subsections.label: KTM Turnaround Plan
points: Focus in 2026 continues to be driving, along with the Executive Board, a broad-based turnaround plan covering portfolio priorities, product development, go-to-market, supply chain (including sourcing), and organizational/structure simplification aimed at rationalizing fixed costs.
Results of turnaround expected to start showing up in the latter part of 2026.

subsections.label: Management Elevation
points: Board of Directors, on NRC recommendation, approved elevation of Rakesh Sharma to Joint Managing Director of the company effective 1 June 2026.

subsections.label: Demand-side Risks
points: Demand environment softened in April due to general inflation, increased vehicle prices, LPG shortages, manpower migration and LPG-shortage-led effect on consumer sentiment.
Price hikes taken by nearly all companies (including Bajaj, from 1 April) mean 30-40% of the GST rate cut benefit previously passed to customers could get rolled back, impacting demand.
Adverse sentiment has set in due to LPG shortage crisis reaching customer homes, causing purchase postponement.
Geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East have caused loss of business in the Gulf region (5,000-6,000 units/month), with hope for no further disruption.
Nigeria fuel prices increased ~30%, which could affect consumer demand even as higher crude prices benefit Nigeria as a net exporter.

subsections.label: Commodity/Cost Risks
points: Cost environment saw a potential rise during the quarter of about 3-5%, driven by the metal complex, partially addressed via price hikes from 1 April and helped by favorable USD realization.

Q1 FY27 commodity environment sharply/hyper inflationary; tight material availability for aluminium alloys and polymers; inflation is largely event-driven (supply shock) and highly volatile — 3 refreshes to the outlook in the last 4 weeks alone.
Uncertainty over how long the event-driven inflation will last and how the situation evolves through the rest of the quarter.

subsections.label: Supply Chain Risks
points: LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired ability to service demand by 10-15%.
Container availability flagged broadly as a market issue amid global logistics chaos.

subsections.label: Currency Risk
points: Company is not hedged on currency and realizes at market rates, meaning it is exposed to currency volatility both as a tailwind and potential risk.

subsections.label: E-Rickshaw Regulatory Risk
points: E-Rick segment itself has slowed down due to enforcement of regulation on the streets, though this is viewed as helping consolidate the industry in favor of larger, better OEMs.

key_figures.label: Dividend payout of profits (100 years milestone)

subsections.label: Near-Term Demand Outlook
points: Motorcycle category expected to slow from ~20% growth in Q4 to an estimated 7-9% in the near term (next few months, not a full-year call), due to inflation, price hikes and sentiment effects.
Growth expected to come almost entirely from the 125cc+ segment, and even more from the 150cc+ segment, which should grow at twice the industry rate; April outcomes support this view.
Electric category (2W and 3W) expected to witness continuity of growth or even a further increase, helping mitigate overall demand softening since 150cc+ and electric are the company's focus areas.

Base effect will start kicking in for H2 FY27 given lower H1 FY26 base and stronger H2 FY26 sales; full year growth exit rate not being wagered at this point — depends on inflation/pricing impact on reversal of GST benefits.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 Growth Tempo
points: Company expects growth tempo to continue in Q1 based on strong competitive positions in 150cc+ domestic motorcycles, EV business (2W & 3W), and continued performance in large stable territories like Latam and parts of Asia.
Through Q1 and rest of FY27, focus remains on gaining share in 125cc+ (particularly 150cc+) via new product launches and brand development timed for the festive season.

subsections.label: Export Outlook
points: Pushing exports to 220K+ units/month level, leveraging sports segment leadership in Latam and more aggressive outreach to gain share in commercial bikes, particularly against China-origin competitors.

Exports expected to continue doing well aided by disproportionate share of growth from strong retail presence and brand/channel investment in key markets; hopeful of pushing beyond 200,000 units/month in Q1.
Whether exports outgrow domestic in FY27 is uncertain given many variables (logistics, currency, demand), but company optimistic about both.

subsections.label: Super Premium (KTM/Triumph) Outlook
points: Plan to accelerate growth in both Triumph and KTM based on network expansion and launch of more tax-friendly 350cc variants.

subsections.label: Electric Business Outlook
points: Plan to deepen leadership position leveraging wider existing product portfolio, planned new launches, and expansion of exclusive network.
KTM AG turnaround support to continue, aiming to bring KTM back to original performance in due course.
Key focus area: balancing growth and profitability optimally through robust operational management given the current environment.

subsections.label: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL) Outlook
points: Continue to build capability and leverage scale in Bajaj Auto Credit to deliver industry-class-leading performance.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 Cost/Margin Management Outlook
points: Intention, once steady state is reached, is to continue holding and driving margins as done historically; but near-term situation remains highly dynamic and volatile with frequent commodity outlook refreshes (3 refreshes in last 4 weeks).

Strategy: continue judicious pricing (40% of impact covered from 1 April), hard look at discretionary spend, accelerate cost savings, and evaluate further pricing only as a later recourse while protecting competitive growth, factoring in currency tailwind.

subsections.label: New Product Launch Timing
points: New range in both 125cc and 150cc-plus segments expected to launch as early as July under Pulsar brand; 125cc affordable motorcycle also in the pipeline (timing undisclosed).

subsections.label: Chetak Capacity Outlook
points: Substantive capacity increase in Chetak deemed necessary; exercise underway to determine how/where to expand capacity in a quantum manner, details to be shared once complete.

subsections.label: Buyback Timeline
points: Shareholder approval process for the buyback (exceeding 10% of free reserves threshold of ~INR3,500 crore) starting now, expected to culminate by end of July with SEBI filing; payouts likely second week of July; dividend paid after AGM, also in July.

guidance_ledger.statement: This is bound to slow down the motorcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.
We expect this growth to come almost entirely from the 125cc plus segment and even more so from the 150cc plus segment, which should grow at twice the industry rate.
The electric category in both 3-wheelers and 2-wheelers will witness not just continuity of growth, but perhaps a further increase in growth.
We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels.

We expect our growth tempo to actually continue in Q1 basis the strong competitive positions we enjoy in the key segments like the 150cc plus in domestic motorcycles, the EV business, both in 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers and the continued performance in large and stable territories like Latam and parts of Asia.

In exports, pushing exports to the 220K plus levels on the back of leadership in the sports segment in Latam and a more aggressive outreach in gaining shares in commercial bikes, particularly from competitors originating in China.
Super Premium segment accelerate growth in both Triumph and KTM basis network expansion and the launch of the more tax-friendly 350cc variants.
In electric business, we will deepen our leadership position, leveraging the wider product portfolio, which is already there and some new launches planned and the expansion of an exclusive network.

KTM AG, we will continue to support the management there in the turnaround, which is well underway to bring back KTM in due course of time to its original performance. I expect the results of this to start showing up in the latter part of 2026 itself.
We will continue to build capability and now leverage scale in Bajaj Auto Credit to deliver an industry-class-leading performance.
We are currently estimating a material cost inflation impact of approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue.
We have taken very judicious pricing actions to offset about 40% of this impact so far.
Once we get to full year basis and when I mean full year, essentially, once we get to steady state, obviously, the intention will be to continue to hold margins and drive margins the way we have.
We have now reached a position where we think a substantive increase in capacity in Chetak is needed... once we are done with that exercise, we'll be happy to talk to you guys about it.

We are seeing in the next 12 months hoping to hit that kind of thing [50,000-60,000 usable capacity]. And as we move forward and hit it, by middle of the year, we will start looking at further enhancing our capacity in the year '27-28.
We will have a new range in both the 125cc and the 150cc plus range... we hope to see these new introductions hitting the market as early as July in the Pulsar brand itself.

This is essentially a process which will run right now, starting now and likely culminate by the end of July with the SEBI filing... payouts would essentially happen sometime in the second week of July likely.

guidance_ledger.metric: Full Year Motorcycle Growth Exit Rate
guidance_ledger.statement: I would say, in the next few months. At this point of time, I won't wager a full year exit.
We could be looking at something like 12% to 15% growth over the next few months.
We expect to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus segment and particularly in the 150cc plus segment.
We expect to start to scale up Riki beginning quarter 1.
We are taking steps to build three-wheeler capacity, particularly in the e-vehicle segment.
We will aim to maintain the leadership position here on.

key_takeaways: Record revenues at INR58,000-plus crores, record EBITDA crossing INR12,000 crores for the first time with margins at 20.5% and record PAT, which was INR9,800-plus crores, also a new peak.

Quarter 4 was a standout quarter with revenues crossing INR16,000 crores, EBITDA at INR3,300 crores and margins at 20.8%. Total volumes reached a new high of 13.7 lakh units, growing 24% year-on-year.
Exports business unit crossed the 6,00,000 units mark for the second consecutive quarter, clocking 25% growth year-on-year, resulting in the highest ever quarterly revenue from exports.
In FY26, Chetak crossed the 5-lakh unit mark at INR4,000 crores in revenue... Market share has moved up to almost 23%, a gain of 170 basis points sequentially.
The commercial vehicle business crossed the 5-lakh unit mark for the full year, a milestone that reflects both our ICE leadership and the scaling up of our electric portfolio.

We expect our growth tempo to actually continue in Q1 basis the strong competitive positions we enjoy in the key segments like the 150cc plus in domestic motorcycles, the EV business, both in 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers and the continued performance in large and stable territories like Latam and parts of Asia.
We are currently estimating a material cost inflation impact of approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue... we have taken very judicious pricing actions to offset about 40% of this impact so far.

The Board of Directors at its meeting earlier today approved a payout of 100% of the profits that we have made last year in recognition of the 100 years milestone of the Bajaj family in India... a final dividend of INR150 per share that will aggregate to INR4,192 crores and the balance of about INR5,633 crores will be towards a buyback under the tender route at a buyback price of INR12,000 per share.

subsections.label: Gross Margin Drivers
points: Substantial inflation seen in input costs across key commodities: aluminum, crude oil, steel, copper, precious metals.
Additional disruption in supply chain and logistics contributed to cost pressure, though challenges have been mitigated so far.
Net impact of about 4% to 4.5% on margin from increased input cost of commodities and processes involved.
Value engineering benefits of about 0.4% achieved; company continues to advance value engineering and cost reduction programs.
Advanced purchase program conducted for critical parts and raw materials, expected to kick in further going forward.
Price increase of 1.75% on majority of 350cc motorcycles in April 2026 partly mitigated commodity impact, contributing about 1.2% benefit against overall commodity piece.
Remaining 0.2% benefit from mix and other factors.
Commodity situation remains volatile; management declined to give forward guidance on commodity impact for Q2, but noted slight softening versus Q1 headwind depending on inventory holding period.

subsections.label: Other Expenses Decline Drivers
points: Other expenses lower by about 7%, driven by multiple factors.
Q4 FY26 had marketing ad campaigns around the Cricket World Cup costing about INR20 crores, which did not recur in Q1 FY27.
INR10 crores benefit from two product launches that occurred in Q4 FY26 but not in Q1 FY27, totaling INR30 crores of non-repeat expenses.
Remaining INR22 crores benefit from controlled marketing expenditure given the current situation.

subsections.label: ASP and Non-Vehicle Revenue Drivers
points: ASP growth of 2.8% from Q4 FY26 driven by price increases (1.2%), international business mix increase (1%), currency depreciation (0.4%), and allied business revenue increase (0.6%).
International business revenue crossed INR1,000 crores for the first time, now 15.3% of revenue vs 13.7% in Q4 FY26.
Allied businesses (spare parts, service income, accessories, apparel) now about 15% of revenue.
Service job cards grew ~20% YoY, averaging about 9 lakh per month, described as a huge growth driver.
Accessories and apparel growth of more than 30%; almost all bookings through 'Make it yours' feature lead customers to add accessories.
Accessories penetration increased from initial 35-40% to current 87% of consumers buying motorcycles also buying accessories; more SKUs being added as penetration rises.
Apparel business has moved to a 'core collection' brand strategy; roadshow received overwhelmingly positive response from dealers and customers.
Extended warranties and customer retention for service are also growing, supporting non-vehicle revenue.

subsections.label: Depreciation Increase
points: Depreciation increase this quarter attributed to capitalization related to new module and Flying Flea launch (start of production and start of sale).
Average gross block increased by approximately INR346 crores.
Some tools and dies depreciation also kicking in.

subsections.label: Standalone vs Consolidated Revenue Gap
points: Gap between standalone and consolidated revenue of over INR400 crores in Q1 FY27 versus average gap of around INR200 crores in the last 4 quarters attributed to growth from subsidiaries, particularly strong performance in Brazil and other international subsidiaries, offset partly by revenues booked in India for exports and subsidiaries.

subsections.label: Capacity Ramp-up and Operational Issues
points: Faced LPG shortage issues in Q1, managed by converting back to PNG.
Faced manpower shortage issues; recruited additional manpower and extended support to contractors.
Faced issues on availability of key commodities, which were managed.
Oragadam and Vallam plants have been running three shifts since April.
First module at Cheyyar kicked in on time in the last week of July, taking build capacity to about 1.5 million motorcycles per year.
Next Cheyyar module targeted to kick in by first week of October; company is trying to prepone this.
Entire brownfield capacity expansion at Cheyyar (from the INR958 crores investment announced in February 2026) will be completed by FY27-28, taking capacity to 2 million.
Andhra Pradesh Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR1,225 crores, Board-approved this quarter) will take overall capacity to 2.45 million by FY29-30, built in modules given continuing growth momentum.
Supplier conference held to discuss inventory situation and align vendor ecosystem; vendors also planning 24/7, 3-shift operations to support production ramp-up.

subsections.label: Inventory / Channel Stock
points: Current dealer inventory stock is about 10-12 days, described as lean due to strong Q1 retail performance.
In-transit inventory adds another approximately 4-5 days on top of dealer inventory (normally max in-transit inventory is about 7 days).

Company is shifting distribution model toward direct billing to dealers to cut inefficiency in secondary transit and depot management; direct billing has grown from about 1-1.5% of volume historically to about 4.5-4.7x that level; expected to save another 4-5 days.
Plan to build inventory ahead of festive season by combining faster capacity ramp-up with logistics efficiency gains (direct billing) and vendor ecosystem readiness.

subsections.label: VECV Distribution/Service Network
points: Added 30 new touchpoints in the quarter to enhance ability to service customers across the country, including the Northeast, in line with focus on uptime.

key_figures.label: International business share of overall revenue
International business growth over last 2 years
International market total size outside India
Royal Enfield market share in international markets
Indonesia CKD plant volume cap without full quota relief

subsections.label: Key International Markets
points: Brazil is the biggest market outside India and is leading growth; retail volume grew over 3x in the last 3 years, built on years of brand-building, riding community development, and events; Royal Enfield holds the number two position in the middleweight segment in Brazil.
Every fourth Royal Enfield motorcycle exported now ships to Brazil; company is setting up its own CKD facility in Brazil due to strong growth momentum.
Rest of LatAm shows strong demand momentum led by Colombia; Royal Enfield is number two in Argentina in the middleweight segment; Mexico is also growing.
USA market has been very slow but showed some green shoots of growth in Q1 following a new trade deal cutting tariffs on motorcycles; management says it needs to wait and see.

Europe is in a market adjustment phase with business pressure on dealers/distributors; company has established its own distributorship/subsidiary performing well, and opened its Riders Club, which has exceeded 42,000 members, building blocks for future growth once market opens up.
APAC market was previously weak due to uncertainties but showed green shoots in Q1 with growth in retail and wholesale.
SAARC (especially Nepal and Bangladesh) saw robust 60% growth last year, driven by strong brand awareness.
Portfolio expanded in Nepal and Malaysia with the launch of 2026 Goan Classic 350; Guerrilla 450 APEX variant introduced in Australia and New Zealand.
Royal Enfield motorcycles (Goan Classic 350, Guerrilla 450, Super Meteor) won industry awards at major automotive shows in Thailand and Malaysia.
Royal Enfield ranked as the world's third strongest automobile brand by Brand Finance.
Company remains cautiously bullish on international markets, expecting normalization of energy situations and tariff conditions to help markets recover strongly.

subsections.label: ASEAN Strategy - Thailand and Indonesia
points: Thailand has a CKD plant; initial expectation was that ASEAN treaty would allow shipping to Indonesia without quota restriction via the Thailand CKD plant, but Indonesia has maintained quota restriction limiting sales to about 10,000 vehicles/year.

Company is exploring setting up a CKD plant directly in Indonesia via an identified assembler/distributor partner; decision expected to be made this quarter; local content requirement for Indonesia CKD is low, allowing a faster path.
Indonesia carries a luxury tax of about 160%+ above 250cc regardless of CBU or CKD status, so a CKD plant would not remove this tax but would remove the 10,000-unit quota cap.

Thailand market has been weak for the past 2 years due to tourism dip and weak economy, but retail momentum and dealer sentiment turned positive in Q1; Royal Enfield holds number two position in the middleweight segment in Thailand.
Company is building brand collaboration in Thailand with Muay Thai and Thailand tourism development to increase consumer awareness ahead of market recovery.

subsections.label: Flying Flea Distribution Strategy
points: First Flying Flea store opened in Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
Plans to expand footprint in Bengaluru first with five additional touchpoints, followed by another five (total 10 locations) over the next 2 months.
City-by-city expansion strategy; once Bengaluru matures across 10 locations, company will open up remaining identified markets (about 6 markets) one by one.

key_figures.label: Royal Enfield India retail volume growth tracked in Q1

subsections.label: Demand Funnel Indicators
points: In India, continuing strong growth momentum, with volumes tracking over about 32% growth over Q1 FY26.

Other funnel indicators such as overall booking, walk-ins, and telephonic inquiries continue to maintain very strong growth, slightly higher than volume growth, indicating unmet demand due to inventory constraints rather than demand issues.
Premiumization trend in the two-wheeler industry continuing over the last 3+ years.

subsections.label: Flying Flea Customer Profile
points: Too early to conclude detailed customer profiling as adoption is at initial adopter stage.
Average age group of interested customers is approximately 25-30 years.
All prospective customers are looking at the motorcycles and taking test rides.
Good interest also shown by existing Royal Enfield owners who have owned motorcycles for more than about 5-6 years.

subsections.label: Customer Demographics
points: Royal Enfield's professional customer profile broadly includes business owners, agricultural workers, students, government employees and other professionals.
Company tracks government employee demand by category (central/state) and tailors marketing activation around pay commission or income tax benefit developments that put free cash in customers' hands.

About 5-6% of buyers are existing Royal Enfield owners upgrading from one Royal Enfield to another; over 70% are upgraders overall; about 25% are first-time buyers, with Hunter and new launches driving increased first-time buyer share.

subsections.label: Growth Outlook for Higher Base Period (H2 FY27)
points: Management expects to continue growth even against a higher base starting September/October, driven by continued strength across the demand funnel (bookings, walk-ins, telephonic inquiries).
Growth strategy includes continued new product launches (Hunter, Guerrilla 450 APEX, Bullet 650, GT Cup series, more CTG updates to come).
Brand awareness and marketing activation spend, which was scaled down last year in Q1 due to supply-demand situation, will be ramped up again.
New business initiatives like Re-own and Assured Buy Back are gaining traction and add to the growth playbook.

subsections.label: VECV Structure
points: Management indicated no current plans to hive off VECV as a separate listed entity; current focus at Eicher Motors level is on EV, with a lot of work still needed there.
Decision on VECV structure has not crystallized.

subsections.label: VECV Fleet Modernization MoU
points: VECV signed an MoU for the fleet modernization scheme PARIVARTAN, announced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for the NCR.
The scheme targets over 2 lakh vehicles; implementation details are being finalized.
VECV is well positioned to address the opportunity with its comprehensive portfolio spanning CNG, LNG, electric and BS-VI diesel solutions.

subsections.label: 125 Years Celebrations
points: Marked 125 years of Royal Enfield with unveiling of World Origin Site plaque at Redditch, birthplace of the brand, with five generations of motorcycles lining Enfield Road for the unveiling.
Flagged off the biggest ever edition of the Himalayan Odyssey, bringing together riders from eight countries, as part of 125-year celebrations.
Opened registrations for the 2026 Continental GT Cup, introducing the GT-R750 for the professional category and expanding the championship to 8 cities in India.
Hosted community experiences including inaugural Himalayan Basecamp: Ladakh Edition, Himalayan Spirit in Kochi, Gymkhana in Chennai, and GRRR Nights in Bengaluru.

subsections.label: Commodity and Input Cost Inflation
points: Substantial inflation seen across key input commodities including aluminum, crude oil, steel, copper, and precious metals.
Supply chain and logistics disruption added further cost pressure, though challenges have been mitigated so far.
Situation remains volatile; management declined to provide forward-looking guidance on commodity impact for Q2, though noted slight softening depending on inventory holding period.

subsections.label: Manufacturing Operational Constraints
points: LPG shortage issues faced in Q1, managed by converting back to PNG.
Manpower shortage issues faced in Q1, managed through additional recruitment and support to contractors.
Issues on availability of key commodities managed during the quarter.

subsections.label: Channel Inventory Tightness
points: Current dealer inventory is lean at 10-12 days due to strong Q1 retail; situation described as tight ahead of the festive season, requiring capacity ramp-up and logistics efficiency (direct billing) to build adequate stock.

subsections.label: Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Uncertainty (International)
points: Dynamic macroeconomic and geopolitical environment affecting international markets.
International markets have been trading through rough patches over past few quarters due to macro uncertainties and industry-specific factors.
USA market has been very slow; Europe is going through a market adjustment phase with dealer/distributor business pressure; APAC previously affected by uncertainties.
Thailand market weak for past 2 years due to tourism dip and weak economy.

subsections.label: Indonesia Market Access Constraints
points: Indonesia maintains a quota restriction limiting sales to about 10,000 vehicles/year regardless of ASEAN treaty expectations from the Thailand CKD plant.
Indonesia luxury tax of about 160%+ above 250cc applies regardless of CBU or CKD status, representing a structural cost hurdle.

subsections.label: Capacity Roadmap
points: Cheyyar brownfield expansion capacity to reach 2 million motorcycles/year by FY27-28.
Andhra Pradesh Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR1,225 crores) to take total capacity to 2.45 million motorcycles/year by FY29-30, built in modules given continuing growth momentum.

subsections.label: Demand and Growth Outlook
points: Management expects growth-led FY27 for both Royal Enfield and VECV, geared for consolidating market dominance.
Confidence that growth can continue even against a higher base in H2 FY27 (Sept/Oct onward) given healthy demand funnel (bookings, walk-ins, telephonic inquiries).
Company will ramp up marketing/brand awareness initiatives to support growth.

guidance_ledger.statement: Entire brownfield capacity expansion at Cheyyar will be completed by FY27-28, taking production capacity to 2 million motorcycles per year.

Board approved investment of INR1,225 crores for Phase 1 of greenfield expansion at Tada, Andhra Pradesh, which at full utilization can produce an additional 4.5 lakh motorcycles per year; total company capacity to reach 2.45 million motorcycles per year by FY29-30.

Both Royal Enfield and VECV businesses are optimistic of growth in remaining quarters of FY27; growth momentum expected to continue even against a higher base from September/October given strong demand funnel indicators.
Company is on track to build inventory ahead of the festive season through capacity ramp-up and logistics efficiency (direct billing), though situation is currently tight.
Management declined to give forward-looking guidance on commodity cost impact for Q2 due to volatility, though noted a slight softening versus the Q1 headwind.

Company continues to advance value engineering programs and cost reduction programs, with value engineering to kick in across all platforms over time, with current focus on the J platform (450cc/650cc).
Decision on setting up a CKD operating plant in Indonesia via an identified assembler partner is expected to be made this quarter.
Flying Flea to expand footprint in Bengaluru with 10 total locations in the next 2 months, followed by phased city-by-city rollout to about 6 more identified markets thereafter.

International markets performance expected to sustain given deep investment in subsidiaries and own teams/CKD plants in markets with potential; growth and profitability from subsidiary formation expected to continue.
No current plans to hive off VECV as a separate listed entity; decision has not crystallized as current focus at EML level is on EV.
Price increases taken in January on select models; focus remains on growth.
Capacity build up will take place in modules without heavy investment.
New products and refreshes will be introduced to support growth.
