quarters.summary: Eicher Motors Ltd anticipates continued demand growth, with strategic capacity expansions and a focus on premium motorcycle segments, while navigating commodity inflation and geopolitical uncertainties.

subsections.label: Demand and channel health
points: Management sees sustained structural demand; explicitly: 'there is no structural correction… demand… continuing.'

Premium motorcycle segment expansion: Govindarajan described premiumization as persistent: 'only the premium segment is growing,' with the premium market expanding from ~70,000/month (FY22/23) to ~1.1 lakh/month now, and RE contributing ~90,000+ of that.
April momentum: Reported April sales ~1.04 lakh, '57% growth' YoY (also referenced strong momentum/'growth of 51%' at one point).

Inventory tightness: Dealer + depot inventory '7, 8 days'; dealer inventory even lower. Short-term constraint attributed to temporary disruptions: 'manpower availability due to elections and LPG shortages' (week-to-10-day phenomenon), now 'back on track.'

key_figures.label: Eicher brand HD trucks market share

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Demand, mix, product actions, and electric entry
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Electric (Flying Flea) entry and commercialization approach
points: Entry into EVs positioned as brand expansion: Flying Flea described as a 'City Plus electric mobility brand.'
Launch: Flying Flea C6 launched in Bengaluru (first week of April 2026) with 'very exciting' response.
Go-to-market: Highly controlled ramp—'deliberate city-by-city approach', currently one store; management stressed 'we are not in a rush' and avoided volume targets.
Product/brand validation signals cited: C6 won the Red Dot Award pre-launch; media ride feedback 'journalists really, really love the motorcycle.'

subsections.label: VECV: Segment performance, market share progress, and EV traction
points: Eicher brand HD trucks: 25,155 units (+14.1%), market share improved to 9.1%.
LMD trucks: 46,195 units, management claimed leadership with emphasis that leadership must pair with 'profitable growth.'
New segment (SUV / small commercial EV platform): 2,452 Pro X delivered including 726 EVs—called out as opening 'an important new avenue for growth.'
Buses: Eicher buses 18,651; Volvo buses record 712.
Volvo trucks: 1,712.
Exports: +33.9% to 6,933 units despite 'challenging external environment.'
Aftermarket: Spare parts sales +13.9% to INR3,045.5 cr (notable scale and growth).

subsections.label: Product portfolio and pipeline (ICE)
points: FY26 upgrades/variants launched: Guerrilla 450 Apex, 2025 Hunter 350, Meteor 350, Goan Classic 350, Himalayan Mana Black; positioned as 'thoughtful upgrades' generating volume gains.
Milestones: Meteor 350 cumulative >6 lakh since 2020. Himalayan 450 +53% to 38,000+ retails globally.
Distribution innovation: Plan to make 350 range more accessible via Flipkart and Amazon (work in progress).

Pipeline disclosure discipline: No detailed timelines, but management confirmed projects shown at EICMA are 'on track… no delay.' Specific callouts: 'S6… will also come in' (Flying Flea S6), and 'Bullet 650… dispatch is already started.'
Segment positioning unchanged: RE reiterated focus on 'middleweight between 250cc to 750cc' and did not signal intent to go below 350cc near term, noting existing platform potential in 350/450/650.

subsections.label: Royal Enfield: Capacity expansion roadmap (key operational lever)
points: Near-term debottlenecking: Current declared capacity ~1.4 million; additional '500 module per day' kicking in June/July raises run-rate to '~1.6 million plus.' Clarified as per-day modular capacity across facilities; effectively brownfield debottlenecking.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion: INR958 cr capex announced; targeted to lift total annual capacity to ~2.0 million by 'Q2 of FY28.'

Greenfield land bank and timeline: Andhra Pradesh greenfield—MoU signed for 261 acres to support future growth beyond 2.0 million. Tentative execution window shared: '24 to 30 months… fully operational' after land and business case finalization.
Strategic rationale: management framed land as the longest lead-time bottleneck—'The longest lead time is always… land parcel in hand.'

subsections.label: Major strategic development: Proposed Volvo JV for captive vehicle financing
points: Eicher disclosed intent to set up a 50:50 JV with Volvo for 'financing, leasing and other financial services business.'
Capital commitment: Eicher investment 'up to INR750 crores for the 50% stake' into Volvo Financial Services India (VFS India) via fresh equity infusion.
Base business scale: VFS India operating 10+ years with AUM INR1,806 cr and net worth ~INR500 cr (as per management Q&A).

Purpose and positioning: Designed as a 'captive financing arm for VECV, EML and Volvo Group products in India.' Meant to improve conversion and customer experience: 'using financing as a lever for… superior customer experience.'
Volvo brings global product capability; Eicher brings distribution and market knowledge to capture business 'in a more aligned and efficient manner.'
Pacing / risk stance: Management emphasized controlled growth and underwriting discipline—JV will be run 'absolutely independently' with decisions based on 'risk profile.'

Capital runway / medium-term AUM aspiration (management math): With additional capital, leverage capacity (they referenced D/E up to 5:1) could support scaling to ~INR9,000–10,000 cr AUM over ~5 years, and 'we don’t think… additional money at least for the next 5 years.'

Notable change: Vinod Aggarwal stated this is the first time Eicher has 'seriously evaluated entering this business,' enabled by the maturity of the Volvo partnership and Volvo’s global financing success.

subsections.label: Margins, commodity inflation, and pricing actions (key investor debate)
points: Q4 FY26 (RE / EML commentary): CFO quantified Q4 commodity impact: ~90 bps margin headwind.
Pricing action: January price increase delivered ~70 bps; residual ~20 bps mitigated via value-driven cost reduction and mix/model price variance.

Q1/FY27 setup: 'war situation' operating environment and mitigation levers Govindarajan described current environment as 'complex because of the war situation' creating both inflation and availability constraints.
Expected commodity headwind: '~3% to 3.5% on the material cost level impact… incremental in Q1.'

Pricing: RE took ~1.75% price increase in April; management implied roughly ~50% recovery of the inflation via price, remaining to be addressed through: accelerated value engineering / cost reduction ('front ending' projects into July/August), austerity measures, and pre-buy and inventory strategies ('we also have done some prebuy'). Management also confirmed operating leverage is an additional mitigant.
VECV pricing response: VECV announced ~2% price increases effective 1 April, alongside ongoing value engineering, commodity optimization, and transaction price improvements.

subsections.label: Industry and demand outlook: Management stance, headwinds, and confidence markers
points: No formal numeric guidance provided for FY27 volumes/industry, but tone remained constructive: RE: strong inquiry/booking rates; 'working on fulfilling the demand.' VECV: 'traction… quite good,' but environment 'dynamic' with 'global uncertainties… supply chain volatility.'
Short-term disruptions: Elections-driven labor migration and LPG availability created ~2–3 weeks of disturbance; management indicated normalization over recent days with production 'back.'
Europe (RE): 'market adjustment year' with industry degrowth and OBD2B pre-registered inventory overhang slowing fresh billings; RE claims to be holding share in a declining market.
US (RE): tariff-related uncertainty acknowledged but characterized as small exposure: 'only about 3% of the total market for us.'
Brazil: explicitly elevated as strategic growth engine—'Brazil is now our largest and the fastest-growing international market, second only to India,' with ~71% growth and product awards.

quarters.summary: Management guided to strong single-digit domestic industry growth for FY'27 with TVS expected to grow ahead of industry, continued EV and scooter momentum, cautious near-term outlook (Q1-Q2) due to commodity inflation (3-5% of revenue) and supply chain/labor disruptions expected to ease within 2-3 weeks, and continued capex/investment behind capacity expansion, Norton, R&D and new product launches including Hyundai-TVS 3-wheeler EV JDA.

key_figures.label: Price increase offset of commodity inflation

subsections.label: Margin trajectory
points: CFO/CEO emphasized looking at EBITDA trajectory rather than quarter-to-quarter movements; EBITDA moved from 6.5% historically to 13.1% in Q4 FY26.

Improvement driven by scale benefits, better product mix, premiumization, 3-wheeler and international business strengthening realization per vehicle, and cost leverage/amortization of fixed costs over larger base.
Management declined to give explicit margin guidance, stating pricing is only one lever alongside value, TCO, technology and connectivity, and variant strategy.

subsections.label: Investment breakdown FY26
points: Of the INR2,400 crores total investment in FY26, the predominant share was for overseas subsidiary Norton, with products readying for Q2 FY27 launch.
INR200 crores invested in TVS Credit Services.
Strategic investment in Dubai (~INR300 crores) to build infrastructure focused on international markets.

subsections.label: FY27 investment/capex outlook
points: Investments (Norton, TVS Credit, Dubai-type items) expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (i.e., INR500-600 crores lower), as many earlier investments are expected to start yielding revenues/results.
New investment opportunities beyond Norton/Dubai/TVS Credit could arise, to be disclosed closer to decision.

Total capex for TVS Motor in FY27 estimated at ~INR3,500 crores, comprising ~INR2,000 crores product development, ~INR1,000 crores+ capacity expansion (1.5 million unit addition), and additional R&D/testing investment.

key_figures.label: TVS Motor International business sales growth
Indonesia products monthly volume (last year avg)

subsections.label: TVS Credit performance
points: TVS Credit achieved record PBT of INR1,248 crores in FY26 driven by sustained growth in disbursements supported by improved consumption sentiment and traction across all retail financing segments.
2-wheeler category witnessed strong demand aided by steady recovery across urban and semi-urban markets; increasing EV adoption supported by broad affordability and good finance penetration.
Consumer durable financing remained steady driven by seasonal purchases and increased discretionary spending.

Company maintained focus on risk-calibrated growth via prudent, proactive underwriting, calibrated credit policy restrictions and sharper credit matrices; overall portfolio quality improved via reduction in total credit cost and GNPA.
TVS Credit continues to focus on leveraging technology, digital transformation, deeper customer relationships while maintaining strong risk management, with external credit rating of AA+.

subsections.label: Domestic portfolio mix outlook
points: EV, scooters, premium and super-premium categories expected to grow well in FY27; economy category expected to face greater challenge due to inflation/fuel price sensitivity among that customer base.
TVS's scooter category share (including EV, SSP) is ~38% currently and is expected to move above 40%.
Strong brands cited: Jupiter, Ntorq, 125, 150 (150 recently launched with outstanding response); Orbiter and iQube doing well in EV; Apache/Ronin doing extremely well in premium/super-premium.
New moped with alloy wheel doing extremely well, indicating customers are willing to pay for added value even amid demand challenges.

Ronin has grown steadily from 2,000 to 4,000 to 8,000+ units/month over the last 3 years domestically, with pull starting in international markets (e.g., Indonesia); management expects it to soon cross 10,000/month and become a long-standing premium brand like Apache.

subsections.label: EV 2-wheeler and 3-wheeler business
points: TVS iQube S launched with 4.7 kilowatt battery, 175 km range, new color graphics; iQube has driven electric mobility adoption in India with 900,000+ cumulative customers.
EV 3-wheeler VAHAN share continuously increasing; company confident of reaching a prominent position in EV passenger and EV cargo segments this financial year.
EV monthly production has moved from average 30,000-32,000 units/month last year to ~40,000 currently, headed toward 50,000/month.

key_figures.label: King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG top speed

subsections.label: New product launches
points: Orbiter V1 (1.8 kW) has done well and targets a different set of customers; now available in 2 ranges - V1 (1.8 kW) and V2 (3.1 kW).
Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) launched across EV portfolio, allowing customers to subscribe to battery usage instead of paying full battery cost upfront.

TVS King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG launched, built on durability and ease of operation with robust leaf spring suspension, ergonomic cabin, top speed of 62 km/h, excellent ground clearance and turning radius; initial response promising and expected to take a prominent position in the cargo category alongside the cargo EV variant.
TVS iQube S launched with 4.7 kW battery and 175 km range, positioned as a favorite EV for families, with new color graphics.

subsections.label: Norton
points: Company invested in Norton since 2021 in building new products; unveiled products at EICMA, Milan with excellent feedback.
New Norton models coming: Manx, Manx R, Atlas, and Atlas GT; more details closer to launch.
Models will be available in Europe and some in India; FY27, especially Q2, seen as a very important period for Norton launches.
Norton products are getting ready at Hosur plant and Solihull; Solihull will manufacture a high-end model while other models will be made in India (Hosur), leveraging India in a big way.
Management views Norton launches as key to redefining the super-premium class globally and a turnaround year for the next phase of growth for TVS and Norton.

subsections.label: R&D and innovation focus
points: Company continues to invest in technology, R&D, innovation and brand building even amid near-term cost pressures.
TVS's strength cited as R&D, software, digital and connected services, driving continuous product investment as a medium-to-long-term growth strategy.
No specific motorcycle category launch other than existing lineup indicated for next 12 months; management reiterated continuous investment behind technology and models that delight customers.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion plan
points: Company is increasing capacity by another 1.5 million units to reach ~8.3 million units given strong demand; this is the first time such significant capacity is being added in the next 12 months.
Work on capacity addition already started in the last quarter of FY26; reviewed quarter-by-quarter.
Company is also planning capacity additions for FY28 and FY29.
Management's stated priority: capacity will not be a constraint to growing ahead of industry.

subsections.label: Norton manufacturing footprint
points: Solihull (UK) plant will manufacture a high-end Norton model; other models will be manufactured in India, primarily leveraging the Hosur plant.

subsections.label: International business performance and outlook
points: Africa, Asia, LatAm remain key regions; Africa has done extremely well; company now focusing on growing LatAm with encouraging traction seen in many markets.
Asia doing well; Sri Lanka fully back on track; Nepal doing extremely well; Bangladesh has undergone some changes with exports expected to start soon.
Q4 exports performance reflects sustained momentum with improved product mix; 3-wheeler export segment has started showing improvement.
Demand for TVS products is strong across every international market; company closely monitoring geopolitical/war-related effects but confident of continued pull for products.
Africa is preferred market for HLX series 100/125/155; demand is so strong company is currently unable to fully meet it.

LatAm growth is ahead of industry (market share gains), but management indicated it will take 2-3 years to build good distributors, brand investment and visibility; LatAm is TVS's focus area going forward alongside strengthening Africa and Middle East (still seen as having huge headroom).
LatAm strategy will use a full portfolio (premium via Apache/Ronin plus entry-level and country-specific models), similar to how Indonesia products (Bebek & Skubek) are performing well.
Company sees opportunity to leverage EV 2-wheelers (iQube, Orbiter) internationally, especially in Asia where response has been good; Orbiter is now being introduced in Asian markets.

Domestic growth in FY26 was aided by GST rate reduction from 28% to 18%; India's large consumer base (1.4 billion) and rural/self-income customers seen as structural demand driver for 2-wheelers; government infrastructure investment (roads) also supportive.

subsections.label: Supply chain disruptions
points: Supply chain disruption emerged post geopolitical unrest (West Asia conflict), with rising gas prices and energy costs affecting commodity prices and availability.

Company keeps only 21-30 days of dealer stock domestically (cash-and-carry model), making it critical to ramp production quickly to meet strong retail demand; delays in energy/raw materials can affect production.
Labor challenges seen across India (not only South), particularly among Tier 2 suppliers; Tier 1 suppliers managing better; company supporting Tier 2 suppliers.

May production improving versus April; channel stock has started improving this month due to better production in first 10 days of May; expect normal 21-30 day range to be restored by end of month/first week of June.
Management expects to be fully out of Tier 2 disruption within 2-3 weeks.
International logistics facing ~15% increase in lead times (about 8-10 days delay) due to container availability challenges, requiring closer planning and support to distributors.
Company working closely with distributors to manage transit delays and support ordering/planning given high demand pull for products in every market.

subsections.label: Competitive/category positioning
points: TVS positioning across EV, scooter, premium/super-premium (Apache, Ronin) segments seen as strong growth drivers versus economy category which faces higher headwinds from inflation and fuel prices.
Value-added products (e.g., new moped with alloy wheel) continue to find demand despite overall category challenges, indicating customers are willing to pay for value.
Company emphasizes pricing as only one lever among multiple (TCO, technology, connectivity, variant strategy) versus pure price-based competition.

subsections.label: Hyundai-TVS Joint Development Agreement
points: TVS Motor signed a joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor Company to commercialize an electric 3-wheeler.
Hyundai Motor will lead design and co-develop the EV 3-wheeler, leveraging its R&D expertise, advanced mobility technologies and human-centric design approach.
TVS Motor will co-develop using its leading-edge electric platform, extensive 3-wheeler engineering expertise and deep local market understanding.

Management declined to give specific timeline/revenue contribution details at this stage, indicating more details will be shared closer to launch; expects the partnership to contribute positively to the company's overall EBITDA journey.

subsections.label: Dubai strategic investment
points: Company established a strategic investment/infrastructure in Dubai with significant focus on international markets, with ~INR300 crores invested cumulatively over a couple of prior quarters.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical risks
points: Ongoing West Asia conflict cited as a headwind affecting commodity prices (steel, aluminum, crude oil derivatives) and input costs, plus supply chain disruption.
Commodity/input cost inflation estimated at 3-5% of revenue for Q1 FY27, described as 'unprecedented' with significant impact concentrated in a single quarter compared to past similar situations.
Company has been able to offset about 35% of price increases needed via pricing actions; continues to monitor and pass on price increases in both domestic and international markets.
El Nino risk could moderate rainfall despite reservoir water levels currently 16% higher, which is good for Kharif season but bears watching for Q3/Q4 impact on rural demand.
Geopolitical situation (war-related) affecting international markets broadly across the industry, not just TVS; company closely monitoring.
Labor availability challenges across India, especially among Tier 2 suppliers, though expected to be resolved within 2-3 weeks.
International logistics delays (~15% increase in lead time, 8-10 days) due to container availability challenges creating distributor planning issues.
Management flagged general 'unprecedented' cost environment requiring close monitoring and countermeasures over the next two quarters (Q1, Q2 FY27).

subsections.label: FY27 outlook
points: Company expects a good single-digit growth for the domestic industry in FY27, with potential for better growth in H2 if conditions improve; TVS expects to grow ahead of the industry.
EV, scooters, super-premium categories expected to grow well; economy category faces greater challenges from inflation/fuel prices.
International market momentum from Q4 FY26 expected to continue through FY27, with company confident of growing ahead of industry despite geopolitical challenges and logistics delays.
Company will remain cautious in Q1 and Q2 FY27 due to raw material availability timing issues and supply chain disruption, though demand itself is not a concern.
Company reiterated it does not give explicit margin guidance but expects EBITDA margin trajectory to keep improving via scale, product mix, premiumization and cost reduction.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR3,500 crores for TVS Motor (product development ~INR2,000 crores, capacity expansion INR1,000+ crores, plus R&D/testing investment).
FY27 investments in overseas subsidiaries/Norton/TVS Credit/Dubai-type items expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (~INR500-600 crores lower than INR2,400 crores).

guidance_ledger.statement: Expecting a good single-digit growth on the industry this year; could be better if things improve in the second half.
Company confident it will grow ahead of the industry across domestic and international markets.
Confident that Q1 will post very good growth better than the industry despite supply chain challenges.
Current scooter category share of ~38% is likely to go over 40%.

guidance_ledger.statement: Prior guidance was that Orbiter would be available all-India by start of Q4; Orbiter has since launched V1 and V2 variants and is expanding into international markets like Asia.
Confident that growth momentum in Africa and LatAm will continue.
Very confident that TVS Orbiter will be available all India by start of Q4.

Challenges seen across India, not only in South, especially among Tier 2 suppliers; company supporting them; expected resolution within a couple of weeks.
~15% increase in lead times (8-10 days) creating distributor planning challenges; company working closely with distributors.

themes.label: Profitability Improvement
themes.note: EBITDA margin improved to 13.1% in Q4 FY26 from 6.5% historically, driven by scale, mix, premiumization and cost reduction; no explicit forward margin guidance given.

themes.label: Supply Chain Challenges
themes.note: Labor availability issues at Tier 2 suppliers, raw material/energy delays and international logistics lead-time increases (~15%) are being closely managed, with resolution expected in 2-3 weeks.

themes.label: International Expansion
themes.note: International business sales grew 33% YoY to 15.8 lakh units in FY26; Africa strong, LatAm identified as next growth focus (2-3 year build-out), Asia markets (Sri Lanka, Nepal) recovering.

themes.label: Product Innovation
themes.note: New launches include Orbiter V1/V2, BaaS across EV portfolio, King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG, iQube S, and upcoming Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas, Atlas GT) plus Hyundai-TVS EV 3-wheeler JDA.

themes.label: GST Impact

themes.label: Input Cost Inflation

themes.label: Capacity Expansion

key_takeaways: TVS Motor Company surpassed all its previous highs and achieved an all-round record performance, achieved the highest ever sales volume, revenue and profit in FY25-26.

Sales volume grew from 4.7 million units to 5.9 million units, a 24% growth. Revenue grew from INR36,251 crores to INR47,270 crores, a 30% growth and operating PBT grew from INR3,563 crores to INR4,975 crores, a 40% growth.
Company's EBITDA grew by 37% to INR6,079 crores; EBITDA margin improved by 60 basis points to 12.9% vis-a-vis last year's 12.3%.
Q4 company achieved the highest ever revenue of INR12,808 crores, a growth of 36% over last year, and achieved the highest EBITDA of 13.1%.
TVS Credit services achieved a record level of PBT of INR1,248 crores in FY25-26; book size is now INR30,631 crores.
TVS Motor International business recorded highest ever sales of 15.8 lakh units in FY26, a growth of 33% year-on-year.
TVS Motor signed a joint development agreement with Hyundai Motor Company to commercialize an electric 3-wheeler.

Company facing near-term challenges from commodity price inflation (3-5% of revenue), supply chain disruption (labor, raw materials) and geopolitical issues (West Asia conflict), but expects to overcome these within 2-3 weeks and remains confident of growing ahead of industry in FY27.
Company is expanding 2-wheeler/3-wheeler capacity by 1.5 million units to reach ~8.3 million units to meet demand; FY27 capex guided at ~INR3,500 crores.

quarters.summary: TVS Motor Company expects continued growth in Q4 FY26, driven by strong domestic and international demand, premiumization, and a focus on cost reduction and product innovation.

subsections.label: Profitability and Cost Management
points: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 120 basis points to 13.1% from 11.9% in Q3 of last year.
On a normalized basis, Q3 FY '25 EBITDA would have been at 12.4%, indicating a year-on-year margin improvement of 70 basis points and a quarter-on-quarter improvement of 40 basis points.
The company recognized INR41 crores as an exceptional item towards the past service cost arising from the new labor codes.

subsections.label: Demand Drivers
points: The low inflation drove demand across product categories, leading to increased sales, deeper market penetration, and enhanced market share.
The company saw a successful festive season with robust demand.
Rural grew by almost 19% and urban by about 21% in Q3 FY26.

subsections.label: Product Performance
points: Scooters have really done well, with a 40% category share of the overall 2-wheeler industry.
Premium and super-premium segments are growing faster than the industry.
The entry-level segment is not growing as much.

subsections.label: Norton and New Products
points: Norton is building the lineup unveiled in EICMA 2025, targeting the super premium category.
The new Manx and Atlas families position TVS in the premium, high-emotion luxury motorcycle segment.
TVS is gearing up for the launch of new Norton products in the Indian markets.

subsections.label: Capacity and Supply Chain
points: There were challenges in EV production due to magnet availability, but the situation is improving.
TVS is investing in capacity increases to meet demand.

points: Material cost ratio: Q4 71.4% of revenue (+80 bps YoY); FY26 also 71.4% (+10 bps).

Commodity pressure: Management flagged 'significant increase… predominantly steel' entering Q1; refused to quantify magnitude ('too early to give a range').
Mitigation toolkit: value engineering, e-sourcing, supplier negotiations, turnover discounts; plus broader OPEX scrutiny.
CFO: cross-functional teams reviewing 'each of the operating expense… head-wise individually' to drive reductions.

Other cost risks into FY27: potential inflation in transportation expense (fuel-linked), conversion costs, and FX (rupee weakening) impacting 'other expenditure.'
Industry pricing discipline: CEO expects discipline to strengthen; 'industry… should look at taking multiple price hikes during the year' given input inflation.

key_takeaways: Demand is being underwritten by replacement + GST-driven TCO reset, with management repeatedly emphasizing baseline resilience despite diesel noise and localized disruptions.

Near-term margin risk is real and concentrated in commodities (steel) plus fuel-linked opex; company response is measured price increases (1–1.5%) + intensified internal cost programs, but with explicit limits if commodities spike sharply.
Mix and product cycle are turning more favorable if mining/infra-led tippers and multi-axles accelerate and new high-HP products ramp—management expects visible share benefit from Q2.

EV strategy moved from 'investment' to 'execution' milestone with Switch India profitability and a tangible battery pack manufacturing timeline; cell manufacturing remains optional/phase-3 contingent on demand.
Capital deployment is flexible and need-based, with likely incremental support for financing and E-MaaS subsidiaries, while Switch India reduces funding burden due to profitability.

quarters.summary: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd achieved record revenues in FY26, with significant growth in emerging businesses and a strong order book providing future growth visibility. The company continues to focus on capacity expansion and strategic partnerships to drive growth.

subsections.label: FY26 headline performance and quality of earnings
points: Record scale: FY26 delivered the highest ever quarterly and annual revenues.
Profitability inflection in Q4 attributed to improving profitability in emerging businesses, particularly lighting and electronics and aerospace.
Margins held despite inflation due to operational excellence initiatives, cost optimization programs, and improving efficiencies across plants.

subsections.label: Balance sheet strengthening
points: Leverage ratio at an all-time low of 0.8x, reinforcing the stated policy of <2.5x and internal aspiration of <1.5x.

subsections.label: Order book, portfolio mix, and strategic roadmap (Vision 2030 / 3CX10 / D.E.M.A.L.)
points: All-time-high book business of USD 96 billion, providing strong visibility for future growth.
Diversified across PV, CV, off-highway, rolling stock, 2W, and geographies.
Management emphasized emerging markets rising in the mix due to growth and manufacturing ecosystems supporting exports under 'globally local'.

subsections.label: Consumer electronics (within Lighting & Electronics / emerging businesses)
points: FY26 revenues increased ~7.5x YoY; Q4 revenues +46% sequentially after the second facility went live in Q3.
Achieved Q4 production run-rate aligned to annual guidance of 14–16 million units.
Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
GF3 described as the group’s largest facility, a size of 33 football fields.

subsections.label: Aerospace (non-automotive adjacency with accelerating scale)
points: FY26 revenues +40% YoY; order book increased >20% to USD 1.6bn.
Won orders across metallic parts, subassemblies, and wire harness for business jets and rotary wing aircraft.
Two new India facilities expected to come up in Q1 FY27 to serve the existing USD 1.6bn backlog.

subsections.label: Wiring harness and broader automotive operations
points: Wiring harness division saw ~170 bps QoQ margin expansion despite copper inflation.
North America recovery optionality expected to support further improvement.

subsections.label: Capacity and ramp characteristics
points: Third facility (GF3) commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27.
Management emphasized electronics ramps faster than auto: orders can move 'straight 0 to 100' once the season/program starts.

subsections.label: Capital allocation, capex pipeline, and shareholder returns
points: FY26 capex: INR 5,911 crore (~49% of EBITDA), allocated to growth, backward integration, and maintenance.
FY27 capex guidance: ~INR 6,000 crore ±10%, with 50% growth / 50% maintenance.
16 facilities under development globally, 13 scheduled to come on stream in FY27; all are in emerging markets.

subsections.label: Supply chain risk mitigation
points: 'Globally local manufacturing strategy' reduced dependence on long-distance supply chains.
Red Sea disruptions had minimal impact.
For customer-nominated components: 'back-to-back supply arrangements' to mitigate escalation.

subsections.label: Inorganic growth pipeline and transaction timelines
points: Atsumitec integration: FY26 was the full first year, progress pleased.

Yutaka Giken acquisition on track to close by end of H1 FY27.
Nexans automotive harness business closing expected end of June, beginning of July.

points: Copper prices increased 16% sequentially in Q4, ~38% YoY.
Middle East tensions led to crude-linked inflation late in the quarter.
Polymer prices in Germany rose significantly post conflict escalation.
Raw materials have long-term pass-through arrangements with major customers; timing lag of 1–2 quarters acknowledged.
Energy/gas/freight and some overhead-type costs are a matter of negotiations, but management expressed confidence in recovery due to strong OEM relationships.

points: Target reiterated: USD 108bn gross revenues by 2030.
ROCE moderated to 16.1% due to capacity build; aspiration reiterated: 40% ROCE across businesses over time.

subsections.label: Automotive production and demand
points: India's automotive production remained robust in the October-December quarter, driven by broad-based strength across Passenger Vehicles, 2-wheelers, and Commercial segments.
Higher festive demand, rural market recovery, and improved supply chain conditions supported manufacturing activity across most vehicle categories.

The Heavy Commercial Vehicle production recorded steady growth, driven by robust infrastructure demand, strong freight movement, and continued momentum from GST 2.0, festive demand, government fleet orders, and ongoing road construction and mining activity.
The bus segment showed notable traction driven by school, intercity, institutional transport orders alongside steady fleet additions by state and private operators.
The LCV production remained robust, fueled by GST rationalization and a visible revival in demand following GST 2.0.
The 3-wheeler segment saw a sharp production increase driven by strong demand for both urban mobility and last-mile delivery during the festive season.
Tractor production showed strong momentum, supported by healthy rabi sowing activity and carryover liquidity from a robust kharif harvest.
The 2-Wheeler production was moderate in October as OEMs adjusted output following earlier inventory buildup, but picked up in November and December.

subsections.label: Sector-wise sales performance
points: The Mobility business has shown significant growth driven by the Power Solutions business, mainly due to growth in Passenger Cars and Off-highway segments.
The mobility aftermarket recorded growth mainly due to GST reforms and strong growth in the OE segment.
The 2-Wheeler business grew significantly due to higher sales of exhaust gas sensors for OBD-II norms implementation.

The Consumer Goods business saw marginal decline due to market challenges but grew in the April-December period due to new launches in entry-level mid-price point segment, measuring tools, and outdoor garden equipment.

subsections.label: Two-Wheeler & Powersports
points: Bosch's strategy focuses on providing advanced technology to enhance end-user experience, playing a key role in the launch of new vehicles by several well-known 2-wheeler OEMs.
The launch of new TVS Apache RTX 300 and Harley X440 T marked significant milestones, integrating Bosch powertrain and safety systems.
Bosch showcased its latest innovations at the EICMA 2025 event in Italy, demonstrating commitment to creating value for partners and end users.

subsections.label: Bidadi plant achievements
points: The Bidadi plant was awarded at the National CII SCALE Awards 2025 for digital excellence and innovation in logistics.
The plant secured the Champions Trophy and the Challengers Trophy at the CI KAIZEN Awards 2025 for developing low-cost solutions in productivity and quality improvement.

subsections.label: Localization efforts
points: Bosch is localizing NOx sensor components for common rails and plans further localization for common rail products.
The company has increased export volumes for spark plugs and components for common rail products, and relocated pumps from Japan to India.

subsections.label: Macroeconomic overview
points: The global economy is adjusting to geopolitical events and trade realignments, with a projected slowdown in global growth from 3.2% in 2025 to 3.1% in 2026.
The Indian economy shows resilience with higher growth compared to peers, supported by resilient domestic demand and easing inflation.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw highest-ever OHT quarterly sales volume (16% YoY growth) with revenue growth of 24% YoY, though EBITDA margin was impacted by raw material inflation and higher India mix; management expects better EBITDA-to-PAT flow-through as On-Highway volumes scale up and core OHT trajectory improves. Forward guidance remains largely qualitative: On-Highway revenue vision of INR5,000 crores by 2030 reiterated, balance capex of ~INR3,000 crores (INR1,500-2,000 crores in FY27) to be spent as per schedule, and further price hikes/raw material impact expected in Q2-Q3, but management repeatedly declined to give explicit forward-looking volume/margin guidance.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin was particularly impacted on account of raw material prices due to geopolitical situation globally and its impact on supply chain.
The impact was partially offset by certain price hikes during the quarter.
India's contribution has increased to overall 40% of the volumes, which has impacted the margin slightly.
India margins are marginally lower than export margins, though not as low as it used to be earlier when India mix was sub-20%.
Company expects better flow-through from EBITDA to PAT as it steadily scales up volumes in On-Highway segment and benefits from improved trajectory of core OHT business.

subsections.label: Employee cost increase drivers
points: Increase in wages in Gujarat contributed to the rise.
Company gave increments to staff.
Staff was increased to support the new (On-Highway) business.
As turnover of the new businesses starts kicking in, employee cost as a ratio is expected to normalize.

subsections.label: Freight cost
points: Freight rate as percentage of revenue is around 5%.
If the geopolitical scenario continues, there may be some increase in freight which will need to be passed on; visibility currently is that it remains similar to Q1 level.

subsections.label: OHT business highlights
points: Highest ever quarterly OHT sales volume reported, led by decent uptick in end markets and segments.
Europe witnessed a stable environment; company working with channel partners across key markets to increase market share.
India performed exceptionally well in Q1 despite a high base from last year, aided by marketing efforts, superior product range, and growing infra capex in India.
In Americas, tariff rate settled at 10% level leading to better performance led by USA; sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets expected to sustain growth momentum.
Long runway of growth expected in Americas given BKT's brand positioning and focus on high-quality products.

subsections.label: Carbon Black business highlights
points: Decent volume growth YoY in Q1 FY27, with third-party sales at around 10% of overall business.
Commissioned Phase II of Carbon Black plant during the quarter, taking total capacity to 360,000 MTPA.
Increased captive power plant capacity to 64 MW as part of energy circularity model.
Geopolitical challenges expected to impact pricing and supply on the back of increased crude prices; some price increases expected to offset raw material inflation.
Demand continues to be robust in this segment.

New Business Head for Carbon Black, Mr. Ashish Kumar Datta, appointed effective July 3, 2026, bringing 36 years of cross-functional leadership experience across chemicals, coatings and polymer industries; previously with Lubrizol Advanced Materials (Berkshire Hathaway company).

subsections.label: On-Highway Business vertical
points: Distribution network and channel infrastructure set up in April; go-to-market strategy went live.
Started supplies in Truck Bus Radial (TBR) segment with positive trade response.
2-wheeler tire product portfolio introduced with select products targeting domestic market, with encouraging feedback from end users.
Launched 24x7 journey assistance program 'YOU FORWARD' in June for 2-wheeler riders across India, positioning company as a mobility partner beyond product offerings.
First digital campaign for the initiative featured actor Rakesh Bedi.
Entry into On-Highway is a strategic adjacency complementing existing OHT strengths.
Business seeded in Q1; gradual ramp-up expected starting Q2.
On-Highway segment currently small; company will refrain from sharing revenue or volume details at this juncture.

Brands launched include Loadxpert, Milexpert, Zenova and Thyros for trucks and 2-wheelers; Q1 was focused on setting up systems and 'seed marketing'; ramp-up of sales and production to proceed as per plan with no surprises expected.
FY27 will be a year of building the On-Highway portfolio; FY28 onwards will be 'serious business'.

Distributor approach is pan-India, not selective; country has been sliced and diced intelligently; distributors appointed across all categories including cars; dealer appointments will increase as production ramps up rather than being over-aggressive upfront.
70 distributors added per Annual Report (context from analyst question).

subsections.label: India growth drivers
points: India revenue growth of over 35% mainly from Off-Highway tire market, coming from all three sectors: agri, mining and industrial construction.
Growth is largely from replacement demand; OE mix broadly remained the same.
Mining sector is also helping aid this growth.
Directionally sustainable growth rather than a one-off, per management.

subsections.label: Capex completed
points: New Carbon Black facility line commissioned in Bhuj, taking capacity to 360,000 MTPA at a capital outlay of INR800 crores.
Power capacity at Bhuj increased from 40 MW to 64 MW at a capital outlay of INR125 crores.
All balance capex projects amounting to approximately INR3,000 crores are progressing as per schedule.

subsections.label: Regional performance and dynamics
points: Europe: stable environment; base last year was lower, and good monsoon/season aided the agricultural segment; company working with channel partners to increase market share.
India: exceptional performance despite high base from last year; India revenue mix higher than Europe revenue mix for the first time in a quarter.

Americas: better performance led by USA with tariff rate settled at 10%; sharper go-to-market strategy and stable end markets support continued growth; long runway of growth given BKT brand positioning and high-quality product focus.

End-user inventory levels described as normal — no buildup or shortage; no meaningful prebuying observed in Europe despite peer commentary on prebuying ahead of price increases (any prebuying, if it happened, would be minimal to the company's knowledge).

subsections.label: US tariff refund
points: Company, like other companies, has applied for US tariff refunds; too early to comment on timing of returns.

Better EUR/INR rate than the Q1 rate of INR102 expected for FY27, though exact rate not shared.

At overall level, company remains focused on: (1) volume growth with margin discipline, (2) leveraging Carbon Black capacities to improve efficiency and quality, and (3) progressively scaling up On-Highway business.
Company not sharing further price hike plans beyond what has already been taken (5% in Q1); still assessing market scenario for additional hikes.

key_takeaways: Q1 started on a positive note; delivered highest quarterly sales volume in OHT segment despite challenges across many international geographies, end markets, and supply chain.
Delivered 16% sales volume growth in OHT on a year-on-year basis, led by decent uptick in end markets and segments.
During Q1, launched on-road products in the TBR and 2-wheeler segment in domestic market.
Stand-alone revenue for the quarter stood at INR3,409 crores, registering a growth of 24% year-on-year.

Stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR703 crores with a margin of 20.61%, impacted by raw material prices due to geopolitical situation and partially offset by price hikes; India's contribution increasing to 40% of volumes also impacted margin slightly.
Profit after tax stood for the quarter at INR432 crores.
Commissioned Phase II of Carbon Black plant during the quarter, taking total capacity to 360,000 MTPA; also increased captive power plant to 64 megawatts.
As on June 30, '26, gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR4,690 crores and INR2,965 crores respectively, with net debt of approximately INR1,725 crores.
Board of Directors recommended a first interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.
pressing_questions: Disha Sheth repeatedly asked about sustaining the 24% sales momentum going forward based on order book, and whether margin profile would tweak as Indian business mix grows to 20%; Rajiv Poddar declined to give forward-looking statements each time, ultimately asking the analyst to refrain from continuing to ask ('I'm repeatedly saying please do not ask the forward-looking statements... third time I'm telling you, please refrain from that. We will not make comments. I'll keep on rejecting the comments.')

Yash Agrawal asked whether investors should expect stronger free cash flow generation and higher capital return from FY28 as the major capex cycle ends; Rajiv Poddar said he cannot comment as it is a Board decision.
Mumuksh Mandlesha asked for an update on the refund of US duty; Rajiv Poddar said it is too early to share details.
Yash Agrawal asked how to think about the core OHT margin profile going forward in the next few quarters; Rajiv Poddar said under current volatility, no comments can be made on future guidance.

quarters.summary: Management flagged raw material cost upticks and margin pressure expected in FY27 due to geopolitical/supply chain headwinds, with price hikes and product mix improvement being used to partially offset the impact. The company stopped giving explicit volume/revenue guidance for FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty, but reiterated its stated 2030 vision for on-highway (INR5,000 crores revenue) and maintained an intent to sustain consolidated EBITDA margins between 23%-25%; total capex plan through FY29 stands at INR6,800 crores (including ~INR3,000 crores already spent), with FY27 capex expected between INR1,500-1,800 crores.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin for the quarter was particularly impacted towards the end of the quarter on account of headwinds faced due to the geopolitical scenario and its impact on supply chain.
FY26 standalone EBITDA registered a degrowth of 10% YoY.
Company is maintaining a steady balance between superior product mix and price hikes to partially offset raw material cost impact.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Other expenses moved significantly in the quarter and for the full year due to increased production (highest ever quarterly and annual volumes), driving higher conversion costs; no theoretical/structural jump, purely volume-linked.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Company paid INR12 per share dividend over the previous 3 quarters in addition to the recommended final dividend of INR4 per share.
Net debt position of INR895 crores as of 31st March 2026, calculated from gross debt of INR4,049 crores against cash and cash equivalents of INR3,154 crores.
Funding source for the balance INR3,800 crores capex (through FY29) will be a mix of sources; company still working on finalizing this.
Management declined to confirm whether current debt level of ~INR4,000 crores represents peak debt, citing volatile environment and ongoing project announcements.

subsections.label: On-Highway business (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR)
points: Entered truck bus radial (TBR) segment with new product launches in February '26, aligned with infrastructure growth and increasing radialization trends, helping tap replacement market opportunities.
Re-launched 2-wheeler tyres with select products targeting the domestic market; products placed in market starting April '26 with focused marketing campaigns featuring brand ambassador Ranveer Singh.
Early market response has been encouraging, reflecting acceptance of product quality and performance.
Company plans to introduce passenger car radial (PCR) tyres by end of current calendar year, following a phased and calibrated approach.
TBR segment impact will be very insignificant in Q1 FY27, but will start gaining prominence thereafter.
PCR positioning is premium — in line with market leaders, not discounted.
On-highway price positioning is at par with market leaders; company banking on product quality, value proposition and operational excellence to gain market share.
Peak revenue vision for on-highway business (TBR + PCR + 2-wheeler combined) stated at INR5,000 crores by 2030.
Distribution: primary distributors nearly complete for both TBR/PCR categories (~90 distributors in all); dealerships will be added as per sales ramp-up.
2-wheeler tyre outsourcing arrangements currently not seen as a limiting factor for scale-up.

subsections.label: BKT brand repositioning
points: Undertook repositioning of BKT brand architecture, differentiating corporate and regular lines by adding 'Tyres' and 'Carbon' to product branding, aimed at making it more contemporary and emotionally engaging while retaining core attributes of performance and reliability.

Integrated product and brand-building campaign 'Elevate Your Drive' with brand ambassador Ranveer Singh across major digital/print platforms and the ongoing T20 League in India received strong engagement and positive customer response.
Initiatives enhanced brand recall, supported new product launches, and strengthened BKT's positioning across domestic and international markets.

subsections.label: VF tyre category positioning
points: BKT has positioned itself as a premium player in the VF (very high flexion) tyre category in US and Europe markets.

key_takeaways: We have been resilient in a challenging external environment. While macroeconomic uncertainties continue to persist, at BKT, we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable and profitable growth over the medium to long term.

We are now witnessing raw material price upticks due to supply chain disruptions and are closely monitoring the situation, while maintaining a steady balance between superior product mix and price hikes to partially offset this impact.

H2 performance was significantly better than H1, which resulted in a strong operational year for the company, where we delivered our highest ever quarterly volumes in Q4, and also the highest ever volumes annually in FY 2026.
India continues to outperform all markets and witnessed a sustained momentum. We are cautiously optimistic for this geography given the weather forecast of IMD for the upcoming monsoon season.
In December '25, we commissioned our new line for carbon black, taking the total capacity available to us at 265,000 MTPA... we have witnessed full utilization levels for the new lines.

We have entered the truck bus radial segment with the new product launches in February '26... Building on this momentum, the company plans to introduce the passenger car radial or PCR tyres by the end of the current calendar year following a phased and calibrated approach.
The Board of Directors has approved an additional capex of INR2,000 crores, which will support capacity expansion and infrastructure development across both OHT and on-Highway tyre categories.

The stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR663 crores with a margin of 22.9%. The margin was particularly impacted towards the end of the quarter on account of headwinds faced due to geopolitical scenario and its impact on supply chain.

So then in that case, like we have about INR4,000 crores of debt in the books. So can we assume that its peak debt that we have in the books today?

key_takeaways: CFO transition: CFO Gauro Kumar announced his decision to leave Apollo Tyres after ~22 years, post completion of the NSCD project ("Having completed the NSCD project… it was an emotional decision to leave Apollo Tires").

Netherlands plant closure executed: The Netherlands plant stopped production in June 2026 as planned; management expects restructuring benefits from H2 FY27 ("financial and operational benefits… from H2 of the current fiscal year").

European mix/footprint reconfiguration underway: Capacity and SKU transfers across Netherlands → Hungary, and lower-end Hungary → India are ongoing; timing and execution risks (transition-related revenue loss, cost overlap) remain key near-term swing factors.
Consolidated Q1 FY27: Revenue ₹74 bn, +12.8% YoY (sequential growth "muted"); EBITDA margin 11.7%, down ~150 bps YoY, primarily due to raw material (RM) cost pressure.
India operations: strongest growth in 14 quarters; volume-led with RM inflation defense. Revenue ₹54.6 bn, +15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ; described as "highest ever revenue" for India.
Europe operations: muted reported growth due to transition; margin impacted by overlap costs. Revenue €147m, +0.5% YoY; EBITDA €13m, margin 8.9% vs 10.8% last year.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres (Europe): expected positive, as Chinese tyres had taken share at the lower end; this could "feed into the Apollo brand volumes."

Manufacturing footprint shifts: Netherlands → Hungary/India transfer; Hungary capacity expansion from ~17,000 to ~21,000 PCR tyres/day; India expansion expected towards end of FY27 with ramp through FY28; India capacity utilization very tight, running into the 90s through FY27.

quarters.summary: Apollo Tyres delivered strong Q4 FY26 consolidated growth (revenue +14% YoY, EBITDA margin 14.6%) and expects to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe despite a tough macro environment marked by West Asia geopolitical volatility hitting raw material, energy and logistics costs. Near-term margins face pressure from steep raw material inflation (mid-to-high teens sequentially in Q1, possibly higher in Q2), being mitigated via calibrated price hikes (6-8% announced in India for Q1, 2% in Europe) and disciplined cost control; balance sheet strength (net debt/EBITDA at 0.4x) provides cushion. Europe restructuring (Enschede plant closure by June 30, 2026) is expected to start benefiting margins from H2 FY27, with a long-term ambition to return to/surpass the earlier normalised 16%+ EBITDA margin.

A&P spend to normalise going forward, expected to settle around 2.5%+ of sales, slightly higher than previous annual trend but not to the extent seen this quarter.

subsections.label: Europe Other Operating Income Decline
points: Of the 3% overall Europe revenue decline, 1% was from pure sales/price-mix decline while 2% was from a drop in other operating income.

Europe had received state aid from Hungary/EU when setting up the plant, amortised over 10 years; as TBR assets move to India, that other operating income accrual moves out of Hungary, causing the YoY drop.
This decline will continue to reduce over the next few quarters as TBR assets are no longer in Hungary; it is not a cash impact since the state aid was already received in full.

subsections.label: Enschede Closure Cash Impact
points: Cash outflow expected in FY27: EUR 50 million social plan payout already provided for in earlier quarters, plus additional legal costs, totaling EUR 55+ million cash provision already taken.
No cash provision expected over and above what has already been taken.

subsections.label: Demand Environment
points: India witnessed strong double-digit growth in both replacement and OE markets in Q4, in line with and in some segments ahead of market performance across all product categories.
Demand remains strong across categories and channels in India, with April already showing equally strong volume growth, and momentum expected to continue through Q1 FY27.
Europe witnessed slow, low single-digit growth in volumes; growth in certain international markets impacted by geopolitical developments in West Asia.
Europe outlook: expect better growth momentum in Q1; April already positive for all segments.
In India, TBR and PCR replacement grew 20%+ each in Q4; OEM TBR grew 20%+ while OEM PCR grew single digit.
Historically, in inflationary environments new vehicle purchases tend to get impacted first before consumer costs are eventually passed through the chain.

subsections.label: Pricing Actions
points: India has announced price increases of 6% to 8% for the current quarter, with 3% to 5% already implemented and the remainder coming through in May; more price increases likely needed to negate raw material cost push.
About half the needed price increase has been taken so far; at least a couple more rounds needed.

Europe: announced a 2% price increase; Apollo follows global majors' pricing actions given its relative size; for the same raw material cost increase, Europe needs a smaller price hike than India (India needs about two-thirds of the RM increase in price hike vs Europe needing less than half).
Export market pricing: US demand weak but increases of mid to high single digits announced; INR depreciation also provides support on exports.
OEM pricing follows a formula with a three-month lag for the majority of customers; some negotiated pricing ongoing; small price increases received so far but not enough to counter RM cost push.
Competitors (including CEAT) have also announced price increases; Apollo and CEAT are slightly ahead of some peers, with timing and quantum differences across the industry.
Management does not expect aggressive discounting given cost push, strong demand, high capacity utilisation, and a strong balance sheet.

subsections.label: Demand Outlook Uncertainty
points: Second-half FY27 demand outlook is uncertain and will largely depend on overall GDP growth, which predictions suggest may be revised down slightly if fuel, tyre, and other material inflation continues.
Immediate outlook (post price hikes, April data) remains as strong as Q4, but management cannot make definitive statements on H2 FY27.

subsections.label: Market Share
points: Official market share data is not published or comes with significant lag; for the full year, management believes Apollo gained market share in TBR replacement and TBR overall.
Believes gained share in passenger car replacement but not in passenger car OEM (internal estimates).
MRF and Apollo are believed to be the two leading players in the TBR category overall by numbers.

subsections.label: Enschede Closure Product Impact
points: Potential revenue loss expected only in the agricultural/OHT product category, which was a small capacity not manufactured in any other plant.
Some of the OE agri business may be lost, which was anyway loss-making — a conscious choice.
For all other product categories with similar production capability in Hungary or India, the company retains ability to supply the markets, limiting revenue loss risk.

subsections.label: Reifencom
points: Reifencom (B2B distribution) posted EUR 40 billion revenue and just under 2% EBITDA margin for the quarter.

subsections.label: R&D and OEM Approvals
points: Continued steady progress across all segments in R&D.
In passenger vehicle tyres, secured fresh approvals from leading OEMs including BMW, MINI, Genesis, KIA and Mahindra.
Introduced upgraded premium products across India and Europe Operations in the replacement category.

subsections.label: Digital & AI Initiatives
points: Started rollout of new B2B e-commerce platform in Europe during the quarter.
Continuing work in India to improve customer experience, inventory visibility, and service efficiency.
Scaling use of artificial intelligence across business functions with several initiatives underway in manufacturing, logistics, and customer service to drive efficiency and cost optimisation.
Recognised by Amazon Web Services as a case study for use of AI and data technologies.

key_figures.label: Prior approved CapEx for AP plant

subsections.label: Capacity Utilisation & Expansion
points: Capacity utilisation was at a high of 90% across both India and Europe Operations.
Given healthy demand outlook, company expects full capacity utilisation and will continue to progress on planned expansion initiatives.
In India, expansion is in both truck and car tyre capacity; in Europe (Hungary plant), only passenger car tyre expansion is underway (already well underway).
Capacity utilisations are already high, so in certain product categories (particularly truck), capacity allocation decisions will be needed given strong India demand.
Through April, the company struggled to keep up with demand given high utilisation.

Some flexibility exists on the large previously announced CapEx (INR 5,800 crores for AP plant), but FY27 CapEx is largely committed; flexibility for pushing out spend would only apply to FY28 if demand slows.

subsections.label: Enschede Plant Closure
points: Closure of the Enschede plant production remains on track; last day of production would be June 30, 2026 — described as a tough, difficult, emotional decision.
Fixed assets at the plant were assessed as the company enters the last month of operation, leading to a non-cash write-off of EUR 43 million taken this quarter.
It will take about another quarter to stabilise after closure; positive margin impact from becoming more cost competitive in European operations expected to start flowing in from H2 FY27.
TBR assets move from Hungary to India as part of this restructuring.

subsections.label: Export Strategy
points: Export strategy will continue to be managed strategically given high capacity utilisations; capacity allocation decisions needed for certain product categories like truck given strong India demand.
India and Europe remain priority markets as the two home markets; remaining capacities allocated to other geographies.
Europe currently showing promising signs, but outcome depends on how West Asia situation evolves; US market currently looking weak entering the new fiscal year.
Truck tyre sales in Europe were impacted by supply issues from India, while passenger car tyre category outperformed the market.

Under transfer pricing regulation, the India standalone entity retains only a fixed margin on exports to Europe and does not directly benefit from rupee depreciation; the overall group benefits from rupee devaluation.

There is scope to increase India production to serve European and other export markets if India's cost structure becomes more cost-competitive, given the different quantum of capacity increases planned in Hungary vs. India.

subsections.label: Channel Inventory
points: In India, there is no marked difference in dealer inventory levels after the strong start to the year.

subsections.label: Imports
points: Tyre imports remain at a certain level, slightly more in passenger car tyre category, very little in truck tyre category; no expectation of a dramatic increase in the near term.

subsections.label: Commodity Price Trends
points: Raw material costs expected to rise in high teens sequentially in Q1 FY27; situation is very volatile and has kept changing about a month and a half into the quarter.
Current estimate is mid to high teens increase; Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1 if the current situation (natural rubber continuing to rise, crude fluctuating) persists.
Natural rubber consumption is much lower in Europe than India, so raw material cost inflation would be lower in Europe versus India Operations.
No significant difference between international and domestic rubber costs; domestic rubber growers price close to landed cost of overseas rubber given a transparent market.

subsections.label: Cost Mitigation
points: Raw material is the biggest cost basket; ability to fully negate cost push through other cost levers is limited.
Non-essential costs such as travel and conferences have been postponed/reduced wherever possible, but this is disproportionate relative to the raw material cost basket.

subsections.label: Brand & Marketing
points: BCCI partnership generated strong momentum, further amplified by the 'Har Safar Mein Dum Hai' campaign launched around the ICC T20 World Cup, reinforcing brand positioning around performance, resilience and trust.
Campaign rolled out across multiple platforms and markets, strengthening brand connect with consumers and enhancing overall brand equity.

subsections.label: Competitive Dynamics
points: Apollo Tyres and CEAT are slightly ahead of peers in announcing price increases; timing and quantum differences exist across the industry.
Aggressive discounting is not expected given cost push, strong demand, high capacity utilisation and strong balance sheets across players.

subsections.label: People & Recognition
points: Apollo Tyres recognised as Top Employer in 2026, with India Operations receiving the recognition for the first time, while European entities continued their strong track record.

subsections.label: Sustainability
points: Climate targets received validation from the Science-Based Targets Initiative during the quarter, reaffirming long-term commitment towards net zero across the value chain.

subsections.label: Geopolitical & Macro Risk
points: Geopolitical developments in West Asia continue to create significant uncertainty and add volatility to raw materials, energy, and logistics costs.
Company is closely monitoring the evolving situation, remaining focused on responding with agility while maintaining disciplined cost controls.
Continued inflation on fuel, tyre and other materials could impact overall GDP growth and hence demand, though this is currently uncertain.

subsections.label: Europe Margin Pressure
points: European market conditions have been sluggish, flattish to negative for two years running, coupled with continuing high energy costs and salary inflation much higher than usual for Western European geographies (e.g., Netherlands salary inflation ~12-13% vs usual 4-5%).
These factors brought down margins from previous normalised levels (16%+) and were a factor forcing the decision regarding the Enschede plant.

subsections.label: India Margin Pressure
points: India margins will remain under pressure due to increased raw material costs, being offset through price increases.
Raw material cost inflation running ahead of price hikes taken so far; more price increases needed to fully offset cost push.

subsections.label: Top-line Outlook
points: Despite tough macro environment, company expects to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe.
Demand remains strong across categories and channels in India; April already showing equally strong volume growth, expected to continue through Q1 FY27.
Europe: expect better growth momentum in Q1 FY27; April already positive for all segments.

subsections.label: Margin Outlook
points: India margins will remain under pressure near term due to increased costs, being offset through price increases; raw material costs expected to rise in high teens sequentially, with 6-8% price increases already announced for the current quarter and more likely needed.
Europe restructuring benefits on margin expected to start flowing in from H2 FY27 as the company becomes more cost competitive.
Long-term ambition to return to and potentially surpass the previous normalised Europe EBITDA margin of 16%+.
Company will continue to monitor the volatile external environment and guide operations keeping an eye on cash flows and ROCE.

FY27 CapEx largely committed given high capacity utilisation and demand; flexibility to push out spend, if needed, would apply only to FY28.

pressing_questions: How much price hike do you need further to pass on the entire cost inflation and go back to the earlier margin trends which we were operating?

quarters.summary: Sona Comstar reported its best-ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue and BEV revenue share, with revenue up 54% YoY, EBITDA up 49% and PAT up 45%, though EBITDA margin (23.1%) and PAT margin (13.6%) were both down ~0.7pp YoY on input-cost inflation, labor cost increases, timing gaps in customer pass-throughs, and adverse product mix from fast-growing lower-margin traction motors; management expects recovery measures to become progressively visible from Q2 onward. The company announced a landmark two-JV partnership with DENSO covering high-voltage EV/hybrid powertrains (JV1, Denso-majority) and 2/3-wheeler traction motors (JV2, Sona-majority), alongside a formal entry into Robotics and Physical AI with an ₹8 billion order book, as part of its "Sona Comstar 2.0" strategy to build another 10x company over the next decade.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in customer recoveries/pass-throughs, especially during April and May, but June was significantly better.
Cost pass-throughs to automotive customers always lag inflation, so recoveries come later; recovery measures are expected to become progressively more visible from Q2 onwards.
There was also a product mix impact as traction motor sales grew quite rapidly, and that product category has the lowest margins relative to company average, dragging margin down.

Between EBITDA and PAT, there was a positive impact on margin from lower depreciation percentage and exceptional expenses booked in Q1 of last year, whereas PAT margin was pulled down by lower EBITDA margin and lower net finance income.

subsections.label: Key ratios
points: All ratios except VA to employee cost showed improvement this quarter.

VA to employee cost declined mainly due to change in product mix in favor of assembly products (motor and railway businesses are more assembly-oriented vs. driveline, which has higher value addition); this ratio can vary quarter to quarter depending on which business grows faster.
Return ratios continue to show gradual improvement; the impact of the QIP fundraise has been absorbed in the ratios, and incremental returns from businesses are now supporting these ratios.
Net debt continues to be negative, so net debt to EBITDA ratio also continues in negative territory.

Both turnover ratios improved this quarter, supported by robust revenue growth; working capital turnover ratio also improved due to a significant reduction in debtor days, making this the best quarter from an operational cash flow perspective.
