Added 2 new EV programs and 1 hybrid program, taking EV order book to 69 programs across 36 customers.

subsections.label: New product/innovation capability
points: More than 35% of revenue comes from products that did not exist in the portfolio 7 years ago; 19 of these products were conceived, designed, industrialized and scaled entirely through own R&D funded from own cash flows.

Annualized Q1 basis, these new products represent a ₹1,800 crore revenue business generating over ₹230 crore of annual profit — described as equivalent to creating a multi-unicorn from scratch in 7 years.

subsections.label: Capital allocation / M&A track record
points: Over last 7 years, invested ~₹2,750 crore across acquisitions of Comstar, Novelic and the Railway Business; these 3 businesses now contribute ~40% of revenue and, assuming comparable margins, ~₹270 crore of net annual profit — despite the railway business being in its first year of post-acquisition integration.

subsections.label: DENSO Joint Venture structure
points: Two JVs: JV1 focuses on high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for 4 and 4+ wheel vehicles (passenger and commercial); Denso holds majority stake, contributes technology/IP and leads management.

JV2 focuses on 2 and 3 wheelers where Sona Comstar already has an established technology position; Sona Comstar retains majority ownership and management control while licensing its own technology into the JV.
Suspension motor business and all other non-traction motor businesses remain completely outside the scope of the DENSO transaction.

Royalty structure is equal and reciprocal: JV2 pays royalties to Denso for high-voltage technologies, while JV1 pays royalties to Sona Comstar for 2/3-wheeler technologies — both companies contribute technology, IP and engineering expertise.
JV1 will lead/kickstart faster; JV2 will follow, per management (Sat Mohan Gupta) — exact timing not disclosed due to confidentiality.

Rationale for including the already-successful 2/3-wheeler business in a JV: access to a customer base not currently open to Sona, export opportunity to markets where Denso is dominant, and a desire to partner fully across the board rather than selectively.

e-axle (integrated motor+inverter+gearbox assembly) is a very tiny market for JV1; JV2 will make motors and inverters that can be sold to e-axle makers, directly to OEMs, or to Sona Comstar's own driveline division to build e-axles — three possible go-to-market models exist.

Denso's electrification business revenue is above $8 billion/year, giving JV2 access to a market-leading position; Denso brings full-spectrum controller technology while Sona Comstar brings motor manufacturing excellence and frugal, cost-targeted design capability.

subsections.label: Robotics & Physical AI business build-out
points: Three distinct revenue streams identified: (1) advanced components and subsystems (motors, gearboxes, sensors) closest to existing capability; (2) perception stack and engineering services, including software and integrated hardware-software solutions; (3) manufacturing of selected full robotic platforms, initially autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and cognitive collaborative robots (cobots).
Showcased prototype of first AMR at CES Las Vegas earlier this year; development continues to progress rapidly.

Secured first order for an advanced robotic subsystem; second order for perception engineering services for AMRs; third order combines hardware and software — a complete short-range radar perception solution for an Indian commercial vehicle OEM.
These three orders add ₹6 billion to the Robotics and Physical AI order book, taking the total for this new vertical to ₹8 billion.
Market for this vertical appears to be developing faster than originally anticipated, unlike the slower ramp historically seen with electrification products or suspension motors.
Company deliberately delayed public discussion of this vertical until it had tangible proof points (orders secured), to avoid loss of credibility from premature announcements.

subsections.label: Diversification (4th strategic priority)
points: Eastern markets contributed 59% of revenue this quarter vs. 56% last year, showing continued shift in geographic mix.
Fastest growing business this quarter was EV suspension motors, followed by EV traction motors.
Emerging product portfolios (often grouped under 'others') include steering bevel boxes, intermediate gears, epicyclic gear trains, input rotor shafts, and several railway products.

subsections.label: Growth ramp-up pattern for new businesses
points: Typical pattern for a new product/technology: first 3 years generate no money, year 4 sees first $1 of revenue, year 5 reaches ~$10 million, year 7-8 becomes a $100 million business — as seen with EV differential assemblies, EV traction motors, and expected with suspension motors.
Robotics business is expected to hit these milestones faster than the historical timeline, though how much faster is too early to tell.

key_figures.label: Global radar market projected growth (25 yrs)
Global reducer market projected growth (25 yrs)
Global electric motor market projected growth (25 yrs)

subsections.label: Technology roadmap and products under commercialization
points: Advancing market-relevant products across automotive and railway applications: magnet-free motor solutions, exterior radar solutions, air springs, HVAC, and door systems.
Products under commercialization this quarter include short-range radar sensors and advanced robotics components.
Short-range exterior radar sensor developed for a leading commercial vehicle OEM is designed to meet upcoming Government of India ADAS (advanced driver assistance systems) regulations.
Business win in advanced robotic components builds on deep expertise and foundational capabilities in automotive product design, tooling and manufacturing.

AMR platform brings together capabilities across motor, driveline and sensor divisions, while establishing expertise in newer domains such as robot perception, motion planning and control, telematics, reinforcement learning and AI orchestration.
AMR platform is being developed for manufacturing and warehousing applications, designed to support use cases across automotive, electronics, pharmaceuticals, FMCG and other sectors.

As smart/flexible manufacturing scales, manufacturers are moving from isolated automation to connected/coordinated operations, creating opportunities in physical AI components, actuators, and in some cases full systems.
Training for physical AI deployment is flagged as an area likely to be the next frontier in cognitive robotics.

subsections.label: Automotive-robotics technology convergence thesis
points: Same technologies (motors, gearboxes, actuators, sensors, electronics, software) power both modern EVs/AVs and intelligent machines (humanoids, AMRs, cobots, robotaxis).
Automotive and robotics industries have already started converging — cited Hyundai's ownership of Boston Dynamics and automotive-sector entrants making humanoids.
Reducer used in an EV (9:1 ratio) is fundamentally the same concept as one used in a humanoid joint (100:1 to 160:1 ratio), just smaller and more precise.

Company already provides a range of service models: pure software/perception stack service (training an AMR, providing perception software stack), and combined hardware+software offerings (device plus software).

subsections.label: AI ethics and data privacy approach
points: Guardrails for AI applications and data are designed before even the data structure mapping stage.
European customer supply requires passing a high GDPR compliance bar for data usage.
Most of the perception stack is built around radar technology, which detects outline/heartbeat but not face or voice, providing an inherent privacy layer.
Customers themselves require privacy/ethics safeguards to be built in as a first layer.

subsections.label: Passenger vehicle EV motor capability build (JV context)
points: Even with a PO today, automotive product development cycle to SOP takes ~32 months / 3 years.

Key building blocks for competitive motor development: frugal, cost-efficient design from day one; building the supply chain (motor is an assembled product with lower in-house value addition); and market/duty-cycle knowledge (e.g., company captured 1 year of duty-cycle data via an MOU with a three-wheeler company circa 2021 before launching a product a year later).

subsections.label: Capacity positioning vs. demand
points: Management stated the company is not constrained by demand for EV products; OEMs are themselves constrained by their own supply chain challenges, not by Sona Comstar's capacity.
Sat Mohan Gupta (Motor Business CEO) confirmed no capacity constraints currently; management stated Driveline business (Vikram) also has no capacity constraints.

Company has historically built capacity ahead of market demand; however, since any vehicle has hundreds of parts, even one bottlenecked supplier in the broader supply chain can constrain overall system sales.

subsections.label: Regional demand trends
points: India delivered another strong quarter, particularly in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers.
Europe has not just remained stable but is actually growing, surprising many.
US has improved meaningfully as the quarter progressed, though EV demand in the US specifically remains weak, with a shift toward hybrids being observed.
China was mixed overall, but was Sona Comstar's fastest growing geography this quarter due to the suspension motor ramp-up and its success in China.
India is considered the fastest growing EV market in the world currently.
Europe is electrifying fast, whether fully BEV, strong hybrid, or plug-in hybrid.
JV2 (2/3-wheeler high voltage) will begin with India, with global/export expansion to other markets where Denso is more dominant planned in phase two, once Indian operations are established.

subsections.label: Rare earth magnet situation
points: Heavy rare earth magnets remain restricted from import; company has shifted almost entirely to light rare earth alternatives, which is working fine.
No material change or update versus prior quarters — situation has been the same for the last 5 quarters.
No real magnet shortage impact, as shown by continued growth in the EV traction motor business.

subsections.label: Debtor days / working capital
points: Significant reduction in debtor days this quarter improved the working capital turnover ratio and contributed to the best quarter from an operational cash flow perspective.

subsections.label: Market sizing for high-voltage JV opportunity
points: Per S&P Global Mobility, Indian hybrid and EV cars plus commercial vehicle market represents an addressable market of over 2.3 million vehicles, amounting to roughly a ₹24,000 crore opportunity by 2030; by 2035 this could be several times larger (management referenced roughly 3x).
This market sizing is before considering longer-term global ambitions beyond India.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape commentary
points: 2-wheeler/3-wheeler traction motor market is far more competitive, where Sona Comstar has been able to take market leadership on its own.

High-voltage motor/control systems market is described as less competitive due to a significant technology barrier, which management believes will allow the company to make a 'fairly big dent' in the market.

Management declined to give specifics on the number of competitors with local, highly localized manufacturing capability in high-voltage motors, citing sensitivity around compliance/PLI claims by some market participants.

subsections.label: Business development wins across markets
points: Secured new business across EVs, hybrids and ICE across India, Europe and North America, and across virtually every product category — a diversified base capable of growing across customers, geographies, products and powertrain technologies.

subsections.label: "Sona Comstar 2.0" strategic framework
points: Framed as natural evolution (not change in direction) of strategy built over past decade; work on this strategy began more than 2 years ago but was not publicized until tangible actions (DENSO JV, Robotics/Physical AI) were ready to show.

Between 2015-2025, revenue increased 10-fold, with more than 85% of that growth coming from just 3 strategic decisions: entering new product verticals, expanding into global markets (particularly the West), and early recognition/action on the electrification opportunity.
Ambition for next decade: build 'another 10x company', addressable market broadened from automotive to mobility.

Three growth engines identified: (1) new product verticals via organic innovation plus disciplined acquisitions/partnerships; (2) 'Look East' strategy — building an equally strong presence in the East via strategic moves (railway acquisition, DENSO partnership) rather than incremental expansion, while maintaining strategic importance of Europe/North America; (3) Robotics and Physical AI as a new long-term technology theme alongside electrification.

What will not change: purpose, values, commitment to customers/shareholders/employees, and principles of engineering excellence, disciplined capital allocation, operational execution, financial prudence and transparency.
What will change: scale of ambition — pursuing larger opportunities, markets, investments and strategic decisions.

Every decision continues to be judged against three questions: does it create meaningful value for customers; does it create long-term value for shareholders; does the company have capability/management bandwidth to execute well — if any answer is no, company will walk away.

subsections.label: DENSO Partnership rationale
points: Described as the most important strategic partnership in Sona Comstar's history and the company's first joint venture.
Fills a prior gap: the company did not previously participate in high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for passenger and commercial vehicles.

Management believes DENSO (world's 2nd largest mobility technology company) chose Sona Comstar for its strong engineering capabilities, proven frugal execution, and complementary technologies (DENSO's hybrid strength plus Sona's electric strength).
Aspiration is to reach the stature of companies like Bosch and DENSO (85 years old) despite Sona Comstar being only 25 years old and roughly 1/100th DENSO's revenue size.
Management noted this may make Sona Comstar the first Indian automotive company to receive royalty income from a global mobility technology company.

subsections.label: Robotics and Physical AI as strategic platform
points: Positioned as the third and 'boldest' growth engine, viewed as building on capabilities developed over the past decade rather than a departure from strategy.
AI viewed as a 'general purpose technology' (in the lineage of fire, the wheel, electricity, internet) now moving from the digital world into the physical world.
Management believes if the company captures even a fraction of the long-term robotics/physical AI opportunity, the outlook is very positive.

subsections.label: Inflation and cost pressure
points: Inflation remains the biggest near-term challenge; commodities and other input costs remain elevated and impacted margins during the quarter.
April was tough, May was even tougher, but June showed improvement as material costs passed through and cost reduction/mitigation measures started catching up.
Cost pass-throughs to automotive customers lag inflation, creating an arithmetic impact on both revenue and cost that may continue to pressure margin as a percentage.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and trade uncertainty
points: Operating environment remains uncertain; trade and geopolitical developments continue to be choppy, though management stated these have been uncertain for so long that they should not be used as an explanation for business performance — the job is to manage through the choppiness.

subsections.label: Supply chain bottlenecks (external)
points: Company is not itself a supply chain constraint, but other suppliers' capacity/supply chain issues can bottleneck the overall vehicle system and limit Sona Comstar's sellable volume, since a vehicle has hundreds of parts and the slowest link determines system pace.

subsections.label: Rare earth magnet import restrictions
points: Heavy rare earth magnets remain restricted for import; mitigated via shift to light rare earth alternatives, with no material change over the last 5 quarters.

subsections.label: US EV demand weakness
points: EV demand in the US remains weak, with a shift toward hybrids observed; despite this, BEV revenue still grew 107% globally.

subsections.label: Confidentiality constraints on JV disclosure
points: SOP timelines and specific revenue-recognition timing for JV1/JV2 cannot be disclosed due to confidentiality agreements involving DENSO and customers.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Recovery measures (cost pass-throughs) expected to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27 onwards.

subsections.label: Robotics order execution timelines
points: Of the three robotics orders comprising the ₹8 billion order book (₹6bn added this quarter), SOPs are near-term: one starts production this quarter, one next quarter, and one within 15 months — most robotics orders expected to start production within 12-15 months maximum.

subsections.label: JV1/JV2 timeline
points: SOP timelines for DENSO JV1 and JV2 cannot be disclosed due to confidentiality agreements; JV1 will lead and kick off faster than JV2.
JV2 will begin with the Indian market; global/export expansion is planned in a 'phase two' once Indian operations are established, timing unspecified.

subsections.label: New business ramp-up timeline (general pattern, applied to robotics)
points: Typical ramp pattern for new products: no revenue for first 3 years, first $1 revenue in year 4, ~$10 million in year 5, ~$100 million business by year 7-8; robotics business is expected to hit these milestones faster than this historical pattern, though the exact pace is still uncertain.

Indian hybrid and EV cars and commercial vehicle market alone represents an addressable market of over 2.3 million vehicles, which would roughly amount to about a 24,000 crore opportunity in 2030; if you go to 2035, it will be many times this (management suggested roughly 3x).

guidance_ledger.metric: Robotics/Physical AI long-term component markets (radar, reducers, motors)
guidance_ledger.statement: Global market for radars, reducers, and electric motors over the next 25 years could grow approximately 260x, 590x, and 260x respectively, reaching an estimated $60 billion for radars, $1.4 trillion for reducers, and $2.5 trillion for motors.

themes.label: Revenue growth
themes.note: Best-ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue and BEV mix; revenue up 54% YoY, EBITDA up 49%, PAT up 45%.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Commodities and input costs remained elevated, pressuring EBITDA and PAT margins by ~0.7pp YoY, though June showed improvement as pass-throughs caught up.

themes.label: BEV segment challenges
themes.note: BEV revenue grew 107% to an all-time high share despite continued weak EV demand in the US.

themes.label: Geographical diversification
themes.note: Eastern markets rose to 59% of revenue from 56% YoY; India, Europe strong, US improving, China mixed but fastest-growing geography this quarter.

themes.label: Strategic collaborations
themes.note: Landmark two-JV partnership announced with DENSO covering high-voltage EV/hybrid powertrains and 2/3-wheeler traction motors, described as the most important partnership in company history.

themes.label: New product ramp-up
themes.note: Formal entry into Robotics and Physical AI with ₹8 billion order book already secured; over 35% of revenue now comes from products created via own R&D in last 7 years.

themes.label: Supply chain adaptation
themes.note: Company not capacity-constrained itself, but broader OEM/supplier supply chain bottlenecks limit sellable volume; rare earth magnet import restrictions managed via light rare earth alternatives.

key_takeaways: This was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue, and BEV revenue share, with very healthy momentum continuing across the business.
Revenue grew by 54% year on year, while EBITDA and net profit increased by 49% and 45% respectively. EBITDA margin was 23.1%.

Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in the customer recoveries or the pass-throughs, especially during April and May, but June was significantly better.

Announced a landmark partnership with DENSO consisting of two joint ventures: JV1 for high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for 4 and 4+ wheel vehicles (Denso majority), and JV2 for 2 and 3 wheelers (Sona Comstar majority).

Formally announced entry into Robotics and Physical AI as a third growth engine, with a ₹8 billion order book already secured across three orders (components, perception software services, and a combined hardware+software radar perception solution).
BEV revenue grew 107% to 436 crores, constituting 44% of automotive product sales; EV order book now stands at 69 programs across 36 customers.
Net order book stands at 240 billion at end of Q1 FY27, with EVs accounting for 64% and Robotics and Physical AI now contributing 3%.
Eastern markets contributed 59% of revenue this quarter, up from 56% last year, reflecting continued geographic diversification.

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 was Sona Comstar's best-ever quarter with highest-ever revenue, EBITDA, PAT, BEV revenue and BEV revenue share. Management flagged commodity inflation, Haryana minimum wage hikes and gas availability as near-term headwinds but expects margins to remain in a 23-25% band post-railway acquisition, with continued momentum in EV order wins, geographic diversification (India >50% mix, Eastern markets 60% of Q4 revenue), and new growth drivers in railways, suspension motors and traction motors.

subsections.label: Q4 EBITDA margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin lower by 2.7% YoY in Q4; of this, base effect of 1.9% is due to fully PLI income accrued in the fourth quarter last year, and the balance 0.8% impact is due to product mix and commodity price inflation.

Of the 80bps mix/commodity impact, roughly half is due to mix (traction motor being the highest growth driver with lower margins) and half is due to commodity prices, largely a pass-through with a lag effect; commodity prices continue to trend up so the impact is ongoing, and there is a numerator-denominator effect that impacts percentage margin more than absolute margin.

subsections.label: Q4 PAT margin drivers
points: PAT margin lower by 4.1% YoY; nearly half of this due to lower EBITDA, 3.4% effect due to lower net finance income from deployment of funds in the railway business during the year, and a net positive impact of about 1.3% from lower depreciation and higher tax.

subsections.label: Full year performance context
points: Full year described as tough given the loss of Sunjay in Q1, US tariffs, the magnet ban, and an increasingly challenging and volatile geopolitical environment, yet the company delivered 26% revenue growth, 13.5% EBITDA growth and 11% PAT growth with sequential improvement across all metrics.
Full year EBITDA margin of 24.7% was achieved despite consolidating the lower-margin Railway Business and high growth from the lower-margin Traction Motor business.
Full year EBITDA margin decline of 2.7% mainly on account of change in product mix and, to some extent, higher fixed costs.

Full year PAT had a one-time impact of 30 crores after tax from the new labor code; adjusted PAT was higher by 11% at 670 crores, with adjusted PAT margin lower by 2.2%, mainly due to lower EBITDA margin and lower net finance income.

subsections.label: Cash flow and capital allocation
points: Cash from operations of 659 crores, net of capex of 369 crores generated free cash flow of 290 crores.
Other major cash movements: ~1,800 crores used for purchase of railway business, 110 crores for additional land, and payment for the last tranche of acquisition of Novelic shareholding.
200 crores distributed as dividend; added ~226 crores of short-term borrowings and 86 crores of interest income as positive cash inflows.
Ended the year with cash and investments of 1,269 crores (management referenced ~1,270 crores).

subsections.label: Key ratios
points: Newly purchased railway business has a different cost structure and working capital cycle, which has caused a dip in value addition over employee cost and working capital turnover ratios.
Return on capital employed (ROCE) has come down mainly due to fresh equity raised in September 2024; expected to improve over the medium term as only part of the capital has been deployed so far.

Return on equity (ROE) has already started to improve compared to the previous two quarters, as deployment of capital in the railway business continues to bring an incremental positive impact over finance income substituted in the P&L.
Fixed asset turnover ratio dropped to 2.9 this year primarily because of new capitalization and land purchase; expected to improve as new capex generates revenue in the following financial year.

points: Won 4 new driveline orders in Q4; 3 from European OEMs in a single quarter, the highest ever from Europe in a single quarter and the first EV order win from Europe in almost 4 years.
One of the four Q4 orders was for a hybrid platform, reinforcing the view that hybrids are an opportunity, not a risk.

New wins directionally important though amounts may not be large: (1) new European customer for differential gears for their EV program in North America; (2) order for EV differential assemblies from a luxury PV OEM in Europe; (3) new order from an existing European OEM for hybrid differential assemblies; (4) EV differential assemblies program in India supplying to both Indian and European OEMs via a tier 1, a shared program with existing customers.
Non-EV order wins in Q4: 7 differential gear programs from existing customers totaling ₹3 billion order book addition; remaining wins came from segments like starter motors and railways.

subsections.label: Order book composition
points: In Q2, a significant correction was made to the order book because of one particular model; despite that, FY26 ended with fairly similar levels to last year despite growth achieved during the year.
Order momentum is broad-based across powertrains, geographies, and customer types.
Net order book stands at 237 billion at end of Q4 FY26, with EVs accounting for 70% of the order book.

subsections.label: Order book visibility and conversion (Q&A)
points: 100% of the order book has volume visibility and pricing stability, but volumes are indicative only (no firm commitments in the industry); the company discounts customer volume projections when adding to the order book based on historical experience.

Currently there is no demand problem; rather, customers are unable to produce enough to supply demand due to weaknesses in the supply chain among certain suppliers finding it hard to ramp up, which works both ways — some orders convert higher than booked, some lower, but over time it pans out around the same number.

subsections.label: European bankruptcy/consolidation opportunity (Q&A)
points: Some opportunity from peers' bankruptcy in Europe has already started flowing in via new wins; the third asset acquired by another party's future performance cannot be commented on, but conversations will continue directly with customers.
Overall, no material change in the opportunity set Europe presents; expected to remain a fairly good place to win business over the next 12 months.

subsections.label: BEV performance
points: Q4 was the best ever quarter for both BEV revenue and BEV revenue share, reaching 39%, despite EV sales in the US declining 28% YoY in Q4, showing EV business is not overly dependent on any one market, category, or customer.

Full year BEV revenue declined marginally due to an extremely weak Q1; since then revenue has improved consistently, ending Q4 with the highest ever BEV revenue and revenue share following a similar trend.

subsections.label: Product diversification
points: Last year top 4 products contributed 86% of revenue; this year the same 86% of revenue is spread across top eight products, meaning the revenue base is becoming broader and less dependent on a few products.

Sequentially, fastest growth came from traction and suspension motors, followed by differential assemblies and differential gears; legacy products (differential gears and differential assemblies) continue to grow alongside newer products.

subsections.label: Suspension motor business
points: Suspension motor launched last year on one customer model; the vehicle has done very well and the customer has now launched a premium model with volumes growing strongly.

Product perceived with very good quality ratings and performance both in China and rest of the world; end customer (Clear Motion) is working with other OEMs in Europe with wide acceptability in the automotive sector.

Expected 3 to 4 times growth compared to last year; will still be single digit as % of revenue this year, potentially double digits next year, though this depends on the customer's ability to win the next OEM.

subsections.label: Traction motor business
points: Traction motor is currently about 10% of revenue and will be the second fastest growing business after suspension motors, with high double-digit growth rates expected for some time.

Growth driven both by higher-than-assumed volumes on existing programs and by new inquiries; policy push for electrification (reducing oil/gas dependence from 80% to less exposure) expected to increase over next 18 months, alongside consumer demand shift due to better TCO for electric vehicles especially for economic-use vehicles (3-wheelers, delivery, two-wheelers, electric LCVs, buses).

subsections.label: Market segment mix
points: The market segment analysis is broadly the same as at the end of nine-months.

subsections.label: Railway product roadmap
points: Received approvals to supply two new products this quarter: electric panels and HVAC systems, expanding railway product offerings beyond safety-critical brake systems and couplers to include products enhancing passenger comfort.
Supplied first batch of electric panels for locomotive applications; will start supplying HVAC systems this quarter.

Addition of railway products to the roadmap marked a significant step in diversifying from pure automotive to the wider, fast-growing mobility space, adding capability in brakes, suspensions, couplers, and railway electronic systems.

subsections.label: Other mobility domains / robotics
points: MoU with Neura Robotics of Germany opened opportunities in cognitive robotics, AMRs, and humanoids.
Progressing on industrializing first-ever in-cabin radar solution for passenger car application (ADAS).
In advanced stage of developing exterior radar solutions to support Indian commercial vehicles in meeting upcoming ADAS regulations.

subsections.label: New product commercialization
points: Latest additions in Q4 are electric control panel and HVAC systems for railways, demonstrating strong capability in designing, developing, and commercializing complex electronics, electromechanical, and electropneumatic systems.
Including the previously announced hydraulic motor controller, three new products were commercialized this year.

subsections.label: Railway market sizing and coverage timeline (Q&A)
points: HVAC market size is about 2,000 to 2,500 crore, and electric panel market is about 1,500 crore — both large segments relative to the size of the railway business, covering locomotives, passenger coaches, train sets and metro applications.

Electric panels development is more advanced and will take 12-15 months to cover all rolling stock types; HVAC will take at least 3 years due to longer approval cycles and field trials, especially in target segments.

New products expected to become a meaningful growth driver from the 3rd year onward; in the next 2 years, growth will come more from operational improvement and filling white spaces in existing product lines.

subsections.label: Non-automotive / robotics and eVTOL timeline (Q&A)
points: New product development, whether organic robotics/eVTOL or otherwise, typically takes 4-5 years to become meaningful: years 0-3 involve spending more than earning, year 4 brings initial revenue trickling in, and later years can scale to hundreds and then thousands of crores if successful.

Suspension motor order was won in 2021; 2026 is the first year it will be in hundreds of crores — illustrating the multi-year cycle. EV differential assembly business started in 2016, became meaningful around 2019.

Company will not rush new product timelines given B2B, safety-critical/mission-critical nature of products requiring long testing and safety cycles; investors with horizon <3 years should not expect meaningful revenue from non-automotive/robotics/eVTOL initiatives yet.

subsections.label: Rare earth magnets (Q&A)
points: No update on rare earth magnet situation as of now; government has released a policy but nothing material/reportable yet; company does not currently use any heavy rare earth magnets in any of its products.

key_figures.label: Reduction in gas requirement at company level

subsections.label: Gas availability mitigation
points: Gas availability has been a challenge; company partially mitigated this by shifting part of gas requirement to electric heating, optimizing gas flows and modifying certain processes, reducing gas requirement by nearly 20% at company level with no production loss so far.

subsections.label: Capex fungibility strategy (Q&A)
points: Fungible capex — usable across multiple customers/models — is preferred over highly specific investments tied to one model of one carmaker, which make capital allocation tricky.

Traction motor capacity of ~1 million electric motors overall is largely fungible with minor tweaks across customers, so as long as overall electrification progresses, that capacity decision should bear fruit.

subsections.label: Novelic India manufacturing (Q&A)
points: Novelic entity set up in India; launch process started for one customer with SOP targeted for end of this year.
Manufacturing lines already set up as it is a sensor assembly unit; will use an in-house SMT line.

subsections.label: Look East / diversification strategy
points: Eastern markets contributed 60% of revenues in Q4 compared to 40% in the same quarter last year, proving the company can diversify without compromising growth or margins.

North America PV sales were clearly weak in the quarter while Europe had its best quarter in 4 years; because the company is a meaningful player in both, the net effect was mitigated — the difference between North America and European car sales was one of the narrowest seen apart from COVID and the semiconductor crisis.

India — passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and electric two-wheelers all hit their best ever quarter in Q4, and India's share in the mix crossed 50% for the full year, showing geographic diversification is working and weakness in one market does not materially affect overall growth trajectory.

subsections.label: Global EV demand trends
points: March BEV sales grew ~45% YoY in the EU; India electric cars and two-wheelers grew 65% and 45% YoY respectively in March, both trending above 50% in April as well, suggesting a sustained electrification growth trend.
North America saw its best monthly BEV run rate in March since US EV subsidy cuts, which had been a setback for that subset of the industry.
War is deeply tragic but has an evident outcome of renewed urgency towards energy security and electrification globally.

subsections.label: US tariff situation (Q&A)
points: Section 232, covering a large part of exports, remains unchanged and was not affected by the Supreme Court ruling (under a different National Emergency Act not addressed by that ruling); other tariffs have become lower/easier as country tariffs have largely gone away.

Tariffs are paid by importers, not exporters; as long as pricing/tariffs are lower than China's, it remains favorable; a roughly 5-year concession exists for OEMs with certain domestic value addition in the US to claim back tariff impacts.
Revenue from the US has not materially come down, nor have margins, despite earlier analyst predictions (called 'half-baked and uninformed') that EBITDA would drop from 25% to 12.5%.

Secondary impact of tariffs is inflationary and dampens demand; US full-year car SAR is now estimated between 16 to 16.5 million units, with about one million cars lost due to this inflationary impact, affecting all suppliers to that market.

subsections.label: China / Chinese OEM opportunity (Q&A)
points: Company supplies to one large Chinese EV customer, both for domestic sales and exports; the constraint is that unless the Chinese OEM moves production entirely to Europe or North America, it will continue relying on the Chinese supply chain, which is harder to penetrate.

Drew parallel to Japan's export model in the 70s, where geopolitical/protectionist pressures eventually forced production to shift to markets being sold into, which then created opportunities for local suppliers; expects a similar evolution over time for China.

key_figures.label: M&A opportunities evaluated over last 3 years

subsections.label: Diversification strategy (Look East, product diversification)
points: Look East strategy from the annual report was a statement of deliberate effort to broaden focus and footprint in new geographies; results are already visible with Eastern markets contributing 60% of Q4 revenue vs 40% a year ago.
Product diversification: top 8 products now needed to reach the same 86% revenue contribution that top 4 products delivered last year, showing a broader, less concentrated revenue base.

subsections.label: Railway business R&D progress
points: Strong and consistent progress in R&D for newly acquired railway business; in about 10 months, product offerings expanded beyond safety-critical brake systems and couplers to include passenger comfort products (electric panels, HVAC).

subsections.label: M&A approach and capital allocation (Q&A)
points: No M&A opportunity currently at a reportable stage; company continuously evaluates opportunities but is disciplined — over the last 3 years evaluated 100+ opportunities and acted on only one (railway acquisition).

Company applies four filters before considering an M&A opportunity: (1) product must last for the next 15 years, (2) must be able to take a top-5 position in that category, (3) must generate good financial returns, and (4) must be good for humanity.
Having cash provides optionality to invest and grow when others may be constrained, but cash will not be deployed hastily just because it is available.

subsections.label: Commodity inflation
points: Steel, aluminum, copper and other major commodities have continued to move up over the last 5 months, amplified by sharp increases in freight, packaging, and energy prices; almost everything linked to petrochemicals has become more expensive.

While a large part of commodity inflation is passed through, some parts are not, and there is always a lag; this lag along with the arithmetic impact on both revenue and cost will put pressure on margins, expected to continue in the foreseeable future.

Commodity price inflation impact is ongoing and unpredictable — management stated it is impossible to know if the worst is behind, tying it to unpredictable macro/geopolitical factors like the war and its impact on oil and gas.

subsections.label: Labor cost / minimum wage increase
points: Haryana government announced an increase in minimum wages effective 1st April 2026, which will have some cascading impact on labor cost.

Company is mitigating through productivity improvement, tighter control in headcount addition, and better workload management; being a high-growth company, it can add less manpower growth relative to revenue/production growth to absorb this impact over time.

subsections.label: Gas availability constraint
points: Gas availability has been a challenge; partially mitigated via shifting to electric heating and process optimization, reducing gas requirement by ~20% at the company level with no production loss so far.

subsections.label: US tariffs and demand impact
points: Section 232 tariffs remain unchanged; tariffs are inflationary and have a secondary impact of dampening demand — US full-year car SAR estimated at 16-16.5 million units with about 1 million cars lost due to tariff-driven inflationary impact, affecting all suppliers to that market.

subsections.label: Model discontinuation / customer concentration risk
points: Last year, the company lost 300 crore in revenue from one customer due to model discontinuation; such events can happen but not frequently. De-risking comes from supplying the same product to multiple customers and across geographies.

subsections.label: BYD / subsidy landscape (Q&A)
points: On the question of BYD's sales decline following removal of EV purchase tax exemptions and whether shifting subsidy landscape is a structural risk given 70% of order book is BEV/PHEV: management does not view this as a structural risk because most orders are in geographies (US, Europe, India) with little to no subsidies, and India subsidies are also on their way out.

subsections.label: Chinese supply chain penetration risk
points: Getting into the China-for-China EV supply chain remains difficult while Chinese OEMs continue to rely on domestic supply chain; this will change only as Chinese OEMs set up production in Europe/US, at which point the company would become competitive due to duty reasons.

subsections.label: Margin band outlook
points: Previously the company guided a 24-26% margin band for the core business prior to the railway acquisition; post-acquisition, the band is now 23-25%, and management is comfortable continuing in that band.

subsections.label: Suspension motor growth outlook
points: Suspension motor is expected to be the fastest growing business by far, with triple-digit growth rates likely given its small base and strong product/performance acceptance.

Expected 3-4x growth compared to last year; will remain single digit as % of revenue this year, potentially reaching double digits next year, though the exact scale depends on the customer's (Clear Motion's) ability to win additional OEM customers.

subsections.label: Traction motor growth outlook
points: Traction motor, currently ~10% of revenue, expected to be the second fastest growing business with high double-digit growth rates for some time, driven by higher-than-assumed volumes on existing programs, new inquiries, and expected policy push over the next 18 months to increase electrification from current ~20% share of energy mix.

subsections.label: Railway business growth outlook (3-5 years)
points: No year-by-year growth guidance given for railways, but management is confident about good, healthy growth over the next 5 years based on: (1) improving own process/supply chain to service unmet existing demand, (2) filling white spaces within existing brakes, couplers, and suspension product lines, and (3) new products (HVAC, electric panels, others in development) becoming significant drivers in about 3 years' time.

New products (HVAC, electric panels) are expected to become meaningful revenue drivers only from year 3 onward given long approval and field trial cycles (12-15 months for electric panels, 3 years for HVAC to cover all rolling stock types).

subsections.label: Railway business returns outlook
points: Railway business is expected to improve overall returns given it is a very high-return business, though it may be slightly dilutive to margins.

subsections.label: Order book conversion outlook
points: 100% of order book has volume visibility and pricing stability, but actual conversion to revenue depends on volatility; historically, order book volumes are discounted based on experience and tend to average out over time despite year-to-year swings.

guidance_ledger.statement: We had already said that it will be 23 to 25% after the railway acquisition. That is the band...24 to 26% is the band prior, when we [talked of] the core business. I think now it is 23 to 25%, and we should be able to continue being in that band.
We are looking at a very high volume...3 to 4 times growth compared to last year.
This year, at the end of this year, it'll still be single digit. Next year, maybe it even touches double digits.
The traction motor will be the second fastest [growing business]... it will have high double-digit growth rates, actually, maybe, yeah, very high double-digit growth rates for some time.

We are confident about good, healthy growth over the next 5 years in the railway business based on products which are already under development and not counting any other products that we may add in future.

guidance_ledger.metric: Railway new products (HVAC, electric panels) as growth driver
guidance_ledger.statement: New products will become a meaningful driver from 3rd year onwards.

guidance_ledger.metric: Railway business return ratios vs core business
guidance_ledger.statement: It will improve returns because from a return perspective, they're very, very high return businesses. It may be slightly diluted on margins, but return-wise, it will be much higher.
In electric panels, it will take us 12 to 15 months to cover all types of rolling stock because our development is more advanced.
In HVAC, it will take at least 3 years for us to cover all types of rolling stock, especially in the segments where we want to play.

If the question is, when will you see meaningful revenue, assume if your investment horizon is less than 3 years, none of this has any meaning for you as an investor... it takes 4 to 5 years for anything which is a new product...to actually get there.
That is a multi-trillion dollar question...I have no idea [if worst of commodity pressure is behind us].
We have the potential to increase this market share quite robustly in the next few years from what we are seeing in our RFQ pipeline and the market in general.
We expect the return ratios to start improving gradually as we invest the cash that we have in various growth initiatives that we have outlined.
Suspension systems expected to start production in Q2 of FY 27.
Production expected to start in the second quarter of FY 28.

key_takeaways: Q4 was the best ever quarter across the board — highest ever revenue, EBITDA, PAT, BEV revenue, as well as BEV revenue share in the history of the company.

Inflation has hit the industry pretty hard — steel, aluminum, copper, freight, packaging, and energy prices have continued to move up, and this will put pressure on margins for the foreseeable future.
Haryana government's minimum wage increase effective 1st April 2026 will have a cascading impact on labor cost, being mitigated through productivity improvement and tighter headcount control.
Gas availability challenge partially mitigated by shifting to electric heating and process optimization, reducing gas requirement by nearly 20% at the company level with no production loss so far.
Won 4 new driveline orders in Q4, including 3 from European OEMs in a single quarter — the highest ever from Europe and the first EV order win from Europe in almost 4 years.

India's share in the mix crossed 50% for the full year, with PVs, CVs, and electric two-wheelers all hitting best ever quarter in Q4, demonstrating geographic diversification is working.
Received approvals to supply two new railway products — electric panels and HVAC systems — expanding beyond safety-critical brake systems and couplers to passenger comfort products.
Revenue grew 47% YoY in Q4 while EBITDA and net profit increased 32% and 17% respectively; full year revenue growth was 26%, EBITDA growth 13.5%, and PAT growth 11%.
Net order book stands at 237 billion at end of Q4 FY26, with EVs accounting for 70% of the order book.

quarters.summary: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd achieved its highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and net profit in Q2 FY26, despite challenges such as a decline in BEV revenue and supply chain disruptions. The company is optimistic about future growth opportunities, particularly in the EV and railway segments.

subsections.label: Quarterly Performance
points: Achieved highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and net profit.
Revenue grew by 24% year on year.
EBITDA and net profit increased by 13% and 20% respectively.
EBITDA margin lower by 2.3% compared to the same quarter last year.
Profit after tax margin lower by 0.6% due to transmission of lower EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Half-Year Performance
points: Revenue and PAT up by 10% and 4% respectively.
EBITDA lower by 3% year on year.
ROE and ROCE declined due to equity capital issue in September 2024.
Return ratios expected to improve gradually.

subsections.label: Cash Flow and Capital Allocation

The switching system business reported revenues of Rs. 1,111 crores, marking a 16% year-over-year growth.
The lighting system business reported revenues of Rs 1,013 crores, reflecting a 13% year-over-year growth.
The casting business generated revenues of Rs. 824 crores, driven by new capacities.
The aftermarket business reported revenues of Rs. 329 crores, contributing approximately 7% of consolidated revenues.
Uno Minda completed the acquisition of the remaining 49.9% stake in UMEVSPL, a joint venture with FRIWO.

quarters.summary: Management expects the Sapphire Foods merger to complete by end of FY27, with NSE/BSE approvals received in June and regulatory filings progressing; the new leadership team is fully in place and building "DIL 2.0"; KFC targets 5-6% SSSG and 105k-110k ADS to cross 20% Brand Contribution margin (~1.5-2 years horizon); store opening guidance remains unchanged; Pizza Hut's full turnaround push is expected post-merger (around FY28); technology platform buildout (with Cognizant) is expected to be ready before merger integration; Biryani By Kilo is targeted to become a INR 1,000 crore brand over the next few years.

key_figures.label: EBITDA (highest ever, as cited by Chairman)
Seasonal factors led to higher utility costs

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: The improvement in Brand Contribution and effective management of G&A costs helped post highest ever Operating EBITDA.
Judicious use of discounting helped restore KFC Gross Margin.
Food commodity inflation, hike in minimum wages and annual increments, and significantly higher LPG prices impacted costs during the quarter.
Teams effectively managed LPG availability during the period.
Slight price increases taken in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate cost impact; raw material and packaging prices being monitored going forward.
Seasonal factors led to higher utility costs and higher wage costs during the quarter.

key_figures.label: KFC Brand Contribution margin YoY increase
Franchise brands (incl. Costa) revenue growth YoY

subsections.label: KFC
points: KFC continued to post double-digit sales growth building on strong H2 FY26 momentum.

Marketing spends deliberately rebalanced towards driving dine-in visits rather than deep online discounting; media investments focused on positioning the brand at the center of consumption and celebration moments, both in-store and on delivery.
Rebalancing investment towards dine-in channel is showing good results, with offline saliency improving YoY.

subsections.label: Pizza Hut
points: Pizza Hut delivered sequentially better SSSG numbers, working on a 'back-to-basics' reset.
Marketing activity remained measured and purposeful, focused this quarter on communicating improved product quality and everyday value, building the foundation for a stronger brand.
Higher costs and operating deleverage led to Brand Contribution margin eroding slightly despite Gross Margin improvement.
Ended quarter with 626 stores as the brand continues to be right-sized.

Pizza Hut remains the number 2 pizza brand nationally (Domino's is number 1); the biggest historical issue has been the 3-way decision-making structure between DIL, Sapphire and Yum!, which is expected to ease post-merger.
Fundamental problem for Pizza Hut is low ADS versus competition, which requires differentiated offering/innovation across all price points, not just entry price points.
Full push behind Pizza Hut expected once merger structure is sorted, likely around FY28.

subsections.label: Own brands (Vaango, Biryani By Kilo)
points: BBK continues to progress well on top line and bottom line; company is on track to realize the acquisition case turnaround of BBK; Brand Contribution has turned positive versus negative at time of acquisition.
Post-acquisition, company has been evaluating expanding BBK in newer formats; BBK Express is a small box, lower capex format showing initial good response in food courts.
Testing BBK in dine-in format through food courts with good response; also launched BBK at a couple of airport locations to test.
Planning to test a sattvic vegetarian portfolio for BBK during the Shravan and Navratri season.
Objective is to grow BBK into a INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.
Vaango continues to do well; company is bullish on the South Indian food space, described as healthy food that works across dayparts; product needs to be stabilized a little further.

Biryani category is the largest ordered online item on platforms in India, yet the biggest branded players are only around INR 300-350 crore, offering a large opportunity for consolidation and standardized product offering.

subsections.label: Franchise brands (Costa Coffee)
points: Costa Coffee leaned into peak summer season with cold beverage and frappe range, driving footfall and trials through April-June heat.
Costa continued to expand presence in high visibility travel and transit locations.
Higher input costs led to lower Gross Margin for the franchise brands portfolio, but Brand Contribution margin was higher than last year on better cost management.

subsections.label: Dine-in vs delivery strategy
points: Delivery today is eating into dine-in sales rather than adding incremental net top line, unlike the post-COVID period when delivery was purely incremental.
Company is making concerted efforts to bring consumers back to dine-in stores for best customer experience and full flavours.
Dine-in pricing proposition ensures dine-in customers get the best deal along with a better experience.
North region typically favors delivery/convenience more than other regions.
Target is to move KFC offline saliency to 59%-60%, not expected to reach 65% in the near future.
Shift towards dine-in is a broader principle across the business, not format-specific, though pizza is inherently more dine-in oriented.

key_figures.label: International Brand Contribution margin YoY improvement

subsections.label: Store network
points: Plan for opening new units remains in line with guidance given earlier.

subsections.label: Aggregator dynamics
points: Indian QSR industry continues to mature; the interplay between aggregator platforms and dine-in-led brands is an evolving dynamic being navigated thoughtfully, brand-by-brand.

subsections.label: Indian food category opportunity
points: Per capita consumption / incidence of eating out is low in India today; consumers currently associate Western brands with eating out while considering Indian food as home food.

As per capita income grows and more women join the workforce, the Indian food category outside home is expected to expand significantly; management believes in a mature market (15-20 years out) Indian food category outside home could be a far bigger category than Western food category.
South Indian food category and North Indian food category are large but under-organized, offering further expansion opportunities beyond biryani.

subsections.label: Sapphire Foods merger
points: Merger process with Sapphire continues to progress along expected timelines; approvals received from both NSE and BSE in June, bringing the company closer to the next phase of regulatory filings.
Timelines broadly on track with stated target of completion by end of FY2027.
Management thanked Yum! Brands for continued confidence in DIL and RJ Corp as long-term partners.
Merger synergies readiness is not seen as an issue; it was important for the new team to join and settle in first so integration becomes easier, which has been demonstrated.
Technology piece is the other big lever that needs to be sorted before the merger; progress being made as per plans, expected to happen before merger approvals with integration starting post that.
IT integration between Sapphire and Devyani should not be a big challenge since both were on the same technology stack (previously controlled by Yum!) and processes on both sides are very similar.

subsections.label: DIL 2.0 organizational build
points: New leadership team fully in place and settling in well in respective roles under Manish Dawar's leadership; encouraged by early cultural and operational shifts across the organization, described as building 'DIL 2.0'.
New hires include COO, CTO, and Chief Marketing Officer; joining timelines ranged from about 2-3 weeks to about 2 months.

As part of DIL 2.0, entire business development (BD) activity has been consolidated under one leader, unlike the past where individual brands handled their own BD; this led to rethinking of the store opening strategy and approach to landlords.
Promoters are very bullish on the business and have never viewed investment as an issue; promoters feel Devyani can become 'another Varun' (referencing Varun Beverages) over time.

Key priorities for the remainder of the year: 1) opening new stores per earlier guidance, 2) maintaining positive SSSG across brand portfolio, 3) improving efficiency/margin structure via technology adoption and cost control, 4) building next level of team and organization structure with right processes, and 5) getting ready for the merged entity.

subsections.label: Technology buildout
points: New Chief Technology Officer hired, with strong QSR industry background from India and overseas.
Rather than building a full in-house tech team, company decided to build a core team in-house and outsource buildout to Cognizant Technologies.
Combination of core in-house team plus Cognizant outsourcing expected to enable faster rollout, on track before the merger.
Technology adoption is a leverage point that will take a few quarters to realize benefits, with 'a few quarters' counted after the merger since platforms are currently being built.

subsections.label: Global KFC brand initiatives
points: Renewed global thrust for KFC brand around three initiatives: beverages (sub-brand 'Kwench'), sauces, and boneless snacking; all three initiatives are planned to come to India, with India part of the global pipeline.
Company already in discussions to experiment with 'Kwench' in India; product needs to be optimized for Indian conditions and taste.

Capex considerations for new rollouts are viewed differently in Western markets versus India; most homework on 'Kwench' from capex and product optimization perspective is done, with planning underway for test launch timing.
Sauces and boneless initiatives are relatively simpler and will follow once 'Kwench' is established.

subsections.label: International business / Thailand
points: International business posted another quarter of 20%+ YoY growth; Gross Margins remained stable sequentially.
Effective cost management and operating leverage helped improve Brand Contribution margin.
Company has been very happy with Thailand results; currently one of three franchisee partners there.
No formal process has been launched for expanding territory in Thailand; no one has approached the company, but management remains keen to look at opportunities if they arise.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: Quarter presented a mixed macro picture; external environment became more challenging as the conflict in the Middle East pushed crude oil to elevated levels through April and May, feeding into LPG and fuel costs, while the rupee remained under pressure.
RBI, in its June policy, held the repo rate steady but moderated its FY27 growth outlook and raised its inflation projection, reflecting these pressures.
Operating environment has remained volatile, along with usual seasonal complexities.
Demand has remained stable so far, but the forecast of a below-normal season combined with El Niño risk is a reminder that consumption recovery in India rarely moves in a straight line.

LPG availability was a big constraint through the cycle, although the company managed to mitigate the impact; macro pressures are not seen as fully behind the company, with periodic news continuing to emerge.

It is too early to comment definitively on Q2 SSSG trends since the quarter is still in its early stage (month of July); Q2 also faces a different drag effect from Shravan timing versus last year, though broadly a positive trend has been seen in July.

key_figures.label: KFC target ADS for 20% Brand Contribution margin

subsections.label: KFC margin trajectory
points: Key driver for improving KFC Brand Contribution margin remains the ADS number; crossing a threshold of 105,000-110,000 ADS is expected to enable crossing 20% Brand Contribution margin, as demonstrated in the past.
Key lever for ADS is a combination of SSSG in existing stores and quality of new stores (starting new stores at a higher ADS number).
Focus on promoting dine-in channel better versus delivery channel is another lever expected to push margins up; positive results already seen from this quarter's experimentation.
As ADS goes up, operating leverage benefit follows, further helping margins.
Given macro uncertainty, margin achievement timing is contingent on stable conditions; company continues to bring efficiency into the business as a continuous process.
Technology adoption is a leverage point expected to help but will take a few quarters post-merger to realize benefits.

subsections.label: Store opening guidance
points: Plan for opening new units remains in line with the guidance given earlier.

subsections.label: Merger completion
points: Company continues to expect completion of the merger with Sapphire Foods by end of the current financial year (FY27).

subsections.label: Pizza Hut strategy timing
points: Full energy and push behind Pizza Hut expected once the merger and structural issues are resolved, referenced as around FY28.

guidance_ledger.statement: Timelines are broadly on track with our stated target of completion by the end of FY 2027; we continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.
We are looking at a SSSG of about 5% to 6% for KFC.

guidance_ledger.metric: KFC ADS threshold for 20% Brand Contribution margin
guidance_ledger.statement: Once we cross a threshold of 105,000 ADS to 110,000 ADS, we will be able to cross 20% Brand Contribution margins in KFC.
Our target remains to get to a number of 59%-60% offline saliency; I do not think we will be able to get to 65% in the near future.
Our plan for opening new units remains in line with the guidance given earlier.
FY28 is when we will put all our energy behind Pizza Hut once the two entities come together.
Our objective is to make sure that this brand gets to INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years.

guidance_ledger.metric: KFC global initiatives rollout (Kwench, sauces, boneless)
guidance_ledger.statement: All of those initiatives will come to India, one after the other; Kwench homework is mostly done, planning test launch timing; other pieces will follow once Kwench gets established.
We are hopeful that piece also should happen before we get the merger approvals and the integration starts post that.
We do not see an issue in terms of readiness for merger synergies; we are on track and making good progress.

guidance_ledger.metric: FY27 net new store additions (DIL standalone)
guidance_ledger.statement: We expect to add approximately 200 to 225 net new stores in FY27 as DIL.
KFC is expected to contribute 100 to 110 stores of these additions (referenced elsewhere as 110 to 120 store levels).
For 2026 (calendar year), we are not planning to add any net new stores for Pizza Hut - the idea is to consolidate and realign the portfolio.
If you put the two companies together, we are going to be almost a USD 1 billion top line by the time we complete the merger.
I feel very confident that we will be able to largely have the new team in place by next quarter.
Having tested Tea Live in India and Thailand, we have decided to discontinue the brand, and the same will happen in the next quarter.
It will take maybe a couple of months by the time we actually launch that in the market.
Maybe we can fix an Analyst Day in the next couple of quarters, and we can take you guys through in detail on what our plans are.
We feel confident that we will be able to sustain the initiatives that you have seen... it will take another couple of quarters by the time we are firmly able to say that the worst is behind us.
If you can help me foresee the inflation in the near future, I will be able to tell you that.

guidance_ledger.metric: Brand contribution breakeven for Sky Gate
guidance_ledger.statement: Achieved brand contribution breakeven for Sky Gate ahead of target.
Plan to open approximately 100 to 110 new KFC stores in FY26.

risk_register.risk: Crude oil / geopolitical conflict impact on LPG and fuel costs
risk_register.note: Conflict in the Middle East pushed crude oil to elevated levels through April and May, feeding into LPG and fuel costs.
The rupee remained under pressure during the quarter.
RBI moderated its FY27 growth outlook to 6.6% and raised its inflation projection to 5.1%.

risk_register.risk: Seasonal complexities / below-normal season and El Niño risk
risk_register.note: Forecast of a below-normal season, combined with El Niño risk, is a reminder that consumption recovery rarely moves in a straight line.
LPG availability was a big constraint during the cycle, although teams managed to mitigate the impact; not fully behind the company.

risk_register.risk: Food commodity inflation and wage cost increases
risk_register.note: Food commodity inflation along with hike in minimum wages and annual increments impacted costs; higher utility and wage costs seen due to seasonal factors.
The biggest historical issue for Pizza Hut has been the 3-way decision-making structure, expected to ease once merger approval is received.
The interplay between aggregator platforms and dine-in-led brands is an evolving dynamic being navigated thoughtfully, brand-by-brand; delivery today is eating into dine-in sales.

risk_register.risk: Macro uncertainty on future inflation trajectory
risk_register.note: It is not that macros are behind us; there is some news or the other that keeps coming in, making a very bullish view difficult.

risk_register.risk: Gas crisis due to Middle East war
risk_register.note: Significant gas crisis impacted operations; managed effectively with minimal business impact, but continues to be an issue in some parts of the country and company is not fully out of it.

risk_register.risk: Input cost inflation (coffee and cocoa prices)
risk_register.note: Elevated coffee and cocoa prices impacted input costs, leading to a 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins for the Franchise Brands portfolio.
Recurring macro issues since COVID; company has no control over macro factors but notes such situations pressure small-scale players more, aiding consolidation for larger players.
SSSG remained negative at -3.7% though improving sequentially; brand contribution slightly negative due to operating deleverage from lower same-store sales.

risk_register.risk: Store portfolio quality reset leading to negative store count
risk_register.note: Negative store count in Q4 reflects a deliberate BD strategy reset to close loss-making stores and build a better-quality pipeline.
Early signs of consumption recovery in a few sectors due to government support and fiscal measures.
Demand environment remains weak, with consumers becoming value conscious.

risk_register.risk: Impact of Shraavana, Navaratri, and unseasonal rains
risk_register.note: External factors like Shraavana, Navaratri, and unseasonal rains impacted sales.
Minimal impact on the QSR category.
Impacted out-of-home consumption.

themes.label: Strategic merger
themes.note: NSE/BSE approvals received in June; merger with Sapphire remains on track for completion by end of FY27.

themes.label: Demand environment
themes.note: Demand has remained stable so far but below-normal season and El Niño risk pose uncertainty; most brands posted positive SSSG.

themes.label: Store expansion
themes.note: Net new KFC and BBK store additions in India in line with guidance; total store count at 1,855 India / 2,255 globally.

themes.label: Technology integration
themes.note: New CTO hired; core in-house team plus Cognizant outsourcing planned to accelerate tech buildout ahead of merger.

themes.label: Leadership transformation
themes.note: New leadership team (COO, CTO, CMO) fully in place and settling in well, driving 'DIL 2.0' cultural and operational shifts.

themes.note: LPG prices rose significantly amid Middle East conflict; food commodity inflation and wage hikes pressured costs, partly offset by price increases.

themes.note: SSSG improved sequentially to -2.2% with higher ADS, but Brand Contribution loss persisted; full push expected post-merger around FY28.

key_takeaways: We begin the new financial year on a strong note. The momentum we built through the second half of FY26, anchored by KFC's strong same-store sales performance has continued into Q1 FY27.
KFC continues to post double-digit sales growth and delivered another positive SSSG of 3.3% during the quarter.
The business has improved profitability and posted its highest ever EBITDA of INR 255 crore at 16.1% of the revenues.
On a consolidated basis, we delivered a 16.5% year-on-year growth in revenues, reaching INR 1,581 crore.

The improvement in Brand Contribution and effective management of G&A costs helped us post our highest ever Operating EBITDA at INR 151 crore. Our consolidated Operating EBITDA grew nearly 38% year-on-year and represents an EBITDA margin of 9.6%.

The merger process with Sapphire continues to progress along expected timelines. We received approvals from both the NSE and the BSE in June, bringing us closer to the next phase of regulatory filings.
We ended the period with 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 stores globally, as of June 30, 2026.
The new leadership team at DIL is fully in place and is settling in well.
pressing_questions: Percy Panthaki: this 105k to 110k kind of ADS, how many quarters down the line or how soon do you think you can achieve that given the macroeconomic construct?

Vivek Maheshwari: If you leave aside this quarter and the previous quarter, your Same Store Sales have been negative for a long time. What is holding you back from giving a very positive outlook on SSSG, let's say even above mid-single digits?

Vivek Maheshwari: what exactly is the issue [with Pizza Hut], is it execution, the market context, higher margins, or competition? What do you think is holding Pizza Hut back? And is it really worth putting more energy behind this brand?

quarters.summary: Devyani International closed FY26 with KFC posting its strongest SSSG (4.9%) in 14 quarters and consolidated revenue growth of 18.5% YoY in Q4; the proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track for completion by end of the current fiscal year, and management guided to 200-225 net new stores in FY27 (100-110 from KFC) while discontinuing the Tea Live brand and continuing to reset the Pizza Hut portfolio with no net store additions planned for CY2026.

key_figures.label: Gas cost as % of sales
key_figures.value: small (approx. 1.5%-2% referenced by analyst, not confirmed by management)

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Consolidated revenue growth of 18.5% YoY in Q4 driven by strong KFC and international business performance.
Full year revenue crossed the INR 5,500 crore milestone, reaching INR 5,611 crore.
Both gross margin (68.8%) and brand contribution (14.1%) improved YoY on a consolidated basis.
Operating EBITDA grew 13.8% YoY to INR 123 crore, representing 8.6% of sales.

subsections.label: Balance sheet movements
points: Increase in debt during FY26 was temporary, raised for an equity infusion required in Thailand; the debt was squared off by the second week of April.
Increase in intangible assets predominantly reflects the Biryani By Kilo consolidation, with the acquisition consideration sitting largely on the intangible/goodwill side along with brands.

subsections.label: Pricing actions
points: A very small menu price correction was taken in KFC, less than 0.5 percentage point on a portfolio basis, only to tweak bits of mismatches; described as a continuous process.
Management could not foresee future inflation trends to comment on further near-term price increases.
