subsections.label: KFC
points: KFC delivered its strongest performance in the last 14 quarters, posting 4.9% positive SSSG, driven by stable demand environment and tailored, sustained customer engagement.
KFC continues to anchor overall growth momentum and network expansion.

Growth was aided by shifting promotional focus from online to offline/dine-in channels; online promotions were reduced while offline deals/pricing were tailored to attract dine-in customers, with offline gains exceeding online losses.

SSSG improvement is a combination of higher average order value (AOV) and higher incremental transactions; historically, negative SSSG was driven more by weak dine-in versus resilient online, and the strategy reversed this by focusing on the dine-in channel.
Company is also working on recovering lapsed consumers while continuing to recruit new consumers.

Approximately 45 days into the current quarter, KFC has been able to maintain SSSG trends in line with the previous quarter, though management said it would take a couple more quarters to confirm sustainability.

Gross margin expansion in KFC was driven by a combination of favourable raw material and packing material costs, and tweaking the mix of promotions/discounting/deal timing in favour of dine-in customers.

subsections.label: Pizza Hut
points: Focus remains on portfolio consolidation and operational discipline.
SSSG improved sequentially despite remaining negative at -3.7%; ADS remained stable at ~INR 30,000 per store per day.
Brand contribution for the quarter was slightly negative, primarily due to operating deleverage arising from lower same-store sales.

No net store additions during the quarter; negative store count this quarter is due to a strategy reset from a business development (BD) perspective focused on better-quality stores and a stronger pipeline, involving closure of loss-making stores.
No net new Pizza Hut store additions planned for calendar year 2026; focus is on consolidating and realigning the portfolio.

New Chief Marketing Officer Sandeep Anand has joined and will oversee Pizza Hut operations; going back to basics by identifying product gaps, missing pricing layers, and reassessing quality (dough, cheese, toppings) on a de novo basis.

Store staff being retrained on both product quality and customer experience (CX); a complete revival strategy is expected to launch in the market in a couple of months, with a possible Analyst Day in coming quarters to detail brand-by-brand plans.

subsections.label: Own Brands (Vaango and Biryani By Kilo)
points: Both Vaango and Biryani By Kilo reported mid-single-digit positive SSSG.

Biryani By Kilo has achieved positive brand contribution, turning around from a loss-making brand; company has started measured expansion into offline channels via test launch of smaller Express formats in food courts.

Wherever new Express outlets have opened, they have been profitable; management is bullish on Biryani By Kilo's potential once performance is further stabilized, seeing scope for further profitability growth beyond breakeven.

subsections.label: Franchise Brands (including Costa Coffee)
points: Revenue growth remained steady at nearly 3% YoY.
Elevated coffee and cocoa prices impacted input costs, leading to a 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins.
Portfolio delivered a healthy brand contribution margin of 16.1%.

subsections.label: International Business
points: International business continues to deliver strong and consistent growth, with Nepal (still a relatively small contributor) posting an impressive 46% YoY sales increase and Thailand growing revenues 19%.
International business crossed INR 500 crore in quarterly revenues for the first time.
Improved gross margins and operating leverage drove brand contribution margins to 17.7%.

subsections.label: Store network and brand discontinuation
points: Ended FY26 with a system store count of 2,256 stores, representing a net addition of 217 stores over the last 12 months.
Having tested the Tea Live brand in India and Thailand, the company has decided to discontinue the brand, effective next quarter.

key_figures.label: Digital kiosk penetration across KFC network

subsections.label: Digital and technology initiatives
points: Achieved more than 80% digital kiosk penetration across the KFC store network, enhancing customer experience, convenience and engagement across physical formats.

Making strong progress on DIL Commerce, a unified technology platform designed to strengthen operational execution, deepen customer engagement and create a scalable digital backbone for future growth.
Technology, automation and data-led decision-making remain central to the DIL 2.0 transformation journey, playing a key role in enhancing efficiency, scalability and customer experience.

Company will manage all tech-related changes within existing budgets, including Yum! charges, and plans to leverage current infrastructure better with overlaying AI technology rather than materially changing store size or capex per store.

Company continues to explore equipment that can work on both gas and electricity, and has begun evaluating a shift to electrical equipment across the portfolio in response to the gas crisis (e.g., successfully switched Biryani By Kilo equipment to electrical).

subsections.label: Demand environment and consumer engagement
points: Demand sentiment during the quarter remained broadly stable, helped by favourable policy stimulus and GST rate rationalization.
Volume-leading growth in adjacent consumption categories like FMCG points to stable-to-improving demand trends.
Owned and franchise brands maintained positive SSSG trends.
Value-led initiatives and accessibility-focused campaigns at KFC are resonating well with customers, resulting in improved average daily sales trends and sequential recovery in SSSG performance.
Company believes business is well positioned for stronger performance during the year, though external and seasonal factors remain fluid.

Dine-in footfalls have improved industry-wide post Q4 per broader QSR commentary; company has treated online and offline as two different businesses with distinct pricing/incentive strategies to give consumers a reason to visit stores.
Management notes geopolitical/macro uncertainties (e.g., COVID and subsequent events) tend to put more pressure on small-scale players, which helps larger players like DIL consolidate further.
Strategic priorities remain unchanged: disciplined expansion, stronger profitability and deeper consumer relevance through innovation and digital engagement.
Company sees significant momentum on the travel segment, driving focus on opening multiple brands' food courts at highways, malls and food courts.

subsections.label: Proposed merger with Sapphire Foods
points: The proposed merger is a strategic combination of two scaled-up and complementary platforms, united by a shared vision for long-term growth.

Upon completion, the merged entity will emerge as one of the largest QSR platforms globally and as one of the largest partners for Yum!, with a diversified portfolio of leading brands, expanded geography reach and enhanced operational capabilities.
The merger is expected to unlock meaningful synergies, strengthen execution and create a more agile and efficient organization capable of accelerating growth across markets.
Process is progressing as per plan; company remains on track to complete the merger by the end of the current fiscal year.
Filings with stock exchanges have been completed; company expects to receive necessary approval shortly, following which it will proceed with the CCI application.
Combined entity, post-merger, is expected to be almost a USD 1 billion top line business.
FY27 store addition guidance of 200-225 stores is on a standalone DIL basis (including all brands: KFC, Costa, Vaango, Biryani By Kilo), not factoring in the merger scenario.
Mumbai territory operations are managed by Sapphire, not DIL, so Mumbai-specific questions must be addressed by Sapphire.

subsections.label: Management team transformation / DIL 2.0
points: Steps taken to transform the management team under new CEO Manish Dawar; largely new team expected to be in place by next quarter.
Focus is on bringing in experienced, forward-looking professionals with deep operational and strategic expertise as the company prepares for the next phase of growth and integration.

DIL 2.0 is a transformation journey led by new leadership and enabled by digital technology, automation and AI, aiming to build a common, scaled-up 'ONE DIL' view and a frictionless organization across employees, brands and technology.
Core pillars of DIL 2.0: reimagining how the company works, expanding brand reach, making the organization more efficient, and focusing on digital transformation.

Opportunities identified in driving greater collaboration across brands: sharing capabilities, common infrastructure, strategic thinking at middle management level, consumer insights and best practices across the portfolio, aiming for a leaner, more agile, more productive growth-oriented organization.

New leadership hires: Neeraj Tiwari as CTO (technology leadership gap identified); Sandeep Anand as CMO (also overseeing Pizza Hut operations, background combines QSR and technology); Robinder to lead Costa and smaller brands (New York Fries, Sanook Kitchen); a new COO (background from FMCG and technology, companies like Unilever and Amazon) also announced, expected to join in the next couple of weeks.
Rationale for leadership hires tied to skill-gap analysis conducted ahead of the impending merger with Sapphire Foods, given the combined entity's scale (~USD 1 billion top line).

Company had previously tied up with a leading IT company as a technology partner to develop its own apps and technology stack in-house, requiring in-house capability to manage the technology going forward.
Possible Analyst Day planned in the next couple of quarters to detail brand-by-brand strategy once the full new leadership team is in place.

subsections.label: Gas crisis
points: A significant gas crisis occurred in the country due to the Middle East war; teams managed it effectively with minimal impact on the business.
The gas crisis continues to be an issue in some parts of the country; company is not yet fully out of it and continues to monitor the situation closely.
Gas cost described as a small cost as a percentage of sales, though management did not disclose an exact figure.
In response, company is evaluating a shift to electrical equipment across the portfolio (e.g., Biryani By Kilo) and exploring dual gas/electric-capable equipment to mitigate future impact.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Elevated coffee and cocoa prices impacted input costs for the Franchise Brands portfolio, leading to a 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins for that segment.
Management stated it cannot foresee future inflation trends and therefore cannot comment on the likelihood of further near-term price increases.

subsections.label: Macro and geopolitical uncertainty
points: Macro-level factors are not controllable; multiple macro issues have recurred over the last 3-4 years starting from COVID.
Company accepts this as a reality and continues to focus on what is within its control, noting such situations put more pressure on small-scale players, aiding consolidation for larger players.

subsections.label: Store expansion outlook

pressing_questions: Just wanted to understand the gross margin expansion on KFC, it is a pretty big number. What has really driven that?

quarters.summary: Management reported the highest-ever Q1 performance across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit, driven by double-digit volume growth and strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate. Q2 FY27 is expected to be optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and full-quarter West Asia cost impact (INR130-140/ton), but management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27, prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter, net debt/EBITDA to stay below 1x, India Cements EBITDA/ton to reach INR1,000 by Q4 FY28, capacity to reach 212.7 million tons (grey, domestic) by end FY27 and beyond 242 million tons consolidated in 2-2.5 years, and Cables & Wires to launch in Q3 FY27.

subsections.label: Q1 FY27 highlights
points: Q1 was the highest ever first quarter performance for UltraTech across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit.

Operating EBITDA per ton has been steady above INR1,200 this quarter, reflecting cost discipline and operating leverage while absorbing the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory on a volume base enlarged by acquired assets still ramping up to system profitability.
The acquired assets' improvement capex-led cash flows through the P&L over fiscal '27 and '28 will result in the per-ton EBITDA trajectory moving upwards sustainably.

subsections.label: Cost pressures - Q1
points: The biggest one-off cost inflation in Q1 was fuel cost and packing bags, with packing bags having the larger cost impact.
Fuel cost went from INR874 to INR915 per ton, a 5% increase; INR25 to INR40 per ton increase in fuel cost alone.

Packing bags went from an average of about INR9/bag to peaks of INR14-15/bag before settling around INR10/bag, averaging about INR12/bag for the quarter (about INR20/ton impact); fuel contributed about INR40/ton and bags about INR20/ton.

Limestone raising cost rose 13-14% QoQ to the highest level in 2 years, driven largely by industrial diesel prices, which rose from INR78-80/litre pre-war to INR150s/litre during the war (about 50% increase, cited also as INR100 to INR157/litre).

subsections.label: Cost outlook - Q2 FY27
points: Q2 FY27 (July-September) will see the full impact of the war since costs will come to a head from July 1, plus monsoon-related maintenance costs (kilns undergoing maintenance) and negative operating leverage from lower seasonal volumes.

Management expects costs to rise by INR130 to INR140 per ton in aggregate, covering fuel, maintenance and operating deleverage combined - cannot attribute one line item specifically to the war versus normal seasonal effects.
The prior INR250 industry-wide cost impact estimate cited previously was described as 'not a very thorough number'; for UltraTech specifically, the increase is expected at INR130-140/ton.
There is a positive offset within the negative operating leverage as UltraTech's size (volumes) has continuously grown, giving some advantage versus smaller peers.

H2 FY27 variable costs (packaging, energy) are expected to be lower on a per-ton basis versus H1 if the war ends and oil, coal and pet coke prices subside; ocean freight insurance premiums have risen to 4-5% from below 1% due to the war.

subsections.label: India Cements turnaround
points: The printed revenue number of INR1,013 crores (vs INR1,021 crores same period last year) reflects an accounting adjustment - since Q1 FY27 the company reports ex-factory sales, net of freight cost; on a like-for-like basis (ex-freight), revenue was INR993 crores vs INR821 crores, a 21% growth backed by 19% volume growth.
India Cements' EBITDA per ton has climbed sequentially and unbroken: from roughly INR386/ton in Q2 FY26 to INR400 (Q3 FY26), INR509 (Q4 FY26) and INR603 (Q1 FY27).

Every lever behind the improvement is owned by the company: brand migration to UltraTech is 100% complete; premium and trade volumes are rising; cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crores is being deployed into waste heat recovery, preheater upgradation, cooler upgradation etc.
Green power trajectory for India Cements is planned to step up from around 3% of power requirements to about 86% by end of FY28.
India Cements' conversion ratio has improved rapidly to already 1.5x for production.

Q2 FY27 may look optically softer for India Cements due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and West Asia cost effects, but management maintains that the INR1,000/ton EBITDA target remains in sight with full benefit of the capex program flowing through from Q4 FY28.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: As of now, the company is fully booked in terms of cash flows: all operating cash flows will be ploughed back into growth, and beyond that, into dividends for shareholders.
No foreseeable requirement for further investment in cables and wires beyond current plan; that business will first mature and milk the investment already made.
Capital allocation remains committed to cement and shareholders.

Dividend is viewed by the Board as a percentage of profits; management is 'expecting good dividends' going forward, without confirming whether last year's payout (which had a one-off/special component) is repeatable.

subsections.label: Historical outperformance vs industry (volume & EBITDA)
points: June 2022 quarter: UltraTech grew 17.7% in volume vs industry's ~15.5%; UltraTech EBITDA/ton of 1,230 vs industry's ~800.
June 2023 quarter: UltraTech grew 20% in volume vs industry's 15.4%; UltraTech EBITDA was 25% higher than industry.
June 2024 quarter: UltraTech grew 6.5% in volume while rest of industry degrew; UltraTech EBITDA was 26% higher.
June 2025 and September 2025 quarters saw a volume shock/degrowth for UltraTech, but the company recovered.
December 2025 quarter: UltraTech grew 15% vs industry growing about half that rate.
March 2026 quarter: UltraTech grew 9% vs industry growing less than half that rate.
June 2026 (Q1 FY27) quarter: UltraTech grew 13%; industry results awaited to assess market share gains.

subsections.label: Demand drivers - infrastructure
points: Maharashtra planning INR20,000 crores greenfield shipbuilding cluster anchored around Mazagaon Dock.
Odisha announced a deep seaport at Ganjam and shipbuilding cluster at Paradip with investment of over INR50,000 crores.
Tamil Nadu signed ~INR18,000 crores MoU for data centres and shipbuilding projects.
Ports, shipyards, data centres are among the most cement-intensive asset classes in the economy.
Cabinet approved ~INR20,000 crores plus Ahmedabad-Dholera semi high-speed rail corridor.
Metro programs continue to expand across Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune and Uttar Pradesh.
Additional ~INR30,000 crores infusion into NIIF with private capital across roads, ports and urban infrastructure.
India's capex revival is also being propelled by power and data centres, both concrete-hungry sectors.
Vadhavan port - multiple packages have already been awarded, meaning that work will commence, adding to positivity.
River linking (e.g., Ken-Betwa project) expected to be cement-intensive: river banks have to be built (concrete), with silting work and concrete structures on either side.

subsections.label: Demand drivers - housing & urban real estate
points: Housing and urban real estate has had a very strong start to calendar '26.

Across India's top 8 cities, Q1FY26 saw a very big growth in number of units sold per registry records; prices have remained strong, indicating a structurally mature end-user-driven market where absorption keeps pace with supply.
Bangalore stood out on the strength of GCC and technology sector employment.

Redevelopment is significant: Mumbai's Slum Rehabilitation Authority set to redevelop about 850 acres of land; developers continue land banking aggressively; private real estate companies continue to acquire land parcels across cities.
India's grade A office market opened Q1 with a very strong start - premium housing, redevelopment, office towers, hotels are building upwards and outwards simultaneously, all built on cement.

subsections.label: Macro backdrop
points: India's macroeconomic engines demonstrate resilience even as global energy markets endured a disruptive supply cycle.
Benchmark lending rates remain attractive, improving housing affordability and lowering cost of capital for infrastructure developers.
Near-term watch points: coal sector growth slowing in May, lower coal and refinery output, and modest 2% YoY state capex growth in April-May - viewed as timing effects, not a change in trend.

subsections.label: Monsoon/weather impact on demand
points: Part of Q1 demand was helped by drier weather, particularly in June; Rajasthan is going through a very dry patch and may face a water crisis next year impacting demand.
July onwards, wet spells have started across various parts of the country; barring 1-2 states, every state has experienced rains.
Still early in monsoon season - August and September data needed to assess weather progression and impact of dry/wet spells.

subsections.label: East region demand outlook
points: East was the slowest region in April-June, partly due to elections and labor availability.

Multiple Eastern states have gone through elections; land reforms about to come into place in one Eastern state; structural change will be visible over next 2-3-4 years, not next quarter - East expected to witness a good demand upcycle.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Cement prices were constructive during the quarter; all-India exit prices improved through June even as monsoon sets in.
East and South led price improvements; Central and West were steady; North was a consistent performer.
Industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter due to cost increases - viewed as a constructive outcome for this time of year.
Cost escalations of the past 2 quarters are still to be fully passed through, and with demand momentum, a supportive price environment is expected as the busy season approaches.
Premiumization and blended cement mix continue to support blended realizations regardless of headline price movements.
Management said prices move with demand: if demand is strong on an all-India basis, prices can go up; if the cost curve comes down, prices are not necessarily forced to reduce.
On pricing outlook for the monsoon quarter, management said 'expecting higher is everybody's desire, we will attempt it, we'll see where we land.'

key_figures.label: RMC as % of overall cement industry business

subsections.label: Brand transition - Kesoram and India Cements
points: Management converted the Kesoram and India Cements brands to 100% UltraTech; these brands were operating in B or C category space and the company did not vacate that space.

Post brand conversion, the true performance of UltraTech is visible; the team successfully converted customers who were buying B/C category cement into A category brand buyers willing to pay a price premium.
This conversion of B/C category markets to UltraTech at higher price points is cited as a key driver of the company's ability to outperform on both volumes and pricing versus peers.

subsections.label: Retail vs institutional market strategy
points: India is fundamentally a retail market for cement given low urbanization and low RMC penetration; management believes cement will remain a branded product play as long as India remains a retail, individual-homebuilder market.

Similar branded dynamics exist in other Indian commodities like steel (TMT rebar) and paints, because these are retail markets too - contrasted with markets like UAE where RMC is the biggest customer and there's no brand play.
For UltraTech specifically, despite having the largest number of RMC plants in the country (477), RMC is only 3.5% of total sales, underscoring the branded retail nature of the business.
The brand play will persist as long as India remains in nascent stages of RMC adoption and urbanization.

subsections.label: Network and reach
points: UltraTech has almost 76 operating facilities spread across the country.
Network of nearly 2,000 plus/minus warehouses.
150,000 channel partners across the country.
Dedicated transporters, with more than 50% of transport service providers dedicated to UltraTech.
16,000-plus employees across the country.
5,000-plus UBS stores (dedicated dealers/outlets for UltraTech Cement).

key_figures.label: New capacity commissioned by UltraTech (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu)
Green power share of total power requirement - exit

subsections.label: Capacity expansion
points: Projects under execution for capacity growth are backed by capex of about INR17,000 crores in the next 2 to 2.5 years.
Consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons, with grey cement capacity reaching 212.7 million tons by end of fiscal '27 and the balance completed the following year.
Every ton of committed expansion is fully backed by secured limestone; there is no raw material constraint on the growth trajectory.
March 2028 exit target of 235 million tons domestic, implying 22-25 million tons added in FY28 beyond the 212 million tons expected by March 2027, and 37 million tons total added across FY27-28.

Team has already started working on growth plans beyond 240 million tons; industry capacity addition estimates for FY27-28 could not be firmly quantified as some industry players are reportedly revisiting their expansion plans.
Inorganic growth opportunities will be examined if they arise, alongside the organic capacity plan.
12 million tons of new capacity commissioned across the country in April-June, of which UltraTech commissioned 8.7 million tons at Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu.
Current capacity stands at 200.1 million tons domestic and 205.5 million tons including international operations.

subsections.label: Green energy transition
points: Green power capacity stands at 1,897 MW, meeting 47% of total power requirement at end of quarter (lower average during the quarter itself).
71 MW of renewables and 19 MW of WHRS commissioned this quarter.
Expect to reach 2.5 to 3 gigawatts of green power very shortly.
Green power is a structural buffer that helped absorb the West Asia fuel cost shock and is cheaper than conventional power.
India Cements green power trajectory planned to step up from around 3% currently to about 86% of power requirements by end of FY28.

subsections.label: Cost efficiency levers
points: Cement lead distance has come down further from 367 km to 360 km, a 7 km reduction; annualized at INR2.5-3 per ton per kilometre, this represents a visible upfront saving.
Clinker conversion has improved to 1.5x, a small improvement.
Power consumption has gone down and power rate has gone down because of power mix changes.
Management prefers to present a comprehensive annual cost-saving number at year-end rather than quarter-by-quarter, since Q2 will show a negative (cost increase) performance.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: East region was the slowest growing in April-June quarter, partly due to elections and labor availability.
South and North grew a shade below 15%.
West and Central grew above 15%.
East and South led price improvements during the quarter; Central and West were steady; North was a consistent performer.

subsections.label: Fuel sourcing strategy
points: Pet coke has become more expensive in energy terms than coal, making domestic coal more attractive to buy.
Company is fully inventory loaded on coal, which is expected to cap fuel cost per kcal from rising further beyond around INR2/Kcal.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires supply chain
points: Sourcing raw material from Hindalco, with a lead distance of only four hours, providing tangible working capital and logistics benefits.

Working capital will initially be higher due to inventory ramp-up; structurally, the company is working on financing suppliers to release working capital, targeting stabilization to around 30 days plus/minus after about six months (around April-June FY28).

subsections.label: Competitive positioning drivers
points: Decades of consistent delivery, bag after bag, site after site, has made UltraTech synonymous with reliability; quality standards apply to every ton, with product complaints resolved ASAP.
Complete network of plants (integrated plants, grinding units, bulk terminals) is focused on meeting customer requirements.
Legacy of governance and ethical conduct at Aditya Birla Group/UltraTech is at its highest pecking order, giving dealers and institutional buyers assurance that commands a premium.
Combination of network reach, brand trust, and quality is described as unique to UltraTech and not replicable by competitors.

subsections.label: Brand vs commodity dynamics
points: India's cement industry will remain a brand-driven, retail play as long as India remains an individual-homebuilder, low-urbanization market; similar to other Indian retail commodities like steel and paints which are also branded despite being commodities elsewhere in the world.
As RMC penetration remains low (industry ~20%, UltraTech 3.5%), brand power in the trade/retail market will remain central to the business for the foreseeable future.

subsections.label: India Cements merger considerations
points: Most targets set at the time of the India Cements acquisition are nearing completion; before contemplating merger into a stand-alone entity, remaining steps include completing the ongoing capex program and disposing of certain non-core assets (land).
Expected completion of the turnaround journey by Q4 FY28 or possibly a quarter earlier.
Certain operating parameters for India Cements still need to be brought in line with UltraTech's stand-alone performance.

Entire India Cements volume is now reported as part of UltraTech's consolidated (stand-alone) volume; the company has stopped reporting India Cements stand-alone volumes separately in the presentation/press release.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires new business launch
points: Project is on schedule and on budget, within the approved INR1,800 crores investment program (INR888 crores spent/committed to date).
Channel partners onboarding is moving at a frantic pace; facility setup is complete; trial runs have commenced; key regulatory approvals are in place; leadership team is on board.
SAP/ERP systems are in place; CRM is under testing and will be live before launch.
Reaffirmed commissioning and product launch in Q3 FY27 (October-December 2026), precisely as previously committed.
Management does not intend to scale up further capex in cables and wires for now; the business will first mature and 'milk' the current investment before any further expansion.
No formal guidance given for the Cables and Wires business other than the aim to be 'profitable, grounded and grow with the market.'

subsections.label: Track record of delivery
points: Company crossed 200 million tons of capacity a year early versus prior commitment.
Brand migration of India Cements and Kesoram was completed a quarter early versus prior commitment.
Cables and Wires launch commitment for Q3 FY27 is being reaffirmed and delivered as promised.

subsections.label: West Asia crisis / geopolitical risk
points: Q1 FY27 opened with the most disruptive situation - the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, crude crossed $100, and coal costs spiked; situation later de-escalated but remains fluid and uncertain.
Management cannot fully separate cost impacts attributable to the war versus normal seasonal/maintenance effects.
Ocean freight insurance premiums have risen to 4-5% from below 1% due to the war, reflecting broader disruption.
Structural buffers (green power, AFR substitution, reduced lead distance) helped the company absorb the shock better than peers.

subsections.label: Cost inflation risk
points: Sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory absorbed during the quarter.
Industrial diesel prices spiked sharply (from INR78-80/litre pre-war to INR150s/litre during war), driving up limestone raising costs by 13-14% QoQ to a 2-year high.
Cost pressure of INR130-140 per ton expected in Q2 FY27 from fuel, monsoon-related kiln maintenance, and negative operating leverage.
Cost escalations of the past two quarters are still to be fully passed through to prices.

subsections.label: Weather/monsoon risk
points: Dry spell in certain states (e.g., Rajasthan) could lead to water crisis and demand impact next year.
Still early in monsoon season; effects on demand to be clearer only in August-September.

subsections.label: Demand-side structural risk (long-term)
points: Management flagged that a slowdown in structural demand growth (e.g., people not buying houses, industrialization stalling, data centers shifting to other countries like Pakistan) would be the biggest challenge for the industry and the company over a 5-year horizon, though this is not currently foreseen.

subsections.label: Capacity constraint risk
points: If demand remains strong, the challenge for the company will be insufficient capacity, necessitating continued expansion.

Q2 FY27 may look optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and West Asia cost effects, but the direction of travel and destination remain unchanged.

H2 FY27 variable costs expected to be lower per ton than H1 if the war ends and oil/coal/pet coke prices stabilize.

subsections.label: Capacity and capex outlook

subsections.label: India Cements outlook

Merger of India Cements into a stand-alone entity is contemplated only after completion of the capex program and disposal of certain non-core (land) assets, expected around Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier.

subsections.label: Cables and Wires outlook
points: Commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Q3 FY27 (October-December 2026), within the approved INR1,800 crores capex program.

themes.label: Demand growth
themes.note: Double-digit volume growth (13.1%) driven by strong demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate; management targets double-digit volume growth for FY27.

themes.label: Cost pressures
themes.note: Fuel, packing bag and industrial diesel/limestone cost inflation from the West Asia crisis; further INR130-140/ton cost increase expected in Q2 FY27.

themes.label: Brand transition
themes.note: Kesoram and India Cements brands fully converted to UltraTech, driving 21.3% brand growth as B/C category customers migrated to the premium A category brand.

themes.label: M&A integration (India Cements/Kesoram)
themes.note: India Cements EBITDA per ton climbed sequentially to INR603 in Q1 FY27, with INR1,000/ton target reiterated for Q4 FY28 and brand migration complete a quarter early.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons with consolidated capacity targeted beyond 242 million tons in 2-2.5 years, backed by INR17,000 crores capex.

themes.label: Green energy transition
themes.note: Green power capacity of 1,897 MW met 47% of power needs at quarter end, helping absorb the fuel cost shock; targeting 2.5-3 GW shortly.

themes.label: Capital allocation / shareholder returns
themes.note: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.87x; cash flows to be ploughed back into growth capex and dividends, with no further Cables and Wires capex planned for now.

key_takeaways: Q1 was the highest ever first quarter performance for UltraTech across volumes, revenues, EBITDA and profit.
Domestic grey cement volumes grew 13.1%, capacity utilization improved to 81% from 76%, EBITDA of INR5,146 crores and PAT of INR2,604 crores, up 17.2% YoY.
Kesoram and India Cements brands have been converted to 100% UltraTech; the converted brand grew 21.3% YoY as B/C category customers migrated to the A category UltraTech brand at a price premium.
Operating EBITDA per ton held steady above INR1,200 despite the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory, reflecting cost discipline and operating leverage.

India Cements delivered a clear turnaround: like-for-like revenue grew 21% and volumes grew 19%, with EBITDA per ton climbing sequentially from INR386 (Q2FY26) to INR400, INR509 and INR603 (Q1FY27); India Cements EBITDA per ton of INR1,000 remains targeted by Q4 FY28.

Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons and total capacity 205.5 million tons after commissioning of Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu; consolidated capacity to go beyond 242 million tons in 2-2.5 years backed by ~INR17,000 crores capex.
Cables and Wires project remains on schedule and on budget, reaffirming commissioning and product launch in Q3 FY27.
Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.87x from 0.94x at start of year, and company remains confident of ending FY27 below 1x.
Q2 FY27 expected to be optically softer due to seasonal monsoon slowdown and full quarter impact of West Asia cost disruption, with an expected INR130-140 per ton cost increase.
pressing_questions: What is the sort of working capital days for the Cables and Wires business, particularly on inventory days given the low lead distance from suppliers like Hindalco?
What steps remain before India Cements could be merged into a stand-alone entity, given most acquisition targets are nearing completion?
Given industry players revisiting expansion plans, what is UltraTech's estimate of industry-wide capacity addition for FY27-28?
Is there a structural shift toward prioritizing profitability/pricing over market share, or vice versa, if input costs decline later in the year?
How cement-intensive are river-linking projects like Ken-Betwa compared to something like a hydropower plant?

quarters.summary: UltraTech expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum in FY27 and beyond, targets double-digit volume growth for UltraTech itself in FY27, plans capex of INR8,000-10,000 crores every year for the foreseeable future to grow beyond 240 million tons capacity (37 million tons already committed to take capacity to 242.5 million tons by FY28), and expects cost-efficiency programs (India Cements/Kesoram) to push India Cements EBITDA/ton beyond INR1,000 by FY28, with near-term cost headwinds from the West Asia conflict (fuel, bags, forex) being managed via pricing and sourcing measures; leverage to be maintained below 1x.

subsections.label: Margin and cost drivers
points: EBITDA per ton improvement driven by improving trade mix and premiumization along with realization gains.
India EBITDA per ton of INR1,240 achieved when excluding last month's bag cost increase and forex mark-to-market loss from rupee devaluation.
UAE operations contributed substantially to EBITDA alongside strong India performance (India capacity ~196 million tons during the year).

subsections.label: Forex impact explanation
points: $950 million of foreign currency borrowings are fully hedged, but mark-to-market accounting at quarter-end (INR94.85/$ on 31 March vs strengthening to ~INR93 subsequently) creates a noncash debit to EBITDA/P&L.
This mark-to-market hit is a noncash item but is accounted within EBITDA, not as an extraordinary or finance cost item.

subsections.label: Dividend rationale
points: Dividend of INR240/share (2400%) proposed, 3x last year's dividend.
Dividend stress-tested against retained earnings remaining adequate for all planned investments and commitments; credit metrics and debt covenants unaffected.
Dividend growth from 10% of profits in 2020 to 37% last year reflects a deliberate Board strategy to reward shareholders as operating cash flows grow.
Management indicates future payout could go up or down depending on annual OCF and Board decision, with intent not to over-leverage the balance sheet.
Company reiterated it will not exceed a leverage of 1x net debt/EBITDA even while funding growth capex.

subsections.label: Wire and cable business capex
points: INR800 crores spent out of committed INR1,800 crores capex for the cable and wire business.
Management indicated the business remains on track, potentially launching earlier (first month of Q3) than the originally committed December timeline.

subsections.label: Demand commentary
points: India's structural growth story intact despite West Asia conflict: government capex flowing, infrastructure execution continuing, housing demand robust; IMF raised India's growth forecast.
India built ~10,660 km of highways in FY25 and maintained similar pace in FY26; PMAY housing program driving cement consumption at scale.
Rural demand remained steady, inferred from capacity utilization above 80% nationally and trade mix holding at 66-67%.
Too early to determine cash flow improvement in rural markets from crop cycles for the current quarter.
Slowdown observed in the last 15 days attributed to excessive heat and Bengal/Tamil Nadu elections, but underlying demand undercurrent remains strong.

Trade/non-trade mix elevated to 65-35 (vs historical 70-30) partly due to temporary reduction in infra offtake (e.g., end of a high-speed rail project phase in Gujarat), expected to normalize as infra activity (e.g., Mumbai's $60 billion infrastructure spend) picks up.

subsections.label: Pricing dynamics
points: Cement price hikes historically muted versus other building material industries (steel, agri, PVC) due to fragmentation of the cement industry.
Price increases typically occur in Q1 of the financial year, not Q4, due to seasonal patterns (monsoon impact in July-September, volume focus in March).
Price increases taken in April 2026 to offset rising input costs; management believes cost-related price hikes are 'here to stay' since cost pressure affects the entire industry uniformly.
Price increases already taken are viewed as adequate to offset the ~INR6/bag cost increase.

subsections.label: India Cements / Kesoram integration progress
points: Sequential improvement in India Cements EBITDA per ton every quarter since acquisition (INR305 in Q3 to INR497 in Q4).
India Cements declared PAT of INR60 crores for the quarter, first time in a long time.

Under a related-party tolling arrangement, India Cements manufactures and sells the UltraTech brand but does not bear direct marketing/distribution costs — those sit at the UltraTech consolidated level, with UltraTech charging a markup per bag on ICL volumes to offset this; hence India Cements' underlying operational progress is understated by the reported INR497/ton figure (true comparable figure ~INR670/ton after accounting for the INR200/ton booked in UltraTech books).
Selling price improvements in southern markets expected to give India Cements further boost.
Kesoram already operating at ~INR1,000/ton EBITDA, broadly in line with other South cement operations.

India Cements and Kesoram together represent ~13% of consolidated capacity, moving from an integration drag to an earnings contributor; expected to become a meaningful and growing source of group-level EBITDA accretion as cost-improvement capex matures.
100% brand migration completed by end of March 2026 for both India Cements and Kesoram, a quarter ahead of schedule.

Post full brand conversion, only ~0.5 million tons of India Cements volume in Q4 remained non-UltraTech branded (0.39 million tons), implying limited further realization upside purely from brand conversion but significant efficiency upside from logistics/operational integration (single product now shipped from all 9 India Cements factories vs multiple brands earlier).
Efficiency improvement of INR200/ton still expected to flow into India Cements' books; full efficiency program (targeting >INR300/ton) to mature further into FY28.
India Cements EBITDA/ton guidance of >INR1,000/ton by FY28 is described as 'all inclusive' — i.e., includes the ~INR200/ton currently booked in UltraTech's standalone books via the tolling markup.

subsections.label: UAE / overseas operations
points: UAE capacity utilization dropped to ~80% during the war from 100% pre-war; now recovering with 'permanent peace program' in place, with utilization and prices both moving up.
UAE operations are entirely bulk (no bag costs) and 100% sold to RMC (zero trade sales).
Stable sequential UAE EBITDA (INR267 crores Q3 to INR278 crores Q4) — described as a 'stable journey'.
UAE economy expected to be among the first to recover, potentially with new government programs reviving the economy.

subsections.label: RMC business
points: RMC considered an integral, strategic part of UltraTech's business and offering, viewed as the future growth engine given increasing urbanization.
No specific numeric target set for RMC's share of volumes (currently 3%); no plan to monetize the RMC business.
RMC revenue growth outpacing volume growth.

subsections.label: Capacity growth trajectory
points: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India — a first for any company in a single country outside China.

Reached 100 million tons in 2019, added 50 million tons over 5 years to reach 150 million by 2024, then went from 150 to 200 million tons in less than 2 years — a full year ahead of the company's own targets.
More than tripled capacity in a decade, from ~65 million tons in 2016 to 200 million tons today.
Outside China, UltraTech is the largest cement company globally by sales volume and the only company anywhere with over 100 million tons of production capacity within a single country.
Committed to add a further 37 million tons in a phased manner, taking total capacity over 242.5 million tons by FY28.

Company has already begun charting its growth story beyond 240 million tons capacity, with further details to be shared next year; incremental capex beyond 240 million tons estimated at plus/minus INR15,000 crores.

subsections.label: Green energy and fuel mix
points: Renewable energy platform has been growing from strength to strength; ~43% of power needs currently met from green sources.
Company committed to reaching ~85% of power requirements from green energy by end of FY30 and is confident of achieving this.
On the fuel side, actively managing the mix by optimizing between petcoke, coal, alternative fuels, and increasing domestic coal share wherever possible.

No new thermal power capacity being added; instead, higher levels of WHRS (waste heat recovery systems) are being added, along with tying up renewable energy, aided by grid availability at several locations.

subsections.label: Logistics / lead distance
points: Lead distance reduced to 367 km, aided by an ever-expanding bulk terminal network including the new Lucknow facility, helping reach customers faster and reduce overall costs.

subsections.label: Clinker factor
points: Clinker conversion ratio currently at 1.48x, targeted to reach 1.54x by fiscal '28.
Company will always remain fully clinker-backed (maintaining historical hypothesis of 70% clinker backing) even as conversion ratio improves.

Management declined to comment on industry-wide clinker conversion trends but noted UltraTech is structurally stronger than the rest of the industry across multiple metrics including EBITDA/ton and growth.

subsections.label: Regional notes
points: Mumbai infrastructure spend of $60 billion cited as a structural demand driver going forward, with 2035 expected to represent a totally new phase for the city.
Western region infra demand expected to turn 'darker green' (i.e., stronger) going forward given large infrastructure spend plans.
India Cements' logistics efficiency set to improve now that a single (UltraTech) product ships from all 9 India Cements factories, versus multiple brands shipping earlier.

subsections.label: Sourcing and mitigation measures for West Asia crisis
points: Company dispatches have not suffered at any location due to the conflict; bag availability has become expensive but has not been a crisis.

Mitigation measures include diversifying procurement sources, identifying new sourcing opportunities, and entering long-term fuel contracts that are expected to be favorable going forward (unlike unfavorable long-term contracts over the last 2 years).
~150 bag suppliers across the country provide sourcing resilience; high-volume customers like UltraTech get prioritized servicing from suppliers.
Diesel price impact remains uncertain and unquantified; management states it will 'wait and watch'.

Some ripples in fuel costs expected in July-September if pet coke prices sustain at elevated levels ($150-160), but company expects to manage better than industry peers due to supply contracts and domestic coal sourcing.
Long-term fuel supply contracts and inventory/sourcing rotation are continuous and expected to persist as a mitigation lever.
Bag cost increase from INR9 to INR15 per bag (delta of INR6) has already occurred; cost has since stabilized/slightly reduced to INR13-14 per bag.
INR90 crore bag-cost hit in March cannot be annualized, as prices have since stabilized and volumes of alternate inventory/sources have been built up.

subsections.label: Premiumization and market positioning
points: Blended cement share and premium portfolio contribution both moved higher during the quarter — a conscious, deliberate strategy going forward.
UltraTech enjoys premium brand positioning, which has helped realizations especially post brand migration of acquired assets (India Cements, Kesoram).
Cement industry has been relatively slower than other building material industries (steel, agri, PVC) in taking price hikes, attributed to industry fragmentation.
UltraTech outperforming the rest of the industry in growth and EBITDA per ton, attributed to clinker conversion improvements (composite cement), RMC integration, and other operational efficiencies.

subsections.label: India Cements legal/merger status
points: Merger of India Cements into UltraTech not yet undertaken due to legacy, long-pending legal cases; management is working to resolve these before proceeding to next phase of integration, to avoid any risk to the main UltraTech Board/company.
No specific timeline provided for full merger.

subsections.label: RCB / balance sheet ring-fencing
points: Management reaffirmed that UltraTech's balance sheet remains ring-fenced and not used to support other group entities (referencing prior Chairman statements made regarding Vodafone-Idea aspersions); no funds have moved from UltraTech's balance sheet for other purposes.
Operating cash flow is committed to meeting UltraTech's own capex requirements (~INR10,000 crores/year for at least 4-5 years, ~INR50,000 crores cumulative) and rewarding shareholders.

subsections.label: Adjacency/diversification stance
points: Wire and cable business remains the sole non-cement adjacency investment; management stated no other building-material-adjacent investments are planned for the next 5 years.

subsections.label: West Asia conflict impact
points: Conflict in West Asia is a real headwind on fuel costs, packing bags, freight, certain import-dependent supply chains, and near-term sentiment in some demand segments.
Rising oil prices could lead to increases in domestic petrol/diesel prices.
Government's monthly economic review for March '26 acknowledged the outlook has become slightly uncertain.
Management characterizes the West Asia situation as a near-term cost moderator, not a structural demand reversal.
Steel prices have seen volatility while cement prices have been largely stable (0-5% movement) over the last financial year.

subsections.label: Currency / forex risk
points: Rupee devaluation created a mark-to-market hit on $950 million of foreign-currency borrowings (fully hedged) due to accounting requirement at quarter-end rate (INR94.85/$ on 31 March vs. subsequent strengthening to below INR93), resulting in a noncash debit to EBITDA/P&L.
Management is not factoring in a scenario of dollar reaching INR100, calling any such move a notional debit risk to the P&L.

subsections.label: Input cost inflation
points: Packaging (bag) costs rose sharply in March (INR9 to INR15/bag, later stabilizing to INR13-14).
Diesel cost impact is unresolved and could surface in the coming months.
Fuel costs could see 'some ripples' in July-September if elevated pet coke prices persist.

subsections.label: Legal/legacy risk (India Cements)
points: Long-pending legacy legal cases inherited with India Cements are delaying full merger; company avoiding taking risk with the main UltraTech Board while working to resolve them.

subsections.label: Outlook commentary
points: Structural growth drivers (urbanization, government infra commitment, PMAY housing targets, rising rural demand) remain firmly in place and undiluted by the West Asia crisis.
Near-term environment complexities remain unpredictable ('nobody knows what will happen tomorrow'); management will 'wait and watch'.
Fiscal '27 P&L expected to start reflecting integration/cost-efficiency benefits from India Cements and Kesoram investments.
Company will maintain leverage below 1x net debt/EBITDA year after year even while meeting growth capex needs.
Future capex pipeline is described as fully funded with the growth story intact.

We expect a sustainable volume growth of 7% to 8% per annum.

key_takeaways: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.

UltraTech is today the largest cement company in the world by sales volume outside of China, and the only cement company anywhere in the world to have over 100 million tons of production capacity within a single country.
Committed to add a further 37 million tons, which will take us over 242.5 million tons in a phased manner by fiscal '28.
Consolidated sales volumes has crossed a rocking 44 million tons this quarter; UltraTech as a brand year-on-year has grown 19%.
EBITDA per ton, excluding acquired assets, is at INR1,296 per ton for the quarter, up from INR1,225 in Q4 '25.

100% brand migration completed at the end of March '26 for both India Cements and Kesoram; India Cements EBITDA of INR497 per ton in Q4 '26 up from INR333 in Q2 and INR305 in Q3, and declared PAT of INR60 crores for the quarter, after a very long time.
Net debt-EBITDA of 0.94x at consolidated level and 0.92x at UltraTech India level; Board has recommended a dividend of INR240 a share for fiscal '26.

We expect a sustainable volume growth of 7% to 8% per annum; growth capex requirement is not shrinking, with a plan of investing around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores every year for the foreseeable future.
pressing_questions: Sir, you also said that packing cost impact was felt only in March month... shall we assume that that's the run rate which will continue given there's no relief on packing?

Given some of the EBITDA of India Cements is getting booked in UltraTech standalone, your INR1,000 per ton guidance includes that one which is getting booked in UltraTech or it is pure India Cements EBITDA per ton, which will come purely through cost savings and all?
India Cements, you're doing the right things, when do we see the day when we actually merge it? I understand there are a few legal cases which are there. But any time lines over here?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw strong volume growth (18% YoY combined grey+white) driven by Central India expansion, with management guiding to ~22.5-23 million tons grey volume for FY27, continued double-digit growth, no change to capacity roadmap (40 million tons by FY28, 50 million by FY30), but near-term cost pressure (~INR150/ton in Q2 from fuel/diesel) expected to weigh on margins, with fuel cost expected to peak in Q2 before declining.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Net sale increase in Q1 FY27 was mainly on account of product mix and some price improvement.
EBITDA margin declined YoY and QoQ due to cost pressures (fuel, diesel) and operating deleverage from lower sequential volumes.

subsections.label: Cost pre-ponement
points: Q1 had a timing difference due to preponement of some maintenance (kiln), which will result in lower maintenance cost in Q2 versus what was earlier projected.
Pre-ponement of maintenance expense from Q2 to Q1 was in the range of INR50 crores.

subsections.label: Debt position
points: Net debt increased quarter-on-quarter as on 30th June 2026 compared to 31st March 2026, alongside a slight decline in cash balance and increase in gross debt.

subsections.label: Pricing
points: Prices in Q1 were more or less flat/same versus average, as some price increase occurred in between the quarter.
Despite monsoon seasonality typically causing sharp price drops, management does not expect price drops this time due to cost pressures from the geopolitical situation.

subsections.label: Volume growth drivers
points: Major volume growth is driven by expansion in Central India, including the grinding unit in Bihar.
In existing markets of North and South, company continues to grow in line with the market as there is no extra volume/capacity available there.
FY27 growth may not fully sustain at Q1's pace due to capacity restrictions in North and South; growth engine remains Central India.
Company reiterated it will not lose market share in any region and plans to grow profitably rather than aggressively chase top-line with a strategic, brand-building approach.

subsections.label: Volume growth outlook (double-digit)
points: Management confirmed grey cement volume growth for FY27 will be double-digit, though North and South growth will be restricted by capacity limitations.
Console white cement double-digit growth may not be possible in FY27 due to loss of ~50% normal Middle East volume from geopolitical restrictions on shipping/loading.

key_figures.label: White business volume growth (implied via geopolitical tailwind)
Paint business revenue growth expected FY28

subsections.label: White cement/putty business
points: Geopolitical situation had a positive impact on white business as imports of white cement/putty from UAE into India did not come through, giving the company an opportunity for extra volumes.

Because white cement availability was limited (due to reduced UAE imports), the company could do extra volume; this positive impact was mainly seen in Q1, may continue partly in Q2, but competitive intensity in putty is expected to normalize/continue longer term.

The 0.6 MTPA putty capacity expansion at Nathdwara is nearing completion and expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27, reducing dependence on toll manufacturing amid peak demand challenges this quarter that required sourcing material from toll manufacturers.
Company plans to grow the putty business in double digits year-on-year but is capacity-constrained until Nathdwara commissioning.

subsections.label: RMC (Ready-Mix Concrete) business
points: RMC business ramping up from 5 plants exited in March to 17 operative plants currently, targeting 50 by FY27 and 100 by FY28.
RMC cost is largely captured under raw material cost consumed.
RMC is not a very high-EBITDA-margin business (4-7% standalone), but strategically necessary because losing RMC supply to a project risks losing associated cement and other building material volumes.
Marginal EBITDA loss currently in RMC as capacities ramp up; each plant takes about 3 months to reach breakeven; no significant loss expected, described as 'single-digit loss', not material.
First time RMC revenue was disclosed separately on a quarterly basis, as earlier volumes were insignificant (only 5 plants as of March exit).

subsections.label: Paint business
points: Entry into paint business was driven by need to diversify the paint counter beyond putty alone, as relying on one product was becoming difficult to retain customers.
Board approved a limited capital allocation of INR600 crore to the paint business, given priority on core cement business.
Paint business achieved EBITDA breakeven in Q1 FY27, ahead of the third-year breakeven expectation.
Paint business is expected to help/support putty volume growth, though the exact incremental contribution from paint synergy is difficult to quantify.
Paint business uses the JK Cement/putty platform for distribution (common customers); JK Cement charges platform/service charges to the paint company for this.

Two brands used: Acro and Maxx; Maxx brand sales are included in standalone JK Cement top line, while Acro brand is a direct sale from the subsidiary; most of Q1 paint revenue (INR125 crore) sits in the standalone entity.
Company plans to fund paint business growth from its own earnings going forward, keeping capital reserved for the core cement business.

subsections.label: White cement UAE/GCC operations
points: Due to geopolitical situation, white cement sales are currently restricted to GCC countries only; unable to export to other regions due to lack of available ship loading.
Some competitor imports (clinker and cement) have started coming into UAE/India but not yet at normal quantities; management is watching this closely for Q2.

subsections.label: Ongoing capex projects
points: Greenfield project at Jaisalmer progressing well; confident it will be commissioned within targeted timeframe of H1 FY28.
Grinding unit at Bhatinda progressing well.
Land acquired for a second split grinding location in Punjab; work to start at that site as soon as possible.
Wall putty expansion in Rajasthan is near completion and expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Panna Line 2 kiln is being worked at an expanded capacity of 4 million tons; expected to achieve this in the current fiscal (FY27); no clinker shortage currently foreseen for Central India volumes.

subsections.label: Expansion schedule/confidence
points: Company reaffirmed no plans to reschedule or push back capacity expansion (40 million tons by FY28, 50 million tons by 2030), despite some competitors stepping back on capacity expansion.
Next phase of expansion beyond the current 40-million-ton program is being worked out; Board approval timing to be decided at an appropriate time keeping the 2030 target in view.

It is premature to give a definite Board approval date for next expansion phase given large ongoing capex; decision will factor in project completion timing and overall business/geopolitical environment; no postponement or delay currently anticipated unless uncertain geopolitical situation aggravates and impacts cash flow.

Decision on next clinker line: company may not wait until full Jaisalmer commissioning; a call could be taken closer to commissioning, likely by end of this fiscal or beginning of last quarter of FY27, after assessing balance sheet position.
In order of priority, the next expansion after Jaisalmer is expected to be Muddapur.
Saifco expansion timing beyond FY28 is not yet clear; company wants to first fully utilize existing capacity, secure approvals, and ensure existing business is profitable before planning further.

subsections.label: Maintenance shutdown
points: Q1 FY27 maintenance shutdown at kiln was a planned pre-ponement (not a sudden/forced shutdown), driven by early detection of a 'red spot' requiring maintenance ahead of schedule; kiln maintenance timing can typically vary by 1 to 1.5 months.

No volume loss occurred due to the maintenance because the company had a huge clinker stock; some minimal clinker purchase was made for the South plant due to maintenance, but this was a minimal quantity.
18% combined volume growth would not have been possible if the shutdown had been an unplanned/forced shutdown.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: Central India (including new capacity such as the Bihar grinding unit) is the primary driver of volume growth this quarter.
Company gained certain market share in Central India across major regions.
Company maintained (did not necessarily gain) market share in North and South regions.
Regional profitability and utilization levels are not shared/disclosed separately by management, other than confirming North/South operating near 85-90% effective capacity.

subsections.label: UAE / GCC white cement geography
points: White cement sales currently restricted to GCC countries only due to inability to secure shipping/loading for exports to other regions amid the Middle East geopolitical situation.
UAE region lost about 50% of normal white cement volume in Q1 due to these restrictions, impacting consolidated white cement growth potential for the year.

subsections.label: Fuel sourcing by region
points: Central India plants consume only domestic (Indian) coal; no petcoke or imported fuel used there.
North plants use a mix: Indian coal (where economical via rail; road movement not economical) supplemented by petcoke and alternate fuel.
South plant uses only petcoke and alternate fuel; Indian coal is not viable there and is not used at all.
Imported US coal (high calorific, cheaper at times) is used opportunistically when economics are favorable versus petcoke.
Fuel mix is not fixed and continuously evolves with geopolitical situation affecting availability and pricing; company adapts to keep fuel cost most cost-effective.

subsections.label: Cost outlook for Q2 FY27
points: Packaging cost expected to be flat to marginally lower in Q2 versus Q1.
Fuel cost expected to increase ~INR75-100/ton in Q2, expected to peak in Q2 before declining thereafter under current fuel environment.

Maintenance cost in Q2 expected to be similar to Q1, maybe marginally lower, as some kiln maintenance is still pending and will be taken up in Q2; this component is separate/not linked to the INR150 variable cost increase guidance.
Operating deleverage impact (over and above the INR150/ton cost guidance) is expected in Q2 due to lower sequential volumes from seasonality.
Railway bulk freight discount benefit is limited only to North plants (where rail facilities exist); Central India and South plant logistics are entirely by road.

Consolidated raw material cost per ton appears higher partly because consolidated numbers include dry-mix mortar business (UAE), which raises raw material cost without a corresponding volume addition to the dividing factor.
In Fujairah (UAE), freight costs increased because dispatch was limited to GCC region sales only; dry-mix mortar business is local and has no freight cost impact.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: Company aims to grow profitably rather than chase aggressive top-line growth, prioritizing long-term brand and market position establishment, especially as most incremental volume comes from Central India.
Some competitor imports (clinker/cement) have started entering the UAE/India white cement market but not yet at normal pre-disruption quantities.

subsections.label: Coal block operationalization
points: Company has two coal blocks; the larger one at Mahan has made good progress and is expected to start yielding coal by end of FY28.
The second (smaller) coal block is expected to follow roughly one year later.
Company has the option to sell fuel externally from these coal blocks and will evaluate strategy for coal sales as it progresses.

Key benefit expected: substantial reduction in fuel-related risk exposure, since domestic linkage coal is cheapest but supply-constrained (especially impacting North plants); own coal block output expected to be cheaper than market-available domestic coal.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and cost risks
points: Ongoing geopolitical situation (Middle East) has affected fuel (petcoke, imported coal) pricing and availability, and has disrupted shipping/loading for white cement exports from UAE to non-GCC regions.

Potential risk to expansion timeline: if the geopolitical situation aggravates and impacts cash flow, there could be some delay to the next phase of capacity expansion, though currently no postponement is anticipated.
Green power capacity ramp-up has faced delays due to state-level approval delays for group power housing (solar), resulting in lower-than-expected green power contribution so far.
Thermal substitution rate target (35% by FY30) needs to be reworked because the original target was based on existing capacities before recent expansions and changes in fuel mix by location.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Management reiterated no plans to reschedule or delay the 40-million-ton (FY28) and 50-million-ton (2030) capacity roadmap, unlike some competitors pulling back on expansion.

Grey cement volume growth for FY27 confirmed to be double-digit, though overall pace may moderate versus Q1 due to capacity constraints in North and South; annual volume guidance is revised quarter to quarter.
Consolidated white cement volume growth may not reach double digits for the year due to the ~50% loss of normal UAE volume in H1 from geopolitical disruptions.
Green power target of 75% by FY30 reaffirmed as achievable, despite recent delays from state-level solar approvals; pace of improvement expected to pick up to 4-5% annually from next year.
Thermal substitution target of 35% by FY30 is being reworked to reflect revised fuel mix due to expansions and plant locations not originally considered when the target was set.

Next phase of capacity expansion decision timing not yet finalized; likely decision point around Jaisalmer's commissioning timeline (by end of FY27 or early Q4 FY27), pending Board approval and balance sheet assessment.
Coal block at Mahan expected to start yielding coal by end of FY28, with associated cost savings and reduced fuel risk exposure expected thereafter; second coal block about a year behind.

guidance_ledger.statement: Plan is closer to 22.5 to 23 million tons in this year for grey volumes.
We will definitely be growing double digit; growth restricted in North/South due to capacity limitation, major volume from Central India.
On a console basis in white, double digit may not be possible because of ~50% volume loss in UAE in H1 due to geopolitical restrictions.
As of now we have no plans [to delay]. We are on schedule. 40 million is already in progress.
Keeping our target for 2030, we shall be putting up before the Board for approval at an appropriate time.

guidance_ledger.metric: Q2 FY27 cost increase per ton
guidance_ledger.statement: Cost should go up by about INR150 a ton in Q2 as compared to Q1, mainly fuel and diesel related.
Fuel cost should definitely see an increase of around INR75 to INR100 per ton in Q2.
Fuel cost per kcal could be around 1.75 or something closer to that, versus 1.53 in Q1, expected to peak in Q2 and decline thereafter.
Q2 would have similar maintenance cost, maybe marginally lower than Q1; some kiln maintenance still pending will be taken up in Q2.
Packaging cost should be more or less flat or marginally lower in Q2 vis-à-vis Q1.

key_takeaways: During this quarter, we saw a good growth in the grey business, year-on-year 19% growth in volumes... and even though vis-à-vis previous quarter it was marginally lower by 2%.

Also, if we see the white business, year-on-year there is a growth of 11% in volumes, marginally lower by 5% Q-on-Q, and the combined growth in volumes was 18% year-on-year and marginal 3% down quarter-on-quarter.

As a result of this, the net sale during this quarter was higher by 23% year-on-year at INR3,786 crores as compared to INR3,068 crores... which was mainly on account of the product mix and some price improvement.

The EBITDA during this quarter was INR639 crores, this is the standalone position, vis-à-vis INR673 crores in the previous year and INR670 crores in the previous quarter. The EBITDA margins was 16.9% in this quarter, previous quarter 18.5%, and previous year 21.9%.
If we look at the work on the projects, the greenfield project at Jaisalmer is progressing well and we are confident that it will get commissioned within the targeted timeframe of first half of FY28.

As far as the debt profile as on 30th June, the gross debt stood at INR5,551 crores as compared to INR5,136 crores as on 31st March... The net debt is higher at INR3,864 crores as on 30th June compared to INR3,370 crores as on 31st March.
So the cost should go up by about say INR150 in Q2 as compared to Q1... overall, you know, with diesel and everything we expect that the cost should go up by INR150 a ton.

Yes, as of now we have no plans. We are on schedule. Once the 40 million is already in progress and immediately we shall -- we are already working out on the next phase of expansion...keeping our target for 2030.

quarters.summary: JK Cement expects continued double-digit volume growth in FY27 (incremental ~2.5 million tons or more) with industry growing 6-8%, driven by capacity commissioning at Jaisalmer/Bikaner/Punjab (H1 FY28) and Nathdwara Wall Putty plant (September). Management remains confident on the 50-million-ton capacity roadmap by FY30 despite rising competitive intensity in Central and Rajasthan markets, though cost pressures from geopolitical situation (fuel, diesel) and moderating incentive income are headwinds; paints business expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27 on higher revenue.

subsections.label: Employee expense drivers
points: Commissioning of new plant in Central India led to salaries earlier capitalized moving to revenue expense.
Increased business requirement led to additional manpower requirement.
Normal annual increments had an impact.
Labor Code impact during the year was provided in this quarter.
One-time liability pertaining to leave travel assistance was provided in this quarter.

Management expects ~INR250 crores sustainable quarterly run rate; annual increment effective 1st April is ~10%; expects full year employee cost to rise 12%-14% YoY from INR937 crores base, partly due to Nathdwara plant commissioning in September requiring additional manpower.

subsections.label: Other expenses drivers
points: Other expenses increased due to higher business volumes, including packing costs, stores and spares, and variable selling expenses.
Increase also due to investment in branding for both gray and white cement businesses amid current market conditions, incremental ~INR50-60 crores.

subsections.label: Incentive income
points: Incentive income lower than earlier guidance of ~INR75 crores due to Aligarh unit exhausting its full 10-year incentive eligibility.
Rajasthan incentive not being availed because GST input credit is claimed instead (input credit received immediately, cannot claim both).
Q4 incentive accrued was INR29 crores; outstanding incentive receivable as on 31 March was ~INR300 crores.
Full year FY26 incentive was ~INR230 crores; FY27 incentive expected to be ~INR250-260 crores.
Bihar incentive not yet accrued pending sanction letter from state government; will be accrued (from back date) only after sanction letter received, per prudent accounting policy.
Incentives from other grinding units (Prayagraj, Hamirpur, etc.) expected going forward.
Incentive run rate may increase further in FY28 if quarterly run rate reaches INR70-75 crores, potentially reaching ~INR300 crores for FY28.

subsections.label: Capex plans
points: FY27 capex guidance of INR3,500-4,000 crores includes normal capex, Wall Putty plant capex, solar tie-up investments, Saifco/paints investments, and coal block investment — NOT the Jaisalmer expansion specifically as a separate line; out of this, normal capex is expected to be INR800-1,000 crores with balance on greenfield expansion.

FY28 capex guidance of INR1,500-2,000 crores is based only on commitments as on date; next expansion (after Jaisalmer) is on the cards but capex commitment will only be given once approved by the Board.

subsections.label: Panna project cost savings
points: Panna project has some spillover capex/expenditure remaining related to railway siding.
Out of the announced INR2,850 crores project cost, expected savings of at least INR200-250 crores, potentially up to INR300 crores, resulting in project completion at lower cost.

subsections.label: Cash balance
points: Standalone and consolidated cash balances are the same because subsidiaries (Saifco and Fujairah) hold hardly any cash balance.

key_figures.label: Consolidated White Cement volume growth expectation

subsections.label: Paints business
points: Paints revenue for FY26 was INR380 crores with an EBITDA loss of INR40+ crores.
FY27 revenue expected at INR500-550 crores (full year number, not exit run rate) with EBITDA expected to be positive/breakeven on the way, driven by improvement in gross margins and other factors.

subsections.label: White Cement / Wall Putty
points: White Cement was previously fed to certain South regions from UAE (Fujairah) plant as it was more economical; due to present geopolitical situation, this is now being fed from the Gotan plant instead — company does not expect to lose White Cement market share.
Prices for both White Cement and Wall Putty have been increased due to substantial increase in chemical input costs, with efforts to pass on cost increases to customers.

White Cement profitability (EBITDA per ton, including putty) not shared separately from gray cement; industry-wide White Cement profitability has been declining due to increased competition, but management expects it should not further reduce going forward.

subsections.label: Fuel mix and cost
points: Q4 fuel mix based on heat value: ~50% petcoke, 12% alternate fuels (AFR), balance Indian coal.
