themes.label: Asset quality recovery
themes.note: Collection efficiency metrics (98.1% unique customer, 99.3% x-bucket) at best-ever levels, current bucket proportion improved for first time in quarters, signaling worst is behind.

themes.label: Growth re-acceleration
themes.note: Disbursements up 24% QoQ in Q4; company guiding ~20% AUM growth for FY27 after 11% growth in FY26.

themes.label: Credit cost normalization
themes.note: FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7-1.75% (down from Q4 actual 1.88%) but steady-state guidance of 1.5-1.6% is structurally higher than pre-crisis levels (~1.3-1.35% AUM-equivalent).

themes.label: Diversified/cost-effective funding
themes.note: Raised $100mn from ADB reinforcing lender confidence, though hedging costs raised incremental borrowing cost this quarter; overall cost of funds continuing to decline YoY.

themes.label: Organizational restructuring (business-collections split)
themes.note: Business and collection verticals fully separated from April 1, 2026 to sharpen focus on new business origination and DPD stabilization respectively.

themes.label: Ticket size / sweet-spot strategy
themes.note: Average ticket size moved from 3.5 lakh to 4.2 lakh but company reiterates no major structural shift beyond its INR3-5 lakh sweet spot, with over 50% of AUM still in that band.

themes.label: Geopolitical/macro risk monitoring
themes.note: No material impact seen from West Asia conflict on customer segment or liquidity so far, but flagged as an ongoing monitorable affecting borrowing costs and asset quality outlook.

key_takeaways: We have just completed one of the most challenging years for Five-Star. The asset quality headwinds faced by MFIs and unsecured loan lenders over the last couple of years creeped into the portfolios of secured loan lenders also, especially those providing small ticket loans.

For the quarter ended March 31, 2026, we clocked a unique customer collection efficiency of 98.1%, which is one of our best in the history of Five-Star. Our x-bucket collections for the quarter came in at 99.3%.
The current proportion of customers who are in current buckets has moved up by close to 1% from 81.77% in Q3 to 82.69% in Q4.

Our disbursement for the quarter came in at INR1,213 crores, an increase of 24% over the previous quarter. Our disbursement for the full year came in at INR4,675 crores, which has allowed us to clock a portfolio growth of 11% even during a challenging year.
We raised $100 million from Asian Development Bank, ADB... during this quarter, which is a reinforcement of lenders' belief in Five-Star.

For the quarter, we achieved a PAT of INR269 crores, while this is 3% lower as compared to the previous quarter on account of higher personal expense... for the full year we grew even in such a challenging year by 2%, and we clocked a full year PAT of INR1,099 crores. Our return on average AUM and return on equity for the financial year 2026 remains healthy at 8.68% and 16%, respectively.
There was a senior management exit during this year, but I want to clearly lay down the fact this has no impact on our performance.
We are geared up to get back on the track of growth and well-poised to achieve AUM growth of around 20% for the financial year 2027.
pressing_questions: Kunal Thanvi: structurally, we have been saying the business is -- because of the lower base and opportunity, 25% was the growth number that we've been giving for last two, three years. Now in one of the comments, Srikanth mentioned that we'll be growing at 18% to 20% over next three years. So, is it fair to assume that structurally our growth rates would be lower, compared to what we had anticipated say three years back, two to three years back?

Chandrasekhar Sridhar: asset quality is beginning to improve, but you're still holding on to somewhat similar credit cost level. Is this because we're trying to up the coverage on some of the lower stages? ...our Stage-2 coverage is lower than what the RBI prescription itself is?

Aravind Ravichandran: given our steady-state credit cost itself, we are looking at a slightly higher [level] than what we had initially anticipated. Should we relook at our pricing also... in terms of revising upwards pricing?

quarters.summary: Q1FY27 revenue grew 16.3% YoY driven primarily by commercial CMS projects, with EBITDA margin at 35.5% aided by operating leverage and favorable customer mix. Management reiterated its long-standing aspiration of ~20% growth for FY27 and FY28, cautioned against reading too much into single-quarter performance given inherent business lumpiness, and highlighted new peptide facility commissioning, the Gland Pharma sterile API collaboration, and continued capex acceleration as key pillars of the medium-term growth story.

key_figures.label: Of which earmarked for strategic growth (Unit 1 capacity expansion)

subsections.label: Revenue drivers
points: Commercial CMS projects contributed a majority share of the revenue and were the primary drivers of growth during the quarter.
The quarter also witnessed healthy execution across the project portfolio and customer programs.

Quarterly revenue performance was broadly in line with expectations; management reiterated the inherent uneven nature of the business and the need to assess performance over a longer period rather than a single quarter.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Higher revenue base, operating leverage and favorable customer mix contributed to the profitability profile during the quarter.
Gross margin improvement was again a function of business mix during the quarter; gross margin includes manufacturing expenses and other costs directly attributable to the product.

subsections.label: Working capital and capex
points: Working capital days improved from 137 days at end of FY26 to 84 days in FY27; optimal utilization of cash remains a key priority, with continued focus on inventory optimization, disciplined execution and strengthening cash conversion.
Capex outflow of INR121.6 crores in Q1FY27 was primarily driven by new R&D and peptide facilities.
New capital investments of ~INR203 crores approved during the quarter, of which INR196 crores earmarked for strategic growth initiatives largely related to capacity expansion at Unit 1.
Against total approved capex of INR1,460 crores over the last 13 quarters, INR870 crores has been spent to date, with the balance committed towards projects under implementation.

subsections.label: Geopolitical monitoring
points: Company continues to closely monitor the evolving geopolitical environment and broader global trade developments; no material impact experienced on operations or supply chain continuity of customer commitments thus far, but remains vigilant.

subsections.label: Transcript clarification
points: CFO clarified a prior question about alleged manipulation of the transcript; earnings calls are recorded and full unedited audio is published on the website; the written transcript is prepared by an external agency and lightly edited for readability; on review, no change was found in the referenced section, though the company acknowledged missing a minor editing mistake.

subsections.label: CMS business
points: Most CMS revenues this quarter came from top commercial products.
Order book from pipeline molecules is encouraging and expected to pan out over the next few quarters.

Healthy engagement continues across both development and commercial programs; depth of customer conversations is significantly stronger than a few years ago, with discussions increasingly capability-led rather than individual-project-based.

A handful of molecules (about 3) are driving most of CMS commercial growth; these are produced every quarter with a fairly healthy future expected over the next 5 to 6 years; there is lumpiness in ordering but no one-off/exceptional contributions.
Expect one more commercialization this year, and possibly one or two more next year, which would add diversity to the molecule mix.
CMS commercial revenue growth over the next 2-3 years will continue to be driven predominantly by the existing handful of molecules while new projects are being added.

subsections.label: GDS business
points: GDS business performance was supported by a number of products that performed well and contributed meaningfully, including Ezetimibe, Mirtazapine, Escitalopram and Aripiprazole, reflecting portfolio strength built over time.
GDS strategic direction continues to evolve, focused on expanding the portfolio of differentiated products while increasing presence in key markets like Brazil, Japan, South Korea and Turkey.
Company has initiated pursuit of life cycle management opportunities with innovators where its process chemistry, development experience and manufacturing capabilities can create long-term value.

subsections.label: Development revenue vs commercial revenue
points: Development revenue is separated from commercial revenue in disclosures specifically so analysts/investors can identify the recurring part of the business; commercial revenue trend is the intended long-term indicator.

Development revenues are product-specific and driven by launch quantities; large NCE launch shipments (10-20 tons) over a multi-quarter period have historically driven development revenue as high as INR200 crores, while other periods see only ~INR50 crores when customers order smaller launch quantities.
No change in approach to selecting development products; large development revenue swings are due to customer-specific launch strategies, not a shift in product selection criteria.
Development pipeline quality is described as continuing to improve, though quantifying pipeline revenue for the current year is considered premature.

At least two new projects have come into the pipeline in FY27, fairly advanced in the clinic (not yet commercial), including some peptide projects not previously visualized a year ago; management is cautious about quantifying their revenue impact for the year but expects them to pave the way for larger volumes in the future.

subsections.label: Historical development revenue context
points: FY26 development revenue was approximately INR90-odd crores, compared to historically higher absolute levels in FY24 and earlier years.

subsections.label: Peptides
points: Peptide process development capabilities have been built over 15+ years; a decision was made ~2 years ago to invest in commercial-scale peptide manufacturing based on conviction of the segment's long-term attractiveness.

Even before the peptide manufacturing asset is fully ramped up, customer interest continues to grow, with expanded discussions and encouraging conversion of opportunities providing greater visibility around Module 1 utilization.
Peptide plant is set to be commissioned next month, with manufacturing qualification to follow; multiple projects are lined up at various stages.

The plant is located within an FDA-approved manufacturing site, but as a new building it will be subject to an FDA audit dependent on how the FDA views the filing; this is not seen as a gating issue given the site's existing approval status.
Order book visibility exists for the new peptide facility even before commissioning, with a couple of projects ready to use it.

subsections.label: R&D and capability investments
points: Investment velocity across the company has increased meaningfully over the last 3 years and into FY27, spanning manufacturing infrastructure, R&D capabilities, peptides, sterile APIs and future capacity expansion, all made with a long-term perspective to remain relevant and competitive as customer requirements evolve.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion / land acquisition
points: Approved capex includes ~INR196 crores earmarked largely for capacity expansion at Unit 1.

Acquisition of adjacent land (6-7 acres) at Unit 1 is a short-to-medium-term convenient strategy to amalgamate land into an existing site, easing FDA approvals and environmental clearances without triggering a greenfield approval cycle.

Company currently operates 3 manufacturing sites; longer-term plans involve additional manufacturing sites with larger headroom for capacity, requiring possession of larger industrial land parcels; this should be expected from the company in the near future.
Adjacent land acquisition strategy is described as only a short-term opportunistic move to ensure comfortable servicing of customer needs over the next 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Future capex direction
points: Next phase of investment is expected to differ both quantitatively (higher overall capex than deployed so far) and qualitatively (new modalities) from past capex cycles.

Company operates at the convergence of GMP and complex chemistry, focusing on complex APIs rather than nonhuman health or starting materials/KSMs; future growth is expected to require presence in newer, more complex modalities.

Qualitative progression may include geographic diversification, potentially via M&A or organic overseas investments, since building infrastructure for more complex modalities may not make strategic/economic sense solely in India.

These moves may not be large individual bets but will be qualitatively different, representing meaningful progression expected over the next 1-2 years, alongside continued conventional organic investment in infrastructure, R&D, manufacturing and complex molecules.

subsections.label: Gland Pharma sterile API collaboration
points: Strategic collaboration announced with Gland Pharma to create a differentiated platform in sterile APIs by combining complementary strengths of both organizations.
Collaboration demonstrates commitment to the specialty GDS business and strategy of building niche capabilities in areas where technical complexity creates meaningful differentiation.

Gland has established sterile (aseptic) manufacturing capabilities that are not widely prevalent globally, with very few players; Neuland brings complex API development and process expertise, including complex sterilization process development.
The companies do not compete with each other; Gland is strong in managing sterile products while Neuland avoids the risks of managing sterile facilities directly.
Arrangement is asset-light for Neuland, allowing reliance on the partnership without creating and managing a sterile manufacturing asset.

Collaboration currently covers products in the niche generic category (not the prime category); management sees a long runway and opportunity for collaborating on more products beyond the initial set.

subsections.label: Relationship/account strategy
points: Increasing emphasis across the CMS business on becoming a long-term strategic partner to customers (platform partner working on a set of programs) rather than being viewed as a provider for individual projects.
Customer discussions increasingly center on capabilities, supply assurance, technical expertise and long-term collaboration rather than individual projects.

Confidence in monetizing these relationships stems from qualitative, substantiated conversations with known accounts (companies worked with for 3-10 years) now discussing increasing their total business/exposure to Neuland.

Illustrative scale shift: 5 years ago the largest visualized molecule opportunity was ~INR50 crores/year; today opportunities of INR500 crores/year or even INR1,000 crores/year per molecule can be visualized, though not every engagement reaches that scale.
This growing opportunity value is informing a more bold capex investment approach over the next 2-3 years.

subsections.label: Geopolitical and macro monitoring
points: Company continues to closely monitor evolving geopolitical environment and broader global trade developments; no material impact experienced thus far on operations, supply chain continuity or customer commitments, but remains vigilant and focused on business continuity, customer service and proactive risk management.

Business operates in a dynamic environment where geopolitical developments, regulatory timelines, customer ordering patterns and broader macroeconomic conditions can influence the timing and shape of quarter-to-quarter growth.

subsections.label: Business volatility
points: Variability remains an inherent characteristic of the business; quarterly performance should be viewed in that context rather than in isolation.

CMS commercial revenue is driven by a handful of molecules and is therefore subject to volatility/lumpiness, though no one-off or exceptional contributions or destocking risk is currently seen for FY27.
Q4FY26 was flagged as an exceptionally inflated quarter (effectively a Q3 spillover into Q4), making sequential Q4-to-Q1 comparisons not meaningful.

subsections.label: FDA audit consideration for peptide facility
points: New peptide facility building, though located within an FDA-approved site, will be subject to a future FDA audit dependent on the nature of the filing; not viewed as a gating issue given the site's existing approval.

subsections.label: Growth outlook
points: Management has always aspired to grow at about 20%, and expects FY27 and FY28 to also grow that way; declined to give a more specific growth rate indication for FY27, noting they had cautioned in the past when a year (FY25) was expected to be flattish and that turned out accurate, but is not giving such an indication currently.

Outlook considering the FY27-FY28 period remains in line with long-term ambitions; customer interest, opportunities under discussion, capabilities coming online and investments made across the businesses reinforce confidence in medium-term trajectory.

No destocking risk currently seen for FY27 commercial contracts; order visibility is consistent with commentary and factors in stocking/destocking dynamics; any such effects are expected to potentially play out beyond FY27.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Company has historically guided to ~25% EBITDA margin as a conservative benchmark and has been pleased to exceed it, aided partly by favorable exchange rates; 25%+ remains the long-term expectation, with anything above considered a bonus.
Margin profile expected to remain healthy given a divergent mix of higher- and lower-margin molecules; average profile will be determined by mix.

subsections.label: ROCE outlook
points: 3-year ROCE is currently healthy but may dip as the company enters an expansion mode requiring more capital deployment and longer gestation periods; guardrails will be maintained; a dip in ROCE is expected but not necessarily a dip in margins.

subsections.label: Development revenue outlook
points: Development revenue is expected to go up this year and is expected to lead to commercial revenue, though not necessarily substantial commercial contribution in FY27; from FY28 onwards, more molecules are expected to start contributing to commercial revenue.

subsections.label: Peptide commercialization outlook
points: One commercialization from peptides remains expected this year, with possibly one or two more next year (in line with prior quarter's stated expectation).

subsections.label: Formal guidance policy
points: Company reiterated it does not intend to give formal quarterly/annual guidance, focusing instead on broader directional commentary.

subsections.label: Stock split/bonus
points: Shareholders have raised the question of a stock split/bonus, including at the Annual Shareholders' Meeting; this is a Board matter and management will take the suggestion to the Board to discuss all elements surrounding such a decision.

themes.label: Business unevenness / lumpiness

themes.label: Gross margin volatility / product mix

themes.label: CMS/CDMO ramp-up
themes.note: CMS commercial revenue driven by a handful of molecules is scaling well, with order book from pipeline molecules encouraging and deeper capability-led customer engagement.

themes.label: Peptide capex and innovator traction
themes.note: Peptide plant commissioning expected next month, with multiple projects lined up and growing customer interest even before ramp-up, validating the ~2-year-old investment thesis.

themes.label: Working capital and inventory build
themes.note: Working capital days improved sharply from 137 days at FY26 end to 84 days in Q1FY27, reflecting focus on inventory optimization and cash conversion.

themes.label: Long-term growth aspiration

themes.label: Trade policy / tariff overhang
themes.note: Company continues to closely monitor the evolving geopolitical environment and global trade developments, with no material impact experienced on operations or supply chain thus far.

key_takeaways: Total income for Q1FY27 was INR650.1 crores vs INR300.6 crores in Q1FY26, a growth of 16.3%, with commercial CMS projects contributing a majority share of revenue and being the primary drivers of growth.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR231.1 crores with an EBITDA margin of 35.5%, aided by higher revenue base, operating leverage and favorable customer mix.
Gross margin for the quarter was 61.2% versus 55.3% in Q1FY26, a function of business mix.
Profit after tax stood at INR147.4 crores versus INR13.7 crores in Q1FY26; EPS was INR114.9 per share.
Working capital days improved from 137 days at the end of FY26 to 84 days in FY27.

Capex outflow of INR121.6 crores in Q1FY27, primarily driven by new R&D and peptide facilities; new capital investments of ~INR203 crores approved during the quarter, largely for Unit 1 capacity expansion; against total approved capex of INR1,460 crores over the last 13 quarters, INR870 crores has been spent to date.
Management reiterated its aspiration to grow at about 20% and expects FY27 & FY28 to grow that way, while declining to give specific FY27 growth guidance.

Strategic collaboration announced with Gland Pharma to create a differentiated platform in sterile APIs, combining Gland's sterile/aseptic manufacturing strengths with Neuland's complex API capabilities, in an asset-light arrangement for Neuland.
Peptide manufacturing plant is set to be commissioned next month, with multiple projects already lined up at various stages even before commissioning.
pressing_questions: Do we feel that this margin profile is peak, particularly if we see in terms of product mix in analyzed manner? Or still we have more scope of operating leverage with CMS expected? How would you try to attract people in CMS or GDS because it's a vast TAM.

Apart from 6, 7 acres adjacent land that we have acquired at Unit 1, we haven't heard anything else on that front. So, some color on where we are on this. Once we are done with this exercise, how much adjacent land would be able to acquire and within what time line?
Are we looking at any stock split or bonus because that question has been asked in several con calls, but never answered.

quarters.summary: Q4FY26 delivered record revenue and margins driven by commercial CMS ramp-up and favourable currency; FY26 growth came in as expected (strong vs FY24). Management does not give formal guidance but reiterates a long-term aspiration of 18-20% CAGR (not linear), expects continued quarter-to-quarter lumpiness over the next 2-3 years, and flags that ROCE/margins will moderate as the company enters longer, larger capital deployment cycles (peptide facility on track for July commissioning; new R&D center planned). Working capital days and inventory/receivables build are expected to normalize in FY27.

subsections.label: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Commercial CMS projects drove growth, with CMS contributing over two thirds of revenue this quarter.
Gross margin improvement driven largely by business mix.
Higher freight cost was managed towards the end of the quarter due to the conflict, while ensuring continuity of supply to customers.
Gross margin includes manufacturing expenses and other costs directly attributable to the product.

Exceptional Q4 operating margin reflects the record high revenue this quarter and is also partly a function of the uneven nature of revenue flows; should not be seen as an indicator of future performance.

subsections.label: Cash flow, working capital and capital allocation
points: Negative free cash flow in FY26 was driven primarily by higher working capital during the year, along with increased capital cash outflows.
Working capital days rise mainly driven by higher inventories and receivables; expected to normalize in FY27.
Approach to capex remains disciplined, phased, aligned with strategic priorities and executed with focus on returns and long-term capability building.
Priority is to ensure approved capex translates into clear execution milestones and business outcomes.
Balance sheet remains resilient with comfortable liquidity; focus on preserving flexibility to support growth investments and operational resilience.

Sharply focused on improving cash conversion; working capital discipline remains a management priority via actions on collections, inventory normalization and tighter controls so profitability translates into cash flows more consistently.

Cost and process improvements seen as a structural enabler for sustainable profitability and stronger cash generation — includes tighter cost governance, procurement efficiency actions and operating discipline across functions aimed at protecting margins, improving predictability and building a scalable operating model.
Closely tracking raw material coverage and price volatility given recent Middle East developments, and taking actions to protect continuity of supplies and manage cost pressures.

subsections.label: Margins and returns outlook
points: FY26 benefited from favorable exchange rate movements.

ROCE remains healthy but is expected to moderate as the company enters longer capital deployment cycles; management is comfortable with this as long as investments strengthen the long-term growth engine and competitive positioning.
Company tends to budget conservatively on exchange rates, raw material pricing and volumes, so margins tend to play out better than expected.

subsections.label: Demand and pipeline visibility
points: In the short to medium term, business visibility continues to be anchored by commercial and near-commercial molecules, giving strong confidence over the next few years.
Growth over the next 2 to 3 years is visible, driven by existing pipeline, while groundwork is being laid for growth beyond this horizon.

Business development efforts over the last year focused on improving quality and maturity of opportunities entering the pipeline; encouraging traction across customer segments including increasing engagement on larger and more complex programs.

Conversion timelines in the industry remain long and non-linear; objective is to prioritize sustainable, high-quality growth opportunities even if that means being selective and patient in the near term.
Growth is expected to remain lumpy over the next 2-3 years; not every quarter will show progression, but a clear trend line should emerge over a longer horizon (10-12 quarters).

PE/VC biotech funding decline (per S&P Global data since 2021) has affected mainly early discovery-phase molecules; Neuland's growth is driven more by molecules in close-to-commercial and clinical phases (from IND filing/Phase I onwards), which continue to show good visibility irrespective of funding environment.

subsections.label: CMS/CDMO business drivers
points: Growth in the CDMO business driven by ramp-up of volumes of previously commercialized products plus contribution from one new commercialization this year.
Currency depreciation contributed to growth given a strong Q4 with a lot of shipments happening as the rupee depreciated, though this does not take away from inherent business growth.

Newer molecules continue to enter the pipeline; company is looking at one commercialization in FY27 and maybe 1-2 more later, though these do not come in at a quantum that changes the growth trajectory.

GDS business was softer in FY26, though good growth potential is seen ahead; substantial resources deployed across development, customer engagement and capability building to support growth in short, medium and long term.

subsections.label: R&D and new R&D center
points: New R&D center will be an important step up in ability to support complex programs across development stages; will strengthen scientific depth, enhance cross-functional collaboration and improve ability to scale customer programs from early development through commercialization.

Investment is not just about capacity addition but about building technical and problem-solving capability to engage earlier and more meaningfully with customers and support larger, more complex programs.

subsections.label: Peptide capability and pipeline
points: Company has invested close to 16-18 years in the peptide space, moving organically from fragments/building blocks/unnatural amino acid-based fragments up the value chain to peptide APIs.
Biggest strength is extensive in-house process development for peptides (process chemistry, not medicinal chemistry) — an important skill set for engaging with clinical-stage peptide APIs.
Close to 8-10 peptide programs in the development pipeline across various therapeutic indications, at differing stages of advancement (some advanced, some early-stage).

The recently announced peptide contract/partnership referenced by an analyst is a very early-stage program; management would not associate near/mid-term revenue with it — will take at least a few years to reach commercial benefit.
Programs expected to be commercialized in Neuland's peptide facility are largely not publicly disclosed.

Peptide CDMO opportunity (estimated at USD 5-6 billion) viewed as more attractive than oligonucleotide or RNAi-based therapy CDMO opportunities because oligos have not reached similar scale; ADCs viewed as a different, more complex category (biologics + small molecule tethered via peptide linker) that could be a future adjacency, potentially reached via peptide-linker capability or strategic acquisitions.

Synthetic chemistry-based techniques provide far higher scale and reliability versus biological processes long-term; advancements in synthetic chemistry (bypassing cumbersome downstream techniques like lyophilization) have enabled scale-up of peptide manufacture from ~100 kg/year (leuprolide, ~10-15 years ago) to metric-ton scale for GLP-1s today.

Company cannot make fundamental research investments itself but R&D groups follow developments closely and aim to partner with knowledge-driven organizations to make new techniques scalable; focus is on synthetic chemistry-based techniques in peptides and potentially oligos.

Peptide synthesis is considered far more complex/challenging than traditional small-molecule synthesis (peptides are long chains of amino acids, delicate, prone to folding and impurity formation if not synthesized appropriately) — this complexity drives higher value creation.

Key selling point to peptide clients is the long track record of in-house process development and now investment in manufacturing infrastructure, making it easier for clients to partner with Neuland; client engagement (e.g., with LIR Life Sciences) seen as helping broaden clientele on similar platform.

subsections.label: AI adoption
points: Company is still exploring AI use in manufacturing; a few pilots have been done in R&D and certain other operations.

Three basic areas of AI application being explored: automating repeat/redundant tasks (R&D is one such area), and in manufacturing, exploring whether AI can scan manufacturing data to help point to root causes of investigations; still early days, but company is committed to bringing AI applications meaningfully into the business.

subsections.label: Peptide facility
points: Large-scale peptide commercial facility investment will help move into a more differentiated space focused not only on peptide fragments but also peptide APIs, expanding scope and quality of opportunities.
Peptide facility remains on track to be ready by July, as per schedule, with no change in the date.

Company has project visibility for ramp-up in this facility, though not yet firm contracts, as these are early-stage/near-commercial projects; focus will first be on completing validations and qualifications (pre-commercialization) before moving into contracts.

subsections.label: Capital deployment mindset shift
points: As facilities are being utilized and the business grows in scale, capital allocation planning has become more long-term rather than tactical.

Illustration: 2-3 years ago, a production block for a CDMO molecule was built only after a long-term contract was secured, making it a comfortable investment; going forward, at ~INR2,000 crores revenue scale and growing (potentially adding INR500-1,000 crores per year), a different level of preparedness is required — creating base capacity/production blocks and being ready to engage, especially with newer clients including big pharma.

subsections.label: Raw material and freight cost management
points: Managed higher freight cost towards the end of Q4 due to the conflict, while ensuring continuity of supply to customers.
Given recent Middle East developments, company is closely tracking raw material coverage and price volatility and taking actions to protect continuity of supplies and manage cost pressures.

subsections.label: Customer engagement and key accounts
points: Over the last year, in addition to strengthening key account management structure, dedicated resources have been put in place to support larger projects across key operating functions.
This enhances ability to serve existing large customers effectively while building capability in anticipation of similar future projects, including deeper engagement with big pharma.

M&A of sponsor/customer companies (e.g., a big customer's acquisition situation referenced by an analyst) is viewed as a natural part of the CDMO business; supply agreements usually carry inherited clauses so change of ownership does not necessarily disrupt supply agreements; customers typically seek continuity of supply and security, and disruption would mainly occur only from performance problems or strategic change — no immediate risk seen from such M&A events, though outlook would be tempered if short-term challenges arise.

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: Role change between Sucheth (moving to Vice Chairman) and Saharsh (taking over as CEO/MD) effective April 1 was part of a preplanned transition.

As the business grows, the Board felt it more effective for one promoter to focus on day-to-day business operations (Saharsh, given his 19-year history building the CDMO business) and the other (Sucheth) to focus on long-term areas important to the business as it grows in size, including operating the Neuland Foundation (a new initiative), enterprise risk and sustainability — areas not previously covered by either individually.
Sucheth continues to be equally involved in the business; described as role clarity and role separation, not a substantive change in involvement.

subsections.label: Long-term strategic vision
points: Long-term growth requires an enterprising vision, decisive strategy and careful capital allocation; much current work is foundational, strengthening capabilities, scale and technical depth to attract the right opportunities over time.

Peptide capability, combined with existing small-molecule capability, seen as potential to create 'another Neuland' in scale over the next 5+ years, though timeline uncertain and dependent on how opportunities play out — drawn as an analogy to how the CMS/CDMO business itself scaled up from ~10-15% of revenues several years ago.
Outside consulting firms evaluated the peptide CDMO market opportunity before the company committed to its peptide investment.

Company views peptide + small molecule capabilities as complementary, not a shift away from small molecules; sees potential synergy ('magic') between the two, and possible future adjacency into ADCs via peptide-linker capability or strategic acquisitions.

subsections.label: Flagged risks and uncertainties
points: Industry continues to be exposed to demand variability, customer ordering patterns, regulatory timelines, geopolitical developments and supply chain volatility.
Revenue realization can be uneven given the nature of the business, and timing of project progression — particularly for complex and long-cycle programs — can vary.

As the company embarks on larger and longer duration capital deployment cycles, execution discipline becomes even more critical; delays in customer programs, changes in development priorities or shifts in market dynamics can influence both short-term performance and capital productivity.

Focus remains on building resilience through pipeline diversification, strengthening operational execution, prudent capital allocation and maintaining a strong balance sheet; these factors may create near-term variability but are not seen as altering the fundamental long-term opportunity.

Lumpiness/volatility in the business is expected to continue, driven by newer high-value molecules; older molecules tend to be less volatile, but as new molecules contribute significant value, volatility persists — this is not necessarily viewed as negative if investors are aligned on this being part of the business model.
Recent Middle East conflict-related developments have led to higher freight costs and raw material price volatility being closely tracked and managed.

Global PE/VC biotech funding has declined sharply since 2021 (per S&P Global data), mainly affecting early discovery-phase molecules; this could affect the pipeline funnel over time, though the company's near-to-medium-term focus (molecules from IND/Phase I onwards) has not been significantly impacted so far.

key_takeaways: Total income was INR788.7 crores, up 134.9% versus INR335.8 crores in the same period last year. Commercial CMS projects drove the growth with CMS contributing over two thirds of revenue this quarter.

Gross margin was 62.1% versus 56.3% in Q4FY25, driven largely by the business mix. Higher freight cost was managed towards the end of the quarter due to the conflict while ensuring continuity of supply to customers.

EBITDA stood at INR319.4 crores and a margin of 40.5%. This exceptional operating margin reflects the record high revenue this quarter, and it is also partly because of a function of the uneven nature of revenue flows and should not be seen as an indicator of future performance.

For the FY, revenue was INR2053.1 crores versus INR1,497.3 crores, a growth of 37.1%. EBITDA was INR603.4 crores versus INR342.8 crores in FY25 with FY26 EBITDA margin at 29.4% compared to 22.9% last year.

For the FY26, the free cash flow was negative at INR49.4 crores, driven primarily by higher working capital during the year, along with increased capital cash outflows. Working capital days stood at 137 days in Q4FY26 versus 107 days in Q4FY25, mainly driven by higher inventories and receivables, and we believe that this should normalize in FY27.

While we have not given formal guidance in the past that we do not intend to do so going forward, we did indicate earlier that FY26 would be a year of strong growth when viewed against FY24... this outlook was accurate.

A key element of this is our investment in large-scale peptide commercial facilities. This will help us move into a more differentiated space, focused not only on peptide fragments, but also on peptide APIs.

As we experienced in FY26, growth over the next 2 to 3 years is also expected to remain lumpy... if performance is assessed over a longer horizon, say, 10 to 12 quarters, a clear trend line should emerge consistent with the growth outlook that we have always outlined.

The role change between Sucheth and me effective April 1 was part of a preplanned transition... the Board felt it would be more effective for one of us to focus more on the day-to-day business and the other promoter to focus more in terms of the long-term.

But in the transcript, some words are changed, which has changed the essence of the question, whereas the audio on your website is crystal clear and SEBI guidelines also don't allow these changes. This looks like actual manipulation somewhere. Can you please justify this? (Management response deferred: 'I'll have to check back on what you have mentioned and then revert back to you.')

quarters.summary: Q3FY26 total income grew 11.4% YoY but gross margin and EBITDA margin declined QoQ due to product mix (absence of a high-margin CMS product and paliperidone shipment delay), plus a one-time labor code impact. Management maintains that the medium-term/2-3 year growth trajectory remains largely preordained by existing CMS/GDS products ramping up, with peptide and big-pharma engagement seen as key drivers of growth beyond 3 years; no specific numeric guidance was given for Q4/FY26.

Profit before tax (prior year, before extraordinary items)

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin was a function of the product mix within the business this quarter; includes manufacturing expenses and other costs attributed to the product.
Lower gross margins combined with increase in overheads led to lower EBITDA margin of 19% this quarter.
Overheads include an impact of INR10 crores towards labor codes in Q3FY26; without this impact EBITDA would be INR95 crores at 21% margin.

One high-margin CMS product did not ship this quarter, and paliperidone (a high-margin GDS specialty product) also did not ship due to operational issues at customer end — these two products were the major factors impacting gross margin.
CMS product margins are significantly higher than prime API/GDS product margins; rest of products were pretty consistent.

Management states this quarter's gross margin is an outlier/aberration due to product mix and a few smaller factors, not a steady representation of future margins; last two-three quarters gross margins seen as better representation.
Business believed capable of 30%+ EBITDA margin if everything favorable, sustainable at higher gross margins; FY24 ~30% EBITDA margin cited as fair representation of business capability.

subsections.label: Working capital and cash flow
points: Deterioration in working capital over last few quarters due to higher inventories and uneven order flow leading to higher receivables at quarter end.
Optimal utilization of cash remains top priority; focus on inventory optimization, accelerated customer collections, and even delivery flow.

Inventory is being ramped up ahead of expected revenue ramp-up from expanded capacities; inventory holding period expected to normalize from ~124 days (4 months) to ~90 days (3 months) over next 2-3 quarters.

Increase in PAT should be correlated with increase in inventory only insofar as inventory is being built for future sales, not as a direct profit-from-inventory-gain relationship (management pushback on analyst's inventory-gain hypothesis).
Free cash flow was restricted to negative INR9.2 crores for the year having secured substantial advances from customers.
Capex investments moving in line with plan, adjusted to deal with evolving nature of the business.

subsections.label: Overall summary
points: Q3FY26 financials in line with expectations even as it was a dip quarter-to-quarter.
Company expects FY26 to be a year of growth and remains optimistic about the future given business potential.
Remain committed to balancing growth and profitability by continuously optimizing costs and processes for long-term sustainability.

subsections.label: Order flow and lumpiness
points: Ramp-up of new production and molecules happening in a lumpy manner, with individual shipments potentially around INR100 crores or INR50 crores.
New business coming in with deliveries expected to happen over 12 to 24 months.
Larger value of individual CMS shipments as business is prospering means small changes in operational/logistical details can have big impact on a quarter's performance, affecting operating leverage.

subsections.label: Pipeline dynamics
points: Development pipeline (preclinical to Phase III) actively maintained; number of commercial molecules (9) has stagnated but value per molecule has increased significantly — first commercial CMS molecule was ~INR30 crores, now several multi-hundred crore molecules exist in CMS pipeline.
Some projects that were previously worked on became unviable, offsetting new project additions; company aims to keep the pipeline list active rather than inflate numbers.

Business development team's goals are aligned around quality of projects and customers rather than sheer count; threshold for engagement with marketplace has risen over the years (now seeking well-funded programs with reasonable chance of reaching clinic).

Company cannot foresee whether a Phase II/III drug becomes a multi-hundred-crore molecule or remains a smaller ~INR50 crores molecule; pipeline table is described as a dispassionate, lagging representation of reality, not predictive of scale.

subsections.label: Prime GDS portfolio
points: Ezetimibe and Mirtazapine continue to be key contributors for the prime GDS portfolio.

On the specialty side, Apixaban and Donepezil contributed, but there was significant impact from Paliperidone due to operational issues at the customer end causing delay in shipments — a reminder of inherent business risk.

subsections.label: CMS/CDMO business
points: Commercial CMS projects contributed to over 50% of the revenue this quarter, along with other priority sustains.
CMS business seeing good traction with a range of customers across geographies; existing portfolio doing well in terms of customer relationships.

Commercialization of a new CMS molecule occurred, with shipments in the tail end of the quarter, though a lot remains to be shipped; expected to be a continuous, growing business into Q4 and next year, though revenue contribution this quarter was small.

Additional volume capacity expansion for a CMS product (in Unit 3) has been successfully completed and ramp-up has started, with volumes shipped in Q3; ramp-up still very early and expected to take another one or two quarters to pick up.

subsections.label: Peptide capability and R&D investment
points: Traction on the peptide side of the business, with customers keen to work with Neuland across the life cycle of products from process design to commercial manufacturing.
At least 5 or 6 innovators have come into Neuland this year with peptide projects underway in development, though still very early stage without revenue certainty.
It would be ideal for Neuland in FY27 to secure at least one commercial manufacturing arrangement for a peptide NCE; considered very much possible and something the company is working towards.
Large peptide facility being set up will be ready for commissioning in July.
Big pharma engaging with Neuland on peptides at an early, conversation stage; peptides seen as a likely entry point to new big pharma relationships not previously familiar with Neuland.
Board approved shifting the R&D facility to a new campus in Genome Valley to build a state-of-the-art R&D center, including a modern process development/scale-up facility for peptides.
Combination of new modern peptide R&D setup with newly created large-scale peptide manufacturing capacity would create a configuration likely unmatched by many Indian CDMOs.

subsections.label: Unit 3 capacity ramp-up
points: Additional volume capacity expansion for a CMS product completed in Unit 3; ramp-up started with volumes shipped in Q3, but still very early — expected to take another one or two quarters to pick up.

Company has not yet reached the capacities it has built; ramp-up timeline and path to full capacity utilization still being uncovered, involving supply chain complexity, inventory management, product manufacturing/modification, and regulatory filings across different markets.

No fundamental problems facing the ramp-up; it is simply a matter of time to reach full production, both for the Unit 3 new facility and other CDMO molecules; CMS business expected to ramp up fairly rapidly.

subsections.label: Peptide facility
points: Large-scale peptide manufacturing capacity is being created and will be ready for commissioning in July.
New R&D campus in Genome Valley will include modern process development/scale-up facility for peptides, complementing the large-scale manufacturing capacity.

subsections.label: Trade deals impact
points: India-EU and India-U.S. trade deals discussed: EU deal reduces tariffs/fees for API import, which is traditionally borne by customers (formulators), making Indian API procurement slightly cheaper for European pharma companies and making Neuland marginally more attractive; no material change expected.

U.S. deal has no direct benefit since pharma has been exempt from tariffs all along; deal removes a bit of an overhang for the industry, but does not alleviate the potential concern about continued U.S. intent to secure domestic API manufacturing, which the company will monitor and strategize around.

subsections.label: Inventory and supply chain complexity
points: Ramp-up of new production facility involves complexity not just in supply chain (inventories and inventory management) but also product manufacturing, modification, and regulatory filings across different markets.
Even the drug product manufacturer (customer) sometimes fails to fully comprehend all these domains that need to be addressed for ramp-up.

subsections.label: Innovator engagement strategy
points: Innovators increasingly viewing Neuland as an integral partner in the innovation journey; increasing interest from a wider range of customers in Neuland's capabilities as a proven commercial NCE drug substance manufacturer and developer of robust processes for complex molecules.
Track record as an agile partner opening more possibilities and increasing share of existing business.
CDMO industry is competitive, but Neuland has carved out a space with focused strategy, building adjacencies and working with customers on cutting edge of innovation.

Engaging with innovators and biotech/big pharma to identify 'white spaces' where they need a partner like Neuland — process led to the peptide manufacturing investment identified 2-3 years ago after recognizing capacity saturation in the West amid emergence of GLP-1/amylin analogues.

Next 2-3 years focus: aggressively find partnerships in peptides to monetize the built assets; beyond that, could pursue other white spaces such as new modalities (e.g., oligonucleotide) or geographic expansion (building capabilities in the U.S. or Europe).
On generic side, customers remain keen to work with Neuland given track record and portfolio of products.

Organizational scaling needed: a team suited to handle an INR1,500-2,000 crore business may not be suited for an INR5,000-10,000 crore business; company working on upskilling and expanding teams to think from a growth perspective and deploy capital appropriately while balancing growth-capital risk.

subsections.label: Business transformation journey
points: Neuland began as a quality-focused API manufacturer over 4 decades ago; evolved over the last 15 years working with venture-backed biotech companies on NCE molecules; business now transitioned such that majority of revenues derive from human-health focused CDMO business, and company has started working with big pharma.

Historic transition (started ~2005-2006) from low-margin APIs to complex APIs/CDMO services involved two major challenges: (1) capital allocation for facility modification to accommodate Phase II/III CDMO molecules with no guaranteed return to underwrite investment, and (2) organizational/internal challenge of discontinuing low-margin, high-volume legacy products (e.g., Ranitidine, once one of the largest products) despite resistance from customers (even with 2-year notice periods) and internal teams.

GDS business mindset shift: operations team's mindspace historically dominated by GDS products even though more value comes from CMS projects; transition in planning team's outlook has been underway over the last 2 years.
Long-term strategic plan takes a longer-term view (2-3 year horizon) given natural unevenness and long gestation periods of CDMO and specialty GDS businesses.

Company aspires to decadal growth; potential for the business to grow at 20%+ CAGR from 2026 to 2036, contingent on a sequence of right plans falling into place; currently viewed as being in the early phase of the growth cycle since ramp-ups are yet to begin.

subsections.label: Flagged risk factors
points: High-risk nature of customers' attempts to bring novel therapies for unmet medical needs impacts Neuland's projections time and again.
Changing regulations and developments in underlying industries are changing business dynamics.
Performance of individual products can significantly influence overall business performance (e.g., paliperidone shipment delay due to customer-end operational issues).
Foreign exchange fluctuations, raw material cost volatility, and unforeseen geopolitical risks flagged as factors that could significantly influence business performance.
Continued U.S. intent to secure domestic API manufacturing remains a potential overhang/concern not alleviated by the India-U.S. trade deal.

Business inherently uneven and lumpy on a quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis, making quarterly performance difficult to predict or model; product-mix-related developments are very difficult to call out ahead of time.

subsections.label: Forward outlook
points: Company expects FY26 to be a year of growth and remains optimistic about future potential, though Q3 was a dip quarter-to-quarter.

Management declines to give specific guidance for Q4 or FY26, citing lumpy ramp-up (potential shipments of INR100 crores or INR50 crores) and preferring to be guarded rather than directional; suggests looking at medium-term horizon rather than quarter-on-quarter.
Growth for the next 2-3 years viewed as largely 'preordained' since products are already in place and just need to be executed, notwithstanding occasional quarterly hiccups.
Growth beyond the 3-year period will depend on newer investments such as peptide capacity, expanded wallet share with big pharma relationships, and other uncertain factors.
Company aspires to a 20%+ CAGR over the 2026-2036 decade, contingent on execution of a sequence of strategic plans.
EBITDA margins of ~25-30% (with FY24 ~30% cited) viewed as representative of business's margin capability going forward, with potential for 30%+ if conditions are favorable.

Gross margin trajectory: this quarter's dip viewed as an aberration; last 2-3 quarters seen as better representation of sustainable gross margins going forward; management declines to give a specific gross margin number/guidance.
Paliperidone-related shipment delay expected to resolve in next financial year (FY27).

guidance_ledger.statement: We expect FY '26 to be a year when we see growth and we continue to be optimistic about the future, given the potential that our business holds.
Management declined to give any specific guidance for Q4 or the remainder of FY26, citing lumpy ramp-up and requesting focus on medium-term horizon instead.
Growth for the next 2 to 3 years is kind of preordained by the fact that these products are already there, and we just need to execute.
There is a potential for a business like this to grow at 20-plus CAGR, but that requires a sequence of right plans to fall in place.

EBITDA margins that we've had in FY '24, which is around 30%, is a fair representation of the kind of margins that this business is capable of; we believe this business is capable of 30% EBITDA margin and higher if everything is in favor.

The gross margin that you've seen in this quarter is more of an outlier or an aberration; what we have seen in the last two, three quarters is perhaps a better representation of the gross margins going forward.
The ramp-up has started and volumes were shipped in Q3, but it is going to take maybe another one or two quarters to really pick up.

A lot of the additional CMS molecule remains to be shipped; going forward in Q4 and into the next year, we believe it will be a continuous business going forward, though revenue contribution this quarter is a very small component.

It would be ideal for Neuland in FY27 if we were able to secure at least 1 commercial manufacturing arrangement for a peptide NCE. That's something that is very much possible and that we are working towards.
Large peptide facility will be ready for commissioning in July.
The paliperidone shipment issue is expected to resolve next financial year.
You will see inventory days coming back to something like 90 days from the current 124 days over the next two or three quarters.

key_takeaways: Total income was INR447.8 crores, which is 11.4% YoY as compared to INR401.9 crores in the same period last year. The commercial CMS projects contributed to over 50% of the revenue and other priority sustains for this quarter.
The gross margin for the quarter was 52.1% as compared to 53.2% in Q3FY25 and was a function of the product mix within the business this quarter.

The EBITDA stood at INR85 crores at a margin of 19%. The lower gross margins this quarter, combined with the increase in overheads led to a lower EBITDA margin of 19% this quarter. The overheads include an impact of INR10 crores towards labor codes in Q3FY26. Without this impact, our EBITDA would stand at INR95 crores with a margin of 21%.
The profit before tax was INR54.3 crores as compared to INR71.8 crores in Q3FY25 before extraordinary items, which is the sale of property and the quarterly EPS stands at INR31.5 per share.
The 9-month performance shows that we have been able to maintain a 56% margin versus the same period of 55% last year.

The working capital for the quarter stood at 145 days of sales... there was a cash outflow of INR254 crores towards capex for the 9MFY26... we have been able to restrict free cash flows to negative INR9.2 crores for the year having secured substantial advances from our customers. Our net debt stood at negative INR202.6 crores.

Ezetimibe and Mirtazapine continue to be key contributors for the prime GDS portfolio. On the specialty side, we saw Apixaban, Donepezil contribute, but there was a significant impact from Paliperidone where we had some operational issues at the customer end, which has caused some sort of a delay in terms of shipments.
During the last quarter, we were able to take that significant step as our Board had approved shifting of our R&D facility to a new campus where we can build a state-of-the-art R&D center.

Only then we can achieve this 20% curve that you are indicating either of the two has to play out?

And last suggestion, because you indicated Q3 was on expected lines. And if you were aware that there is going to be a significant product mix, a qualitative callout would help given that our quarterly are very volatile, a qualitative callout will help us then outsiders. If it was on expected lines as you indicated in the beginning?
So, prima facie, it looks like whatever profits we do are due to inventory gain. So, can you please provide some clarity on these points? Or will we be seeing any write-off?

Management expects Q2 FY27 to show double-digit YoY volume growth, second half FY27 stronger than first half post-monsoon, and continues to guide for high double-digit volume growth in FY27 and coming years, with EBITDA margins sustained at 7-8% over the next 12-15 months before inching up with operating leverage from Varanasi and Window profile plant ramp-ups.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Consol EBITDA was hurt due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and fixed expenses for new business verticals.
One-offs included upfront costs linked to Varanasi plant ramp-up and additional salary costs to build a ground-level team for the Window profile (D2C) business.
Majority of the shortfall from the 7% consol EBITDA margin was attributable to inventory losses, per management's simple math explanation.
At Kisan, business-level EBITDA margin is actually 5-6%, but P&L optics were hurt by inventory losses amid PVC price volatility; margin improvement expected once volumes pick up.

subsections.label: Working capital initiatives
points: Inventory at 80 days reflects softer sales volume in the last six months; scope to rationalize as sales momentum picks up in coming quarters and by FY27-end, releasing funds at both raw material and finished goods levels.
Debtor days stable at 30, supported by cash-and-carry schemes working well in stronger markets (South and West India experience improving, cash-and-carry being gradually introduced there too).
Credit terms with suppliers expected to improve as raw material buying scale increases from Q2/Q3 onwards (following flattish volumes in FY26 and Q1 FY27), aiding further working capital release.
Company working on all three working capital levers - inventory, debtors, and creditors - to bring net working capital days down from current 45 to target of 30.

subsections.label: Funding strategy
points: Company is almost net cash; past CAPEX of Rs.500-600 crores was funded via internal cash flow and fundraise from promoters and a foreign fund.

Ongoing CAPEX is 100% expected to be funded from internal cash flow with no requirement for debt or equity raise; only if incremental funding is needed beyond internal generation would debt or equity be considered.

Return ratio math (25% ROC on Rs.5,000 crore revenue target) remains unchanged from previous call; based on gross block of ~Rs.1,500 crores, working capital of Rs.300-400 crores, and EBITDA margin of 10-12%.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Both primary and secondary demand in April were worst hit due to extreme PVC price drop of 30% in first 20 days; recovery started from May onwards.
Construction segment forms 60% of sales and is expected to be the main driver of sales momentum as monsoon recedes.

Agri demand normally strong in March/April but April suffered due to PVC price crash; some pent-up demand seen in May/June; monsoon currently slowing agri demand, with construction expected to take over as main contributor.
July trends are in line with the decent momentum seen in May and June.
Over next 15-20 days, overall demand expected to be slightly soft due to peak monsoon, before construction activity picks up strongly post-monsoon.

Distributors have been very cautious on restocking given PVC price volatility; if price stability sustains for the next 10-15 days, restocking is expected to begin, boosting overall industry sales in Q2.
Despite industry-wide volume contraction, Apollo maintained flattish volume YoY, suggesting market share gains as smaller players with weaker balance sheets struggled to absorb inventory write-downs.

subsections.label: Pricing environment
points: Minimum Import Price (MIP) applied ~12 days back at $766 per MT (~Rs.82/Kg on export basis); current Reliance price is slightly above this, and market price is 1-2% above MIP level, creating a premium.

Premium sustained despite monsoon due to low channel-partner inventories and steady demand; prices expected to remain stable to slightly downward in the coming weeks but cannot fall below the Rs.82/Kg MIP floor set by the Indian government.

PVC resin availability issue in past few days attributed mainly to extensive rains disrupting port de-stuffing, not to customs duty or MIP-related supply constraints; global availability is not a problem (material available within +/-10 days of schedule).

Following the extreme Q1 price drop, importers had been discouraged from importing resin; with market stabilization and MIP providing a price floor, importing activity is resuming, and no supply disruption is expected in the near future.

subsections.label: Product-wise performance commentary
points: CPVC grew YoY in Q1 despite flattish company-level growth; Lubrizol tie-up is showing results already, and co-branding/co-marketing activities are expected to create more visibility for both brands and house of APL Apollo; CPVC portfolio growth is expected to be a major contributor to targeted high double-digit company volume growth.
Window profile is ramping up as a direct D2C product offering, requiring additional salary/team-building costs at the ground level.
Bath fittings are kind of flattish.
Water tank is growing in double-digit.
Government infrastructure business (O-PVC or HDPE) is almost zero, one of the major drags on overall volume remaining flat.
Fittings is doing fine with single-digit growth despite tough last five quarters.
Company has stopped sharing segmental data; segment-wise growth across agri, plumbing and infra not separately disclosed given flattish overall performance.

subsections.label: Plant ramp-up and expansion
points: Varanasi plant is newly commissioned and ramping up; Q1 industry scenario is not the right barometer for its performance, but traction is being seen from Q2 onwards.
Maharashtra plant (under Kisan) continues to ramp up.
Long-term target by FY31: four large plants across India, each contributing Rs.800-1,000 crores revenue with 10%+ EBITDA margin from the PVC pipes business (piping, UPVC, CPVC, fittings).

Other products (window profiles, water tank, solvents, bath fittings) plus new additions are targeted to generate a combined Rs.1,000 crores revenue portfolio within the next four years - the long-term five-year goal for Apollo Pipes in plumbing and bath fitting.
Kisan-side rationalization: team rationalization undertaken, a few plants within Kisan shut down, focus placed on Tarapur plant to feed all of Maharashtra and neighbouring states.
Kisan brand being launched at some Apollo Pipes distributors in South and North India.

South India plant: land identification underway with some pockets already identified; land acquisition expected to be completed in FY27, with plant construction starting from Q2 of the following year; two milestones (Varanasi ramp-up and Maharashtra/Kisan plant ramp-up) are prerequisites before starting South India plant, but timeline can be fast-tracked if these plants perform better than expected.

Plant geographic positioning strategy: Secunderabad mother plant covers North; Kisan plant covers West (Maharashtra, Gujarat, partly Madhya Pradesh); Varanasi plant covers Uttar Pradesh and Bihar belt till Odisha; missing piece is a larger South India plant (small existing Bangalore plant has very limited capacity); once all four plants ramp up fully, additional satellite plants could be added if required.

subsections.label: Regional demand and distribution notes

South India identified as an attractive growth region with plans for a larger plant to cover the whole country once operational.

points: Company has already filed the scheme for merging Kisan Mouldings into Apollo Pipes at some point.

Synergies already achieved include one source of raw material and one source of managing finance and technology; however, Kisan will retain its own sales team and admin cost at the plant level as a separate brand.

subsections.label: Flagged headwinds
points: Geopolitical situation continues to disrupt global supply chain, contributing to a soft start to FY27.
High volatility in PVC resin prices in Q1 FY27, with prices falling by Rs.32/Kg in April, slightly in May, and by Rs.5/Kg again in June.
Extreme 30% price drop in first 20 days of April hurt both primary and secondary demand.
Monsoon impacting construction industry performance in near term (next 15-20 days of peak monsoon expected to soften demand further before recovery).
Recent PVC resin availability issues attributed to extensive rains at ports delaying de-stuffing of ships, not to structural supply shortage.

Government CAPEX/Nal Se Jal fund disbursement has seen some budget encouragement but no actual pickup yet; new budget allocations, disbursement of funds, new tenders and contractors is a long-driven process expected to take time - four months into FY27 with nothing concrete yet, though pickup hoped for in next 3-4 months.

Competitive intensity remains high, with smaller players facing disruption from PVC price volatility due to weaker balance sheets and margin spread, unable to absorb inventory write-downs as well as Apollo.

Kisan Mouldings historically had operating losses over the last three quarters, reflecting a weak plant, weak brand and lack of macro industry support over the last 12 months; P&L optics distorted by inventory losses despite reasonable business-level EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Overall outlook
points: Second half of FY27 expected to be much better than first half as monsoon impact eases and construction industry performs better.
Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1 FY27 on a QoQ basis, and will show double-digit growth on a YoY basis.

Company continues to maintain high double-digit volume growth guidance for FY27 and coming years, supported by Varanasi plant ramp-up, continuous ramp-up of Maharashtra plant (Kisan), and new products like Window profile starting to contribute to top line, fueling growth into FY28 and FY29.
Margins guided at 7-8% EBITDA at business level for next 12-15 months; once plants stabilize and operating leverage benefits kick in, margins expected to inch up.
PVC prices expected to remain stable in the near future given the MIP price floor of Rs.82/Kg.

guidance_ledger.statement: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 total sales volume was flat YoY.
It will be double-digit growth on YoY basis in Q2.
We are confident of high double-digit volume growth for next coming years, including FY27... we continue to maintain our high double-digit volume growth in the coming years.

At the business level, we believe that 7% to 8% EBITDA margin for the next 12 to 15-months is what we are going to achieve. Once the plants stabilize and we start getting the operating leverage benefits, then margins will start inching up.
There is always a room to improve our margins by 50 bps to 100 bps... as Varanasi plant and Window profile plant stabilize, margins will further inch up by 50-to-100 bps.
We expect that business to contribute 7% to 8% to our revenue in FY27, and gradually, it will keep on improving and maybe it will settle at around 10% as per the current capacity.
Once the current capacity gets consumed, then we will expand more capacity and the business has potential to be like 15% to the overall Apollo Pipes portfolio.
Our long-term target by FY31 is to have four large plants across India, each plant contributing Rs.800 crores to Rs.1,000 crore of revenue with 10% plus EBITDA margin from the PVC pipes business.
That portfolio in the next four years should be generating Rs.1,000 crores revenue... that is our long-term five-year goal for Apollo Pipes as a business in the plumbing and bath fitting segment.

Next leg of CAPEX requires Rs.600-700 crores put together in five years... I think 70%-80% will be met from our internal cash flows... we are 100% sure that the ongoing CAPEX will be funded from internal cash flow.
The margin profile is 10%-15%... whatever new product addition takes place, it should be like double-digit margin, and more than that, the focus is that it should generate 25% ROC.

CPVC has grown in Quarter 1 on a YoY basis despite the flattish growth for the company at a consolidated level... the CPVC portfolio growth is going to be the one major contributor [to high double-digit growth].
In both the years, the total CAPEX will be near about Rs.200 crores divided by like Rs.100 crores in each year. This will be funded from operating cash flow.

We will have a net working capital day target of 30, which right now is 45, but we are confident that there is scope of release of working capital by 10-to-15 days eventually, if not this year, but definitely by next year.
Idea is to bring debtor days to maybe 25-days, maybe by FY27-end or maybe in first half of FY28, but there is a clear visibility.
We should be able to utilize 30% of the plant in FY27, and then 50%, 60%, 70% in FY28, and then balance in FY29.
We are confident that from Quarter 2, Quarter 3, you will start seeing better volume growth [for Kisan].
Even if we make 10% to 12% EBITDA margin, which is like Rs.500 crores to Rs.600 crores broad range, so that gives like 25% ROC. That math remains same, there is no deviation from that.
Probably in FY27, this financial year, we will finish the land acquisition, and then from next year, second quarter onwards, we will start putting up the plant.
Once everything becomes one, so there could be like a 1% cost synergies, which could come at the overall company level.
We feel that the prices should remain stable in the near future [given MIP floor of Rs.82/Kg].
Targeting 35% revenue CAGR for the next 5 years, plus additional upside from allied products.
Targeting INR400 crores plus revenue for Q1 FY27.
Targeting INR8,000-10,000 per ton depending on market push/pull, with gradual improvement to INR8,500-9,000 per ton as volumes rise.
First target INR5,000-6,000 per ton on sustainable basis; eventually improving toward INR10,000 per ton as Kisan revenue ramps beyond INR500-600 crores.
Consol basis expected to move from INR6,000-8,000 per ton towards INR10,000-12,000 per ton in next 2-3 years.
Window profile business expected to contribute minimum 4-5% to construction plumbing segment revenue this year.
Targeting 3-3.5% market share in next 3-4 years, up from current 2-2.5%, assuming industry grows at 7-8%.
Net-net distributor addition expected to be 4-5% as smaller dealers are cleaned up and consolidated with larger ones; more relevant numbers to be given after ~2 quarters.
Expect inventory days to fall by 5-10 days during FY27; targeting working capital cycle below 35 days by FY27 exit, with internal target of 30 days.
Total capex requirement for FY27 estimated at near about INR100 crore, covering Kisan plant capacity expansion and brownfield expansions at existing plants.
Plan to take Kisan plant to INR1,000 crores revenue capacity with minimum 10-12% EBITDA margin via brownfield expansion (~INR50-60 crore capex).
Ultimately plan to merge Kisan Mouldings into Apollo Pipes Limited; timelines to be shared in future investor calls.
3 existing plants (North India, West India, Varanasi) targeted to reach INR1,000 crores revenue each within next 5 years.
Targeting INR1,000 crores revenue from allied products such as windows and bath fittings.

key_takeaways: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 total sales volume was flat YoY.
Both primary and secondary demand in April were worst due to extreme price drop of 30% in first 20 days, but it started to recover May onwards.
Our consol EBITDA was hurt due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and fixed expenses for our new business verticals. Our normalized business EBITDA margins were 7% on consolidated basis.
Now, the focus is to sustain EBITDA margins and increased volume in high double-digit. This will be supported by our newly commissioned Varanasi plant and continuous ramp-up of Maharashtra plant.
Looking at the current scenario, I believe the second half will be much better than the first half as the monsoon impact will be over for the construction industry to perform better.
The current MIP was applied around 12-days back and it is $766 per MT, which in Indian terms amounts to Rs.82 approximately per Kg on export basis.
In terms of volume, we are confident of high double-digit volume growth for next coming years, including FY27... We continue to maintain our high double-digit volume growth in the coming years.
At the business level, we believe that 7% to 8% EBITDA margin for the next 12 to 15-months is what we are going to achieve.

quarters.summary: Apollo Pipes reported a challenging FY26 with consol EBITDA down 30% due to inventory write-downs, aggressive pricing and new-vertical fixed costs, but management is bullish on FY27 and beyond, targeting INR400 crore+ revenue in Q1 FY27, gradual margin recovery, and a 5-year plan for 35% revenue CAGR to reach INR5,000 crores revenue by FY31, backed by capacity expansion (existing 3 plants to INR1,000 crore each, new South India plant, allied products vertical) and Group Chairman Sanjay Gupta joining the Board.
