Some provisioning still remaining for MBBL and JLG (85% provisioning bucket and portion of 70% bucket still to be recognized) over next 2 quarters.

SFBs exempted from Ind AS/ECL implementation from April 1, 2027; bank runs pro-forma Ind AS but ECL provisioning may be equal to or higher than current provisioning given last year's slippage-driven provisioning.
Net NPA target of below 1% by FY28, from ~3.3% in FY26, via recovery of past NPAs and continued provisioning over next few quarters.

subsections.label: Write-off Recovery
points: Back-of-envelope calculation of write-off recovery (credit in P&L for write-off vs write-off number on inventory) works out to 12-14% recovery, unchanged from prior range.

Collection headcount ramped up primarily to arrest slippages from X-bucket to SMA; once normalization completes (expected in ~1 quarter more), ~30% of that headcount will be reallocated to collecting write-off/NPA pool.
Last quarter, ~INR50 crores collected from NPA/write-off pool with ~900 people in the field, ~20% of collected value from this pool; expected to remain stable for next couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Opex vs Growth
points: Management expects to achieve 20-30% portfolio growth largely with the same cost base as collection machinery is already built.
For the ~1,200-1,300 hardcore collection people, cost is estimated at ~25-30% of amount recovered (illustrative: recovering INR1 lakh costs ~INR30,000).
Case load per collection person has come down significantly to a range of 330-350, supporting expectation of ~25-30% additional portfolio growth with the same cost base.

subsections.label: Disbursement Recovery Drivers
points: Disbursements improved across both JLG and non-JLG segments in Q4 FY26, reflecting a calibrated return to lending activity.
Guardrails implemented in April'25 caused a sudden increase in PAR, shifting focus to collections; by Q3 (Oct-Nov) collections had nearly stabilized, after which trust was placed back on sales.
Industry-wide also saw an upward trend in disbursements; FY25-26 portfolio post-guardrails is behaving well with respect to collections.
Bank is currently at only ~70% of optimum disbursal capacity and expects to stabilize in similar ranges going forward.
Fresh NPA slippages declined sharply versus year-ago levels, a direct outcome of tightened underwriting, stabilized collections and targeted collection initiatives.

subsections.label: Structural de-risking of unsecured exposure
points: Central theme of FY26 was structural de-risking of unsecured exposure and a strategic pivot toward secured and higher-yield, lower-risk portfolios, a deliberate long-term shift to reduce cyclicality in credit cost and create multiple avenues of growth beyond JLG lending.

JLG exposure moderated to ~28% of Gross Loan book (30% incl. BC JLG) as on March 2026, down from ~88% (90% incl. BC JLG) in March 2020, reflecting both selective contraction of the JLG book and purposeful shift of new flows into alternative products.
Secured lending now comprises 51% of Gross Loan book, up from 43% a year ago; structural shift already changing risk profile and expected to enhance margin stability over time.

subsections.label: MBBL (Micro-Banking Business Loan)
points: MBBL targeted at graduating JLG customers with proven repayment discipline has shown exceptional traction.
Penetration remains below 15%, giving significant headroom to scale this product to a much larger share of customer base while preserving asset quality.

subsections.label: CGFMU Credit Guarantee Coverage
points: Registered with CGFMU for credit guarantee coverage on eligible JLG and MBBL disbursements effective 17th January 2025.
Coverage materially reduces incremental portfolio risk on new disbursements and supports portfolio stability as the bank scales higher-quality secured products.

Cost of premium has been embedded in P&L for over a year (since Q4 of last year) but no accounting benefit or claim has been taken so far, nor has capital adequacy or risk weight been adjusted for the guarantee — only the expense has been recognized; benefit would accrue only in future if claims mature (claims typically take ~1.5 years to mature/settle).

subsections.label: Diversification beyond JLG
points: Non-JLG lending businesses saw healthy momentum in FY26, broadening revenue base and delivering attractive yields with more resilient collateral profiles.
MSME loan book growth supported by the newly started Micro LAP segment delivering ~18% disbursement yield.

CV and CE segment loan book contracted QoQ as management assessed mix of new vs used vehicles, with new vehicles signaling riskier behavior; strategic tilt toward used vehicles (more resilient asset class) reflected in rising used vehicle disbursement share.

MSME portfolio largely secured by hard collateral (residential/commercial properties), providing security to the bank in case of default; bank funds normal ticket sizes and does not fund large exporters with foreign currency exposure, so no abnormal behavior seen from geopolitical (Iran-U.S.) situation monitored over last 2.5 months.

subsections.label: Non-MFI / Wheels asset quality
points: Wheels (CV/CE) has been a problem area historically; collection efficiency/resolution percentages across buckets improved since November, controlling NPA percentages and arresting flow into SMA1/2 and NPA buckets.
Portfolio disbursed post-October 2024 (last 18 months) is performing well with NPA levels below 2%, aided by shift toward used vehicles and policy/parameter interventions based on portfolio analysis.

Other retail portfolios (Housing, LAP, Micro LAP, BBG working capital) are under tolerance levels as they are backed by hard collateral; Wheels expected to come under control within another 2 quarters.

subsections.label: Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation
points: Delivering tangible benefits in automation, productivity and risk control.
Digital underwriting capabilities helping avoid lending to over-leveraged borrowers.
360-degree control parameter mapping strengthening monitoring across the credit cycle.
Bank is in the process of launching new CBS in Q2/Q3 of FY27.

subsections.label: Liability franchise focus
points: Focus on building a granular, low-cost deposit base and aligning deposit growth with disbursements.

Total deposits broadly stable with retail term deposits and CASA growing faster than overall deposits, reflecting better quality of account sourcing and conscious reduction in reliance on bulk deposits.

In response to RBI repo rate cuts, phased reductions in interest rates on savings and term deposits made to remain competitive while optimizing cost of funds; further cost of funds reduction expected as repricing continues.

subsections.label: Operational discipline
points: Expanded collections workforce for JLG and MBBL to more than 1,200 as on March 2026.
Operationalized a specialized call center for overdue accounts and split larger micro-banking branches to improve oversight and control.
Training programs for new frontline staff emphasized core processes such as center meetings and customer onboarding, ensuring consistent execution across the field.
These structural investments contributed directly to improved collection metrics and reduction in SMA and fresh slippages reported in Q4 FY26.

points: Following creditors and shareholder approvals obtained per the amalgamation process, the second motion petition was filed with NCLT on April 5, 2026 for the scheme of amalgamation of holding company (UCL) with and into the bank.
Reverse merger expected to complete in the next few months, subject to NCLT proceedings.

subsections.label: Cross-sell / wallet share
points: Steps taken to improve quality of new account sourcing and to cross-sell asset products through liability-focused general banking branches, increasing product penetration per customer and improving wallet share.

subsections.label: Legacy stress
points: FY26 began under the shadow of legacy stress and a cautious environment; net loss and elevated credit cost for the quarter driven by provisioning for legacy stress/legacy portfolio.

subsections.label: Employee cost one-offs
points: One-time impact related to new Labour Codes, LTIP and ESOP grants and other employee benefit obligations incurred in Q3 FY26 with incremental impact in Q4 FY26, weighing on near-term profitability.

subsections.label: Geopolitical situation (Iran-U.S./West Asia)
points: Close monitoring of Iran-U.S. situation over the last 2.5 months; no abnormal behavior or portfolio behavioral change observed in MSME portfolio as bank does not fund large exporters with foreign currency exposure.

subsections.label: Prime Minister's comment on growth/credit cost
points: Management addressed a question on the Prime Minister's recent comment in context of the bank's 30% growth target and geopolitical situation; does not foresee major credit cost challenge as portfolio is largely income-generation, smaller ticket size, and collection machinery is strong.

subsections.label: Wheels (CV/CE) asset quality
points: Non-MFI slippages running high at ~4%, with Wheels segment being a major contributor; expected to come under control in another 2 quarters.

subsections.label: FY27 as consolidation year
points: FY27 viewed as a consolidation year — a period to convert green shoots seen in Q4 FY26 into sustained momentum while continuing to strengthen the franchise.

Near-term priorities: sustain improved collection performance, continue calibrated disbursements into higher-quality segments, deepen secured lending and accelerate liability mobilization to support growth prudently.
Achieving medium-term targets will require steady execution across underwriting, collections, product diversification, liability mobilization and technology-enabled risk management.
Sectoral headwinds and regulatory transitions may continue to influence near-term performance, but management remains confident in the strategic direction over the medium term.

subsections.label: Credit cost trajectory
points: Previously guided 3-3.5% steady state for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28; management reiterates this as a conservative number given SMA declines and improving collection trends, and expects to potentially do better given the CGFMU cover and industry-wide disbursement/collection recovery (99.5%+ collection).

subsections.label: ROE and worst-behind confirmation
points: Management confirmed the bank is on track for 15% ROE and will exit FY28 above 15% ROE.

Management confirmed 'the worst is behind us,' noting current provisioning (including Q4) is largely on the legacy portfolio, while the new portfolio created under guardrails with guarantee cover is performing well.

key_takeaways: The fourth quarter of FY '26 has been a period of renewed growth, proof of resilience and cautious optimism.

By quarter 4 of FY '26, we began to see tangible green shoots: disbursements improved meaningfully, SMA pools contracted, fresh NPA slippages declined sharply, recoveries and upgradations increased and collection efficiency strengthened.
JLG disbursements grew 58% quarter-on-quarter and 2% year-on-year, while non-JLG disbursements grew 41% quarter-on-quarter and 51% year-on-year.
Our X-Bucket collection efficiency in the JLG segment improved to 99.7% in March 2026, up from 98.5% in April 2025, the highest level in the last 4 quarters.
Fresh NPA slippages (net of recoveries and upgradations) reduced to ~INR170 crores in quarter 4 of FY '26 against ~INR710 crores in the quarter 4 of FY '25.
Our GNPA ratio improved by ~330 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 7.7% as on March '26.
We have consciously moderated our JLG exposure to around 28% of the Gross Loan book (and around 30% including BC JLG) as on March 2026, down from nearly 88% (and 90% including BC JLG) in March 2020.
Secured lending now comprises 51% of our Gross Loan book, up from 43% a year ago.
We reported a net loss of INR188 crores for the quarter, driven by provisioning for legacy stress.
In the coming years, we are aiming for loan book growth of 25% to 30%, with secured lending comprising around 55% of the portfolio, maintaining NIMs of above 8% and delivering a ROE of around 15%.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was MobiKwik's most profitable quarter yet (3rd straight profitable quarter), with management targeting full-year PAT profitability for FY27, continued GMV/revenue growth in both payments and financial services, anchored fixed costs so incremental contribution flows to EBITDA/PAT, lending disbursements targeted at INR1,000 crores/quarter going forward (already on that run-rate in Q2), merchant business scale-up continuing with FY28 breakeven expectation, and NBFC transition to a wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026.

subsections.label: Profitability drivers
points: Q1 FY27 is described as the most successful and profitable quarter yet, balancing current profits with calibrated investments for the future.
Company profitable for three straight quarters.
Both payments gross profit and financial services gross profit grew strongly, driving contribution profit up 66% YoY.
Credit quality improved 25% with 60% of loans going to repeat customers, indicating robust credit quality.
Direct costs compressed at scale: overall down 21% YoY, payments down 15% YoY, lending down 40% YoY.

subsections.label: Cash and debt position
points: As of FY26-end (31 March), the company repaid all long-term loans.
Only remaining loans are short-term working capital facilities from two major private banks, used solely for payment settlement refunding.
IPO proceeds earmarked for capex (merchant equipment) still have ~INR25 crores available; company does not expect to need more than that for this year.

subsections.label: Tax position
points: Company has substantial accumulated losses (~INR900-1,000 crores) providing a tax shield; not expected to pay taxes for some time.

subsections.label: Fixed cost trajectory
points: Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crores to INR53 crores quarter-on-quarter, largely attributable to new merchant businesses which are manpower-intensive on the offline side.
Merchant-related manpower cost could rise 5% to 15% year-to-year, but will be directly linked to break-even progress and margin generation from that business.
Merchant business burn is being run on a ~INR15 crore/quarter basis (annualized INR50-60 crores), consistent with prior guidance timetable.

subsections.label: Payments business dynamics
points: Platform GMV reached all-time high, marking the 14th straight quarter of growth in payments GMV.
UPI transactions grew 5x faster than industry, making MobiKwik the second fastest-growing TPAP UPI app in the country, though it remains ranked 13th overall in the NPCI UPI stack rankings.

High revenue-generating card-linked categories (credit/debit card linked) were paused in Q4 and Q1 due to regulatory guardrail changes across the industry (similar to competitor disclosures on categories like rent, education), causing a dip in both revenue and direct costs in payments.
Company plans to re-launch paused payment categories and expects to recover from the payments revenue dip in coming quarters.

Despite revenue growth difficulty, 50% YoY GMV growth translated into 31% YoY gross profit growth, driven by cost efficiency (comparable revenue base of INR208 crores generated INR77 crores gross profit vs INR59 crores a year earlier).

PPI wallet transactions grew 68% YoY but GMV grew only 24% YoY because more users are using wallet/Pocket UPI for lower ticket-size transactions, while higher-ticket card-linked transactions declined due to the pause.

Wallet-on-UPI transactions do not generate MDR revenue for MobiKwik currently (unlike wallet-to-wallet-merchant transactions), even though RBI mandated PPI-on-UPI MDR; NPCI has not implemented it despite 2.5 years, representing a revenue loss for wallet players industry-wide.

subsections.label: Lending / Financial Services business
points: Revenue held strong this quarter despite a dip in disbursements.

Disbursement growth planned via new lending partners (added in Q1, more in Q2), pre-approved/pre-qualified offer generation to the large engaged user base, and an in-house AI engine to detect and address funnel drop-offs.
Recoveries from the old/past loan book are also contributing to revenue, performing better than expected.

Gross margin improvement in lending was partly due to write-back of guarantee cost from previous-year loans (1.87% of gross lending revenue, ~INR16 crores); write-backs expected to continue every quarter but not necessarily at the same value, as upfront collateral held with lenders has been reduced over time as credit cohorts improved.
Collateral/provision to lenders varies by partner (up to the RBI-permitted 5% max; e.g., 4.75%, 4.5%, 5% across the nine lenders) depending on lender risk assessment.
Financial services net margin guided at 4.5% to 5.5% long-range, even though it has recently been running higher (5.4%-5.9%); management does not want investors to assume 5.9% is sustainable.

Disbursement de-growth over the last two quarters attributed to (1) deliberate reduction of lender concentration from 91% (Q2/Q3) to 87% (prior quarter) to 71% (this quarter) to diversify risk, and (2) technology/business migration disruption from moving the digital lending business to a new wholly-owned NBFC subsidiary, which consumed significant focus in Q1.
Company is already running at the INR1,000 crores/quarter disbursement run-rate as of the date of the call (early Q2 FY27).
New lending partners and new lending products (different ticket sizes, pricing models) planned to continue being added through the year.

subsections.label: Merchant / Zaakpay business
points: Merchant business (encompassing online Zaakpay payment gateway and offline QR/soundbox/EDC merchant acquiring) began scaling only at the end of last quarter/start of this quarter.
Company declines to share merchant device counts, merchant counts, or merchant revenue at this early stage, citing it is 'too early'.
Merchant business expected to have lower gross profit margins (net take rate industry-wide reported at less than 10 bps for merchant-focused competitors) versus consumer payments.
Zaakpay GMV for the quarter given as INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed separately.

subsections.label: Cross-sell
points: Largest cross-sell product is lending, targeting the ~96 million engaged user base for roughly INR150-250 crores of additional disbursement per quarter.
Wealth products in development to further diversify cross-sell opportunities.
UPI acts as a low-cost acquisition funnel; UPI-acquired users are cross-sold into revenue-generating payment categories.

subsections.label: AI-based lending funnel engine
points: Company built its own AI engine to automatically detect the step at which a user drops off in the lending funnel (from loan-offer interest to disbursal completion) and take corrective action (e.g., engaging users in their own language, addressing the specific drop-off trigger) to re-engage and convert them.
This engine is expected to generate approximately INR100 crores per quarter in additional disbursements.

subsections.label: Merchant vs consumer market positioning
points: Merchant business (offline and online) allows monetization via MDR unlike UPI on the consumer side where there is no way to make money.

Fewer competitors in merchant acquiring (can be counted 'on one hand') versus UPI consumer side, which is much more competitive (13 players ranked on NPCI stack), making it easier to acquire and retain merchants.
Multiple monetization levers exist in merchant business: CC-on-UPI MDR, device rental (soundbox/EDC), card MDR, and potential lending cross-sell to merchants.
Management believes merchant acquiring has a strong value proposition given the large TAM and few serious competitors.

subsections.label: UPI monetization outlook
points: UPI monetization (MDR/subsidy) depends entirely on government decision; management has no visibility into timing.

RBI had mandated that PPI-on-UPI should earn MDR similar to RuPay credit cards on UPI rails; documentation exists and is public, but implementation by NPCI (which runs the UPI stack) continues to be pushed back/delayed despite 2.5 years.

Wallet players, including MobiKwik, have submitted written representations at multiple government levels seeking this MDR flow-through, given the cost of full KYC compliance required for wallet-on-UPI transactions.
Management describes itself as demoralized about the lack of progress, citing it as a disadvantage of operating a fintech in a heavily regulated market like India.

subsections.label: NBFC transition to subsidiary
points: RBI approved the company's NBFC application in April, conditional on moving the digital lending business from parent MobiKwik to a wholly-owned subsidiary.
Shareholder approval for the transition was received on July 2nd.
The transition involves re-contracting with all NBFC partners, technology migration, and people migration — a large, cumbersome process.
Company intends to close this transition in August, after which it will seek the final Certificate of Registration (CoR) from the regulator.
Own NBFC lending/disbursal launch is still some time away; a better update expected in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Growth initiative sizing (from investor presentation slides 21-23)
points: Two growth initiatives — pre-approved/pre-qualified offers to the 96 million engaged user base (INR150-250 crores/quarter) and the AI drop-off re-engagement engine (~INR100 crores/quarter) — are together expected to generate roughly INR300 crores of incremental disbursals, supporting the INR1,000 crores/quarter disbursement target using Q1 as baseline.

subsections.label: Merchant business scale-up
points: Merchant business planned to scale up 10x over the next two years.

subsections.label: Regulatory headwinds
points: Card-linked (credit/debit) payment categories with higher take rates have faced regulatory guardrail changes across the industry (not just MobiKwik), leading to a pause of some products in Q4 and Q1, with re-launch planned for Q2.
PPI-on-UPI MDR monetization, though mandated by RBI, has not been implemented by NPCI despite 2.5 years, resulting in ongoing revenue loss for wallet players.
UPI monetization overall depends on government/regulatory decisions outside company control.

subsections.label: Lender concentration risk
points: High lending concentration in top three lenders (91% in Q2/Q3 FY26) was identified as a risk; company has deliberately reduced this to 71% this quarter by diversifying across more NBFC partners.

subsections.label: NBFC transition execution risk
points: Moving digital lending business to the new wholly-owned subsidiary is a cumbersome process involving re-contracting with lenders/bureaus and technology/people migration, which disrupted disbursements in Q1; expected to close in August.

PAT of INR7.6 crores in Q1 (annualized to INR30.2 crores) plus expected incremental improvement of INR2-3 crores per quarter is seen as sufficient to reach ~INR40 crores full-year PAT target.

key_takeaways: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
Q1 PAT stood at INR76 million. We are now profitable for three straight quarters. The PAT swing from Q1 last year to Q1 this year is INR495 million.
EBITDA delivered at INR158 million with an improvement of INR470 million YoY.
Payments gross profit landed at INR777 million, up 31% YoY, whereas the financial services gross profit grew 5.6x YoY and landed at INR433 million, demonstrating robust credit quality.
Platform GMV reached an all-time high of INR587 billion, 50% up YoY, marking the 14th straight quarter of growth in payments GMV.
UPI transactions grew 5x faster than the overall industry, making MobiKwik the second fastest-growing TPAP, UPI app in the country.

quarters.summary: Q4 FY26 was a landmark quarter with back-to-back profitable quarters; FY26 was an inflection year with EBITDA near breakeven and PAT halved YoY. Entering FY27, MobiKwik's core payments and lending business is generating real profits (~INR50 crores EBITDA) which is being reinvested into four new growth engines - offline and online merchant payments, NBFC lending, and AI - targeting significant scale-up by FY28, with near-term margins expected to stay in a similar baseline-profitable range while investments continue.

subsections.label: Profitability turnaround
points: Full year FY26 was an inflection year with EBITDA near break-even (negative INR 5 crores), a swing of INR 742 million from minus INR 794 million in FY25 to minus INR 52 million in FY26.
Full year PAT halved to minus INR 621 million, an improvement of INR 594 million YoY from negative INR 1,215 million in FY25.

H1 FY26 was spent catching up, rebuilding credit quality, compressing costs, and restoring margins; by H2 the business had fully turned around with both Q3 and Q4 EBITDA and PAT positive, delivering INR 84 million cumulative PAT for H2 FY26.
Reported PAT of INR 44 million for Q4 includes a INR 37.6 million one-time exceptional charge due to Labor Wage Code changes; underlying PAT excluding this would have been INR 81 million.

Core payments and lending business generated real profits of INR 50 crores EBITDA in FY26; company is deliberately reinvesting these profits into new growth engines, which is why full-year reported EBITDA was negative INR 5 crores instead of positive INR 50 crores.

subsections.label: Fixed cost trajectory
points: Fixed costs increased on purpose to build new businesses (merchant payments, NBFC, AI) as detailed in the earnings presentation.
Q4 fixed costs of INR 117 crores were about INR 4 crores higher than the previous quarter, including a one-off exceptional cost of INR 4 crores.

Current fixed cost run-rate is INR 115-120 crores per quarter; expect roughly 15%-20% increase in fixed costs in the next year as merchant business scales, driven by rising depreciation and people costs for device distribution.

Company intends to remain 'baseline profitable' - generating profit margins from consumer payments and lending (scale businesses) and redeploying a portion into new businesses while ensuring overall PAT profitability each quarter.

subsections.label: Debt and working capital
points: All long-term debt has been paid off; only remaining debt as of 31 March is INR 261 crores of short-term working capital lines, generally used for holidays and long weekends when settlement volumes run into hundreds of crores over 2-3 non-banking days.

Net owned unencumbered cash is about INR 434 crores, but a good chunk of this is still IPO proceeds not yet fully available/trickling in as used, so not all cash can be deployed to replace working capital lines.

Working capital usage has remained stable even as payments GMV has grown multi-fold; finance cost has come down from INR 7.2 crores in Q3 to INR 5.1/5 crores in Q4, reflecting efforts to reduce finance cost.

key_figures.label: Recharge and bill payments GMV scale-up

subsections.label: Payments business performance
points: Payments GMV hit an all-time high in Q4, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of record high GMV.
MobiKwik remains the largest wallet in India by GTV as of March 2026 with about 20% market share.
MobiKwik is the second fastest growing UPI app in India; customer-initiated UPI transactions grew 170% YoY versus industry growth of 26% YoY, i.e. 6.5x the market rate.
In Bharat Bill Payments ecosystem, MobiKwik is the sixth largest COU by GTV as of March 2026; BBPS COU GTV is a subset of the broader recharge and bill payments GMV.
Recharge and bill payments business (a mature business) scaled 2.2x to INR 269 billion in FY26, with a 48% three-year CAGR.

Revenue in payments generally follows/lags GMV growth; because of increasing UPI mix in overall payments GMV, revenue growth has not kept pace with GMV growth so far, but PPI-over-UPI MDR (Pocket UPI), expected to be introduced, has not yet come through, causing a revenue lag which management expects to normalize in coming quarters.

Ex-UPI GTV has been growing north of 30% for several quarters, but this hasn't translated into proportional revenue growth; management attributes this partly to moderation of take rates and a mix shift (thanks to UPI and addition of lower-margin categories) even though net margins have held up.

Some revenue has started to be generated in the UPI business on the consumer side even without PPI-over-UPI MDR; bill payments revenue contribution is also picking up, and both are expected to meaningfully contribute to consumer payments revenue growth within 12 months.

subsections.label: Financial services (lending) business performance
points: Delivered highest ever quarterly gross margin (59%) in Q4, reflecting disciplined expansion with profitability prioritized over volume.

Focus has been on increasing disbursements to super-prime and repeat users: super-prime mix in disbursements improved from 10% to 32% YoY; repeat loans mix rose from 20% to 63.5% YoY; near-prime customers make up about 22% of the mix.

Digital credit GMV growth was subdued sequentially this quarter because the company is prioritizing quality and profitability over volume, tilting the portfolio toward repeat and super-prime cohorts for higher net margins rather than higher disbursals.

Lending margin (spread) came in at 5.3%-5.4% this quarter, aided by 35% lower credit cost on the maturing portfolio and gains from previously matured cohorts due to strong collection efforts; however, management does not consider 5%+ sustainable long-term and guides to a 4%-4.5% 'sweet spot' range.

subsections.label: Merchant payments business
points: Merchant partners currently number 4.9 million, having grown only 7% this year; management is not focused on the raw merchant count but on categories - organized retail, petrol, and small mom-and-pop stores - targeting 10%-20% of the market leader's size in 18-24 months.
On Zaakpay (online merchant acquiring), identified categories such as education, government, and BBPS as areas where even double-digit market share could help achieve the 10x GMV target in 18 months.

This is the first quarter the company has broken down and disclosed detail on subcategories within payments (bill payments, merchant payments, etc.); more disclosure expected in coming quarters as growth KPIs are tracked.

Merchant business unit economics: UPI transactions on merchant side don't generate MDR; it is credit-on-UPI-rails or RuPay credit card transactions that generate MDR, plus device rentals; after strong merchant engagement, a merchant credit pipe can be built as a further economics layer.

subsections.label: Payments take rate outlook
points: Company has been achieving a payments net take rate around 16 basis points in recent quarters but guides conservatively to 12-15 basis points for the next 2 years given regulatory uncertainty in India's payments market, cautioning against modeling 16 bps over a 2-year horizon.

subsections.label: Four new growth engines
points: Company is reinvesting core business profits into four new growth engines: offline merchant payments, online merchant payments (Zaakpay), NBFC lending, and AI.

Merchant payments (offline and online) represent what management believes is the single largest untapped opportunity in Indian payments, operating on MDR, device, and settlement economics with significantly less competition than consumer payments.
Offline merchant payments targeting a 5x device scale-up to enable 10x revenue growth by FY28.
Zaakpay (online merchant acquiring, wholly owned subsidiary) targeting 10x GMV by FY28.

Both merchant payment businesses are on track for EBITDA breakeven by FY28; management deliberately chose a 10x scale target rather than an earlier breakeven at smaller scale (e.g. 3x-4x) because reaching 10x avoids repeated investment cycles and leverages already-achieved execution rigor and competitive product positioning.

subsections.label: NBFC setup and lending strategy
points: NBFC application approval is described as the most consequential regulatory milestone in the company's lending journey, providing the foundation for scaling lending in the most regulated model available.

Strengths built over 7 years in digital lending - underwriting/credit risk expertise, collections tested in stress cycles, lender partnerships - will transition from the current LSP model to the new NBFC co-lending model.

NBFC will unlock better economics on own-book and co-lending, enabling partnerships with more banks/NBFCs and access to a larger universe of regulated PSU and private banks; it will also provide product velocity, allowing the company to design products on its own timeline rather than through lender approval cycles as an LSP.

Regulatory process: existing digital lending LSP business will first move to a wholly owned subsidiary of MobiKwik (expected to complete in 2-3 months); NBFC setup work will then take 3-6 months from now; operations/disbursals under the co-lending model are expected to launch in a 6-9 month timeframe.

For regulatory ring-fencing, LSP and NBFC businesses will sit in separate wholly owned subsidiaries with inter-company agreements on customer sourcing and billing; the Holdco (One MobiKwik) itself will not hold LSP or NBFC business directly.

LSP business is expected to continue in similar fashion in its wholly owned subsidiary, with NBFC-generated business being incremental; NBFC will be one of several lending partners for the LSP, not a replacement.
Capital allocation for the NBFC subsidiary will go through Board and shareholder approval process to infuse funds.
Long-term split between NBFC piece and pure distribution mix is not yet determined; management says it is too soon to reveal, pending completion of NBFC setup.

subsections.label: AI strategy
points: MobiKwik intends to be an AI-first company by FY28; AI is already deployed across the business - 80% of code is AI generated, 55% of early collections are AI driven, and 86% of customer support is self-served by AI.

Going forward, AI will own the full lending lifecycle, identify funnel drops, drive user personalization at scale, acquire better cohorts at lower spend, and detect frauds in real time; AI is positioned as a compounding competitive moat, not just a productivity tool.

subsections.label: Regulatory and market risks
points: PPI-over-UPI MDR (Pocket UPI), which was expected, has not yet come through, causing a lag between wallet/UPI GMV growth and revenue realization.

Payments take rate guidance is conservative (12-15 bps) despite recent performance of ~16 bps, because India is a heavily regulated market and various regulatory changes could impact take rates; management cannot predict if/when regulatory change could affect this.
NBFC regulator expects proper governance and compliance, especially as the business scales, versus the more lightly regulated LSP model.

FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) requires the company to bear up to 5% of credit cost as book grows, requiring continuous additional FLDG deposits against future losses; funds are only returned if the business de-grows.
Working capital is described as a 'necessary evil' - required to fund settlements during bank holidays/long weekends when settlement volumes run into hundreds of crores over non-banking days.
A portion of net owned unencumbered cash (INR 434 crores) is still IPO proceeds not yet fully available, limiting the company's ability to substitute cash for working capital debt lines.

For FY27, management expects investments to continue in similar range as FY26 (~INR 55 crores) into merchant payments business, with net EBITDA margin expected to remain in the same broad ~5% range as investments increase alongside better underlying margins.
Both merchant payment businesses (offline and Zaakpay online) are targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven by FY28.
Digital credit GMV is guided to grow 30%-35% in FY27 from FY26 base of ~INR 3,200 crores.
Payments and lending GMV growth both guided at 30%-35% range going forward.

Payments net take rate guided conservatively at 12-15 basis points over a 2-year horizon despite recent ~16 bps performance, due to regulatory uncertainty.
NBFC operations/disbursals expected to launch within 6-9 months from now, following a 2-3 month LSP-to-subsidiary transition and 3-6 months NBFC setup.

key_takeaways: Q4 FY26 was a landmark quarter for MobiKwik. We ended the year with back-to-back profitable quarters.

The full year financial year '26 was an inflection year for us. We achieved an EBITDA of near break-even (negative INR 5 crores), with a total swing of INR 742 million from minus INR 794 million in FY25 to minus INR 52 million in FY26.
The full year PAT halved to minus INR 621 million, an improvement of INR 594 million year-over-year from the previous financial year where it was negative INR1,215 million.

The payments GMV hit an all-time high of INR 524 billion in the fourth quarter, which is a 58% Y-o-Y improvement and a 9% Q-o-Q improvement. This is the 13th consecutive quarter of record high GMV that the company has reported in the payments business.
In our financial services business, we delivered our highest ever quarterly gross margin at 59% in Q4, which indicates our objective of disciplined expansion - profitability prioritized over volume.
H2 FY26 delivered INR84 million of cumulative PAT, and both Q3 and Q4 were EBITDA and PAT positive as we had committed to all of you in the last few earnings calls.

MobiKwik now has a core business which is generating real profits - INR50 crores of EBITDA is what our core business, payments and lending, has generated. And now we are deliberately reinvesting these profits towards building new growth engines.
We are focused on four new growth engines: merchant payments (offline and online), NBFC application approval, and AI.

MobiKwik as a company intends to be an AI-first company by FY28. We are already running AI across the business. 80% of code is AI generated, 55% of early collections are AI driven, and 86% of customer support is self-served by AI.
pressing_questions: Raj Shah: our payments business from last four to five quarters is struggling to grow in terms of revenue. So, what are we doing about this excluding our new growth engines, and do you expect it to cross INR220 crores, INR210 crores revenue per quarter anytime soon?

Ankush Agarwal: last quarter we had this commentary that the fixed cost base is expected to settle between INR 105 crores – INR 110 crores...But if I look at this quarter, I think the fixed cost base has grown to like INR 120 crores and the commentary now is that we expect the merchant business to sort of reach breakeven in FY '28. So just wanted to get a sense of what has changed and, what is driving this.

Ankush Agarwal: the GTV ex of UPI is still not up 30% plus the growth... the revenue hasn't been growing, but obviously the profitability has been improving...that divergence is something that that I'm not able to understand because obviously the total GTV growth is much stronger because of UPI...so that is not adding up honestly?
Divyansh Thakur: why are we not using our cash and using the short-term facilities for the to meet our working capital requirements? I missed the answer?

subsections.label: Margin recovery narrative
points: EBITDA margin had dropped to about 42% operating EBITDA following pricing adjustments and climbed back over the next 4-5 quarters to 46%, now at 46.4% (up 270 bps YoY from 43.7%), still below the historical peak of a shade above 47%.
Margin improvement occurring despite AUM not growing as much as it traditionally would, reflecting cost discipline and productivity gains.

EBITDA of INR183 crore grew 18% YoY; PAT grew 17% YoY; operating revenue of INR395 crore grew 11.5% YoY, with MF revenue growth under 10% (asset-based growth a little over 11%, blended MF growth 11.2%) and non-MF revenue growth collectively over 28%.
Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR980 crore at end of Q1 FY27; interim dividend of INR2.5 per share declared.

subsections.label: Cost management
points: Appraisal impact (salary increases) deferred by a quarter — effective July 1 instead of April 1 — so additional cost impact will show in Q2 rather than Q1, though full-year impact is unaffected by timing.

Total cost increase (excluding depreciation) was less than 7% YoY and almost negligible QoQ; target remains less than 10% YoY overall across all expense heads as an endeavor for the next two-three years.

Employee cost base last year was INR470-500 crore (excluding one-off); targeting an increase of INR25-30 crore (~5%) in FY27, while other cost areas like risk, compliance, and software development still require investment.
Headcount just shy of 8,300 in Q1 FY27, down ~85 YoY and down ~200-225 QoQ; targeting 4-5% headcount reduction for FY27, with 2-3% achieved so far.

Net headcount reduction expected to be less than the full 4-5% target on a cost basis (perhaps 3-3.5%) because expensive AI/automation resources are being hired/backfilled even as frontline positions are automated away.

subsections.label: Depreciation dynamics
points: Depreciation declined QoQ mainly due to written-down-value depreciation method causing steep year-2 decline versus large capex outflow in the similar quarter last year, plus very muted on-prem capitalization in Q1.
This QoQ depreciation decline should not be extrapolated for the rest of the year; depreciation is expected to increase due to re-architecture capitalization.

Re-arch capex capitalized in the quarter was INR40 crore, with INR80 crore of capitalization expected for the remainder of FY27, adding INR4-5 crore of incremental depreciation for the rest of the year and an additional INR12 crore of depreciation in FY28.
On-prem capex outlook for FY27 is INR75 crore.

subsections.label: Capitalization policy
points: Company follows a conservative capitalization policy: core MF platform, KRA platform, payments platform expenses (AI, automation, maintenance) are all taken as employee cost, including 100% subsidiary Sterling Software.

Only cost of people involved in coding the new re-architecture platform on the cloud is capitalized as capex — the INR290 crore capex portion of the INR500 crore total re-architecture project, of which INR123 crore has been spent cumulatively to date.

subsections.label: PAT and EBITDA context
points: In a specific quarter referenced during discussion, EBITDA growth was around 45% and PAT growth around 31%; PAT margin expectation going forward is 30-31%, with current overall EBITDA margin at 47%.

key_figures.label: New AMC logos live last year
New AMC logos live this year

subsections.label: MF growth drivers
points: MF AUM reached INR56 lakh crore, up just under 15% YoY, with market share of 67.2%.
Equity AUM growth of 16-17.6% and equity net sales grew ahead of industry, along with live SIP account counts — considered foundational metrics since 60-65% of MF asset revenue comes from equity.

SIP collections held up at just short of INR60,000 crore in Q1 despite market volatility (April-May-June muted, markets bottomed then peaked then declined again), reflecting resilience of Indian retail investor.
SIP collections growth and unique investor base growth also outperformed industry.
July has been notably better than April-May-June, with AUM nearing INR60 lakh crore.

subsections.label: GIFT City / SIF new asset classes
points: GIFT retail is very formative/early — started with first cohort of 10,000 investors nudging INR750 crore AUM; strategy has shifted from metal ETFs to using GIFT City for overseas investing.

SIF segment is only 10 months old (first launch early October last year), with 11 unique launches to date and 3-4 more expected; net sales run-rate about INR1,000 crore/month, cumulative AUM just in excess of INR12,000 crore, and almost 50,000 investors.

SIF economics identical to MF — schemes slotted by asset type (mostly equity-led) with same rates as AMC; some separate-schema setup cost already absorbed at the INR10,000-12,000 crore base, so scale-up will help defray that cost.
Both GIFT and SIF expected to grow into meaningful franchises over time, comparable to how alternatives grew, though this may take years.

subsections.label: Non-MF segment detail
points: Non-MF revenue grew 28%+ YoY, now about 15% (also cited 14%) of total revenue, targeting certainly 16% by FY27 end; blended non-MF revenue growth expected to stay upwards of 20% for the year, potentially 22-23%.

Pay segment revenue grew just short of 70% (also cited 67%) YoY, largely riding on cards; cards is a high-bank-charges, margin-limited business that management wants to grow but scale intelligently/step-by-step, not aggressively — started about a year back.
Alternatives AUM grew mid-20s% YoY (AIF growth cited at 25% by CFO) crossing INR3.2 lakh crore, with 50 new mandates won and several new logos despite competition from new entrants.
KRA revenue declined in Q1 due to known 1 April rate revision (~29-30% rates down) combined with a slightly subdued market; expected to improve from Q2 onwards.

Non-MF EBITDA margin dropped to 13% in Q1 (from 17%+ in Q4 FY26) because KRA — a high contributor to non-MF margin — declined; expected to recover toward 17%, possibly closer to 20% (alternate framing: 16-17%), as KRA recovers and losses in repository/account aggregator narrow.
Rep's Bima Central user base expanding but not yet meaningful revenue.

ConsentPro (built in-house for consent management across MF, KRA, CRA, pension, insurance repository) — first signed contracts expected shortly; work started with 7-8 clients across capital markets and other sectors; too early to project revenue.
Education segment opened for payments but not attributed much revenue increase.

subsections.label: EBITDA breakeven status by business
points: Account aggregator, pension, and CAMS Repository not yet EBITDA positive.
CAMSRep expected to become EBITDA positive at least on a final-quarter basis.
Think Analytics is almost EBITDA positive.
Account aggregator adoption bottleneck exists — concept being adopted more on fintech/lending side than capital market side.

subsections.label: AMC renewals and new logos
points: A few midsized AMCs up for renewal this year; a couple concluded, 2 more in discussion; impact from concluded renewals already reflected in Q1 pricing and expected to be very muted.
6 new AMC logos went live last year (FY26); only 1 (AlphaGrep) live so far this year, with 4 more (Carnelian, ASK, Neo, Oaklane) expected to be installed before December.

key_figures.label: Transaction types live on new platform
AI-based acceptance of gross payload converted

subsections.label: Re-architecture / transaction acceptance platform
points: Transaction acceptance module (external work with markets — money coming in, KYCs, exchanges, depositories, sellers, banks) beginning to go live step by step in August/September, with 4 of 8 transaction types live in Q1 FY27; company believes it will complete the entire transaction acceptance part of the platform by end of financial year.
By November, all 8 transaction types expected to be live; pace of AI conversion within those is company's choice.
AI-based acceptance has converted 10% of gross payload in Q1 FY27, with a target to scale to 100% at maker level within the next 12 months.
Company states it could convert the entire transaction acceptance to AI-led 100% today, but is not doing so due to risk of moving too fast — a manual checker remains in place.
Data warehouse, CAMS Lens (revamped KRA offering), and capabilities on eKYC and deepfakes are now live.
Physical transaction acceptance capability now going through the new AI-based process.

subsections.label: AI/automation strategy and industry impact
points: Base automation (distinct from new AI platform) has kept enterprise headcount roughly constant over the last 10 years; new re-architecture program is expected to accelerate automation speed further.
AI-led benefits are attributed to the new platform being built because the current platform is 2.5 decades old and lacked current-generation technology capability.

Management expects the AI/automation productivity process to continue for the next 3-4 years, with productivity gains accruing not just within CAMS but across the industry (AMCs, distributors, exchanges) — expected to be more accretive for the industry than for CAMS itself.
Not all productivity gains will show up in CAMS's own P&L because rising cloud/data center/hardware costs (driven by hyperscaler demand for AI) are increasing cost inputs faster than expected.
Management does not expect AMC client behavior/efficiency attitude to change materially as a result of these productivity gains.

key_figures.period: 2023 origination; tranches at year 3 and year 4

subsections.label: Think360 stake expansion
points: Transaction originated in 2023; both founders and CAMS have options to expand shareholding at the end of the third and fourth year.
Current stake expansion reflects execution of the first tranche of the call/put option; second tranche expected to be executed about 12 months from now.
Company may continue running Think360 separately (NBFC/fintech segment) and may never sunset the name, rather than merging it with CAMS — decision still pending.

subsections.label: ConsentPro build-out
points: Built in-house between CAMS and Think (Think360) given the need for controlled consent capability across MF, KRA, CRA, pension and insurance repository businesses.
Not limited to capital markets/financial services — broader applicability; first signed contracts expected shortly with work started across 7-8 clients.

subsections.label: GIFT City expansion
points: In-principle approval received to start a KRA operation in GIFT City, which has broader application beyond capital market entities.

Company is in the process of applying for a payment service provider license in GIFT City (application pending due to process requirements); intends to offer a wholesome combination of RTA, fund accounting, KRA and payments in GIFT City.

subsections.label: KRA pricing reset
points: KRA rate revision effective 1 April at ~29-30% rates down caused revenue decline in Q1, compounded by a slightly subdued market.

Some previously-free KRA services (certain 'fetch' checks) are now priced under the new dispensation, applicable uniformly across industry participants — no charging asymmetries between CAMS and competitors, though business mix (MF/DP/broking split) differs, affecting comparability of impact versus peers like CDSL.
Impact from KRA repricing viewed as not a large impacting item and only the first quarter of invoicing under new structure.

subsections.label: Rising technology/infrastructure costs
points: Cloud, data center, and hardware costs are rising faster than expected due to hyperscaler demand from AI-led segment, which will add some cost pressure that could offset productivity gains.

subsections.label: Non-asset-based MF revenue decline drivers
points: Decline in non-asset-based MF revenue driven by OPE (application fee) reduction, some transaction reduction, NFO decline, and wind-down of an arrangement with a customer (NSE) — this component does not keep pace with AUM growth.
Overall transaction counts rose ~20% YoY but revenue declined because most transactions are digital and only a subset of paper transactions (less than 10% of total) are charged.

subsections.label: Account aggregator adoption bottleneck
points: Adoption bottleneck exists for account aggregator — the concept is being adopted on the fintech/lending side but not as much on the capital markets side.

subsections.label: FY27 targets
points: Blended revenue growth guided at 13% and blended EBITDA growth at 16% for FY27.
Non-MF revenue growth guided at 20%, potentially up to 22-23%; MF revenue growth guided at least 12%.
MF yield expected to decline 2.5-3% annually (ongoing / by May), with margin expansion expectation of 1%, up to 1.5% annually.
Employee cost growth target around 5% for FY27 and next 2-3 years; overall cost increase target less than 10% for FY27 and next 2-3 years.
Headcount reduction target of about 5% (enterprise) for FY27.
PAT margin outlook of 30-31% going forward.

subsections.label: Second half outlook
points: Management expects KRA, alternatives/pay to fire on non-MF side, and MF/SIF/GIFT City retail to fire on MF side in Q2, forming a good combination if all plays out.

guidance_ledger.statement: Blended, we are expecting about a 13% overall revenue growth.
About a 16% EBITDA growth. So it seems to be on that track.
We believe that for the year, overall blended non-MF revenue will certainly be 20%. If you're lucky, it could come at 22%, 23%.
MF revenue, we would like it to grow at least 12%.
Non-MF revenue just getting to about 15%. I'm hoping this will certainly be 16% by the end of the year, but we'll watch this closely.
We are confident of getting it if not 20%, at least close to 20% by the end of the year... you should expect probably 17% kind of a margin.
Our target is to keep it around 5% employee cost increase on a year-on-year basis.
We will keep our cost increase down to less than 10% overall across all the heads of expense for the next two, three years.
In this year, we've stated, if you take FY27 that we will drop enterprise headcount by about 5%.
We have stated in the past that you can expect about a 1% margin expansion from our side. Can we get to 1.5%? I would say yes.
You've said historically that you should see 2.5% to 3% annually. My guess is that's perhaps the number you'll end up seeing when we speak to you in May.
We expect that our PAT margins will continue to be around 30%, 31% going forward also.
We expect for the coming year the on-prem related capex, including tools and servers and storage and premises, etcetera, to be in the region of INR75 crores.
The overall project cost, as we have said, is around INR500 crores... out of which we expect around INR290 crores to be the capex number.
In the rest of the year, we will expect that at least another INR80 crores will get capitalized.

You should expect in the current year at least an increase in depreciation to the extent of INR4 crores to INR5 crores for the rest of the year... next year onwards... another INR12 crores additional depreciation next year.
This 10% will scale to 100% acceptance at the maker level in the next 12 months.
We believe we would have concept the entire transaction acceptance part of the platform by the end of the financial year.
When I come back to you and talk to you in November, all will be live.

We have 3 large installations, which should be live from now up to the end of the year, which is Carnelian, ASK and Neo... Oaklane, sorry... which are expected to -- they will definitely go live before December.
11 unique SIFs have launched, 3 or 4 more will launch.
We do expect CAMSRep at least on a final quarter basis to become EBITDA positive.
You will see the second tranche of this get executed about a year from now... it will certainly happen in about 12 months' time.
We will have our first signed contracts shortly... hopefully, when we come back to you, I will have something meaningful to report and share with you in a quarter from now.

We are projecting a flat revenue for KRA in FY27 on a base of about INR42-43 crores: ~INR8 crores price-down impact, ~INR3 crores upside from NSE KRA, and the remaining ~INR5 crores gap made up through natural growth and new logo wins.
In a bad quarter, EBITDA margin will be less than 45%; in a good quarter, it will be around 46-47%.
Non-MF revenue is currently about INR60-65 crores a quarter, and I'll not be surprised in 3 years if it is INR100 crores a quarter.

We have about 8 additional SIFs which are either licensed from a product perspective or have made announcements and will get licensed soon; launches will happen between May, June, July, August or maybe even faster, but certainly within those 4 months.
We are expecting that almost 40,000 to 50,000 Indian companies will end up buying this (DPDP compliance product) in the next year, 1.5 years.

This was envisaged to be a 4-5 year project; my advice would be to strictly think of it as a 5-year project; about 2 years are done, and you will see significantly increasing momentum as we move forward.

guidance_ledger.metric: Data lake / transaction origination platform go-live
guidance_ledger.statement: The data lake will go live again in 1H of this year; the data warehouse is ready to go, both of these within the next 3 or 4 months.

risk_register.risk: KRA industry rate revision (~29-30% rates down effective 1 April) causing revenue decline
risk_register.note: First quarter of invoicing under new structure; expected to be not a large impacting item and to recover from Q2.

risk_register.risk: Rising cloud/data center/hardware costs due to hyperscaler AI demand
risk_register.note: Costs becoming expensive faster than expected, could partly offset AI/automation productivity gains.

risk_register.risk: AUM growth muted in April-May-June due to market conditions
risk_register.note: July has been much better, AUM nearing INR60 lakh crore versus muted Q1 months.

risk_register.risk: Non-asset-based MF revenue decline (OPE reduction, transaction reduction, NFO decline, wound-down NSE arrangement)
risk_register.note: This component does not keep pace with AUM growth; transaction count up ~20% YoY but revenue down due to digital vs paper transaction mix.
Adopted more in fintech/lending than capital markets segment.

risk_register.risk: Risk of moving too fast on AI-led automation
risk_register.note: Company retains manual checker despite capability to convert 100% of transaction acceptance to AI today, citing risk of blindly automating.

risk_register.risk: External macro volatility (Middle East-related turmoil) impacting AUM
risk_register.note: AUM fell from a peak of INR58.5 lakh crores to INR55.1 lakh crores during the quarter due to external turmoil, particularly in March.

risk_register.risk: Passive fund mix shift compressing yields
risk_register.note: Yield compression of <1% QoQ attributed to mix shift toward passives (which have inherently low yields), not to declines in individual asset-class yields; passives are less than 10% of AUM so impact seen as muted going forward.

risk_register.risk: AMC fee reduction (3-5 bps) potentially passed to RTA
risk_register.note: Some AMCs may face a 3-5 bps fee cut and could seek to pass some of that to distributors/RTAs; no concrete discussions yet with CAMS, and any impact expected to be muted.

Uniform 20% KRA price cut effective 1 April industry-wide, following prior partial remissions for small-value consumers; expected to cost CAMS ~INR8 crores in FY27, offset by NSE KRA upside and new logo growth to keep KRA revenue flat.

risk_register.risk: Slowdown in demat/broking/F&O account opening affecting KRA
risk_register.note: Geopolitical and market conditions led to slower new folio openings; the associated revenue hit has already been absorbed in FY26.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory shift toward unified 'One KYC' (CKYC) potentially disintermediating KRA
risk_register.note: Finance Ministry has discussed a unified KYC framework linked to CKYC for all financial sectors; management believes CKYC does not yet replicate KRA's 2-leg verification process and expects any full transition to take considerable time.
Compliance deadline set at 1 May next year; Board setup in progress; company built ConsenPro to address this and expects decisive market action in coming quarters as the deadline approaches.

risk_register.risk: Slow AMC/NFO launches affecting non-MF product ramp
risk_register.note: Not every licensed AMC/app has launched yet; some have deferred launches, affecting Alternatives and other new product scale-up.

themes.label: Non-MF diversification
themes.note: Non-MF revenue grew 28%+ YoY led by Pay (~70%) and Alternatives (mid-20s AUM growth), with KRA a drag this quarter due to repricing but expected to recover from Q2.

themes.label: MF yield/mix stability
themes.note: No yield decline quarter-on-quarter in asset-based revenue; company has come out of the compression reported in 4Q'25/1Q'26, with residual impact for rest of year expected to be insignificant.

themes.label: Margin sustainability via automation
themes.note: Cost increase kept below 7% YoY excluding depreciation; headcount down ~85 YoY and ~225 QoQ; management guides ~1-1.5% annual margin expansion from productivity.

themes.label: KRA industry repricing
themes.note: 1 April rate revision (~29-30% rates down) drove KRA revenue decline in Q1, dragging non-MF EBITDA margin to 13% from 17%+; recovery expected from Q2.

themes.label: Rearchitecture/AI-led productivity
themes.note: 4 of 8 transaction types live on new platform with 10% of gross payload AI-processed, targeting 100% maker-level acceptance in 12 months; rising cloud/hardware costs partly offset gains.

themes.label: Regulatory change management (DPDP/KYC)
themes.note: ConsentPro built in-house for consent management across MF/KRA/CRA/pension/insurance repository; first signed contracts expected shortly across 7-8 early clients.

themes.label: Market share gains vs industry
themes.note: Equity AUM growth, equity net sales growth, and live SIP account growth all outperformed industry; market share held at 67.2%.

key_takeaways: EBITDA grew over 18% year-on-year to get to INR183 crores. This is our highest ever number.
EBITDA margin expansion, 270 basis points... from 43.7% a year back to 46.4%.
Operating revenue grew 11.5% to INR395 crore... non-MF businesses, they grew collectively over 28%.
MF AUM grew just under 15% year-on-year to be about INR56 lakh crores... Market share stayed at about 67.2%.

KRA was a bit of a story in the first quarter... a rate revision starting 1st April about 29%, 30% rates down... slightly revenue down quarter. We expect that from the second quarter, things will look -- well, better.
We ended the quarter with a very comfortable INR980 crores almost cash balance, and the Board has declared INR2.5 interim dividend for the Q1.
11 unique SIFs have launched, 3 or 4 more will launch... accumulated to about just in excess of INR12,000 crores now, almost 50,000 investors.
We will demonstrate that [headcount decline]... expected to have a 4% to 5% down impact in the financial year... We are about 2%, 3% down already.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: EBITDA margin scaled back to highest ever despite flat MF revenue, driven by cost optimization and operational efficiency/automation.
Cost increase kept well within control target of 11% YoY guided earlier; actual was 9% including depreciation, 7.8% excluding depreciation.
Margin creep from 45% to 46.5% YoY attributed to diversification into non-MF and cost discipline.
Non-MF profitability improved from earlier 12-13% range to upwards of 16% this quarter, expected to reach 20% margin by end of next year and eventually 25%.

subsections.label: Margin sustainability discussion
points: Management contends the 46-47% margin level (previously hit ~5 quarters back before dropping to 42% due to price adjustment) is not a one-off but reflects structural automation gains.

Investments have been made in non-money-making businesses (repository, account aggregator, pension, Think Analytics, ConsenPro) over CY22-CY26; standard business architecture is to breakeven near INR14-15 crores annual revenue then contribute to bottom line.
Management does not want to sacrifice right investments merely to optically expand margin by ~1%/year.
Aim for FY27 is to at least retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin levels after absorbing salary increases, other investments, and yield compression (expected muted).

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Board declared final dividend of INR4 per share (subject to shareholder confirmation), translating to INR305 crores disbursement for the year.
Company retained 35% of profits (not distributed as dividend) while maintaining 39% ROE, positioning it top of market.

subsections.label: Cost/headcount outlook
points: Company strength grew by ~100-120 people YoY even as 11% revenue growth was achieved, with reduction seen in core MF operations headcount (~70 headcount drop in MF), offset by increases in risk/compliance and rearchitecture hiring.
Rearchitecture hiring (~200 engineers) accounted for more than 100 of the incremental headcount; excluding this, overall MF headcount was flat YoY.
FY27 target: sub-5% employee cost growth and overall sub-9% expense growth (aiming lower).

subsections.label: CAMSPay
points: Payment Aggregator (PA, now licensed) and Payment Gateway (PG) both delivered ~23% YoY growth, continuing to add new clients and scale the PG offering.

Non-MF share of CAMSPay revenue is much more than 50%, driven by cards business; PG credit card business (mainly for insurance companies and some loan repayments) grew from near zero a year ago to ~25% of quarterly revenue.
Most non-MF CAMSPay revenue derives from insurance and EMIs for NBFCs; exact split to be shared separately.

subsections.label: AIF
points: Strong quarter with revenue growth over 25% YoY; AUM crossed INR3 lakh crores; 50% share of outsourced market maintained.
44 new full-service mandates added, including 14 new logos — almost one new logo per week or faster.
Not every AMC/app with a license has launched yet; some have deferred launches.

subsections.label: KRA
points: Business underwent several 'moments of recurring' over the past year due to industry-wide shift as investors moved to direct participation via demat/broking accounts, plus geopolitical impact on new folio openings.
Despite this, KRA delivered 28% YoY revenue growth for the quarter; added a couple of active large accounts (brokerages/DPs) and expects to continue gaining share.
NSE KRA acquisition (clump sale, acquired January) integrated smoothly with no service issues or social media complaints; added 13-14 lakh new PANs.

Industry took a uniform 20% price cut on KRA fees effective 1st April, driven by industry desire to broaden franchise to lower-value/non-salaried consumers (e.g., 'choti SIP' campaign); a voluntary, industry-level decision made after dialogue with regulator.

FY27 KRA revenue expected to be flat: base of INR42-43 crores, minus ~INR8 crores price-down impact, plus INR3 crores NSE KRA upside, with the remaining ~INR5 crores gap made up via natural growth/new logo wins.

KRA architecture enriched with daily demise reconciliation and disability records; conducts full 2-leg verification (name match, face match, DOB, address from source via DigiLocker/UIDAI) versus CKYC's single-leg process, seen as a competitive moat versus potential 'One KYC' regulatory push.

subsections.label: Repository / Insurance
points: Rep delivered 6% YoY revenue growth for the quarter.
Bima Central doubled its active user base.

LIC started policy issuance in demat format (largely digital origination); agreement signed March 2025, integration took until Feb/March 2026; expected to add a new dimension to insurance demat industry within this year as other insurers follow LIC's lead.
IR (Insurance Repository) market share expanded to 40%.

subsections.label: Non-MF growth outlook breakdown
points: FY27 incremental non-MF revenue growth of INR45-50 crores expected across businesses even with flat KRA revenue: Payments ~INR20 crores, AIF ~INR7-8 crores, Rep ~INR7-8 crores, and the balance ~INR15 crores from AA, TSP, pension, and new lines like ConsenPro and GIFT City.
Management does not want to chase too many new product lines where it lacks 'right to win'; ConsenPro and a device (unified payments+KYC) adjacency are the only new products being pursued.

subsections.label: Rearchitecture program
points: Program is building a brand-new cloud-native platform for entire MF service delivery, hosted on Google Cloud, using a feature-by-feature/module-by-module rollout approach rather than a big-bang build, to reduce execution risk.

Of 9 significant modules, the transaction origination module (handling inflows from exchanges, banks, websites, partners, fintechs, paper, branches) is fully built and now launching to market for broad consumption by thousands of integrating partners; includes better rules engine and real-time rejection/remediation capability, reducing net transaction shrinkage.

Data lake / data warehouse (on-prem data migrated AMC-by-AMC to BigQuery on Google Cloud) is technically ready and will go live in H1 of this year; enables MIS, insights, analytics and natural-language queries for CAMS staff, AMC clients, and other partners.
Other modules (payments and settlements, transaction posting with exchanges, internal accounting) will go live progressively as built.

Smaller internal-only automations already live include AI-based form data extraction that removes the 'maker' step in a two-person maker-checker process for ~1 million monthly physical forms; live in production for ~2 months with no beta/testing issues, to be deepened over time.

Project envisaged as 4-5 years; company advises thinking of it strictly as a 5-year project; roughly 2 years completed with momentum expected to increase going forward; company is running ~3-4% behind overall trajectory versus plan, described as normal for IT projects of this nature.

Benefits will show up in obvious metrics: flat/declining headcount with rising revenue, revenue per headcount, lower complaints per transaction ratio (already significantly ahead of industry despite 1.5-2x transaction base), fewer frauds and risk incidents/charges in the P&L.

subsections.label: KYC/Face-match technology
points: Company differentiates via proprietary face-reading, video-reading, and face-match technology enabling a 10-minute KYC process, positioned as unique in the market.

subsections.label: SIF product category
points: SIF (product category announced early 2025) went live September/October 2025; considered set to become a very relevant competitive new product category for the industry and for CAMS.

subsections.label: GIFT City retail funds
points: Retail fund launches in GIFT City not yet a major AUM story, but seen as compelling for domestic investors wanting site-asset exposure without ETF constraints (some of which have hit ceilings).

subsections.label: ConsenPro (DPDP compliance product)
points: Built to address the DPDP (Digital Personal Data Protection) bill compliance requirement, which management likens loosely to India's version of GDPR, now being contemplated across industries with financial services expected to be among the biggest consumers.

Company built in-house expertise rather than buying it externally; product includes a consenting mechanism, full data discovery tool, and regulatory reporting/consulting capabilities, built inside Think360.
Was originally a captive/internal offering leveraging existing data discovery and consulting practice (evolved via MF Central and account aggregator/AI work); now packaged as a commercial offering.

DPDP compliance deadline set at 1 May next year (Board setup in progress); market inquiry currently concentrated in financial services, less so in hospitality/airlines/retail/food delivery, though expected to broaden.
CAMS may hold processor status in several business segments and fiduciary status in one or more (including KRA, repository, RTA).

subsections.label: MF market position
points: MF AUM growth in line with industry at 21% YoY, holding 68% overall market share.
AUM decline from earlier Q4 peak of INR58.5 lakh crores to INR55.1 lakh crores attributed to impact of events in the Middle East.
Equity assets share grew from 66% to 67% YoY (~90 bps, approx 1%), growing faster than industry.

Historically CAMS held ~60% share of active equity market and ~80% of fixed income market 4-5 years back (pre-passives popularity); equity share has climbed ~1%/year to current 67%, viewed as a durable, foundational trend rather than a one-quarter event given equity is the most retailized, sticky, remunerative, and growth-oriented segment.
Equity net sales share grew from 71% to 76% quarter-on-quarter — considered the most formative metric given it reflects real money flows.

subsections.label: SIP & new business momentum
points: New SIP registrations (1.26 crore) significantly above typical baseline of 1.0-1.1 crore/quarter, growing 46% YoY vs industry's 27%.
Annual SIP registrations of 4.7 crore, up 17% over FY25 — almost 2x industry growth.
SIP collections crossed INR20,000 crores in March alone; quarterly collections of ~INR59,000 crores grew 17% YoY vs industry's 4%, driving share gain from 57% to 64%.

subsections.label: New logo strategy
points: Strategy focuses on scale-play logo wins (brand + scale fit) rather than competing on price; new AMC licenses (Neo and Oaklane) fit this scale-play philosophy.
31 total licensed domestic AMC clients, though not all are live yet.

subsections.label: Transaction/productivity metrics
points: Financial transaction volumes reached 107 crores, growing 20%, viewed as a core revitalization/penetration metric.
Over the last 3 years, transactions grew 27% while headcount grew only 6-7%, reflecting productivity gains; this trend is expected to accentuate as the rearchitecture platform scales.

subsections.label: External environment
points: January and February were classified as 'normal' months, but March saw significant impact from broader environmental/market conditions, affecting AUM (Middle East-related turmoil cited).
MF AUM growth was muted (~1%+) during the quarter due to this external volatility.

subsections.label: Yield/mix risk
points: AUM mix shift toward passives (which grew faster than active funds in the quarter) is driving yield compression, though individual asset-class yields (including passives) have not themselves declined — the effect is purely a mix effect (~0.9% impact cited).
Passive AUM yields are described as already extremely low with little room for renegotiation; less than 10% of overall AUM is in passives currently, limiting materiality.

AMCs are reportedly facing a 3-5 bps fee reduction that some may seek to pass on to distributors; CAMS has had no concrete negotiations on this yet but does not rule out future discussions; any impact expected to be muted given CAMS believes price-value equation is already balanced.
Some midsized AMC contracts are coming up for renewal during the year; no material yield decline expected from these.

Historical yield decline benchmark of 3-3.5%/year cited as a conservative planning figure, though management aims for and expects a figure below that (less than 3%) for FY27, based on equity mix staying near 54-55% and factoring some growth from larger AMC customers plus midsized AMC discussions.

subsections.label: KRA industry pricing pressure
points: Industry-wide 20% KRA price cut effective 1 April, adopted voluntarily at an industry level (with regulator dialogue) to reduce cost friction for onboarding lower-value/non-salaried consumers.

KRA business experienced multiple 'moments of recurring' over the past year due to a broader industry shift as investors moved toward direct equity participation via demat/broking accounts, plus geopolitical effects reducing new folio openings, and now the price cut itself; despite this, revenue growth remained positive due to share gains.

subsections.label: Regulatory/compliance risk (DPDP, One KYC)
points: DPDP Act compliance deadline (1 May next year) approaching; company preparing governance (Board) and commercial response (ConsenPro) ahead of expected market-wide decisive action in coming quarters.

Government/Finance Ministry discussions around a unified 'One KYC' (CKYC-linked) framework for all financial sectors could, in theory, reduce KRA's differentiated verification value; management says CKYC does not yet fully subsume KRA's 2-leg verification (name match, face match, DOB, address-from-source authentication) and expects this transition, if it happens, to take considerable time ('Rome wasn't built in a day').
