subsections.label: FY27 productivity outlook
points: Management expects FY27 revenue growth to be achieved on a falling headcount (choosing not to backfill some roles), a step-up from the flat-headcount productivity seen in FY26.
Rearchitecture benefits (data lake, transaction origination platform going live) expected to compound productivity over the next 3-4 months and beyond.

subsections.label: Non-MF growth outlook
points: Management is confident of at least 20% non-MF growth in FY27 even with flat KRA revenue, driven by Payments (~INR20 crores), AIF (~INR7-8 crores), Rep (~INR7-8 crores), and remaining ~INR15 crores from AA/TSP/pension/ConsenPro/GIFT City.
Company does not intend to chase many new product lines outside areas where it believes it has a 'right to win'; ConsenPro and a payments+KYC device adjacency are the primary new initiatives.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Aim is to at least retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin for FY27 after absorbing salary increases (effective Q2), other investments, and expected yield compression (which will be much less severe than last year's price-adjustment episode).
Company will not provide a specific EBITDA margin number, preferring to guide within its historical range (45% in a bad quarter, 46-47% in a good quarter).

guidance_ledger.statement: We believe we have absolute confidence in growing at least 20% on the non-MF side, even assuming no growth in KRA.

We are projecting a flat revenue for KRA in FY27 on a base of about INR42-43 crores: ~INR8 crores price-down impact, ~INR3 crores upside from NSE KRA, and the remaining ~INR5 crores gap made up through natural growth and new logo wins.
Our aim is to at least retain what we are in Q4 in terms of EBITDA margins for next year, after absorbing cost increases and yield compression.
In a bad quarter, EBITDA margin will be less than 45%; in a good quarter, it will be around 46-47%.

guidance_ledger.horizon: end of next year and onwards
guidance_ledger.statement: We are hoping that we'll get to 20% and onwards to 25% EBITDA margin for the non-MF business.
We are looking at a sub-5% growth in employee cost and overall definitely sub-9% growth in expenses; we'd like to make it a little lesser than that.
In FY27, we will see all the revenue growth on falling headcount; some backfill we may choose not to do.
Historically 3%-3.5% yield decline per year, but our aim will always be to build it much lesser than that; going by last quarter, we are on track to have a number lesser than that.
Non-MF revenue is currently about INR60-65 crores a quarter, and I'll not be surprised in 3 years if it is INR100 crores a quarter.

We have about 8 additional SIFs which are either licensed from a product perspective or have made announcements and will get licensed soon; launches will happen between May, June, July, August or maybe even faster, but certainly within those 4 months.
We are expecting that almost 40,000 to 50,000 Indian companies will end up buying this (DPDP compliance product) in the next year, 1.5 years.

This was envisaged to be a 4-5 year project; my advice would be to strictly think of it as a 5-year project; about 2 years are done, and you will see significantly increasing momentum as we move forward.

guidance_ledger.metric: Data lake / transaction origination platform go-live
guidance_ledger.statement: The data lake will go live again in 1H of this year; the data warehouse is ready to go, both of these within the next 3 or 4 months.

risk_register.risk: External macro volatility (Middle East-related turmoil) impacting AUM
risk_register.note: AUM fell from a peak of INR58.5 lakh crores to INR55.1 lakh crores during the quarter due to external turmoil, particularly in March.

risk_register.risk: Passive fund mix shift compressing yields
risk_register.note: Yield compression of <1% QoQ attributed to mix shift toward passives (which have inherently low yields), not to declines in individual asset-class yields; passives are less than 10% of AUM so impact seen as muted going forward.

risk_register.risk: AMC fee reduction (3-5 bps) potentially passed to RTA
risk_register.note: Some AMCs may face a 3-5 bps fee cut and could seek to pass some of that to distributors/RTAs; no concrete discussions yet with CAMS, and any impact expected to be muted.

Uniform 20% KRA price cut effective 1 April industry-wide, following prior partial remissions for small-value consumers; expected to cost CAMS ~INR8 crores in FY27, offset by NSE KRA upside and new logo growth to keep KRA revenue flat.

risk_register.risk: Slowdown in demat/broking/F&O account opening affecting KRA
risk_register.note: Geopolitical and market conditions led to slower new folio openings; the associated revenue hit has already been absorbed in FY26.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory shift toward unified 'One KYC' (CKYC) potentially disintermediating KRA
risk_register.note: Finance Ministry has discussed a unified KYC framework linked to CKYC for all financial sectors; management believes CKYC does not yet replicate KRA's 2-leg verification process and expects any full transition to take considerable time.
Compliance deadline set at 1 May next year; Board setup in progress; company built ConsenPro to address this and expects decisive market action in coming quarters as the deadline approaches.

risk_register.risk: Slow AMC/NFO launches affecting non-MF product ramp
risk_register.note: Not every licensed AMC/app has launched yet; some have deferred launches, affecting Alternatives and other new product scale-up.

themes.label: Non-MF diversification
themes.note: Non-MF revenue grew ~25% YoY (24.5%), now 15.3% of enterprise revenue, with management confident of sustaining >20% growth in FY27 across Payments, AIF, Rep and new lines.

themes.label: MF yield/mix stability
themes.note: Yields held stable QoQ with <1% compression driven by passive mix shift, not individual asset-class declines; management expects <3% yield decline in FY27, better than historical 3-3.5% trend.

themes.label: Margin sustainability via automation
themes.note: EBITDA margin climbed back to 46.5% on flat MF revenue, driven by cost optimization and automation; management argues this reflects structural, not one-off, gains, targeting flat-to-lower headcount with growing revenue in FY27.

themes.label: KRA industry repricing
themes.note: Industry-wide 20% KRA price cut effective 1 April to broaden franchise to lower-value consumers; expected ~INR8 crore hit offset by NSE KRA integration upside and new logo growth to keep KRA revenue flat in FY27.

themes.label: Rearchitecture/AI-led productivity
themes.note: Cloud-native rearchitecture program (~2 of 5 years complete, ~200 engineers) delivering transaction origination platform and data lake going live, alongside AI-based form processing, driving flat-to-declining headcount with rising revenue and transactions.

themes.label: Regulatory change management (DPDP/KYC)
themes.note: DPDP compliance deadline set for 1 May next year prompting launch of commercial ConsenPro offering; potential 'One KYC'/CKYC unification discussed but management sees KRA's 2-leg verification as a durable moat.

themes.label: Market share gains vs industry
themes.note: CAMS outpaced industry across AUM growth (21%), equity AUM share (67%, up from 66%), SIP registrations (46% vs 27% industry), and SIP collections share (64%, up from 57%).

key_takeaways: We posted our highest ever quarterly revenue in Q4 '26.
We grew non-MF revenue close to 25% year-on-year. You know our promise has been 20%.
The MF business revenue was almost flat. It just grew about 0.5%.
Absolute EBITDA scaled back to the highest ever... we've climbed up to about INR183 crores now.
Percentage EBITDA climbed back to just in excess of 46%, about 46.5%.

AUM at INR55.1 lakh crores is obviously significantly lower than the INR58.5 lakh crores that we achieved at some time in 4Q, but because of the impact of what's happening in the Middle East, it came down.
Equity net sales... our share grew from 71% in the past quarter to 76%.
New SIP registrations went up to about 1.26 crores... grew about 46%. Industry grew 27%.
SIP collections crossed the INR20,000 crores milestone in the month of March, grew 25% year-on-year and almost touched INR59,000 crores for the quarter.
KRA now decisively be the number 2 player, leapfrog from being number 3 about 1.5 years back to number 2.
We are expecting to hold KRA revenue in FY '27 after all the puts and takes.
We will get to a 20% margin by the end of next year... for non-MF EBITDA.
pressing_questions: So Ram, just a follow-up on the yield cost -- yield question. One was that because there is a mix effect, there's a hit on the overall yields. Does it allow you in any way to kind of have a stronger bargaining power when it comes to the yield negotiation on the active book?

Firstly, just on this renegotiations with AMCs, there is a 3 to 5 basis points impact, what we've heard from all the AMCs that is likely to come, and they have indicated they'll be passing it on to distributors. But any negotiation that has happened with you guys on the commission changes -- sorry, on the RTA fee changes that should come through because of that change?

Structurally, we've been talking about the 3.5% to 4% decline in yields every year. Should we start thinking about this for FY '27 and FY '28 basis and that should be the way? Or how should we think about the yield drop on a regular basis?

But post that, again, we kind of -- there is a renegotiation or there are some investments that come in, and then we dropped back to 42%, 43%, 44%. So at this point of -- at this juncture, what gives you confidence that this is more of a sustainable margin trajectory than what we've seen in the past?
Do you see any impact on the KYC business because of the changes that are expected from April 1 that were implemented from April 1st? And would that impact profitability in the near term?

Firstly, sir, just on the margins, you did mention you don't see any significant yield pressure, but you also said that the new TR regulation for some of the large AMCs are underway. So if this were to kind of fructify, the impact will be retrospective starting from 1st of April. Is that correct or this will be more like a retrospective starting from 1st of July?
What is the kind of pressure that we are going to see on the KRA business? What sort of pricing decline are we seeing? And how is this determined?

I think Finance Ministry and we have off late have spoken about one KYC thing for all financial sectors, including capital markets. So does it change the conduct of the business, whether the pricing because it will be CKYC linked?

quarters.summary: Ather Energy reported its first-ever positive EBITDA quarter (Q1 FY27) driven by strong demand tailwinds (e-2W penetration surge, policy push, fuel availability concerns), despite a sharp commodity cost escalation that hit gross margins. Management guided that AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase-1 (Aurangabad) go-live is tracking for later this calendar year, taking total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units p.a., with an EL platform launch imminent (unveiling at Ather Community Day, 29 Aug) and a possible AURIC Phase-2 fast-track (to 14.2 lakh units p.a.) funded via a Rs. 2,500 crore total fundraise (Rs. 1,300 crore QIP completed + Rs. 1,200 crore preference issue pending). Commodity headwinds are expected to persist for another 100-200 bps before potentially cooling, but price hikes (ASP up to Rs. 1.61 lakh) are expected to largely offset further RM increases into Q2 FY27.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Structural gains (price hikes, SKU management, AtherStack Pro attach rates, cost reductions) drove AGM improvement, expected to survive even the current commodity crisis.
Near-term commodity inflation more than canceled out structural gains, leading to a 5.6% drop in gross margins in Q1 FY27.
ASP increase to Rs. 1.61 lakh occurred by end of Q1, so full benefit will only flow through in Q2.
Bulk of ASP increase came from price hikes (100% margin accretive); roughly one-third from improved SKU management, of which about 25% flows back into gross margin.
First-ever positive EBITDA quarter driven by tight fixed-cost discipline, particularly on marketing and sales, despite strong demand that could have supported higher spend.

subsections.label: Cost structure outlook
points: Management does not view Q1 cost discipline as exceptional; company has historically run a tight ship and set cautious internal messaging for FY27 after a 'blowout' FY26.

As AURIC ramps up, associated costs will rise but may be partly capitalized initially, with P&L impact expected from Q4 onward; volume growth is expected to offset the incremental cost, limiting net impact.
For Q2 FY27, price hikes already implemented are expected to largely offset further commodity increases, without fully capturing upside until commodities cool.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Rs. 2,500 crore total fundraise (Rs.1,300cr QIP + Rs.1,200cr preference issue) intended to fund capacity fast-tracking (own and suppliers'), accelerate new product launches, and provide balance sheet resilience against commodity/supply crises.
Fundraise sizing also factored in potential AURIC Phase-2 fast-track requirement.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Four macro shifts underpinning demand surge: (1) transport electrification as a national agenda championed by the Prime Minister; (2) strong policy support (PM E-DRIVE, Delhi EV Policy) driving consumer confidence; (3) availability concerns on petrol/diesel shifting consumer sentiment toward electricity as a more reliable commodity; (4) rising petrol prices improving total cost of ownership (TCO) for EVs.
Colloquial sentiment shift from 'ghar me ek petrol gaadi to honi padegi' to 'ghar me ek electric gaadi to honi padegi' captures the changing consumer mindset.
Retail has outpaced wholesale for another quarter, driving urgency to ramp supply and capacity.
Company estimates it could have sold an incremental 13,000-15,000 units per month beyond the ~30,000 units retailed on average in Q1, indicating unmet demand.
Dealer inventory has fallen sharply (14 days to 3 days) reflecting tight supply relative to demand.
Existing stores meeting only 50-60% of demand; new store expansion has been slowed deliberately until supply catches up.

subsections.label: Customer profile / financing
points: Management does not believe the underlying customer profile has shifted toward motorcycle buyers despite ASP crossing Rs 1.6 lakh; still largely the same scooter buyer, aided by limited supply pushing SKU mix upward.
Continued success of retail finance is helping customers absorb higher costs.
TCO gains from electric vehicles are becoming a powerful factor, with customers more willing to pay a premium given enormous petrol savings, aided by fuel-availability concerns.

subsections.label: Volume/registration dynamics
points: Growth achieved despite production constraints and supply challenges early in the quarter (labor crisis, West Asia war-induced crisis) that kept April production soft.
Retail (registrations) outpaced wholesale growth (102% vs 81%), reflecting supply-constrained wholesale relative to underlying retail demand.

subsections.label: Non-vehicle revenue
points: AtherStack Pro (software) is the largest non-vehicle revenue contributor and has performed better than anticipated.
Growth potential also lies in accessory sales (quietly compounding, no public color yet, may be disclosed in future quarters) and service revenues (a function of fleet size).
Service revenues currently at 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for established two-wheeler businesses, indicating long growth runway over the next decade.
Short-term non-vehicle revenue support came from price increases on AtherStack Pro; medium-term growth expected from accessories; long-term compounding expected from service and spares.

subsections.label: Product mix / platform fungibility
points: EL platform expected to primarily cannibalize Rizta demand rather than the 450X, which is unlikely to be impacted by EL's launch.

If Rizta demand surprises on the upside, company may look to build Rizta on the EL platform in the mid-to-long term, since AURIC is purpose-built for the EL platform; short-term Rizta capacity remains well covered out of Hosur (35,000/month).
EL attach rate for AtherStack Pro cautiously guided at least 75%, with hope for higher, despite EL likely being at a lower price point.

subsections.label: EL platform launch
points: EL scooter platform (unveiled last year) is now under production; high-volume trials, homologation and SOP already completed; production has begun at Hosur, to run there for a few months before scaling out of Aurangabad.

Brand name for EL platform to be unveiled shortly (not yet disclosed at call time); product to be formally unveiled at Ather Community Day on 29 August in Bengaluru (KTPO, Whitefield), themed 'A New Dawn of Magic'.
Ather Community Day will also include announcements on the software stack, charging infrastructure, and other ownership products.
EL platform expected to be a major driver of future demand and cost reduction, lowering cost structures in coming quarters.
EL likely to depress overall ASP slightly as it scales, being priced/positioned differently, though management expects margins overall to remain fine.

subsections.label: Motorcycle segment / Zenith platform
points: Multiple OEMs preparing to launch electric motorcycles in the next 12-18 months; Ather is laser-focused on EL for now and does not intend to pioneer the motorcycle segment immediately.
Company will watch market response before a maiden motorcycle launch, expected to be more than a year away, probably two years plus.

subsections.label: Geo launch strategy for EL
points: EL launch expected to be initially skewed toward Middle India / northern markets given strong customer pull for favorably priced variants there, before expanding nationally.
Launch geo sequencing likely different from Rizta's (which started in Middle India, then Rest of India, then South India); EL may start with Rest of India, then Middle India, then South India.

subsections.label: Capacity ramp-up
points: Monthly production ramped from 24,000 units in April to 28,000 in May to 31,000 in June, reaching near-100% utilization at Hosur by quarter-end.
Ramp-up occurred despite navigating a labor crisis and West Asia war-induced supply crisis at the start of the quarter.

AURIC (Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar) Factory 3.0 Phase-1 progress: assembly line already set up, warehouse and utilities under construction, paint shop under trial; tracking for go-live later this calendar year.

AURIC equipment installation ending in the next couple of months; trial production expected to start from the festive period; reliable daily output expected throughout Q4, from January; ramp-up to 42,000 units/month expected to take 4-5 months from trial start, finishing near end of Q4 or into Q1 (possibly spilling into early FY28).
Big step-up in capacity (rather than linear increases) expected to hold steady for a few quarters before any need to ramp to Phase-2.

subsections.label: AURIC Phase-2 planning
points: Land for Aurangabad was secured with larger capacity in mind, with some common facilities already planned for Phase-2, and many approvals already in place, so Phase-2 should take less time than Phase-1.
Company has not yet started investment in Phase-2 but sees a capturable opportunity if current demand trajectory continues; total fundraise sizing considered this potential fast-track.
Management wants to see Phase-1 go live first before committing more firmly to Phase-2 timeline; expects more clarity in a quarter or two.
Would not rule out material fast-tracking of Phase-2 if demand momentum from EL/current trends continues over the coming couple of quarters.

subsections.label: Capacity allocation / fungibility
points: AURIC is fully dedicated to the EL platform; Hosur has some fungibility and additional capacity that can be flexibly allocated between EL (up to 18,000/month) and existing Rizta/450X production (up to 35,000/month total at Hosur), but the two cannot simply be added together due to line capacity limits.
EL total capacity potential of 60,000/month = 42,000/month from AURIC Phase-1 + up to 18,000/month flexible allocation from Hosur.
Allocation between EL and Rizta at Hosur will be decided dynamically based on early demand trajectory.

subsections.label: Regional performance
points: Middle India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha) is the top growth driver, growing 141% in retail YoY, followed by Rest of India at 118%, followed by South India at 76%.
Tier-2/Tier-3 stores have become the biggest volume drivers as company adds more cities and stores there; absolute throughput has become more Tier-3 heavy in recent quarters.
EV penetration has been highest in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets for a while, supporting stronger traffic there.
Roughly a year to a year and a half ago, sales were more evenly split between top 20 cities, next 100 cities, and the long tail; mix has since shifted toward the long tail.

subsections.label: Store network / dealer strategy
points: New store openings have been deliberately slowed in Q1 FY27 since existing stores are only meeting 50-60% of demand; ramping inventory to new stores is not seen as prudent currently.
Company expects to resume a surge in new store openings once EL and AURIC go live (around festive season), at which point it will provide more guidance/color on store expansion metrics.

Store cohorts historically reached operational profitability in five to six months on average (faster than guided to retail partners); given the current demand surge, profitability could occur even faster, potentially within two months.

subsections.label: Supply disruptions
points: Company navigated a labor crisis and West Asia war-induced supply crisis at the start of Q1 FY27, which kept April production/volumes soft.
Dealer inventory levels fell sharply (from 14 days to 3 days), reflecting tight channel stock amid strong demand and constrained supply.

subsections.label: Brand and demand proxies
points: Every demand proxy (industry registrations, inquiries, preorders, brand searches) is inflecting sharply upward, reflecting both category (EV) and Ather-brand-specific demand strength.
Strong pricing power demonstrated by the market absorbing price hikes and by high AtherStack Pro attach rates, reflecting brand quality perception and customer confidence.

subsections.label: Customer demographics
points: No material shift observed in customer profile despite crossing into premium price territory (Rs.1.6 lakh ASP); still largely the traditional scooter buyer rather than a motorcycle buyer switching to scooters.
Retail finance availability and improving perceived TCO (total cost of ownership) advantage of EVs are helping customers absorb higher price points.

subsections.label: Fundraise / capital strategy
points: Rs.1,300 crore QIP recently closed with strong participation from Indian and international funds.
Additional Rs.1,200 crore fundraise via preference issue pending shareholder approval, together totaling Rs.2,500 crore.

Funds intended to fast-track capacity expansion (own and supplier-side), support faster new product launches given market growing faster than anticipated, and provide balance sheet resilience against commodity/supply crises.
Fundraise sizing also considered the potential need to fast-track AURIC Phase-2.

subsections.label: Commodity cost inflation
points: Commodity index has risen 46% over the last 5 quarters; Q1 FY27 saw an escalation across the board that was, in some ways, higher than management's own anticipation.
Management believes there is still some risk of further escalation in the coming months but expects to be near the top of the cycle rather than the bottom.
Residual risk estimated at another 100-200 bps of potential hit if nothing else changes, though there is also a possibility of cooling, which is difficult to predict.
Price hikes already implemented are expected to largely manage any further commodity increases from here, though the 5.6% hit already incurred could only be partly absorbed.

subsections.label: Supply-side disruptions
points: Labor crisis and West Asia war-induced crisis disrupted supply and kept April production soft at the start of Q1 FY27.

subsections.label: Subsidy uncertainty
points: Roughly 15-20% (possibly more) of vehicles sold in Q1 FY27 were without subsidy; company has not yet baked in subsidy for the full quarter.
No clarity yet on whether PM E-DRIVE subsidy will be extended for Q2 FY27 and beyond, though signs of government intent are described as strong.

subsections.label: Capacity constraints
points: Current facilities were running at near-100% utilization, with retail demand growth outpacing wholesale/production, creating urgency to scale supply and capacity.
Even after AURIC Phase-1 (9.2 lakh units p.a.), management believes capacity could become tight again in coming quarters given the current demand trajectory.

subsections.label: Capacity and platform outlook
points: AURIC Phase-1 go-live expected later this calendar year (festive period for trial production), taking total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units p.a.; full ramp-up to 42,000 units/month expected in 4-5 months from trial start, likely finishing near end of Q4 FY27 or spilling into early FY28.
AURIC Phase-2 (potential additional 5 lakh units p.a., total 14.2 lakh) remains in planning stage; firmer timeline/guidance expected in a quarter or two, contingent on demand trajectory holding up.

EL scooter platform commercialization/launch expected imminently, to be unveiled at Ather Community Day on 29 August 2026; combined EL capacity target of 60,000 units/month across Aurangabad and Hosur.
Q1 2028 (by around March, though could spill into early FY28) total capacity guided in the vicinity of ~75,000 units/month, i.e., ~40,000 (Hosur incl. debottlenecking) plus 35,000.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Further commodity cost hit estimated at another 100-200 bps of risk; company confident of managing/absorbing this via already-announced price hikes and EL-driven cost reductions.
Q2 FY27 margins expected to see largely offset commodity pressure due to the full-quarter benefit of the ASP increase to Rs.1.61 lakh (versus partial benefit in Q1).
Structural gains (price hikes, SKU management, cost reductions, AtherStack Pro attach rates) expected to outlast the commodity inflation cycle.

subsections.label: Store expansion outlook
points: No updated specific target for dealer/store additions currently; new store expansion has been slowed deliberately and will resume with a surge once EL and AURIC go live (around festive season), at which point more color/metrics will be provided.

subsections.label: Non-vehicle revenue outlook
points: Accessory sales business has been quietly compounding; more public color to be shared in a few quarters.
Service revenue (currently 2-3% of revenue) has long-term potential to reach levels seen at established 2W players (10-12%) over the next decade.

risk_register.note: Commodity index up 46% over last 5 quarters; Q1 FY27 hit (5.6% gross margin drop) was higher than anticipated; another 100-200 bps of risk seen, though possibly nearing the top of the cycle.

risk_register.risk: Labor crisis / West Asia war-induced supply crisis
risk_register.note: Disrupted supply and kept April production soft at the start of Q1 FY27; company ramped up production month-on-month thereafter.
Roughly 15-20% of Q1 vehicles sold without subsidy; no clarity yet on subsidy status for Q2 and beyond, though signs of extension intent are described as strong.
Facilities running near 100% utilization; retail outpacing wholesale; even post AURIC Phase-1 (9.2 lakh units p.a.) capacity could remain tight if demand trajectory continues.
Difficult to pin down exact ramp-up month to 42,000 units/month; could spill into early FY28.

Global memory cost spike hit FY26 results; company paying more to secure long-term capacity to avoid disruption.

Aluminum content comparable to ICE vehicles; expected to rise further due to the Hormuz crisis; EL platform designed to reduce aluminum dependence.

Hosur facility running at 90-95% utilization, at the edge with little room for error; retail demand running ahead of estimates creating localized ramp-up challenges.
November-December variant-specific constraints resolved; April election-season labor disruption also appears resolved; described as localized, not secular material-access issues.
Management describes an 'extremely volatile macro' with continued short-term cost/supply impact expected.
Outcome of Delhi EV policy uncertain, though broader societal support observed this time versus past mixed-support policies.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: Every demand proxy (registrations, inquiries, preorders, searches) inflecting sharply upward, with registrations up 102% YoY and preorders up 158% YoY.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Commodity index up 46% over 5 quarters, causing a 5.6% gross margin drop in Q1 FY27, with another 100-200 bps of risk flagged ahead.

themes.label: Pricing power
themes.note: ASP raised to Rs.1.61 lakh from Rs.1.5 lakh, absorbed by the market, reflecting strong brand-driven pricing power and margin-accretive price hikes.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: AURIC Phase-1 go-live tracking for later this calendar year (4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units p.a.), with a possible Phase-2 fast-track to 14.2 lakh units p.a.

themes.note: EL scooter already in SOP/production, to be unveiled at Ather Community Day on 29 August, with combined EL capacity target of 60,000 units/month.

themes.note: Ather registration growth (102% YoY) outpacing industry registration growth (68% YoY), alongside strong regional gains led by Middle India (141%).

themes.note: Ather brand searches up 118% versus 75% industry-wide EV searches, with tight fixed-cost (marketing/sales) discipline enabling first-ever positive EBITDA quarter.

key_takeaways: E-two-wheeler penetration is up by 44% at 11% in the two-wheeler industry, and electric penetration in the scooter industry is upwards of, I believe, 25% now.
Industry registrations are up 68% in the last one year, hitting 525k in Q1 FY 2027.
In Q1 FY 2027, we received more than 7 lakh inquiries for our products. Ather preorders... were up 158%, hitting a first-ever seen 1.5 lakh preorders in Q1 FY 2027.
Our wholesale volume grew 81%, from 46,000 units in Q1 FY 2026 to 83,000 units in Q1 FY 2027.
Our current facilities have a max production capacity of 35,000 units, and I am happy to announce that we are almost at 100% utilization as we speak now.
The average sales price of Ather has now hit Rs. 1.61 lakh across the country, up from about Rs. 1.5 lakh as of last quarter.
We saw 94% AtherStack Pro attach rates in Q1 2027.
Net it out, we have landed up at 22.4% AGM for Q1 2027... this led to a 5.6% drop in gross margins.
Our EBITDA came in at a Rs. 9 crore margin for Q1 2027, which is roughly about 0.8%... this is the first time ever we have delivered one.
Go-live of AURIC will take our total capacity up from 4.2 lakh units to 9.2 lakh units later this calendar year.
With AURIC Phase-2, we can incrementally add another 5 lakh annual capacity, taking our total capacity up to 14.2 lakh units in the coming time.

Recently, we finished closure of our Rs. 1,300 crore QIP a few weeks ago... We are also in the midst of seeking shareholder approval and closing a fundraise of another Rs. 1,200 crores via preference issue, leading to a total fundraise of Rs. 2,500 crores.
pressing_questions: Are you seeing a similar 5%-6% further commodity headwind that you saw in this quarter? Are you thinking more like it will be stable at these levels and hopefully come down at a later part of the year?
Is this a new baseline [for employee and other expenses] and then EL helps us? Because I think when the new capacity comes in, these costs will go up, right?
Are you expecting to hit a full ramp-up in AURIC phase one by March? Is that something which will happen sometime in fiscal year 2028?
What is happening on the PM E-DRIVE subsidy and the price hikes that you have taken, have they been able to cover up for the cost increases when we look at Q2 and beyond?
Any thought given to AURIC Phase-2. Is it possible to bring it earlier if the demand momentum continues like this, especially with the new product launch?
On the acceleration of Phase-2, is there a timeline that you can put that how soon can it be done if you had to do at AURIC?
How do you see the ramp-up of production happening [at AURIC Phase One]? While the plant starts in November, how do you see the ramp-up there?

quarters.summary: Ather closed FY'26 with strong volume growth (up ~66% YoY) driven by Rizta, doubled store count and improved AGM/EBITDA, but flags near-term margin pressure from a commodity supercycle (rare earth magnets, memory chips, lithium-ion battery costs) that will only be partly offset by price hikes; the company expects EL platform launch and AURIC Factory 3.0 capacity to be the key growth and cost-reduction drivers from H2 FY'27 onward, with new capacity contributing to topline before end of FY'27 (most likely Q4).

subsections.label: Unit economics improvement
points: AGM improved by about 5 percentage points with subsidy, from 19% to 24%.
Without subsidy, margin improvement was sharper, from 12% AGM to 21% AGM.
Driven by a consistent reduction in COGS, which reduced by about 9 percentage points through FY26.

Supported by strong performance of AtherStack and Pro-Packs; Pro-Pack attach rates held steady and even rose despite quarterly volumes compounding from 43,000 to 81,000 units, with Q4 FY26 hitting an all-time-high 93% attach rate.

subsections.label: EBITDA drivers
points: EBITDA improvement driven by two factors: continuously improving unit economics and strong operating leverage.
About three-fourths of cost below gross margin is fundamentally fixed in nature, making operating leverage very powerful.
EBITDA losses improved 1500-1600 bps from FY25 to FY26, with Q4 alone showing a 2000 bps improvement, from -23% to -2%.

subsections.label: Cost pressure and pricing
points: Commodity price inflation (rare earth magnets, memory, lithium-ion battery costs) is expected to pressure margins in the short term.

Only a small part of the inflation has been passed on till now due to procurement management and stock-piling; company expects to push some inflation but expects the bulk burden to fall on company/customer as suppliers have limited leverage over commodity costs.
Company took roughly INR1,000-1,500 price hike in Q4 FY26 and an additional ~INR2,500 blended hike in April (Q1 FY27), totaling ~INR4,000 in CY26 so far; another hike may follow in coming months.

ASP flat QoQ in Q4 despite price hike and higher AtherStack attach, attributed to how offers were structured at start of Q4 and expansion in Middle/North India with newer stores having lower ASP; expected to normalize as stores mature.
Realization (as reported in financials) will take a INR5,000 hit whenever FAME subsidy expires, but ex-showroom market ASP will continue to inch up due to disciplined periodic price increases.

subsections.label: Other expenses and depreciation
points: Other expenses up ~34% QoQ, driven by increased marketing spend and warranty/logistics costs (variable expense tied to 23% QoQ volume growth) plus a year-end warranty provisioning calibration made conservatively given rising commodity prices.

Depreciation increase driven by three factors: (1) 450 platform (shared by 450 and Rizta) has a 7-year useful life being amortized/depreciated; (2) increased Hosur plant utilization moving from single to dual to triple shift raising depreciation; (3) useful-life calibration of tools/jigs/platforms based on actual usage (more shots).
EL platform is still in development; its amortization will begin next financial year once start of production happens.

subsections.label: Other financial assets / balance sheet
points: Increase in other financial assets in current assets largely reflects fixed deposits/term deposits from IPO money sitting there.

A very nominal sum relates to EV subsidy receivables; FAME/PM E-DRIVE incentives come in regularly, while Maharashtra state subsidy (newly introduced) reflects a small amount in other financial assets.

subsections.label: Demand trends
points: Retail demand has been running higher than estimates; in Q4, retail (dealer sales to customers even pending registration) was higher than wholesale despite Q4 typically requiring a material wholesale dial-up after channel stock cleanup in December.
EV category searches surged 140% from Q1 to Q4 FY26, reflecting fast-growing consumer interest.
Industry growth has become broadly visible as the sub-INR1 lakh segment stabilizes/grows and the above-INR1 lakh segment continues to compound.
Demand is becoming more mainstream — market share growth in Tier 3 cities is currently higher than Tier 2 cities.
Higher comfort for paying for assurance features observed; products communicating assurance (e.g., 8-year battery warranty product) are seeing strong traction.

subsections.label: Rizta-led growth
points: Almost all FY26 volume growth is ascribed to Rizta, which has grown remarkably and is now almost three-quarters of Ather's sales.
Rizta improved market share by ~1100bps, from ~8% to ~18.6% in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Store network expansion
points: Store count doubled from 351 to 700 by March 2026, built on the back of Rizta.
75% of new stores opened with existing dealer partners; company focused on ensuring dealers have strong unit economics.
Service centers more than doubled this year, particularly scaling in the last two quarters.

New store cohorts on average reach operational break-even in about one to two quarters; ramp-up has been much faster than initially expected (originally guided as a couple of years to operational break-even).
Ramp-up is faster when new stores open with existing dealer partners (three-fourths of cases) vs newer partners.

subsections.label: Middle India strategy
points: Company targeted 'Middle India' zone (Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Maharashtra) believing it could behave like South India given high scooter penetration and premium scooter share.
Middle India received highest share of new stores (125% YoY store expansion) and quadrupled market share from ~4% to 17.3%.

Gujarat and Odisha (better brand equity, previously lacking the right product) saw market share triple from 4% to 14% after Rizta launch in Q2 FY25, then rise further to ~20% after store expansion — now behaving like South Indian states.

Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh (newer states) and Maharashtra (fiercely competitive) saw a similar but more gradual trajectory, from ~8% to 16%+ market share, with more headroom expected as supply constraints ease.

subsections.label: Rest of India and South India performance
points: Rest of India (including Rajasthan, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh performing well; Bihar and Uttar Pradesh nearing double-digit shares) tripled market share from under 4% to over 12%.

South India, the most penetrated and largest EV market, surprised management by growing as fast as the rest of the country in recent quarters, despite expectations of slower growth given high penetration.
South India quarterly sales grew from ~27,000 to ~41,000 units by Q4; market share broadly maintained even as store count increased rapidly to match a deepening market.
Management believes rightful market share for South lies even higher, requiring more capacity/supply unlocks in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Pro-Pack attach rate trends by region
points: Highest attach rates in South India (Kerala ~98-99%), followed by Middle India, then Rest of India (weakest zone) at 81%.
New stores/cities start with much lower attach rates (e.g., Madhya Pradesh was 40-50% less than a year ago, now consistently 80-85%).

Takes two to four quarters for new sales teams/stores to become comfortable upselling beyond the vehicle (Pro-Pack concept alien to traditional automotive upselling like throttle covers/rain jackets/mats).
Management expects even Rest of India (North India) to reach ~90% attach rate over the next couple of years.

subsections.label: Non-vehicle revenue streams
points: Four streams of non-vehicle revenue: Pro-Pack, service revenues, accessories division, and charging infrastructure division.
Currently only Pro-Pack trends are shared publicly; company plans to bring visibility to other P&Ls in coming quarters.
Accessories division revenue per unit has been growing rapidly (30-40% in recent years) though still a sub-INR100 crores P&L.

subsections.label: AtherStack 7 launch
points: Launched AtherStack 7 in FY26 with new features including Infinite Cruise, Vernacular Dashboards, and pothole detection.

subsections.label: R&D and IP
points: R&D engine firing on full gear with 643 patents filed till date, of which 283 were filed in FY26 alone.

subsections.label: EL platform technology
points: EL platform unveiled with concept vehicles at Ather Community Day in August last year; extremely versatile, focused on safety, convenience, and designed with cost in mind.

Key tech upgrades include Ather Charge Drive Controller (onboard charging, reducing charger size), larger wheelsets, and AEBS (Advanced Electronic Braking System) mimicking ABS-like braking in a large percentage of safety scenarios at a fraction of the cost.
Better cost structure achieved by moving from aluminum frames to steel frames and a simpler transmission system.
EL is fundamentally a platform, not a single product; can support multiple variants across price segments (mass, mass premium, and potentially premium) in coming years.
For motorcycles, a separate new platform called 'Zenith' would be needed; EL cannot be stretched to cover motorcycles.

subsections.label: Charging infrastructure / LECCS standard
points: Charging infrastructure has deepened the ecosystem moat; number of charging sessions on public fast chargers has compounded faster than the number of chargers, positive for underlying unit economics.
Fast charging business already has positive unit economics and management sees line of sight to positive EBITDA as a standalone business in coming years.

LECCS charging protocol, created by Ather, has evolved into a broader Indian charging standard with more than 20 stakeholders (OEMs, CPOs, suppliers) forming a new consortium called LEAF, pushing it toward becoming a national and international charging standard.

subsections.label: Factory 3.0 (AURIC, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar)
points: Largest factory till date, initially planned for 10 lakh total capacity with 5 lakh capacity going live in Phase 1.

Phase 1 commencement expected by end of this calendar year (Q3 FY27); trial production expected around festive season timeline this calendar year, with full 42,000 units/month capacity operationalized before end of this financial year (FY27).

Plant will drive bulk of EL's growth and improve unit economics through higher vertical integration — battery pack assembly, transmission assembly, painting, electronics assembly, and CED coating coming in-house.

Located in a vibrant supplier ecosystem in Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar; AURIC park has become a large EV OEM geography, with Ather among the first entrants and now joined by other large names.
Expected to help long-term logistics costs given Middle India and North India (especially with EL) are expected to remain large, important markets.
New factory expected to start contributing to topline before end of FY27, most likely Q4.

subsections.label: Current facility capacity constraints
points: Current Hosur facility designed for 35,000 units/month capacity, running at 90-95% utilization over the last few months — running at the edge, leaving little room for error.
Depreciation has risen partly due to increased utilization moving from single to dual to triple shift at Hosur.

subsections.label: Regional market share evolution
points: Middle India (Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Maharashtra) quadrupled market share from ~4% to 17.3% via targeted product+distribution strategy.
Rest of India tripled market share to over 12%; South India market share grew from 13% to 23%.
Growth in Tier 3 cities currently outpacing Tier 2 cities, indicating mainstream demand spread across the country beyond tech-forward markets.

subsections.label: Commodity cost inflation
points: Three big supply chain headwinds hit FY26: rare earth magnet prices, spike in memory costs globally, and spike in lithium-ion battery prices due to commodity inflation.
Lithium prices rose from a base of $8/kg to about $24/kg in a short span, cooling slightly since but still up more than 2x-2.5x; similar trajectories seen in nickel, manganese, cobalt.
Finished lithium-ion cell prices are up considerably — potentially 30-50% depending on procurement timing/source.
Overall commodity price inflation estimated at 40-50%, though BOM cost increase will be a fraction of that; still considered larger than any commodity supercycle the industry has seen.
Cells used to be 15-16% (sub-20%) of overall BOM until a few quarters ago, now a slightly larger share due to the spike.
Aluminum content in current platforms is comparable to ICE vehicles (which use aluminum heavily in transmission/engine); aluminum expected to rise further given the Hormuz crisis.
EL platform expected to substantially de-risk aluminum exposure given it uses far less aluminum.

subsections.label: Mitigation strategies
points: Strategic sourcing, pre-buying, and inventory planning allowed the company to sidestep or push out cost hits in FY26.
Engineering for alternate technologies (e.g., LFP) helped mellow or buy through the spike in lithium-ion battery prices.
Continuous VAVE (value analysis/value engineering) work and product-led design changes delivered overall COGS reduction achieved to date.

De-risking strategy across technology (LFP, NMC, NCA), vendor, and geography for every component; willingness to pay more for critical components like memory to secure long-term capacity and avoid disruptions.

subsections.label: Supply/production ramp challenges
points: Biggest challenge has been ramping production as fast as market demand; localized supply challenges occurred (e.g., November-December constraints on fast-growing variants), since resolved with increased supply/sales every month.
Retail demand running ahead of estimates; in Q4, retail sales to customers exceeded wholesale despite typical need to dial up wholesale after December channel stock cleanup.
April saw a localized challenge due to election season labor disruption, since resolved.
Challenges described as localized rather than secular material-access issues — mainly about squeezing more out of current capacity until next capacity comes online.

subsections.label: Marketing strategy pillars
points: Increased marketing spend visible in Q4 other expenses.
'Zayada Mat Socho, Ather Lelo' campaign continues as a long-term pillar driving assurance in the market, particularly North India.

New campaign 'It's Easy on an Ather' launched in Q4, focusing on why Ather's products deserve a premium and highlighting experiences like skid control, superfast charging, and accurate range prediction.
Ather became the number one searched EV brand across the country in Q4, despite still being some distance from being number one in volume.

subsections.label: Brand equity metrics
points: Internal brand tracking shows awareness up ~100% from Dec'24 to Dec'25, consideration up 31%, and preference up 50%.

subsections.label: Industry structure and TAM (E2W price segments)
points: Four price segments defined: entry (<INR1 lakh ex-showroom), mass (INR1-1.25 lakh), mass premium (INR1.25-1.5 lakh), premium (>INR1.5 lakh).

Ather currently has an inverted variant portfolio versus top-5 peers: 6 variants in premium, 3 in mass premium, none in mass or entry — while peers have more variants concentrated in mass/entry segments (peers: 4 premium, 6 mass premium, 12 mass, 10 entry).

Based on rough estimates from an early Vahan beta site and field intelligence (not exact), premium is ~10-15% of market, mass premium ~15-20%, combined ≥INR1.25 lakh segment ~25-30%, mass segment potentially as high as 45-50%, and sub-INR1 lakh entry segment shrunk to ~15-20%; these figures based on top-5 manufacturer volumes only and should be treated as rough estimates.
EL is expected to unlock the mass segment (INR1-1.25 lakh) where Ather currently has zero presence — nearly half the industry.

subsections.label: Industry growth and EV adoption tailwinds
points: EV category searches surged 140% from Q1 to Q4 FY26; overall EV volume growth has been strong particularly in recent quarters.

Growth previously masked by decline of the abnormal sub-INR1 lakh segment, which has now settled at a more sustainable level and also started growing, while the above-INR1 lakh segment continued compounding — combined growth now visible even to outsiders.

Demand becoming more mainstream — market share growth in Tier 3 cities currently outpacing Tier 2; higher comfort observed for paying for assurance-oriented products (e.g., 8-year battery warranty product selling well).

Delhi EV policy discussion seen as reflecting unusually broad societal support for EV-friendly policy compared to past initiatives like the odd-even policy; larger macro shift (oil crisis, LPG crisis) is nudging consumers to view electricity as the more reliable commodity, potentially shifting sentiment from 'keep one petrol vehicle' to 'keep one electric vehicle.'
Management believes electric bikes/motorcycles are technically buildable but await sufficient market proof; will build a portfolio of motorcycles (via new Zenith platform) when demand justifies it.

subsections.label: Commodity cost inflation risk
points: Rare earth magnet prices, memory cost spikes, and lithium-ion battery price spikes hit FY26 results; expected to remain inflated in the short term due to volatile macro.
Lithium prices up from $8/kg to $24/kg (cooled slightly, still up 2-2.5x); nickel, manganese, cobalt similarly elevated; finished lithium-ion cell prices up 30-50% depending on procurement.
Overall commodity inflation estimated at 40-50%; considered the largest commodity supercycle the industry has faced.
Aluminum content comparable to ICE vehicles; aluminum prices expected to rise further given the Hormuz crisis.
Margin pressure in the short term cannot be fully mitigated via price hikes and accessory/software work alone.
Only a small portion of inflation passed on to customers so far; bulk of the burden expected to fall on the company/customer as suppliers have limited leverage over underlying commodity costs.

subsections.label: Capacity constraint risk
points: Current Hosur facility running at 90-95% utilization — at the edge, with little room for error; any gaps are unforgiving.
Retail demand has been running ahead of company estimates, creating localized supply ramp-up challenges (e.g., November-December variant-specific constraints, April election-season labor disruption).

subsections.label: Macro/regulatory uncertainty
points: Living in an extremely volatile macro environment with continued short-term cost impact expected.
Delhi EV policy outcome uncertain, though broad support observed this time versus previous mixed-support policies like odd-even.

subsections.label: Capacity and production timeline
points: AURIC Phase 1 commencement expected by end of this calendar year (Q3 FY27).
Trial production expected around festive season timeline this calendar year; full 42,000 units/month capacity to be operationalized before end of FY27.
New factory expected to start contributing to topline before end of FY27, most likely in Q4.

subsections.label: EL platform launch and cost reduction
points: EL platform expected to be commercialized and in the field before end of this calendar year, likely around festive season.
Biggest cost reduction ahead will come from EL going live, though it will take a few quarters to become visible in the P&L; largest source of COGS reduction expected by end of FY27, more backloaded.
Some cost reduction will also come on the 450 platform (Rizta first, then 450), though smaller than in the past two years as focus shifts to EL.
EL to unlock better margins in premium and mass premium segments while opening the mass segment (INR1-1.25 lakh) where Ather currently has no presence.

subsections.label: Store expansion

Management hopes the current pace of EC (store) opening on a quarterly basis will more or less continue, but declines to give specific FY27/FY28 store count guidance.

subsections.label: Pricing

Ex-showroom market ASP expected to continue inching up due to disciplined periodic price increases, even as reported realization takes a INR5,000 hit once FAME subsidy expires.

risk_register.note: One of three big supply chain hits in FY26, expected to remain inflated in the short term.
Global memory cost spike hit FY26 results; company paying more to secure long-term capacity to avoid disruption.

Lithium up from $8/kg to $24/kg (cooled slightly, still 2-2.5x up); nickel, manganese, cobalt also up; overall commodity inflation estimated at 40-50%, described as the largest commodity supercycle the industry has seen; expected to persist and even worsen in Q1 before any relief.
Aluminum content comparable to ICE vehicles; expected to rise further due to the Hormuz crisis; EL platform designed to reduce aluminum dependence.

risk_register.risk: Margin pressure / inability to fully pass on cost inflation
risk_register.note: Only a small part of inflation passed on so far; price hikes and accessories/software can mitigate but not fully offset short-term margin pressure; bulk of burden expected on company/customer as suppliers have limited leverage.
Hosur facility running at 90-95% utilization, at the edge with little room for error; retail demand running ahead of estimates creating localized ramp-up challenges.
November-December variant-specific constraints resolved; April election-season labor disruption also appears resolved; described as localized, not secular material-access issues.
Management describes an 'extremely volatile macro' with continued short-term cost/supply impact expected.
Outcome of Delhi EV policy uncertain, though broader societal support observed this time versus past mixed-support policies.

themes.label: Demand recovery
themes.note: EV category searches surged 140% from Q1 to Q4 FY26; retail demand running ahead of estimates; industry growth becoming visible as sub-INR1 lakh segment stabilizes and above-INR1 lakh segment compounds.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Rare earth magnets, memory, and lithium-ion battery price spikes drove ~40-50% commodity inflation, expected to pressure margins in the short term despite mitigation efforts.

themes.label: Pricing power
themes.note: Ather took ~INR4,000 blended price hikes in CY26 so far and may take more, but only a small part of cost inflation has been passed through so far.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: AURIC Factory 3.0 (10 lakh planned capacity, 5 lakh Phase 1) to add 42,000 units/month, easing current 90-95% utilization constraint at Hosur.

themes.label: New platform / EL launch
themes.note: EL platform, designed for lower cost and targeting the untapped INR1-1.25 lakh mass segment, expected to launch before end of this year and drive FY27 cost reduction and margin expansion.

themes.label: Market share gains
themes.note: Middle India market share quadrupled to 17.3%, Rest of India tripled to 12%, South rose from 13% to 23%, driven by Rizta and store expansion strategy.

themes.label: Brand equity / marketing investment
themes.note: Ather became the number one searched EV brand in Q4 FY26; brand awareness, consideration, and preference scores rose sharply over the past year on the back of increased marketing spend.

key_takeaways: FY '26 was a breakthrough year: overall volumes up almost 66%, with Q4 delivering 83,000 units, almost 80% of the volume done just a couple of years ago.
Almost all growth is ascribed to new product Rizta, now almost three-quarters of sales, improving market share by about 1100bps from ~8% to ~18.6% in Q4 FY26.
Store count doubled from 351 to 700 by March '26; 75% of stores opened with existing dealers; service centers more than doubled this year.
Middle India market share quadrupled from about 4% to 17.3%; Rest of India tripled from under 4% to 12%; South grew from 13% to 23% market share.

Unit economics: AGM improved by about 5 percentage points (with subsidy, 19% to 24%; without subsidy, 12% to 21%), driven by ~9 percentage point COGS reduction; Pro-Pack attach rate hit an all-time high of 93% in Q4 FY26.
EBITDA losses improved more than 1500-1600 bps from FY25 to FY26, with Q4 showing a 2000 bps improvement, from -23% to about -2%.

FY '26 faced supply chain challenges from rare earth magnet prices, memory cost spikes, and lithium-ion battery price spikes due to commodity inflation; short-term margin pressure expected to continue.
Factory 3.0 in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (AURIC) planned for 10 lakh total capacity (5 lakh in Phase 1), expected to commence by end of this calendar year (Q3 FY27), enabling EL platform scale-up.
EL platform, targeting the INR1-1.25 lakh mass segment where Ather has no current presence, expected to be commercialized before end of this year.

How is the commodity cost inflation getting distributed across the supply chain, assuming Ather will not absorb the complete inflation, and how much of the commodity cost inflation in the last six months has been passed on so far?
AtherStack attachment rate increased this quarter with a price hike taken in January, but ASP seems flat QoQ in Q4 — what explains this?

Depreciation increased sequentially in Q4 — is this due to the new plant or EL platform launch, or something else?

CLEANMAX.company: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Ltd

quarters.company: Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Ltd
quarters.summary: CleanMax reported strong Q1 FY27 growth driven by doubling of revenues, EBITDA margin expansion in both segments, and lower interest costs, leading to substantial PAT growth. Management reiterated confidence in meeting the FY27 target of minimum 1.5 GW new opex capacity addition and issued a new FY28 guidance of minimum reported EBITDA of INR3,000 crores (~2.3-2.4x FY26 EBITDA of ~INR1,290 crores), supported by an expected 4.6 GW minimum opex capacity by 1 April 2027 and steady-state net debt of ~INR16,000 crores. Data & AI and industrial C&I segments both continue to show strong demand, while CTU curtailment at Bikaner and DSM/ALMM policy dynamics remain key risks/opportunities being monitored.

subsections.label: Drivers of PAT growth
points: Terrific growth in PAT to INR55 crores driven by three factors: doubling of revenues, improved EBITDA margins in both business segments, and lower interest costs.
RE power sales EBITDA margin improved from 76% to 84%; RE services EBITDA margin increased from 9% to 11% (also cited as 8.7% to 11.2%).
Weighted average rate of interest fell about 100 basis points from 9.4% in April 2025 to 8.4% in June 2026 due to efforts of CFO and team.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin expansion drivers (RE Power Sales)
points: Gross margin remains flat in range of 92-93%, but EBITDA margin continues to expand primarily because SG&A to total income continues to decrease due to operating leverage with increase in capacity base.
EBITDA margin has moved from ~75% a couple of years back, to ~82-83% last fiscal, to ~84% this quarter, with expectation of further expansion.

subsections.label: Run rate EBITDA / debt build-up
points: Run rate EBITDA means EBITDA from all operational assets as on that day projected for next 12 months.

Of INR494 crores EBITDA, INR334 crores comes from projects fully stabilized at start of year, 7% from RE services business, and remaining INR125 crores primarily from projects commissioned in last 12 months still stabilizing.

Of total net debt, ~44% (INR5,154 crores) is against projects operational 12 months prior to start of year; ~38% (INR4,483 crores) is against under-construction assets, reflecting velocity of new construction and future pipeline.

Company does not publish run-rate EBITDA every quarter as it could give a wrong indication to markets since assets take time to stabilize; better to look at run-rate EBITDA at end of fiscal vs likely EBITDA for next year (historically 1x to 1.1x).

subsections.label: Credit rating and financing
points: Credit rating upgraded to AA (from A+ last year), enabling first-ever domestic corporate bond issuance as AA is the threshold barrier required for domestic corporate bonds.
23-year weighted average PPA tenure against 18-19 year loan profile reflects strong asset-liability coverage.
Combination of long PPA tenure and strong asset-liability match reflected in cost of financing falling to 8.4% (30 June 2026) from 9%+ (1 April 2025).

subsections.label: Debenture trust deed reclassification
points: Existing listed debentures reclassified from unsecured to secured; security cover lifted from a range of 0.7x-1.25x to a fixed 1x.

Reason: part of corporate debenture was repaid using IPO proceeds; company chose fixed 1x (instead of range) for consistency with upcoming bond issuance which will likely also offer similar 1x security; not an increase in obligation, but standardization.

subsections.label: Capex disclosure
points: Management declined to give a specific capex figure for Q1, noting capacity commissioned was ~500 MW overall (400 MW RE power sales, slightly above 100 MW RE services); offered to share fixed asset growth breakup offline.

subsections.label: Pipeline quality metrics
points: Three metrics tracked closely for new contracted volumes: (1) share of customers rated AA/AAA or multinational subsidiaries, which has remained above 80% for over a decade; (2) tariff on the 2.5 GW contracted-yet-to-be-built pipeline (without storage value) is about INR4/unit, indicating profitability parity with existing volumes; (3) share of repeat business, with ~80% of new volumes contracted with existing clients last quarter.
Pipeline of contracted capacity under construction has remained stable at 2.5 GW or more, providing locked-and-loaded backlog for next 18 months of growth.
New volumes carry similar quality and profitability standards as prior volumes across these three dimensions.

subsections.label: Pipeline growth drivers
points: Pipeline refers to hundreds of ongoing conversations to sell more energy, not yet contracted.

Data & AI segment: every 1 GW of data center IT load requires ~1.5 GW round-the-clock power, translating to ~6 GW of renewable capacity; if data center market grows by 5-10 GW over next 5 years, this implies 30,000-60,000 MW of new renewables needed to supply 75% of that capacity.
Make in India / industrial segment: large total addressable market (INR3 lakh crores EBITDA pool for C&I RE generation) with only 7-8% current penetration, implying large headroom.
Company is doubling down in strongest markets (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) while entering new states (Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan) via new transmission capacity.

subsections.label: Tariff trend explanation
points: Under-construction tariff increased from INR3.85 to INR4 quarter-on-quarter; tariff for operational assets is INR3.93, indicating tariffs stabilizing to rising in the renewables market.
ALMM extension benefit is not being passed to customers via tariff renegotiation for contracted quantities being built over next 3-4 months; capex risk/benefit accrues to company's own account.

subsections.label: Growth outlook for next 2-3 years
points: Contracted capacity growth was 3x over the past 2 years (1,850 MW to 6,000 MW), with ~4,000 MW of incremental capacity added.

Management believes it can meet or exceed 4,000 MW of new capacity signed over next 2-3 years, but cautions against assuming another 3x (12,000 MW) as that would risk signing more than can be executed, damaging customer trust.

subsections.label: Order book composition
points: Total contracted capacity is 6 GW as of 30 June 2026, comprising 3.5 GW operational RE power sales, 2,500 MW under execution in RE power sales, 682 MW operational RE services, and 147 MW RE services contracted under execution, for a total portfolio of 6.8 GW built plus under construction.
Additional transmission capacity of ~6 GW is available or applied for, supporting further growth.
Footprint spans 7 states with active power evacuation, 3 states contracted/under execution, and 10 states in total; ~600 unique C&I customers served.

subsections.label: Data & AI segment
points: Data & AI remains a big business segment, at 42% of contracted capacity, with ~10x growth between March 2024 and March 2026.

Deals announced in calendar 2026 with global hyperscalers including Meta, Apple, Google, and Amazon; also energy partnerships with data center companies NTT, STT, L&T Data, Equinix, Iron Mountain, and others.

Estimated 35% market share of hyperscaler business in India, built through years of relationships and multiple deals; hyperscalers likely to use multiple vendors given scale of requirements, so market share may decline as a percentage even as absolute volumes grow.

Equation: 1 GW of data center IT load translates to ~1.4-1.5 GW round-the-clock power load, requiring ~6 GW of generation capacity (e.g., 3 GW wind + 3 GW solar), equating to ~INR40,000 crores capital investment; many more GW of data center capacity expected in India over next 5-7 years.

subsections.label: Industrial/Make in India segment
points: Industrial (non-Data & AI) segment doubled contracted volumes in last 2 years, growing at ~46% CAGR.

Growth driven by low starting penetration (only 7% of industrial power consumed via bilateral green sources, implying 93% headroom) and strong customer value proposition (>25% energy cost savings plus lower carbon footprint).
Data & AI is 42% of volumes; Make in India is 58%.

subsections.label: RE Services business model
points: RE Services is an EPC + O&M model for corporate customers who choose to deploy their own capex to own their facility (e.g., Sun Pharma, Himalaya Drugs & Chemicals, Honda Motorcycles); plant remains on client's books.
Revenue sources: upfront EPC margins plus sustained annuity revenue from O&M and use of common transmission infrastructure on CleanMax's solar/wind farms.
Order-book driven business; current order book is 147 MW contracted yet to be executed; order-to-execution cycle is within 12 months.

subsections.label: EAPA/VPPA contract mechanics for hyperscalers
points: Hyperscaler contracts (EAPA/VPPA) give customers the right to either take power directly to India data centers or use it as an energy attribute offset.
Net tariff to CleanMax under EAPA/VPPA is fixed (assured revenue ~INR3.7/unit) regardless of merchant market pricing fluctuations, so merchant price declines make no difference to company revenue.
Hyperscalers view India both as an offset source and as a future direct-consumption market as their data centers ramp up operations.

key_figures.label: MOUs signed for BESS with clients

subsections.label: BESS strategy - natural evolution
points: BESS represents a natural evolution of the corporate journey: rooftop solar, then offsite solar, then wind, then carbon solutions, and now BESS.

First BESS investment greenlit at STU project in Rajasthan; MOUs signed with three clients in the past month, since BESS investment requires a customer committed to pay for it (not a blind investment).

BESS opportunities identified in three C&I market segments: (1) solar-only states (e.g., Uttarakhand, Haryana) where BESS pairs daytime solar with storage to improve energy offset since wind resource unavailable; (2) states with day/evening price differentials (e.g., Maharashtra, where daytime energy is cheaper and evening peak carries premium) where customers want stored power delivered in evening; (3) BESS-as-a-Service tenders from large customers already contracted with multiple suppliers.

BESS increases the power offset a customer can be offered, enlarging CleanMax's addressable market; company has resolved technical issues, finalized vendor choices and contracts, and started building first projects.
Currently BESS does not form a substantial part of this year's capex program and is not material at this stage; initial projects involve about 2 hours of storage.
Estimated tariff uplift for BESS-as-a-Service (porting daytime electricity to evening) is roughly INR3-4/unit (excluding cost of generation), with some references suggesting INR3.5 or more.

subsections.label: Execution pace improvement
points: Capacity addition pace improved from 450 MW in trailing 12 months (as of June 2025) to ~1,740-1,750 MW in trailing 12 months (as of June 2026), reflecting improved organizational execution capacity.
STU and rooftop capacity addition alone grew from 450 MW to 1,200 MW; company has also started building CTU capacity, targeting about one CTU site a year (~500 MW/year).

Organizational capacity has scaled from adding 500 MW/year two years ago to over 1,500 MW/year now, demonstrated via project development (land buying, evacuation), engineering, supply chain management, and project execution capabilities.

subsections.label: On-time, within-budget execution
points: Over the last 3-3.5 years, including the most recent quarter, all projects have been installed below Board-approved budgeted cost, a critical operating discipline metric in a projects business.

subsections.label: Grid uptime and curtailment
points: STU grid uptime (87% of EBITDA base) remains above 99%.
CTU capacity, as with other players, remains a problem area; Bikaner project commissioned around start of FY27 is experiencing ~70% curtailment, expected to continue through the year.

CTU capacities represent only ~13% of start-of-year run rate EBITDA, limiting overall impact; management estimates EBITDA would be 8-9% higher absent this curtailment, translating to ~INR170 crores annualized impact.
Management is conservative and assumes heavy curtailment continues for the rest of FY27, as timeline for PGCIL transmission line fix is uncertain despite Power Grid/government efforts.

subsections.label: Power generation performance (PLF)
points: PLF is best evaluated on trailing 12-month basis due to seasonality rather than single-quarter figures.
Wind PLF has marginally improved; solar and hybrid PLF remain broadly similar; PLFs across technologies remain industry-leading and at high levels.
Quarterly PLF/generation and solar-wind breakup not separately disclosed on a quarterly basis; onsite/offsite generation breakup available in greenhouse gas reporting section of disclosures.

subsections.label: Koppal CTU BESS project
points: 543 MW of the 1.5 GW FY27 target linked to CTU project at Koppal, where two BESS bays have been allocated, commissioning by October '26 and March '27 respectively.
Having two BESS bays provides fungibility of evacuation capacity across bays; even if second bay is delayed, spare capacity in the first bay is expected to allow target to still be met.

key_figures.label: Rajasthan share of 2.5 GW contracted pipeline

subsections.label: Geographic expansion strategy
points: Continuing to double down in the biggest industrial markets - Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu - where the company is already market leader.
Entering new states such as Uttarakhand, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan via new transmission capacities being constructed.
Footprint across states is vital as customers require RE capacity in the same state as their power consumption.

Tamil Nadu experienced 1-2 months of administrative flux/approval delays following change in state government, but approvals are now moving normally and issues have been resolved; no structural continuing delay.
Total state footprint is 10 states, with 7 states having active power evacuation and 3 states contracted/under execution; Rajasthan accounts for ~150 MW (5-7%) of the 2,500 MW contracted pipeline.

key_figures.label: Number of client SPVs with client equity

subsections.label: Competitive positioning / moat
points: Competitive advantage rests on: (1) an existing pool of 600+ customers contributing ~75-80% of new volume growth annually, valuable because customers bear high risk contracting equity for a 23-year plant yet to be built, so track record and de-risking matter; (2) ability to supply both wind and solar in the four biggest industrial C&I states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu), and presence in 10 states overall, important because average PPA size is only ~13 MW; (3) sheer 100% business focus on C&I renewables for 15-16 years, unlike diversified large players.
Nearly 100 SPVs exist with client equity, since customers often put in 26% equity themselves.

Market is highly fragmented, not winner-takes-all; even as market leader, CleanMax holds only ~14% share (up from ~12%), leaving ample scope for multiple players including new entrants like Adani, Reliance, and NTPC who have expressed interest in entering C&I space.

Large diversified players entering the space are being driven by analysts highlighting attractive segment profitability (e.g., citing CleanMax's INR4 without-storage tariff), but company remains confident in its ability to keep winning given long-standing focus and relationships.

subsections.label: Hyperscaler relationship dynamics
points: Hyperscalers do not necessarily maintain single preferred vendors; given their extremely large volume requirements, they need multiple vendors simultaneously even as they announce data center contracts with multiple players.

CleanMax's ~35% market share of hyperscaler business may decline as a percentage over time as the market expands dramatically, but absolute volumes for CleanMax are expected to remain substantial ("a quite a few gigawatts").

subsections.label: Organizational capacity for growth
points: Organization has scaled execution capability from 500 MW/year two years ago to demonstrated 1,700+ MW/year (TTM), covering project development, land buying, evacuation, engineering, supply chain, and execution.

Management acknowledges ongoing organizational gaps in a fast-growing business; five-six specific gap areas were discussed with the NRC subcommittee of the Board at the most recent board meeting (specifics not disclosed on the call).

subsections.label: Domestic bond issuance plan
points: Company plans to tap the domestic corporate bond market for the first time, enabled by recent credit rating upgrade to AA (from A+), since AA is the threshold required for domestic corporate bond issuance.

Debenture trust deed amended to reclassify existing listed debentures from unsecured to secured, with security cover standardized at a fixed 1x (versus previous 0.7x-1.25x range), for consistency with the planned new bond issuance which is expected to offer similar 1x security.

key_figures.label: Module price differential (Indian-made vs imported cells)

subsections.label: CTU/transmission curtailment risk
points: Bikaner CTU project is experiencing ~70% curtailment since commissioning at end of last fiscal/start of this fiscal, expected to continue through the current financial year.

Management is conservative on timeline for PGCIL to fully resolve the transmission line issue, as this keeps changing and remains difficult to predict; assumption is heavy curtailment continues for rest of FY27 despite acknowledged speed and effort from Power Grid/government.
Impact is limited because CTU capacities represent only ~13% of start-of-year run rate EBITDA; overall EBITDA impact estimated at 8-9% or ~INR170 crores on a full-year basis if curtailment persists.

subsections.label: ALMM policy transition / module sourcing
points: Government deferred ALMM 2, allowing projects commissioning before 31 March to continue using domestic modules made with Chinese or imported cells, which are cheaper by about INR60 lakh/MW versus Indian-made cells.

Company is examining pulling forward some projects (originally slated for Jan/Feb) to commission by 31 December to capture this cost benefit, though exact megawatt quantum is not precisely quantifiable.

Some acceleration in client decision-making observed at a few brownfield STU sites (e.g., Maharashtra, Karnataka) where quick commissioning is feasible, potentially generating some incremental sales; not yet contracted for modules, pricing still under negotiation.
Benefit accrues to company's own account (capex risk/benefit) on the ALMM-driven acceleration; no tariff renegotiation with customers for these contracted volumes.

subsections.label: State-level administrative risk
points: Tamil Nadu saw a temporary 1-2 month period of administrative flux in C&I project approvals following a change in state government; management describes this as resolved, with approvals now moving normally and no structural continuing delay.

subsections.label: Execution risk / not over-committing
points: Management flags the inherent business risk of signing contracts that cannot be executed, which would result in penalties and damage to customer trust; this constrains how aggressively contracted capacity growth can be scaled (ruling out tripling contracted capacity in 2 years).
