subsections.label: Distribution franchise depth
points: Distribution franchise continues to be deepened, supported by over 23,000+ SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, and over 90 banking partners including State Bank of India, enabling reach at over 98% pin codes across the country.

Company remains market leader in B30 locations with MAAUM market share of 19% (later cited as 25%+ market share by MD); strong presence in Tier-2/Tier-3 markets reflected in robust B30 market share, with nearly 65% of SIP contribution originating from these markets despite contributing 44% of AUM by amount, underscoring deepening penetration.
New customer addition is also majorly from B30 markets.

subsections.label: SBI/YONO channel penetration
points: SBI is the largest distribution franchise; via YONO, reach extends to around 12 crore customers who regularly engage with the platform.

NISM certified bank employees have gone up to 15,700; company available at 98.2% pin codes through SBI's franchise; SBI has been supporting distribution network reach, especially in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities where market share is strong.

Company has been involved with YONO since the YONO 2.0 launch around December-January 2026; mutual fund folios, transactions, and SIP creation are now directly accessible/creatable via YONO with two-way compatibility; around 2.5 lakh YONO users applied through the platform directly during the recent IPO in addition to other channels; YONO is expected to be enlarged further with the upcoming KYC 2.0.

subsections.label: B30 strategy
points: Leadership in B30 attributed to SBI's distribution network which is predominantly present in B30 locations; company has also enlarged its mutual fund distributor network to B30 cities and is engaging with other agencies for investor awareness as part of a long-term strategy around SIPs, mutual funds, and investments in these locations.

subsections.label: Macro and industry backdrop
points: Quarter characterized by steady domestic economic momentum, healthy corporate earnings, and constructive equity market conditions, even as global markets witnessed intermittent volatility in interest rates, liquidity, and commodities.
Indian household savings continued their structural shift towards financial assets, supporting stable participation across investment categories.
Industry mutual fund QAAUM grew around 15% YoY and remained broadly stable sequentially, driven by market strength and sustained retail flows.
Equity-oriented assets saw strong YoY expansion with notable outperformance in small and mid-cap segments, while large-cap delivered more moderate gains.
Monthly SIP inflows industry-wide remained resilient at over ₹31,000 crores, signalling durable investor behaviour through market cycles.

Debt assets moderated due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short-term liquidity, while passive products (ETFs and index funds) continued to expand meaningfully among institutional and retail investors.
Overall industry flows remained constructive despite short-term volatility across categories.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning
points: B30 market remains underpenetrated and competition has been chasing market share in these locations; company maintains leadership via SBI's distribution network, expanded mutual fund distributor network in B30, and investor awareness initiatives.

SEBI's proposed entry of PMS through mutual fund route (for INR 25 lakh ticket size) viewed very positively by management — expected to increase number of players; company expects to be one of the leaders in this category and wants to scale it up significantly, citing dual benefit of launching PMS products with mutual funds embedded and expecting PMS products from others to include the company's mutual funds in their portfolios.

subsections.label: Strategic pillars
points: Strategy guided by four core pillars: democratizing wealth creation, accelerating digital delivery, strengthening investor performance, and building new growth engines.
Company remains committed to delivering consistent outcomes for investors, deepening industry leadership, and building a resilient, technology-led, future-ready asset management franchise.

subsections.label: IPO and listing
points: This is the company's first earnings call following its listing, described as a significant moment; management thanked investors for participation in the IPO and for trust placed in the organization.
Company committed to continued transparency, disciplined execution, and regular engagement with stakeholders following listing.

subsections.label: Alternates business build-out
points: Alternate business is a very large focus area; company has huge ambition plans to grow this business, has started hiring resources, and will launch one more product in this category this quarter.

subsections.label: Regulatory changes
points: Regulatory change around transition to base expense ratio and removal of exit load structure required prudent management to preserve long-term margin resilience; company navigated this TER reduction efficiently — majority of the reduction was passed on to distributors in a calibrated manner from April itself, resulting in a net neutral to slightly positive impact rather than a negative one; confident this will continue as majority (70-80%) of business involves distribution channels getting a percentage of TER that moves dynamically with any increase or decrease.

subsections.label: Market volatility
points: Global markets witnessed intermittent volatility in interest rates, liquidity, and commodities during the quarter.
SIP flow was slightly flattish quarter-on-quarter due to market volatility and geopolitical conditions, though flow was still maintained.
Debt assets moderated industry-wide due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short-term liquidity.

subsections.label: Other income volatility
points: Dip in other income compared to last year attributed to mark-to-market impact on the company's investment portfolio, which impacted the last quarter's book.

subsections.label: Silent period constraints
points: Management repeatedly declined to give specific forward guidance (on QAAUM growth for the year, opex, ESOP costs for FY27) citing that results were declared today and the company is in a silent period.
Management pointed to historical trends (e.g., 17% YoY growth in operating profit) as reference points rather than providing explicit guidance.
Opex is expected to remain focused on technology and human resources — quality of manpower, fund managers, people, and technology upgradation in AI/digital areas, without specific numerical guidance.
Distribution mix endeavour is to maintain roughly one-third from SBI channel and two-thirds from other/direct channels going forward, using digital tools and delivery.
Endeavour to increase the revenue contribution from PMS/AIF/international business by focusing on high-revenue AIF and PMS products going forward.
Company is very bullish on SEBI's proposed PMS-via-mutual-fund framework and wants to scale that opportunity up in a big way.
Dividend payments will continue as per the newly created and published dividend policy, subject to board and AGM approvals.

guidance_ledger.statement: Management declined to project QAAUM growth for the year, citing silent period post-results.

Opex will be mostly focused on technology and human resources — quality of manpower, fund managers, people, along with technology upgradation in AI, digital and other areas; no numerical guidance given due to silent period.
Management declined to disclose ESOP cost details for FY27, citing board-approved policy followed internally; offered to discuss one-to-one but not in this forum.
Endeavour is to maintain the equivalent split of ~35% from SBI channel and ~65% from direct and other channel by using digital tools and digital delivery going forward.
Endeavour is to increase the revenue contribution from PMS, advisory and international business by getting into high-revenue AIF and PMS products going forward, from current ~8% share.
Company has huge ambition plans to grow the alternate business significantly, has started hiring resources, and will launch one more product in this category this quarter.
Company is very bullish about SEBI's proposed PMS through mutual fund route for INR 25 lakh ticket size and wants to scale it up in a big way, expecting to be one of the leaders in this category.
Company will continue to pay dividends as per its newly created and published dividend policy, depending on final board and AGM approvals.
Company will continue to improve its cost-to-income ratio.
Company is confident it will continue to remain net neutral or positive on TER reduction impact even as it grows further, as majority (70-80%) of distribution channel business shares TER dynamically.

risk_register.note: Company navigated this efficiently, passing majority of reduction to distributors in calibrated manner from April, remaining net neutral to slightly positive; confident of continuing this even with future growth.

risk_register.risk: Global market volatility (interest rates, liquidity, commodities)
risk_register.note: Global markets witnessed intermittent volatility during the quarter even as domestic momentum remained steady.

risk_register.risk: Market volatility and geopolitical conditions impacting SIP flow
risk_register.note: SIP flow was slightly flattish quarter-on-quarter due to market volatility and geopolitical conditions, though flow was maintained near ₹4,000 crores.
Debt assets moderated due to institutional redemption patterns and tight short-term liquidity.
Other income was a little muted due to mark-to-market impact on the company's own portfolio, similar to some impact last year.
B30 market remains underpenetrated and competition has been chasing market share there; company countered via distribution network expansion and investor awareness initiatives.

themes.label: SIP flow resilience
themes.note: SIP AUM grew 15% YoY, monthly SIPs grew 14% to ~₹4,000 crores, with 1.7 million fresh SIPs added despite slight flattishness from market volatility.

themes.label: B30/Tier-2,3 penetration
themes.note: Company leads B30 with strong market share and ~65% of SIP contribution from these markets, driven by SBI's distribution network depth.

themes.label: Margin resilience amid TER regulatory change
themes.note: Despite TER-related regulation changes, net margins improved via asset-mix shift toward higher-yielding equity/hybrid/arbitrage funds and calibrated pass-through to distributors.

themes.label: Alternates (AIF/PMS) scale-up
themes.note: AIF assets grew 29% YoY to ₹6,800 crores; company views alternates as a large future growth focus with new hiring and product launches planned.

themes.label: Digital/AI-led distribution and cost efficiency
themes.note: 94% of transactions processed digitally, ~50,000 distributors using partner app, and AI tools (InvesTap Nxt, Neo) driving customer experience and cost discipline.

themes.label: Guidance withheld (silent period post-listing)
themes.note: Management repeatedly declined specific forward guidance on QAAUM growth, opex, and ESOP costs citing the silent period following the day's results declaration.

themes.label: SBI/YONO channel synergy
themes.note: YONO integration (reach ~12 crore customers) and deep SBI branch/advisor network continue to be key growth and distribution levers.

key_takeaways: This is our first earnings call following our listing and it is a significant moment for us.

Mutual fund QAAUM for the quarter stood at ₹12.6 trillion, registering Y-o-Y growth of 11%, compared to 11.4 trillion in the same quarter last year. Our market share based on the overall QAAUM stood at 15.1%.
Active QAAUM increased by ₹8.6 trillion, up 10% year-on-year and a robust three year CAGR of 21%, supported by consistent performance and healthy flows.
Our unique investor count expanded by 12% to 1.82 crores as on 30th June '26, compared to 1.63 crores as on 30th June '25.
SIP AUM increased by ₹2.1 trillion, reflecting 15% year-on-year growth and monthly SIPs grew by 14% to nearly ₹4,000 crores.
We continue to remain market leader in B30 locations with an MAAUM market share of 19%.

Our operating revenue for the quarter stood at ₹1,149 crores compared to ₹997 crores a year, 15% Y-o-Y growth. Operating profit stood at ₹907 crores, registering a healthy growth of 17% profit after tax, which stood at ₹873 crores, registering 37% growth quarter-on-quarter basis.

Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable during the quarter, while net margins have improved at overall level despite change in regulation around transition to the base expense ratio and removal of exit load structure.

Shreyas Pimple: on the ESOP cost, if you can explain if we have any ESOP plan that is going on and if it comes up, how much will be the ESOP cost for the year FY27? (Management declined to give details in this forum)

quarters.summary: Management guided to sustained strong growth momentum across Beauty and Fashion verticals with continued margin expansion, reiterated Superstore's 35%+ NSV CAGR guidance (to be achieved by FY2030) and Fashion's long-term 3-3.5x growth guidance over 4-5 years from Investor Day, and outlined plans to expand Nykaa Now to 25+ cities by FY27-end while expecting no EBITDA dilution from that expansion; GST-led GMV/NSV gap in Superstore is expected to normalize from Q3 FY27 onwards.

EBITDA margin improvement of almost 200 basis points versus a year ago
Return on capital employed improved significantly on the back of tight capital execution, i.e., capital employed kept under control while revenue/earnings grew

subsections.label: Capital allocation philosophy

Prudent capital utilization philosophy has enabled an increasingly strong balance sheet
Improvement driven by disciplined inventory and receivables optimization

Fulfillment expenses increased due to continued investment in infrastructure expansion leading to O2D efficiencies, offset by a like improvement in marketing efficiency
Continued marketing investments support strong customer acquisition across both beauty and fashion
EBITDA growth driven by combination of marketing investment, scale, and productivity efficiencies

subsections.label: Beauty vertical drivers
points: Growth accelerated on the back of strong customer acquisition and successful execution of key sales during the quarter
Retail continued to strengthen performance with double-digit same-store sales growth, remaining an area of growth
Growth strategy pillars are penetration and premiumization, both playing out well
Premiumization occurring across ASP growth, average basket size (ABS) growth, and frequency of purchase (FOP) growth; AOV premiumization driven by both ASP and ABS

New brand launches this quarter: Rare Beauty (Selena Gomez) launched June 2026, quickly became top-5 prestige brand; K18 (Unilever prestige hair care), SK-II (P&G Japanese skin care), Anua (trending Korean brand)
Two flagship sales this quarter: Pink summer sale (May) and Nykaa birthday sale, both delivering strong traffic, customer acquisition and revenue outcomes
Sequential order volume dip framed as seasonal; Q3 is typically the best quarter due to festive season/weddings/flagship sales; management prefers YoY comparison (~20% growth) over QoQ

subsections.label: Fashion vertical drivers
points: One of the fastest growth quarters in past many quarters on GMV and NSV
Growth driven by assortment growth across categories (women's, men's, kids, and emerging categories like home), consistent addition of strong brands, continued customer acquisition investment
Encouraging early signs from Nike partnership (D2C platform operation plus marketplace listing)
Structural improvements in customer flywheel led to marketing and overhead efficiencies, making the quarter overall profitable, building on Q4 already being profitable
Customer funnel metrics (visits, MAUs, transacting customers, orders) all improved due to both acquisition and retention
Women's category growth led by footwear and activewear; athleisure becoming mainstream across men and women
New marquee brand launches: Birkenstock, Debenhams portfolio, H&M Move (H&M sub-brand)

Marketplace remains predominant model for multi-brand fashion retail (e.g., H&M is a standard marketplace agreement, not inventory-based); inventory-based business remains a very small portion; Nike D2C is a selective, deeper end-to-end partnership
No current plan to open physical stores for Fashion; focus remains on building out digitally with partners

subsections.label: House of Nykaa Brands detail
points: Portfolio comprises 13 brands: 7 in beauty, 6 in fashion
3 large anchor brands: Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Cosmetics
Dot & Key had 2 launches this quarter: Melty Lip balm and Dragon Fruit Bound sunscreen
Kay Beauty launched Cashmere Lipglow (collaboration with Saba Azad), became a huge success and top seller
Nykaa Cosmetics had strong lip launches including Lip Grip
Kay Beauty won Best New Brand award at CEW Awards UK; brands also won recognitions from Femina, ET and other Indian platforms

Announced acquisition of Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skin care brand with strong R&D depth (30+ proprietary formulations) and existing salon distribution; bootstrapped by founders Prachi and Aman; acquiring 51% now with remaining 49% over next few years; Aminu fills a premium skin care gap in portfolio not currently addressed by existing brands; has 3 hero products (longevity serum, eye serum, sleep oil) with assortment expansion planned across lip, moisturizers and face washes over the next year

subsections.label: Nykaa Distribution (Superstore) detail
points: Growth driven by retailer network expansion (30% more retailers) plus higher AOV from existing retailers
GMV growth slightly lower than NSV growth due to GST-led MRP impact

EBITDA improvement driven by S&D expense efficiency (getting more from same retailer base and field force) and overhead efficiency from increased scale; partially offset by one-off fulfillment cost increase from new labor code
Brand flywheel expanding into wellness/pharmacy categories (e.g., Yoga Bar, Cipla)

Leveraging technology/data science: automated WhatsApp ordering for retailers, engagement gamification (spin the wheel), predictive engine guiding field force on which retailer to target with which brand

Superstore leveraging tech and data science, soon AI, for customer engagement and productivity: automated WhatsApp ordering, gamified engagement (spin the wheel), predictive engine for guiding field force on which retailer to target with which brand at what time

Exclusive brand outlets set up in strategic partnership with Charlotte Tilbury and Kiehl's
50% of stores now in Tier 2 cities and beyond, indicating a well-diversified geographical network
Store count has grown ~2x versus 3 years ago, with city presence expanding from 60 to 105 cities; 11 new stores added this quarter to reach 324 stores across 100+/105 cities

subsections.label: Nykaa Now expansion
points: Expanded from 3 cities with limited assortment in Q1 FY26 to 13 cities with 1,000+ brands currently
Combines 60-minute delivery speed with widest assortment of beauty and personal care products among quick commerce platforms

Category mix on Nykaa Now not meaningfully different from mainline — dominated by makeup, skin care, hair care, bath and body, fragrance; new incremental subcategories emerging such as low-ASP face washes, cleansers, bath gels for personal care needed in a hurry
No differential pricing between Nykaa Now and mainline platform since brand funds all consumer discounts, not the retailer

subsections.label: Superstore distribution reach

Distribution network touches 1,200+ cities and 19,000 pin codes

subsections.label: Consumer engagement initiatives
points: Scaling up immersive/experiential events: L'Oreal Paris Cannes, beauty bars, flagship sales, makeup master classes, experiential pop-ups, Rare Beauty launch event, House of Nykaa launch events, campus programs for Gen Z
Nykaaland and other consumer engagement initiatives attracting significant consumer participation
Building communication in vernacular languages and enabling voice-based search to reach a wider audience

subsections.label: Demand engine / flywheel
points: GMV grown to $2.4 billion powered by demand, assortment, and distribution flywheel
Huge headroom exists from 60 million ever-shoppers vs only 20.8 million annual unique transacting buyers — opportunity to reactivate infrequent shoppers
Frequency of purchase and ticket size for existing annual transacting buyers are low compared to global averages, indicating room for growth
No price filter needed for TAM given assortment spans mass/masstige FMCG-type SKUs to most premium products
Platform serves both women and men; increasingly adding men's grooming/personal care mix and via Nykaa Man

subsections.label: Growth drivers - overall qualitative
points: Growth acceleration attributed to a combination of a good/strong market and strong execution — not a single factor
Both Beauty and Fashion have consistently grown faster than the industry
Fashion structural improvements: more than 1,200 brands added over the last year including H&M and Nike; addition of new business lines like Nike D2C partnership and enterprise business line

subsections.label: Marketing efficiency dynamics
points: Marketing costs have not come down significantly in Beauty; company is protecting marketing spend at similar levels while pushing customer acquisition
As the business matures, share of revenue from existing/repeat buyers grows, giving marketing spend leverage since new-customer-acquisition-oriented spend gets spread over larger revenue base

Fashion has shown improvement in CAC (30% lower than 2 years ago) driven by better assortment/conversion and improved targeting via technology, alongside continued 44% YoY growth in new customer acquisition at healthier CACs
Superstore growth has largely come without adding feet on street, improving unit cost economics; additional feet-on-street investment could unlock further growth

subsections.label: Aminu acquisition
points: Nykaa is acquiring 51% of Aminu now, with remaining 49% to be acquired over the next few years per agreed terms
Aminu addresses a premium skin care price-point gap not currently covered in House of Nykaa's brand portfolio
Founders Prachi (a cosmetologist) and Aman will continue running the business with Nykaa's support
Attraction includes strong R&D depth (30+ proprietary formulations) and existing distribution set up in salon businesses, viewed as formidable moats

subsections.label: Nike partnership structure
points: Partnership has two parts: (1) standard marketplace listing of Nike products on Nykaa Fashion, similar to other brands, and (2) end-to-end operation of Nike's D2C customer platforms (Nike.in and apps on iOS/Android), including fulfillment, run 100% by Nykaa Fashion
Management declined to disclose financial/contractual details, but indicated a retailer-like arrangement with commission-like income and protection against inventory risk on the D2C side
Multi-dimensional partnership: marketplace side plus deeper strategic engagement on D2C side; both off to a strong start in first 6 months
Partnership becomes part of Fashion's reported base numbers in mid-Q4 FY27

subsections.label: H&M and other brand partnership structure
points: H&M is a standard marketplace agreement (not an inventory-based partnership), listing products just like other brands

Fashion vertical's multi-brand retail business, barring the Nike D2C partnership, remains predominantly marketplace; inventory-based business is a very small portion; future partnerships like Nike D2C will be selective

subsections.label: Superstore CAGR guidance
points: Guided 35%+ NSV CAGR target versus current 28% NSV growth, gap to be closed via 3-pronged approach: expanding retailer network, expanding category footprint into wellness/pharmacy, and leveraging data science/technology to drive more brands into more stores
Management expects to be on guidance trajectory by FY2030

subsections.label: GST normalization
points: GST-led MRP impact causing GMV/NSV growth gap in Superstore expected to normalize from Q3 FY27 onwards, at which point NSV and GMV growth numbers should converge

subsections.label: Nykaa Now expansion plan
points: Plan to expand Nykaa Now presence to over 25 cities by end of FY27
Aim to have Nykaa Now cater to a meaningful percentage of overall orders via the 60-minute fulfillment model
Early read suggests no EBITDA dilution from Nykaa Now expansion; increased frequency of purchase and consistent AOV are offsetting higher point-to-point fulfillment costs

subsections.label: Fashion long-term growth guidance
points: Reiterating Investor Day guidance of 3 to 3.5x growth over a 4-5 year period for the Fashion vertical
Underlying core platform growth expected to remain healthy irrespective of adding further partners like Nike

subsections.label: Beauty AOV / TAM outlook
points: Repeat customer AOV growth considered sustainable given ongoing work on premiumization
New customer AOV expected to rise as affordability, awareness, and availability of beauty products increase in India
TAM estimated at $65 million to $100 million relevant addressable customers over a 5-year horizon

guidance_ledger.statement: Guidance was 35%+ CAGR (small gap versus current 28% NSV growth); via retailer network expansion, category footprint expansion into wellness, and leveraging data science/technology, expect to be on guidance by FY2030
GST impact will start normalizing from Q3 onwards; you will see very close numbers between NSV growth and GMV growth
Plan to be in over 25 cities by end of FY27 and cater to a meaningful percentage of orders coming through Nykaa Now fulfillment model (within 60 minutes)
Still guide to 3 to 3.5x growth over a 4- to 5-year period as shared at Investor Day; retain that guidance
Early read is that Nykaa Now will not be dilutive to EBITDA, if at all; seeing accretive LTV via increased frequency of purchase and consistent AOV, though fulfillment cost per order is being watched

Repeat customer AOV growth is sustainable; on new customers, as affordability, awareness and availability increase, new customers will come into beauty category at higher AOV; average order value moving in the right direction is base case

Relevant TAM for Nykaa estimated between $65 million and $100 million (fashion online consumer base currently 55-65 million, expected to grow to about $100 million in 5 years); large headroom remains from 60 million ever-shoppers vs 20.8 million annual unique transacting buyers
Most festive dates fall in Q3 this year, similar to past years; some benefit could accrue in Q4 if dates are pushed there, but most dates seem to fall in Q3
Acquiring 51% now; remaining 49% to be acquired over the next few years as per agreed terms
April and May have been good overall for the business in terms of growth momentum; broadly expect to sustain growth in the same zone as recent quarters, barring inflationary/macro concerns

Each of the three Beauty sub-businesses (multi-brand retail, house of brands, B2B Superstore) will continue to improve their respective margin profile; consolidated outcome depends on relative growth weightage; core beauty retail plans to reinvest some efficiency gains into growth
Trajectory should be positive on margins for the fashion business from here on; will not speculate on long-term numbers

Not claiming 65% YoY growth forever for next 5 years; growth to come from acceleration of big brands, incubating brands crossing threshold, and portfolio strategy; full plan to be detailed at annual day in ~1.5 months

guidance_ledger.horizon: 3-4 years from ~2 years ago (i.e., through FY28/29)
guidance_ledger.statement: Plan to reach about 500 stores over the next 3-4 years; on track, roughly 170-180 more doors needed over next 2-3 years, averaging 50-60 doors/year
Store expansion in FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 pace, i.e., ~50-70 new doors, with focus shifting to increasing density (2-5 stores per city) in Tier 2/Tier 3 towns
FY27 plan is to market Nykaa Now more aggressively given assortment and delivery speed are established; expect it to contribute a much more meaningful percentage of overall orders in coming quarters

guidance_ledger.metric: Owned brands price increase / brand pricing
guidance_ledger.statement: Price increases by brands to pass on freight/currency cost pressure has not happened yet and is not likely in the near term, but could happen
There is headroom for growth on customer acquisition; AUTC growth can more or less continue at the current growth rate

risk_register.note: GMV growth for Superstore lower than NSV growth because of the GST-led MRP impact; expected to normalize from Q3 onwards

risk_register.note: Slight increase in Superstore fulfillment costs led by one-off impact of the new labor code

risk_register.risk: Fulfillment cost increase from faster delivery investment
risk_register.note: Fulfillment expenses increased by 42 bps as company continues to invest in infrastructure expansion (O2D efficiencies); offset by like improvement in marketing efficiency of 42 bps
Point-to-point fulfillment of a Nykaa Now order is naturally more expensive on a cost-per-order basis; being offset by increase in frequency of purchase and stable AOV

risk_register.risk: Low per-capita beauty consumption / low frequency & ticket size vs global averages
risk_register.note: Frequency of purchase and ticket size for existing annual unique transacting buyers are low compared to global averages, indicating headroom but also a structural gap

risk_register.risk: Global macro concerns - high oil prices, currency depreciation, inflation impacting consumption
risk_register.note: Makes management cautious for the next year, despite good April-May momentum.

risk_register.risk: Freight cost and currency-driven pressure on brands to raise prices
risk_register.note: Hasn't happened yet, brands trying to avoid passing to consumer; deemed unlikely near term but could happen; unclear consumer reaction.

risk_register.risk: Potential pull-back in brand advertising/marketing spend due to inflation
risk_register.note: Mitigated by low revenue/ad-dollar concentration across thousands of diversified brand partners on the platform.

risk_register.risk: Margin dilution risk from mix shift in Beauty vertical
risk_register.note: B2B Superstore is a lower (single-digit) margin business; if it grows faster than higher-margin owned brands/multi-brand retail, aggregate vertical margin can be diluted even as each business individually improves.
Direct imports are a relatively small portion of business; company operates fully hedged for forex with 2-3 month forward hedge coverage, limiting near-term currency volatility impact.

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: EBITDA margin rose to 8.5% (up ~200bps YoY) and PAT margin to 2.9%, with both Beauty (10.3%) and Fashion (0.1%, near breakeven) verticals expanding margins.

themes.label: Fashion turnaround
themes.note: Fashion NSV grew 54% YoY with EBITDA margin near breakeven (0.1%) versus -14.1% three years ago, and the vertical was overall profitable for a second consecutive quarter.

themes.label: House of Nykaa / owned brands scale-up
themes.note: House of Nykaa portfolio grew to 13 brands with 36% YoY GMV growth and announced the Aminu acquisition (51% stake) to enter premium skin care.

themes.label: AI-led efficiency
themes.note: Multiple AI initiatives launched this quarter — Virtual Closet, Nynaa voice assistant, Ask Nykaa — driving conversion and customer service efficiency.

themes.label: Retail store & Nykaa Now expansion
themes.note: Store count reached 324 across 105 cities with the largest-ever ultra-luxe store opened; Nykaa Now expanded to 13 cities with plans to reach 25+ by FY27-end without EBITDA dilution.

themes.label: Capital efficiency
themes.note: ROCE rose to 26.8% from 12.7% three years ago on disciplined capital employed, improved fixed asset turnover (10.7x) and working capital days under 30.

themes.label: Nike partnership traction
themes.note: Nike D2C partnership crossed 1.5 million app installs in under 6 months and Nike is now a top-3 brand on the Nykaa Fashion marketplace.

key_takeaways: GMV for the quarter at INR 5,590 crores, a 34% year-on-year growth; net revenue at INR 2,782 crores, a 29% year-on-year growth

Gross profit of INR 1,276 crores, a growth of 33% year-on-year and a margin of 45.9%; EBITDA at INR 236 crores, a 68% year-on-year growth and an 8.5% margin; PAT at INR 80 crores, a 226% year-on-year growth, with a 2.9% PAT margin
Both Beauty and Fashion verticals have seen acceleration in growth and profitability
Beauty NSV at INR 2,371 crores, 29% YoY growth; EBITDA margin 10.3% vs 9% a year ago
Fashion NSV at INR 451 crores, 54% YoY growth; EBITDA margin improved from -14.1% in Q1'24 to almost breakeven at 0.1% in Q1 this year
Almost 60 million consumers have ever bought from Nykaa, a 33% growth year-on-year

House of Nykaa now has almost 13 consumer brands, growing at 36% year-on-year; announced acquisition of Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skin care brand (51% stake now, remaining 49% over next few years)
Retail business now at 324 stores across 100-plus cities, 11 stores opened this quarter, including largest-ever ultra-luxe Nykaa store in Vasant Kunj (5,000 sq ft)
Nike partnership showing strong early traction: 1.5 million app installs in under 6 months on D2C platform; Nike now among top 3 brands on Nykaa Fashion marketplace
Return on capital employed improved to 26.8% from 12.7% a year earlier; capital employed kept controlled at INR 2,211 crores vs INR 1,658 crores in Q1'24

quarters.summary: Nykaa closed Q4 and FY26 with continued mid-20s to high-20s growth in GMV/net revenue and highest-ever EBITDA/PAT margins; management expects growth momentum to sustain into FY27 (April-May trends good) but flagged caution from global inflation, oil prices and currency depreciation, while citing AI-led efficiency gains as an offsetting tailwind. Beauty, Fashion, House of Nykaa and Superstore verticals are all guided to continue improving profitability/margins, with Fashion expected to sustain a positive EBITDA trajectory and retail store expansion continuing at ~50-70 doors/year toward a ~500-store target over 3-4 years.

subsections.label: Margin drivers
points: Gross margin improvement of 132 bps in FY26 led by strong performance of House of Nykaa and improved service income across businesses.
Fulfilment expenses up 23 bps as company continues to invest in fulfilment capabilities to improve delivery efficiencies.
Marketing and S&D expenses up 10 bps YoY due to investments in customer acquisition across businesses.
Strong productivity gains evident in improvement in employee cost and other expenses, resulting in EBITDA margin moving sharply to 7.5% for the year.

subsections.label: Balance sheet & capital efficiency
points: Fixed asset turnover improved to 9.9x in FY26 from 9.1x in FY25, led by increasing mix of House of Nykaa and Fashion which tend to be asset light.
Working capital days improved from 34 to 28 days, driven by both inventory and receivable optimization.
ROCE improved sharply to 21.2% in FY26 versus 11.3% a year ago, reflecting strong P&L performance and higher balance sheet efficiency.
Capex utilization stands at about 1% of revenue, steadily improving (lower salience to revenue); continued investment in beauty retail store expansion, fulfilment capabilities and technology.
Capital employed in the business has not grown much even as revenue growth has come on the back of already existing capital employed — reflecting capital prudence.

subsections.label: Multi-year journey (FY23-FY26)
points: Revenue grew from ~INR 5,000 crores in FY23 to INR 10,000 crores in FY26.
EBITDA margin improved from 5.0% to 7.5%.
PAT margin improved from 0.4% to 2.0%.
ROCE improved to a healthy 21.2%.

subsections.label: Beauty vertical performance
points: Beauty vertical had a strong quarter to cap a strong year, with acceleration in both growth and profitability as FY26 ended.
Growth accompanied by improvement in marketing efficiencies at all levels of the funnel despite large visit/traffic scale.
Visits converting into meaningful activity: strong conversion and unique transacting customers placing multiple orders in the year.

Nykaa remains trusted partner for global beauty groups: retails all 27 L'Oreal brands in market, exclusive launch partner for several including La Roche-Posay, CeraVe, Redken, Urban Decay; similar relationships with Estée Lauder (most of 11 India brands launched exclusively), Unilever, PUIG, P&G, Beiersdorf, Amorepacific.
FY26 was a defining year of marquee brand launches, including Korean beauty brands Aestura, Arencia, Anua, Mise en Scène, and global brands La Roche-Posay, IT Cosmetics, Supergoop, Nexxus.
Nykaa building ultra-luxury positioning via partnerships with Chanel, La Prairie and SK-II for India launch retail partner of choice.

Key trend - K-Beauty: Nykaa ahead of the curve identifying and capitalizing on the Korean beauty wave; has the largest assortment of Korean brands in the country, coupling online curated experience with offline influencer/retail engagement.

Key trend - Dermacosmetics: brands recommended by dermatologists, high in efficacy; Nykaa has the largest assortment of dermacosmetics skin care brands; created AI-powered skin scan and online derma recommendation engine with voice/video consultations.

Key trend - Premiumization of beauty: pioneering premiumization consumption, biggest/best assortment, immersive online and offline (high-quality retail stores) experience, marketing/content education to help consumers premiumize into luxury beauty.

Retail store formats: Nykaa On Trend (mass-masstige, Tier 2/3), Nykaa Luxe (luxury/prestige, Tier 1), House of Nykaa stores (owned brand stores across multiple formats), Nykaa Perfumery concept (drive fragrance penetration).
Nykaa took over Kiehl's India business (L'Oreal Group prestige skin care brand) — operates boutique stores, kiehls.com, and is exclusive retailer for Kiehl's online on Nykaa.com.

Charlotte Tilbury relationship: exclusive retail agreement since 2020, extended over 6 years; now building/operating exclusive brand stores in the country — first for Charlotte Tilbury not just in India but APAC region.

subsections.label: House of Nykaa performance
points: Unit includes 7 Beauty brands and 5 Fashion brands, with increased focus on Nykd.
Strong innovations became category leaders on the platform; focus on driving right unit economics channel by channel drove large EBITDA expansion.

Dot & Key dominates large categories: #1 sunscreen brand across Nykaa, Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit; #2 moisturizer brand; #3 face wash brand; predominantly online-focused but expanding offline beyond Nykaa stores/Distribution into GT and MT.

Kay Beauty: breakout brand, right product at right price filling a market gap; selective, premium distribution via Kay Kafés kiosks (with coffee partner collaboration) in top premium malls; expanding via Space NK partnership in UK, unlocking more doors; presence in GCC via JV Nysaa; focus for now is UK and GCC.
Nykaa Cosmetics: namesake brand, distributed more widely (62,000 offline stores) plus online via Nykaa, Nykaa stores and kiosks; 24% of sales from new launches this year.
Incubating brands for future scale: Wanderlust (bath and body), Earth Rhythm (clean beauty), doubling down on fragrance/perfumes, and Nykaa Skin — engines of future growth.

subsections.label: Superstore (B2B) performance
points: 4-year-old business; growth driven by retailer base/scale and brand attraction.
~30% of orders now placed by retailers via self-serve, showing behavior shift.

220+ leading brands across traditional large FMCG, newer D2C brands building distribution, and regional brands taken national; new brands increasingly choosing Superstore as first distribution choice ahead of building own 300+ distributor networks.

EBITDA margin improvement of >500bps spread across levers: gross margin improvement (mix shift to more profitable D2C and in-house brands), lower fulfilment cost, lower S&D expense (from more organic/self-serve orders), lower overheads.

subsections.label: Fashion vertical performance
points: Year of revival in growth and strong performance for full year; even higher growth in Q4 particularly on NSV (42% YoY).
Significant EBITDA margin improvement from -8.3% (FY25) to -2.6% (FY26), 570bps improvement for full year; positive 30bps EBITDA reported in Q4 FY26.

Consumer funnel healthier throughout the year — all metrics from visits to orders trending up; new customer acquisition 41% higher YoY with sustained focus on high-quality premium customers (marketing efficiency, AOV held steady).
Aggressively onboarded 1,200-1,300 brands across categories; still women-centric platform but brand addition fairly democratic across men's, kids, home accessories.

Marquee brand onboarding: H&M (onboarded November, now #1 brand on Nykaa Fashion since launch) and Nike (onboarded more recently); strategic partnership with Nike for end-to-end management of Nike.com and Nike app digital commerce in India since February.

Marketing shift toward creator economy: amplified activity with creators of various sizes (pan-India and regional) alongside celebrity events (e.g., girl's night-out event with Shanaya Kapoor and Adarsh Gaurav); leaning into content-commerce integration.

subsections.label: Vertical-level P&L reporting
points: Beauty vertical margin improved 70bps YoY led by productivity gains and scale efficiencies.
Fashion vertical margin improved 570bps as covered by Abhijeet, with strong improvement across marketing, S&D and other expenses.
Fashion vertical became profitable at 0.3% EBITDA for Q4.

subsections.label: International expansion
points: Kay Beauty launched in UK last year, strengthening partnership with Space NK (leading UK retailer); unlocking more doors as partnership progresses and outperforming in many stores.
Presence in GCC via JV Nysaa; current focus is on doing UK and GCC markets well rather than rapid further international expansion.

subsections.label: Nykaa Now (quick commerce) build-out
points: FY26 was the year of building out the rapid store network; well covered in top 7 metros with ~75-80 rapid stores enabling 80-90% pin code coverage with 30-min to 2-hour delivery (vs 10-minute delivery deemed unnecessary for BPC category).
Coupling speed with largest BPC assortment on a rapid-delivery platform; retail stores also used to fulfil Nykaa Now orders where required, enabling access to prestige brand portfolio.

Meaningful percentage of orders in top 7 metros now serviced through Nykaa Now (exact number undisclosed); FY27 plan is to market Nykaa Now more aggressively now that product-market fit (assortment + speed) is established.

subsections.label: Store network expansion plans
points: Brick-and-mortar expansion in FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 pace: ~50-70 new doors.
Currently covering top 99 cities; future focus is increasing density in Tier 2/Tier 3 towns (targeting 2-5 stores per city there).
Long-standing target (stated ~2 years ago) to reach about 500 stores over 3-4 years; on track — roughly 170-180 more doors needed over next 2-3 years, averaging ~50-60 doors/year.

subsections.label: Import exposure and FX hedging
points: Direct imports form a relatively small portion of the business, limiting exposure both from forex volatility and potential supply chain challenges.
Company operates on a fully hedged basis for forex; exposures for the next 2-3 months continue to remain hedged, providing protection from near-term currency volatility.

subsections.label: TAM and diversification strategy
points: Company addresses $15bn online BPC, $14bn organized offline beauty, $15bn unorganized retail beauty, and $55bn online fashion TAMs; with House of Nykaa, TAM can be almost doubled and played through two angles.

Diversification-cum-growth expansion journey since 2023: core multi-omnichannel beauty and fashion businesses grew 2x on GMV over 3 years; newer businesses (Superstore, House of Nykaa) grew 4x over same period.

subsections.label: Advertiser base diversification (Beauty)
points: No single brand or brand company accounts for double-digit revenue share on the platform — low revenue concentration and correspondingly low concentration of ad dollars.
Platform made more inclusive over years, allowing more brands to participate in advertising, diversifying advertiser base — not overly reliant on FMCG, international, luxury, or mass brands.
New advertising properties and consumer insights (aided by AI) being provided to brands, seen as helpful, which could counter any pullback in ad spend due to inflation/currency pressures.

subsections.label: Own brands vs marketplace positioning
points: Own brands do not account for 20% of retail revenue yet per management (analyst's assumed figure was not confirmed); own brands also sell on other platforms (offline and other online platforms), so % on Nykaa platform alone is not the full picture.
Strategy is not about penetrating a particular share of Nykaa as a platform, but building an independent house-of-brands unit with brands hitting their own potential and distribution strategy.

Multi-brand retail relationships and commitments come first; platform aims to create a fair and balanced playing field for all brand partners — owned brands have as much right to win or lose as any other brand, not solving for market share increase of owned brands specifically.

subsections.label: Fashion competitive positioning
points: Competitive intensity has not abated, but Nykaa Fashion is uniquely positioned — focuses on premium, trend-forward, style-focused online fashion market rather than mass market categories.
Fashion is a younger business than BPC with more headroom for growth given the $55bn TAM and small current market share.

subsections.label: Customer growth economics (Beauty B2C)
points: Growth for the retail platform (Nykaa.com + stores) comes from both new customer acquisition and existing customer basket evolution (annual consumption value).
New customer AOVs are lower than repeat customer AOVs; in quarters with strong new customer acquisition, aggregate AOV growth can look muted due to higher mix of new customers.

Focus has been on driving purchase frequency rather than just AOV, targeting annual consumption value; initiatives in place to improve AOV/ACV for existing/repeat buyers going forward via personalization and premiumization.
Still tremendous headroom for customer acquisition given the size of India's beauty consumer base relative to current AUTC.

subsections.label: Earth Rhythm acquisition completion
points: Company had acquired 76% stake in Earth Rhythm over a couple of tranches between FY23 and FY25; completed the acquisition in the reported period by acquiring an additional 24% stake at pre-agreed terms.

subsections.label: House of Nykaa portfolio strategy
points: Three-pronged strategy: (1) ensure big brands (Dot & Key, Nykaa Cosmetics, Kay Beauty, Nykd) continue to hit potential, take market share, make right distribution calls; (2) get incubating brands through the ~INR 150 crore+ threshold so they can sustain independently; (3) pursue acquisitions or in-house brand building to supplement category coverage.
Company plans to detail the full House of Nykaa plan at an upcoming annual day event (in about a month and a half).

subsections.label: Nike partnership
points: Strategic partnership entered with Nike to manage end-to-end their digital commerce/direct-to-customer platforms in India, including Nike.com and Nike application, effective since February (previous quarter).

subsections.label: Macro headwinds
points: Global concerns translating into high oil prices and depreciating currency, and their impact on inflation and consumption, make management cautious for the next year, despite good April-May momentum.
Inflationary pressures may emerge for consumption in general, though management believes the company's small-luxury consumption categories are less impacted during tougher times.

subsections.label: Input cost / pricing risk
points: Freight cost and currency issues are creating some pressure on brands to consider price increases; this hasn't happened yet, and brands are trying to avoid passing increases to consumers, though it could happen — deemed unlikely in the near term.

Uncertain how the consumer would react to a price increase if it occurs; company believes beauty's low ticket size and habitual/daily-use nature could keep the category relatively more immune than others.

subsections.label: Advertising spend pull-back risk
points: Possibility that certain brands pull back on ad/marketing spend on digital platforms including Nykaa's, if inflation persists; mitigated by Nykaa's low revenue/ad-dollar concentration across a diversified brand base.

subsections.label: Margin mix risk (Beauty vertical)
points: B2B Superstore is currently a lower (single-digit) margin business; if it grows faster than owned brands/multi-brand retail at the aggregate vertical level, that mix shift can be margin-dilutive even as each business individually improves its own margin profile.

subsections.label: FY27 outlook commentary
points: April and May FY27 trading has been good in terms of growth momentum, though global macro concerns (oil, currency, inflation) create caution for the year ahead.

Management does not see specific concerns beyond general environmental/macro factors currently, but acknowledges inflationary pressures could emerge; small-luxury nature of category expected to provide some resilience.
AI-led growth benefits expected to continue on both top line (marketing efficiency, personalization-led conversion) and cost side.

Each of Beauty's three sub-businesses (multi-brand retail, house of brands, B2B Superstore) expected to continue independently improving margin profile; consolidated vertical outcome depends on relative growth rates of each; core beauty retail business plans to keep reinvesting efficiency gains into growth.

Fashion business trajectory expected to remain positive on margins going forward, driven by continuing intrinsics (customer acquisition, retention, assortment, marketing efficiency); management declines to give specific long-term numbers.

House of Nykaa growth in FY27 will depend on both acceleration of existing big brands (Dot & Key, Kay Beauty, Nykaa Cosmetics, Nykd) and incubating brands crossing meaningful scale; not guiding to 65% YoY growth in perpetuity; full detailed plan to be shared at upcoming annual day (~1.5 months out).
Brick-and-mortar store expansion in FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 pace (~50-70 doors/year), on track for ~500 store target over 3-4 years.

Nykaa Now: FY27 plan is to market the rapid-delivery proposition more aggressively now that assortment and delivery speed are established, aiming for it to contribute a more meaningful percentage of overall orders in coming quarters.

guidance_ledger.statement: April and May have been good overall for the business in terms of growth momentum; broadly expect to sustain growth in the same zone as recent quarters, barring inflationary/macro concerns

Each of the three Beauty sub-businesses (multi-brand retail, house of brands, B2B Superstore) will continue to improve their respective margin profile; consolidated outcome depends on relative growth weightage; core beauty retail plans to reinvest some efficiency gains into growth
Trajectory should be positive on margins for the fashion business from here on; will not speculate on long-term numbers

Not claiming 65% YoY growth forever for next 5 years; growth to come from acceleration of big brands, incubating brands crossing threshold, and portfolio strategy; full plan to be detailed at annual day in ~1.5 months

themes.label: Margin expansion
themes.note: Highest-ever EBITDA (8.4% Q4, 7.5% FY26) and PAT margins driven by gross margin gains, productivity and scale efficiencies across verticals.

themes.label: Fashion turnaround
themes.note: Fashion EBITDA margin improved 570bps to -2.6% in FY26 and turned positive (0.3%) in Q4, driven by customer funnel health, brand onboarding (H&M, Nike) and marketing efficiency.

themes.label: House of Nykaa / owned brands scale-up
themes.note: House of Nykaa Beauty GMV grew 65% YoY to INR 2,788 crores, led by Dot & Key (13x in 3 years) and Kay Beauty (3x), with international expansion via Space NK (UK) and Nysaa JV (GCC).

themes.label: AI-led efficiency
themes.note: Management cites AI-driven gains in marketing funnel efficiency, personalization for new/existing customers, and cost efficiency as a growth and margin tailwind.

themes.label: Macro/inflation caution
themes.note: Good April-May momentum but management flags caution from high oil prices, currency depreciation and potential inflation impact on consumption for FY27.

themes.label: Retail store & Nykaa Now expansion
themes.note: 313 beauty stores across 99 cities with plan to reach ~500 stores in 3-4 years; Nykaa Now rapid-delivery network built out in top 7 metros, to be marketed more aggressively in FY27.

themes.label: Capital efficiency
themes.note: ROCE improved sharply to 21.2% (from 11.3%), fixed asset turnover to 9.9x, and working capital days down to 28, reflecting disciplined capital allocation alongside growth.

key_takeaways: For the quarter 4 financial year '26, we are really seeing continued growth momentum in both GMV, which grew at 28% year-on-year and net revenue, which grew also at a similar pace of 28% year-on-year.

Net revenue for the quarter was INR 2,648 crores... some of the highest growth we've seen in the last 12 quarters as well as around now for the last 14 quarters, we have sustained a mid-20s growth in our GMV and net revenue on a broad basis.
On the gross profit... INR 1,203 crores, which is 45.4%, about a 32% increase year-on-year... one of the highest gross margin ever in the last 14 quarters.
On the EBITDA front, the EBITDA was at INR 223 crores, 8.4% to net revenue and 67% growth year-on-year... one of the highest EBITDA margin ever, not just in the last 14 quarters, but ever.
And on PAT, it came out at INR 79 crores, a 3% PAT with a 313% year-on-year growth. Again, this is one of the highest PAT margins ever.
Financial year '26 performance was also strong. Again, the GMV growth was 28%, net revenue at 26% and we touched INR 10,000 crores net revenue for the first time ever, a $1 billion revenue mark.

We crossed the milestone of INR 100 billion revenue in FY '26, our revenue from operations has doubled in the last 3 years... The profitability improvement was even stronger with EBITDA at 3x and PAT at 10x versus 3 years ago.
I have to admit that April and May have been good overall for the business in terms of the growth momentum. However, you are right that the global concerns... makes us cautious for the next year.
pressing_questions: As we are starting a new financial year so I thought that it would be appropriate to ask your outlook for the next year and all the key segments, what are your thoughts, both in terms of growth and margins? We are seeing some signs of inflation as well. So any thoughts there? How does it impact demand and margins?

I would love to understand where should we see steady state margins of BPC coming up to?... A relative question out here is, how should we look at the inference cost, adding some pressures to the margins? And my second question is on impact of a higher fuel price we should see on raw materials and should we see procurement cost increasing and hence an impact on margins out there?

On private labels, in BPC, we already had 20% kind of a contribution. Is there a possibility that Nykaa as a platform can say even touch a 30% without sort of impacting the health or the way other independent brands look at our platform?

To sustain this kind of 50%-60% growth, do we then need another new brand in this portfolio? I'm just trying to gauge how should one think about the growth of this portfolio in FY '27 considering it did really well in FY '26.
What's the salience sales of Nykaa Now for you in FY '26 or as you exited the year? And any specific call-outs on offline store expansion targets for FY '27?

quarters.summary: Management described Q1 FY27 as a "work in progress" quarter — revenue growth outpaced the industry on the back of greenfield expansion and new customer program ramp-ups, but profitability was hit by elevated copper prices and exceptional minimum wage hikes (especially in NCR). Constructive discussions with customers are ongoing to recover these cost increases, with copper pass-through lag continuing at 3-6 months and wage-hike recovery timeline undetermined. Greenfields have reached break-even (ex copper lag impact) but are yet to meaningfully contribute to margins/EBITDA; capacity utilization at greenfields is in line with the previous quarter. Management remains ROCE-focused (target >40%) rather than purely margin-focused, and expects capex for planned new facilities to be funded via internal accruals.

subsections.label: Cost headwinds
points: Elevated copper prices and increased manpower costs, including exceptional minimum wage increases, impacted profitability in Q1 FY27.
Company continues constructive discussions with customers to recover cost increases and maintain business momentum.
Out of the total 37% revenue growth, 7% is attributable to copper inflation, with the remainder from volume growth, content increase, premiumization, and presence on new OEM model launches.

Copper pass-through lag remains 3 to 6 months; the delta currently sitting unrecovered in results is 7%, versus 17% in the preceding quarter, indicating quarterly-reset customers have already been compensated while 6-month-lag customers' recovery is yet to come.
Majority of customers are on a 3-month pass-through basis, barring a few.

Minimum wage hikes were not anticipated at the start of the fiscal year; NCR region saw an increase of 30-40% (also referenced as 35-40%), which is fully reflected in Q1 FY27 results as mandated by the government so far.

There would be certain usual VDA increases and adjustments in different states, but the unusual/exceptional increase was specifically in the NCR region; one of the greenfield plants is also located in NCR.
Quantifying the exact wage impact was not separately disclosed, but management stated the quarter-on-quarter increase in employee cost is largely attributable to minimum wage increases.
Other material/component costs specified by customers are negotiated mutually when component makers raise prices.

Gross margin impact from copper pass-through lag in Q4 FY26 was 200-250 bps, with a historical gross margin level of 34-36% referenced by an analyst as the prior benchmark; greenfield margin was -3% for the full quarter in Q4 FY26.

subsections.label: Margin trajectory / normalization
points: Endeavor is to get all costs back to normalized levels where there is a lag or where increases are not yet considered.

Company has supported customers in difficult/turbulent times and invested together to be a partner in progress; however, once costs are fully compensated, the sales-to-raw-material ratio will not be the same as in the past because the cost itself gets compensated (changing the ratio composition).
Over the medium to long term, as the company develops new products, localizes more, and provides more solutions to customers, the idea is to again improve margins.
Company positions itself as a ROCE-focused company (not purely margin-focused), targeting greater than 40% ROCE, consistent with performance shown in past years.

subsections.label: Capex funding
points: Current year's budgeted capex will be funded from internal accruals, not debt.

subsections.label: EV vs ICE mix
points: Company is engine-agnostic and a key supplier to leading ICE and EV platforms in India.

EV revenue figure (8.5%) represents business done for EV vehicles overall, not specifically the high-voltage business; breakdown given is between EV vehicles and ICE vehicles, not a further split within EV (e.g., high voltage vs low voltage) which was not disclosed.

subsections.label: Greenfield plant performance
points: Greenfields already achieved break-even in the previous quarter (Q4 FY26) and maintained the same level of revenue and break-even point in Q1 FY27 (run-rate of ~INR450 crores).
Some plants are in the ramp-up stage; contribution to bottom line expected to start in one or two quarters.

Plant-level profitability is not considered the right lens because the three greenfield plants came in simultaneously, causing significant impact; better to view performance at an overall company level since productivity in these newer plants has not yet reached the level of plants that have been in operation for many years.
Notion that material/import cost is relatively higher in greenfield plants is not 100% correct — it is more about scalability and productivity levels not yet matching mature plants.
When greenfields reach 90-95% capacity utilization (similar to parent/existing plants), they are expected to merge into regular business operations and deliver the same margin as the company overall.
Excluding the copper price lag impact, greenfields are at break-even; in totality, greenfields have yet to start meaningfully contributing to margins/EBITDA.

subsections.label: New vehicle architectures (zonal, 48V)
points: Company states it is fully geared up to make use of any new architecture that customers decide upon; different vehicle models in the country already use different architectures, and the company contributes significantly to each.
New architectures involve greater use of data cables and video cables, which the company produces and assembles as special cables — described as more value-enhancing products.

Management has not seen de-contenting in India despite new architectures; instead, content per vehicle has risen significantly due to increased features and consumer-facing enhancements (a 'lifestyle vehicle' trend).

Company has been part of some global developments exploring simplification of wiring harnesses, but such simplification, if it happens, would be a long-term development seen in very few vehicles globally and is not being pursued across all new launches by carmakers.

In a hypothetical long-run scenario, new architectures with more electronics could simplify wiring harnesses and enable reshoring of production to countries where manufacturing/assembly was previously difficult; multiple studies and projects explore this direction, including automation of harness assembly.
Complexity of harness design has been increasing, especially recently, due to new design requirements.

Company is a design partner for a Japanese OEM's future vehicle years and does not foresee a very significant change in architecture in the near term, only that vehicles will become more feature-loaded.

key_figures.label: Capacity utilization threshold for plant expansion decision

subsections.label: Capacity utilization
points: Capacity utilization for greenfields is viewed in totality across plants, not specific to individual greenfield sites; utilization is at almost the same level as the previous quarter, with some improvement already visible.
As in the past, company begins expansion planning once utilization reaches 80%; given industry forecasts, updates on new expansion plans are expected to be shared in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Pune greenfield / new plant plans
points: Specific Pune plant utilization was not separately disclosed; management addressed utilization only in totality across plants.
No new big plant confirmed for FY27 as of this call; management is still working on plans based on customer forecasts and will update on new expansion plans for MSWIL in coming quarters.

subsections.label: Customer relationships and cost recovery
points: Long-term, transparent relationships with customers underpin negotiations on cost recovery; customers acknowledge that manpower-intensive wiring harness assembly requires cost compensation for extraordinary cost increases.

Cost-increase discussions and pass-through mechanisms are a matter between the company and each customer; management declined to disclose commercial specifics beyond stating that unusual/extraordinary costs are typically considered by customers in the interest of sustainable business operations.
Company continues to view itself as engine-agnostic and a key supplier across leading ICE and EV platforms in India.

subsections.label: Cost headwinds
points: Elevated copper prices continue to create a pass-through lag of 3 to 6 months, with uncertainty over how copper prices will move in coming quarters described as abnormal versus past quarters.

Exceptional/unusual minimum wage hikes mandated by the government (30-40% increase in NCR) were higher than anticipated at the start of the fiscal year; timeline for full recovery from customers cannot be predicted, and uncertainty exists over whether other state governments will follow with similar mandated increases.
Plastic and other component cost increases (specified/sourced components) require case-by-case negotiation with customers rather than an automatic pass-through mechanism like copper.

subsections.label: Architecture change risk
points: Potential long-term risk from new vehicle architectures (zonal, 48V) that could simplify wiring harnesses and reduce content, though management currently sees this as a low-probability, long-term, and narrowly-adopted phenomenon rather than an imminent threat.

subsections.label: Forward commentary
points: Management expects greenfield plants to contribute to bottom line/EBITDA in one to two quarters as ramp-up continues.
Company intends to reduce the copper price pass-through lag period (currently 3-6 months) to a desired 15 days to 1 month in discussions with customers, though no confirmed timeline was given.
New capacity expansion plans, informed by industry forecasts and customer plans, are expected to be communicated in the coming quarters.
Current year's capex will be funded from internal accruals, not debt.
Company remains committed to a ROCE target of greater than 40%, consistent with past performance.

guidance_ledger.statement: In terms of contribution towards our bottom line, that we need to wait for one or two quarters, which they will start contributing in that way also.
That's the direction in which we are discussing with the customers to reduce the lag period... if possible, we would like to reduce this lag.
Seeing into the forecast and the plan given by the customer, we are still working on that... in the next quarters, you can hear from us that what are the new expansion plans for MSWIL.
The current what we have budgeted for this current year, the capex, we will do from the internal accruals.
Idea is to have it more than 40%, and we all committed to that, and we have shown that in the past also.
As we develop new products, as we are localizing more, as we provide more solutions to the customer, the idea would be in a medium-term to a longer-term perspective how we can again improve that.
As soon as we are going to reach to 80%, we started expanding ourselves... maybe in the next few quarters, you will hear us for that as well.

risk_register.risk: Elevated copper prices with 3-6 month pass-through lag
risk_register.note: Copper price increases continue; lag mechanism means a 7% delta remains unrecovered in Q1 FY27 results (down from 17% in Q4 FY26), with abnormal/uncertain price movement described by management.

NCR minimum wages rose 30-40%, far higher than anticipated at start of fiscal year; timeline for customer compensation/recovery is unpredictable, and there is uncertainty whether other state governments will follow suit.

risk_register.risk: Other commodity cost increases (e.g., plastic, specified components)
risk_register.note: Customer-specified component cost increases require case-by-case negotiation, unlike the automatic copper pass-through mechanism.
Long-term possibility of harness simplification/de-contenting exists but management sees it as low-probability, long-term, and narrowly adopted so far; no de-contenting observed to date in India.

risk_register.risk: Greenfield plant productivity/scalability not yet at mature-plant levels
risk_register.note: Newer plants have not reached the productivity/scale of plants operating for many years, affecting near-term contribution to margins.

themes.label: Input-cost inflation
themes.note: Elevated copper prices and 3-6 month pass-through lag left a 7% unrecovered delta in Q1 FY27 results, down from 17% in Q4 FY26.

themes.label: Minimum wage hike impact
themes.note: Exceptional NCR minimum wage increases of 30-40%, higher than anticipated, are fully reflected in Q1 FY27 results with recovery timeline from customers uncertain.

themes.label: Greenfield ramp-up
themes.note: Greenfields maintained ~INR450 crore revenue run-rate and prior-quarter break-even, but have yet to meaningfully contribute to margins/EBITDA; contribution expected in 1-2 quarters.

themes.label: EV content growth
themes.note: EV revenue share stood at 8.5% in Q1 FY27, with the company positioned as engine-agnostic across ICE and EV platforms.

themes.label: Capacity expansion
themes.note: Utilization is tracked in totality across plants; expansion typically begins at 80% utilization, with new expansion plans expected to be announced in coming quarters.

themes.label: Content per vehicle / architecture evolution
themes.note: Despite emerging zonal/48V architectures, management has observed rising content per vehicle due to increased features, with no de-contenting seen so far in India.

themes.label: ROCE focus
themes.note: Company reiterates it is a ROCE-focused (not purely margin-focused) business, targeting greater than 40% ROCE.

key_takeaways: The company has delivered resilient performance during Q1, reflecting the enduring strength of our customer relationships.
Our expansion into greenfield projects and successful ramp-up of new customer programs supported revenue growth, outpacing the industry, despite ongoing cost headwinds.
Elevated copper prices and increased manpower costs, including exceptional minimum wage increases, have impacted our profitability in this quarter.
We continue to have constructive discussions with our customers to recover cost increases and maintain business momentum.
Contribution from EVs continues to be strong, with 8.5% of our revenues coming from EVs in Q1.
We are an engine-agnostic company and a key supplier to leading ICE and EV platforms in India.
pressing_questions: On the greenfields, can you broadly indicate how has been the performance in Q1? If possible, please do share revenue and EBITDA, or qualitatively please do indicate whether the revenue has further grown and break-even has been achieved.

In terms of greenfields, at optimal utilization for these greenfields, margin may be lower than existing plants owing to high import content, but would ROIC be similar or lower because there will be a better asset turnover for these plants?

On the cost side, on the copper prices, there is an automatic pass-through which is likely to be received with a lag of 3 to 6 months... in addition to copper prices, there is an increase also in other commodities like plastic. Would that also be an automatic pass-through? And the minimum wage hike impact — by when do you expect customers to compensate? And would you be able to pass on, say, 80%-90% of the impact?
Is it possible to just sort of get an understanding of the 37% revenue growth that we've had in this quarter?... what would be the element of copper price inflation that is reflecting?
Are we sort of shifting to a monthly lag for some customers going ahead, or it continues to be a 3 month or 6 month lag which you are working on?

In the 4Q results, you had mentioned that there was a 200 bps to 250 bps gross margin impact because of lag of copper pass-through. Could you update us what is the situation now... where is the shortfall stand today?
If we expect the raw material cost to stay where it is currently, is it fair to assume that in next 6 months, we would be back to 35%-36% -- 34%-35% gross margin which we used to make earlier?
