Expansion beyond 6 GWh and into prismatic capacity is contingent on raising capital separately at the cell subsidiary; no committed timeline beyond 'this financial year' and 'in due course.'

themes.label: Gross margin expansion
themes.note: Consolidated gross margins reached 38.5% in Q4 FY26 (33.5% ex-PLI), described as industry-leading and structurally sustainable due to vertical integration.

themes.label: Cash flow turnaround
themes.note: Q4 FY26 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter, with Auto business also generating free cash flow.

themes.label: OpEx reduction
themes.note: Consolidated OpEx nearly halved YoY (844cr to 428cr in Q4), with further reduction to ~350cr/quarter and 100-120cr/month targeted.

themes.label: Demand recovery / volume rebound
themes.note: Registrations rebounding V-shaped (10k in March to 14-15k trending in May) with orders/backlog outpacing registrations; EV demand rising broadly.

themes.label: Gigafactory scale-up
themes.note: 6 GWh installation largely complete, capacity entering scale/commercialization phase, with plans to expand to 20 GWh via subsidiary capital raise.

themes.label: Service/execution turnaround
themes.note: Warranty costs down from 500+cr (FY25) to 59cr (FY26); service stats down 88%, part dependency down 69%, but some execution gaps (parts, store experience) still being resolved.

themes.label: Bike/motorcycle expansion (Roadster)
themes.note: Roadster becoming a second growth engine with 50%+ EV motorcycle market share, though supply- rather than demand-constrained.

key_takeaways: Exited FY26 with industry-leading gross margins at 38.5%, a much lower cost base, sharply improved execution metrics, better product quality, first operating cash flow positive quarter, and a Gigafactory now entering scale-up.
Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margins reached 38.5%, up from 34.3% in Q3 and 13.7% in Q4 FY25; excluding PLI gross margin was 33.5%.
FY26 consolidated revenue stood at 2,253 crores with 173,794 deliveries and consolidated gross margin improved to 30.6%.
Q4 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter: Consolidated CFO was 91 crores; Auto business delivered 213 crores of CFO and 173 crores of free cash flow in Q4.

Consolidated OpEx, including lease expenses, meaningfully reduced from 844 crores in Q4 FY2024-25 to 428 crores during Q4 FY2025-26; expect OpEx to move towards approximately 350 crores over the next couple of quarters.

With the reset OpEx base and current gross margin structure, adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven is achievable at around 20,000 to 25,000 units per month, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions.
Looking ahead to Q1 FY27, expect 40,000 to 45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of 500 to 550 crores, nearly double of the Q4 level.

Roadster is becoming Ola's second Auto growth engine: 50% market share in electric motorcycles, bikes contributed 15% of April gross orders, products going up to 9.1 kWh battery capacity and 500 plus kms certified range.
The Gigafactory is now entering the scale phase: 2.5 GWh operational capacity currently, installation up to 6 GWh largely complete with commercialization expected by end of this quarter.
Around 15% of orders are already on Ola's own Bharat Cells, and the company plans to transition the full vehicle portfolio to its own cells by September 2026.
pressing_questions: Since breakeven is around 20,000 odd units a month, what is the bridge from current levels to that — is it driven by motorcycles or driven more by service?
In terms of granularity on own cells versus imported cells, what is the cost advantage currently, and would it increase further when moving to 6 GWh?
Is the battery capacity currently operational 100% being consumed in the scooter segment, with nothing available for Shakti?
On monetizing the cell business (media reports of ~₹2,000 crore monetization) — are things moving in that direction?
On the Gigafactory ramp-up to 20 GWh — what is the rationale for ramping up so quickly, and can more light be shed on the order pipeline?
How should total CapEx be viewed for the next 2-3 years given lower CapEx commentary and near-complete battery plant capacity build-out?
Why was NMC selected for BESS (Shakti) instead of LFP, given that LFP is used globally and would be cheaper?
Why are service issues, particularly around parts unavailability, still occurring even for Gen 1/Gen 2 scooters?

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 saw consolidated revenue growth of 55% YoY (INR3,955mn), broad-based across aerospace (+40% YoY) and consumer (nearly tripled, +190% YoY), with operational EBITDA (ex-other income) improving ~3.5x sequentially on narrowing consumer losses. Management reiterated FY27 targets: aerospace revenue growth 25-30% at >20% segment EBITDA margin, ~45-50% consolidated revenue growth, doubling of operational EBITDA, and consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27, while flagging potential acceleration of aerospace capex given new Farnborough wins (including a 15-year A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems) that will reflect in next quarter's order book.

key_figures.label: Net reduction in short-term/working capital borrowings
Exceptional gain in Q4 FY26 PAT

subsections.label: Reported vs Operational EBITDA
points: Reported EBITDA at INR215 million is lower than Q4 FY26, but that movement is mainly due to other income/foreign exchange, which was unusually high in Q4.
Excluding other income, EBITDA improved from INR42 million in Q4 to INR148 million in Q1, a more than three-fold sequential improvement, driven by narrowing consumer loss.
The operational trajectory, not the currency line, is described by management as the measure of execution.

subsections.label: Depreciation
points: Depreciation increase YoY reflects the expanded consumer electronics asset base.

Q4 FY26 depreciation was already close to the Q1 FY27 level because Q3-end saw capitalization stop and commercial operations for consumer electronics begin; Q4 was a full quarter of depreciation at low utilization.
Depreciation expected to remain at similar levels going forward unless additional capex increases it.

subsections.label: Finance cost & debt reduction
points: Finance cost reduction followed debt reduction undertaken in the previous quarter, including loan repayments and net reduction in short-term/working capital borrowings.

subsections.label: PAT
points: On a comparable basis (excluding Q4 FY26 exceptional gain), PAT loss improved sequentially from INR631 million to INR532 million.

subsections.label: Working capital
points: Improvement in working capital efficiency reflects better conversion of higher operating scale into cash, supported by improved receivables and payables management, even as inventory was maintained to support the ongoing production ramp-up.

subsections.label: Other expenses
points: Other expenses roughly doubled YoY because Q1 FY26 did not include the consumer electronics piece in the P&L (expenses were capitalized); from Q4 FY26 all expenses came into the P&L.
Other expenses have a variable and fixed component; variable will grow slightly with revenue, fixed will remain largely stable in the near term; exact fixed/variable split not disclosed.

subsections.label: Other income guidance
points: Other income is driven by interest income and foreign exchange fluctuation; foreign exchange fluctuation is not projected for future periods; interest income expected to remain in a similar range to Q1.

key_figures.label: Quarter-end order book (as referenced pre-Farnborough wins)

subsections.label: Order book drivers
points: Aerospace order book crossed the USD1 billion mark, following a 13% sequential increase from USD889 million; described as validation of trust placed in Aequs by leading global OEMs, scale/depth of program portfolio and enduring strength of aerospace business.

New Farnborough wins (two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers and the Safran wheels contract) come after the quarter-end order book of over USD1 billion and are not yet reflected in current order book; they should show up in the next quarter's order book.
Given scale and delivery requirements of new wins, company is evaluating acceleration of aerospace capex plan to ensure capacity is available in line with customer timelines.

subsections.label: Demand drivers
points: Consumer demand described as customer-demand driven, not inventory restocking driven; whatever is produced is shipped, with no demand issue.

Management does not see specific changes in customer sourcing behavior due to tariffs; customers have taken a strategic view of global supply chain positioning, and supplier allocation commitments/strategy have not changed for either aerospace or consumer.

key_figures.label: Consumer capacity utilization (Q4 FY26, per presentation)
Consumer share of overall revenue (5-year target)
Consumer share of overall top-line (current year guidance)

subsections.label: Aerospace drivers
points: Aerospace growth supported by higher customer build rates and progression of additional parts into production.

Aerospace focus remains on scaling production in line with customer build rates, moving awarded parts into serial production, and increasing value addition across the integrated manufacturing ecosystem.
Selectively expanding into high-value adjacencies including aero-engine and landing gear system components.

Integrated ecosystem at Belagavi is described as a key differentiator, bringing multiple processes together to reduce complexity, strengthen control over quality/delivery, and continuously add a breadth of parts difficult to replicate.

subsections.label: Aerospace segment margin moderation
points: Aerospace segment EBITDA growth of 35% YoY moderated sequentially from Q4 FY26 due to significant other income in Q4 FY26, which mainly included foreign exchange gain.

subsections.label: Consumer drivers
points: Consumer revenue increase reflects production volume increases across the portfolio.

16% QoQ revenue growth achieved while operating at a similar capacity utilization level as Q4, reflecting enhanced throughput, better product mix, and improved execution, enabling higher revenue from the existing manufacturing footprint.

Utilization dip from 23% (Q4) to 22% (Q1) was NOT due to any capacity expansion; management attributed higher revenue at similar/lower utilization to better utilization of assets and yield, not added capacity.

Year-on-year consumer EBITDA loss comparison reflects commencement of consumer electronics commercial operations and resulting recognition of operating costs in Q1 FY27, whereas these costs were capitalized in Q1 FY26.
Sequential consumer EBITDA loss narrowing supported by increasing production volumes and improving operating performance.
Utilization across consumer electronics and toys sub-verticals moves in tandem; both were underutilized even before consumer electronics ramp began, so utilization must improve across both together.
Company does not break out consumer electronics vs toys/ATP revenue split; certain assets are used in common across both sub-verticals.
Toys customer Mattel is scaling up well and remains a strategic customer.
Consumer durables customer is Tramontina; consumer electronics customer name undisclosed due to confidentiality but described as one of the largest consumer electronics brands.
Company is entering into a few more programs in consumer electronics, beyond scope already assigned.

Consumer priorities: near-term focus on steadily scaling existing product portfolio and improving utilization; as business matures, intend to deepen customer relationships by broadening component portfolio and progressing towards integrated kit supplies; from FY2030-31 onwards, ambition to engage earlier in customer NPD cycles and evolve from component supplier to preferred manufacturing/co-development partner.

subsections.label: Segment mix outlook
points: Consumer share of revenue seen rising from 19% currently to 40-60% over next 5 years as utilization increases.
Even with faster consumer growth, aerospace (already at large base, growing 30-40%) expected to remain larger than consumer for at least the next 5 years.

subsections.label: Hosur ecosystem
points: Proposed Hosur ecosystem represents the next phase of expansion, extending Aequs's integrated manufacturing model into new areas of opportunity and strengthening ability to participate in larger, more complex programs; revenue expected to kick off from FY29.
Hosur facility is integrated, focused on aero-engine and landing gear components, end-to-end like Belagavi's aerostructure focus.
First Hosur facility (machining) to commence between September-March timeframe of FY27-FY28; forging and other vertical integration to follow.
All investment predominantly on vertical integration side to be completed by 2030 timeframe; machining will continue over a period of time.
JVs will be extended from Belagavi capabilities into the Hosur zone.
Goal is to be the largest manufacturer of aero-engine components; Hosur will bring a whole lot of new capabilities as part of an internal roadmap toward vertically integrated products.

subsections.label: Capex allocation & funding
points: Aerospace capex may see acceleration, potentially compensated by reduction/optimization in consumer capex, within the overall INR660 crore FY27 capex.

Aerospace capacity additions are continuous - literally adding a machine a week since last December, tied to order book growth; comfortable ceiling to run up to ~75% utilization before requiring further capex.
Consumer capex commitment (INR400-500 crores) is for capacity augmentation and new programs with customers; if utilization ramp-up is slower, some portion of capex will not happen.
Company has not finalized specific capex numbers for next year beyond the current INR660 crore FY27 figure and the 5-year USD350-400 million plan.
Company has already planned capital allocation between Hosur (INR1,900 crores) and Karnataka clusters (INR2,800 crores) for aerospace and consumer combined.

subsections.label: Capacity tracking approach
points: Management does not project total capacity in million hours over the next 2-3 years or provide an aerospace/consumer split, as it depends on component type and machine mix signed up; company models the business on expected revenue and component type rather than capacity hours.

subsections.label: Raw material sourcing
points: Approximately 99% of raw material is imported; management does not see any possibility of this changing soon due to lack of qualified sources in India.
Company deals with hundreds of different raw materials globally sourced; only one or two alloys have been qualified in India so far, developed over several years.
India produces significant aluminum, but not necessarily commercial-aerospace-qualified grades for customers; only two grades have been qualified so far, for forging.
Customers support sourcing of super alloys and titanium on both aerospace and consumer sides.

Developing a qualified domestic raw material ecosystem described as a long journey, both globally and nationally; management hopes recent wins/vertically integrated contracts could help accelerate some of this.

subsections.label: Customer relationships
points: Toys customer Mattel is scaling up well and continues to be viewed as a strategic customer.
Consumer durables customer named as Tramontina; consumer electronics customer name withheld due to confidentiality, described as one of the largest consumer electronics manufacturer brands.
Company entering into a few more programs in consumer electronics beyond originally assigned scope.

subsections.label: Tariff / trade policy impact
points: Management is not seeing any specific changes due to tariffs; customers have taken a strategic view of global supply chain positioning and supplier allocation commitments have not changed for aerospace or consumer.

subsections.label: Farnborough wins
points: Signed long-term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers, expanding global base.
Signed first contract for fully integrated Airbus A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems - a 15-year agreement, the longest in Aequs's history.

Aequs will deliver completely assembled wheels built from India-sourced aerospace-qualified aluminum with forging, machining, surface treatment, and assembly, all within the Belagavi Aerospace ecosystem - described as 100% Make in India for a flight-critical product.

This is the first time the customer (Safran) has moved this capability outside its own facilities (previously managed in-house); instead of investing in capacity internally, the customer is leveraging Aequs's ecosystem strength.
Contract is a single-source order for Aequs.

Management declined to disclose specific contract value; margin on this contract described as much larger than aerospace segment average, though management would not comment on specific margin numbers, noting each business will deliver the right level of returns/ROCE.

Wheel product: aircraft wheel for Airbus A320 without tires - two half-wheels joined together to form a full wheel, including assemblies; Aequs already does forging and some machining of the wheel and will now add surface finishing and assemblies, all from Belagavi using an approved/qualified raw material source.

subsections.label: Fundraise plans
points: Company previously communicated a probable ~USD150 million capital raise requirement; not planning to raise this year unless there is an advanced pull-in of capex or an inorganic opportunity.

subsections.label: Leadership transition
points: CFO Dinesh Iyer stepped down at the end of June, as communicated in May; search for a full-time CFO progressing well.
In the interim, Harish Bang (VP Finance) is leading the finance function.

subsections.label: Import dependence
points: ~99% of raw material is imported with no near-term possibility of localization due to lack of qualified domestic sources for many alloys.

subsections.label: Utilization dependency for capex
points: Consumer capex commitment is contingent on utilization ramp-up; if utilization ramp-up is slower, some portion of capex will not happen.

points: CFO Dinesh Iyer stepped down end of June; search for full-time CFO ongoing, interim leadership by VP Finance.

subsections.label: Tariff/trade policy
points: No specific negative or positive changes seen from tariffs/trade policy shifts; customer supplier allocation strategy unchanged.

Second, drive consumer utilization to unlock operating leverage embedded in existing asset base.
Third, move consumer EBITDA breakeven to Q4 FY27, described as a major inflection point in consolidated profitability.

At consolidated level, continue to expect ~45-50% top-line revenue growth for the full year with doubling of operational EBITDA, a target weighted to the second half as consumer utilization builds through the year.

Company declined to disclose specific PAT margin percentage estimates for FY30 or beyond the stated milestones.

key_takeaways: Consolidated revenue grew 55% year-on-year to INR3,955 million, up 8% sequentially on what was already the strongest quarter in our history.

Aerospace grew 40% year-on-year and our consumer segment nearly tripled, reflecting the consumer electronics ramp at Hubballi. Consumer contributed 19% of our revenue this quarter, up from 10% the year ago.
Reported EBITDA at INR215 million is lower than the Q4, but that movement is mainly due to other income, foreign exchange, which was unusually high in the Q4.

On the operational basis, excluding the other income, EBITDA improved from INR42 million in Q4 to INR148 million in Q1, a more than three-fold sequential improvement, driven by narrowing consumer loss.
Our consumer segment EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million sequentially. The path to consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 '27 now has its first quarterly proof point.

We signed long-term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers, expanding our global base. And we signed our first contract for fully integrated Airbus A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems.
These wins come after a quarter-end order book of over USD1 billion. You should see these new wins reflect in the next quarter's order book.
The defining achievement of the quarter was our aerospace order book crossing the USD1 billion mark, following a 13% sequential increase from USD889 million.

At a consolidated level, we continue to expect approximately 45% to 50% top-line revenue growth for the full year with the doubling of our operational EBITDA, a target that is weighted to the second half as consumer utilization builds through the year.

quarters.summary: FY26 was a landmark year with consolidated revenue growing 33% to INR12,304 million and EBITDA growing 43% to INR1,545 million (13% margin); Q4 was the strongest quarter ever with INR3,671 million revenue (47% YoY growth). For FY27, aerospace is guided to grow 25%-30% revenue with EBITDA margins maintained at 20%, consumer revenue growth of 125%-150% with EBITDA break-even targeted by Q4 FY27, and consolidated revenue growth of approximately 45%-50% with operational EBITDA expected to double; consolidated PAT is expected to hit break-even by H1 FY28.

key_figures.label: Consolidated Revenue incl. JV proportionate share
Consumer division capex funded through internal accruals this year

subsections.label: Margin & Cost Drivers
points: Margin compression from Q3 reflects the timing of consumer electronics capacity coming fully online.

In Q4, the company saw the full run rate of depreciation on consumer capex alongside the full operating costs while the plant is still operating at low utilization; this is the expected profile during the manufacturing ramp-up phase.
Reported Q4 PAT loss includes higher depreciation from consumer capex and increased tax provisions on the profit from the aerospace segment.
Full year PAT loss margin improved by 200 basis points from -11% in FY25 to -9% in FY26.
EBITDA margin improved by 100 basis points from 12% in FY25 to 13% in FY26.

subsections.label: Balance Sheet Drivers
points: Increase in total assets reflects significant capital invested in consumer electronics capacity during the year, increased working capital in line with revenue growth, and retained IPO proceeds.
Net debt-to-equity improvement to 0.23x shows the company is well capitalized for the next phase of growth.

Fixed asset turnover moderated because significant consumer electronics assets have been added that are not yet generating proportionate revenue; as utilization improves through FY27, this ratio is expected to recover meaningfully.

Net working capital days increased primarily driven by growth in revenues, and also by proactive inventory build-up (4-6 weeks ahead of time) to protect customer deliveries amid West Asia crisis-related logistics disruptions, predominantly on the aerospace side.

Company is taking these inventory precautions for probably another two quarters until stabilization is seen; sea logistics lead times have increased by five to six weeks and air logistics by six to eight days.

subsections.label: Capex & Funding
points: Aerospace segment capex planned at approximately INR160 crores for FY27.
Consumer segment capex planned at approximately INR500 crores for FY27.
FY27 capex will be funded through leveraging borrowings along with internal accruals.
Consumer segment gross block stands at approximately INR830 crores, expected to reach ~INR1,330 crores after the planned INR500 crore addition.
Karnataka MoU investment of INR2,856 crores is planned over the next 5 years across Belagavi and Hubballi clusters, covering both aerospace and consumer segment capacity.

subsections.label: Leadership Transition
points: CFO Dinesh Iyer has informed the company of his decision to step down at the end of June 2026 for personal reasons.
Company is searching for a CFO replacement; Harish Bang, VP-Finance, will be in-charge and the single point of contact in the interim.

subsections.label: Aerospace Portfolio Expansion
points: Added 433 new parts in Q4 alone, taking total aerospace portfolio to 5,654 SKUs, a 26% increase since last year.
Each SKU represents a rigorous qualification cycle, a secured long-term contract, and a deep-rooted customer relationship acting as a high entry barrier to others.

Company is actively moving up the value chain into landing gear and engine components, where integrated forging, machining, and surface treatment capabilities deliver competitive advantages; these are higher complexity, higher value products commanding better margins and deeper customer relationships.
Aerospace segment EBITDA of 27% includes other income and excludes unallocated corporate costs; like-for-like (excluding these two elements) the company continues to drive a 20% EBITDA margin.

subsections.label: Consumer Segment Ramp-up
points: Consumer business scaling steadily with growing contribution to overall top-line, reflecting a planned transition from pilot production to commercial ramp-up.
Based on increasing requirements from customers, company is expanding capacity; primary focus this year is driving capacity utilization from 23% today to 40%-50% by year end.

Hasbro has revised its manufacturing and sourcing strategy and informed the company it will stop raising POS with Aequs; this was unexpected but will not impact overall growth of the business as the company continues serving other equally large and strategic customers.
Company signed a long-term agreement with Mattel, and both sides are fully committed to scaling volumes; Mattel volumes are expected to absorb the capacity impact from Hasbro.

Consumer segment tracked at overall consumer level; consumer durables is a 50-50 joint venture that does not get consolidated in the consumer segment, so a split between consumer electronics, plastics, and durables verticals is not disclosed separately.
On plastics/toys, the company operates as a contract manufacturer for brands and does not own IP for these products; it may develop internal process IP but does not patent it.

Heavy depreciation load from strategic consumer investments will keep overall consolidated PAT negative for much of the year, but as consumer volumes ramp up and aerospace continues strong performance, consolidated PAT is expected to hit break-even by H1 FY28.

Q4 was the first quarter where all manufacturing costs hit simultaneously with new capacity recently commissioned; consumer electronics team is moving through the learning curve of a new production environment, which is standard in a manufacturing ramp-up phase.
As utilization improves from 23% to the 40%-50% target, depreciation and fixed costs will be absorbed across higher volumes and margins will recover sharply.
At steady state, consumer segment is expected to deliver similar ROCE as the aerospace segment.
Consumer segment margins expected to reach 18%-20% (similar to aerospace) once utilization reaches around 75%-80% level; journey is driven by utilization progression.

subsections.label: Geographic Entities within Aerospace
points: US entity works predominantly on US ITAR/US defense programs.
France entity works on engine and landing gear components; helps bring engine and landing gear capability to the group.
No capacity additions are planned for France or US entities; all capacity expansion focus is on India.
In France and US, utilization is driven by people-hours (single shift basis) rather than machine hours as in India; the published metric appears lower because it is measured on machine hours.

subsections.label: Manufacturing Footprint
points: Manufacturing footprint spans three integrated clusters in India — Belagavi, Hubballi and Koppal — supported by facilities in Cholet, France, and Paris, Texas in the United States.

Company scaled manufacturing operations steadily throughout the year to support new and existing programs, closing FY26 with 434 CNC machines and 179 molding machines, representing a disciplined expansion of manufacturing muscle.
Company evaluates capacity requirements continuously and keeps adding based on requirements.

subsections.label: New Investment Announcements
points: In February 2026, signed an MoU with the government of Tamil Nadu to invest INR1,900 crores over 10 years for a new vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem within a new aerospace and defense park at Hosur, across 250 acres in the SIPCOT Shoolagiri Industrial Park — India's first fully vertically integrated aero engine and landing gear components manufacturing ecosystem.

In March 2026, signed a second MoU with the government of Karnataka, committing INR2,856 crores over five years across existing clusters in Belagavi and Hubballi, covering expansion of aerospace precision engineering operations in Belagavi and significant capacity enhancement for the consumer segment at Hubballi.
Collectively, these investments accelerate the broader objective of making Aequs and India a premier destination for global aerospace and consumer precision manufacturing.
Karnataka investment is over the next 5 years; a similar annual investment pattern to this year's (INR500 crores consumer, INR160 crores aerospace) is expected to continue over the 5-year period.

subsections.label: Consumer Capacity Economics
points: Consumer segment gross block of approximately INR830 crores, expected to grow to ~INR1,330 crores after the planned INR500 crore capex addition.
Expected asset turnover at peak utilization for consumer electronics is closer to 1.5x, not 2x.
Management expects to reach a turnover figure (~INR2,000 crores implied) around calendar year 2029.

Additional capex in consumer segment is driven by clear customer demand and the opportunity to capture a meaningful share of the customer's India manufacturing requirement; if the company doesn't scale, the customer will look at alternates.

subsections.label: Vertical Integration Benefits
points: Vertically integrated ecosystem approach (e.g., forging, machining, surface treatment) gives a solution to the customer beyond just margin — enables customers to give more work in an integrated ecosystem within a single zone.
ESG requirements increasingly favor parts not traveling long distances, which the single-zone Belgaum ecosystem addresses, creating a competitive advantage and higher 'right to win' business.
Success of aerostructures ecosystem gives customer confidence to support Aequs building out the engine ecosystem as well.

Company believes it has achieved the right level of margins for the business; increasing margins further could reduce win rate in the competitive global environment; feels it is achieving the right combination of ROCE and growth.

subsections.label: Currency/Export Exposure
points: Including deemed exports, approximately 93%-94% of overall sales are US dollar-linked, even though most domestic sales are deemed exports/domestic dominated.

subsections.label: Raw Material Procurement & Lead Times
points: Titanium and superalloys/some steels involve long lead times; specific steels currently have some of the longest lead times in the industry at 65-75 weeks; titanium is typically 52 weeks.
Company can buy spot material but at prohibitive cost; procurement strategy is all about planning and executing based on customer demand signals.

Material for aeroengine vs aerostructure is mostly enabled/directed by the customer in terms of where to buy; it is more of a different process than a fundamentally different material sourcing approach.

Due to West Asia crisis and geopolitical disruption, the company has proactively increased material coverage to approximately 125% of a quarter's needs (which may spill into next quarter demand), up from a historical ~70% coverage at the beginning of a quarter.
This strategy change costs additional working capital but ensures customer delivery commitments are protected.
Precaution of elevated inventory buildup is expected to continue for probably another two quarters until stabilization is seen.

Material prices are largely covered under long-term agreements on the aerospace side; company saw some supply constraints and a slight increase in logistics costs during the last quarter, but these were not viewed as material to the business.
On the consumer side, plastics material prices have risen, but this is passed through to customers under back-to-back agreements, so there has been no significant impact on performance.

Regarding critical equipment dependency on China (flagged in DRHP) and reports of Chinese restrictions on certain equipment, the company has faced similar challenges in the past that continue to evolve; it is working with customers to find alternate geographic locations including India, but developing and qualifying suppliers for such equipment takes time since Chinese capability developed over decades.

subsections.label: Leadership & Talent
points: Ravi Kumar Assudani to join as Head of Engineering for the consumer segment effective Q1 FY2027; brings over 16 years of experience at Apple Inc., where he led global tooling and manufacturing design operations across multiple product lines.
Deepening leadership bench to scale precision component manufacturing for global consumer electronics OEMs, requiring a unique combination of engineering depth and operational discipline.

subsections.label: R&D Partnership
points: Established an advanced materials R&D ecosystem at IIT Dharwad campus, focused on cutting-edge material characterization, failure analysis, and manufacturing process simulation.
Partnership reflects Aequs' long-term commitment to strengthening India's advanced manufacturing ecosystem through sustained investment in research, innovation, and skill development.
Collaboration will enhance IIT Dharwad's applied research capabilities and industry engagements, apart from enabling Aequs to deliver cutting-edge products to customers.

subsections.label: Platform Strategy / Business Structure
points: Management describes the business as building a common precision manufacturing platform (e.g., CNC machines used in both consumer and aerospace metal operations, injection/molding machines used across both sides), not two independently siloed businesses subject to a holding-company discount.

When asked about a potential future spin-off of the consumer portfolio from the core aerospace business, management indicated the intent is to build a shared capability/platform to scale in the right way, not to run it as two separate discount-inducing businesses.
IPO completed during FY26 described as a transformational milestone marking a new chapter in the company's journey; retained IPO proceeds contributed to the increase in total assets.

subsections.label: Customer Concentration / Loss
points: Hasbro revised its manufacturing and sourcing strategy and will stop raising POS with Aequs — an unexpected development, though management does not expect it to impact overall business growth given other large strategic customers and the new Mattel agreement.

subsections.label: Geopolitical / Logistics Disruption
points: West Asia crisis has caused airspace closures and increased air freight costs; company saw supply constraints and a slight increase in logistics costs last quarter, though these were viewed as not material for the business.
Sea logistics lead times have increased by five to six weeks and air logistics by six to eight days due to the crisis.
Company has increased material coverage to ~125% of quarterly needs (versus historical ~70%) as a precaution, expected to continue for about two more quarters until stabilization.

subsections.label: China Equipment Dependency
points: DRHP had flagged dependency on China for critical equipment; there is recent feedback of Chinese restrictions on certain equipment.

Company has faced similar challenges in the past which continue to evolve; working with customers to find alternate geographic locations including India, but developing/qualifying suppliers for such equipment takes time since Chinese supplier capability developed over decades.

subsections.label: Raw Material Lead Times
points: Titanium and specific steels have very long lead times (52 weeks and 65-75 weeks respectively), requiring careful advance planning; spot buying is possible but cost-prohibitive.

subsections.label: Consumer Ramp-up Profile
points: Heavy depreciation load from consumer electronics capex will keep overall consolidated PAT negative for much of FY27, per management, though this is described as an expected ramp-up profile rather than an unexpected risk.

subsections.label: FY27 Priorities
points: First priority: continue to grow aerospace revenues profitably, supported by order book, capacity, and customer relationships, delivering 25%-30% revenue growth with EBITDA margins maintained at 20% at the segment level.
Second priority: drive consumer utilization, unlocking operating leverage embedded in the existing asset base.
Third priority: move consumer EBITDA to break-even by Q4 FY27, described as a major inflection point for consolidated profitability.

At consolidated level, expecting approximately 45%-50% top-line revenue growth with operational EBITDA projected to double, reflecting operating leverage embedded in the business model; FY27 is about translating expanded capacity into significant financial returns.
Consolidated PAT expected to hit break-even by H1 FY28 as consumer volumes ramp up and aerospace continues strong performance.

subsections.label: Long-Term Aerospace Growth Outlook
points: Management believes the aerospace growth rate (20%-plus) is achievable over the long term based on customer demand and order book visibility; there are not many aerospace companies of Aequs' size growing at this rate organically.
Engine components are not expected to materially impact FY27 revenue; this is a long-term opportunity starting FY28, with aerostructures continuing to be the core driver of this year's guidance.
Similar rate of EBITDA margin guidance is expected to continue long-term alongside the growth guidance.

subsections.label: PLI Income
points: No Production Linked Incentive (PLI) income was booked for FY26; FY27 will be the first year the company is eligible for PLI.

subsections.label: Depreciation & Interest Outlook
points: Q4 FY26 depreciation run rate of approximately INR45-46 crores will continue as a base, plus additions during FY27 for capacity enhancement in both aerospace and consumer segments.
Interest expense is expected to reduce compared to the previous year.

key_takeaways: FY26 has been a truly landmark year for Aequs, defined by strong execution, meaningful business expansion, and our IPO, a transformational milestone that marks a new chapter in our journey as a company.
Full year consolidated revenue growing by 33% to INR12,304 million. EBITDA grew 43% to INR1,545 million, with the margins expanding to 13%.
We capped-off the year with the strongest quarter in Aequs history, with INR3,671 million in revenue and 47% year-on-year growth.

In February 2026, we signed an MoU with the government of Tamil Nadu to invest INR1,900 crores for 10 years for a new vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem within a new aerospace and defense park at Hosur.
In March 2026, we signed a second MoU with the government of Karnataka, committing investments of INR2,856 crores over five years across our existing clusters in Belagavi and Hubballi.
As we enter FY27... this should deliver 25% to 30% revenue growth, with EBITDA margins maintained at 20% at the segment level [aerospace].
At a consolidated level, we are expecting approximately 45% to 50% top-line revenue growth... we project doubling our operational EBITDA.
Move our consumer EBITDA to break even by Q4 FY27, which will be a major inflection point for our consolidated profitability.
We fully expect to see consolidated PAT hit break-even by H1 FY28.

Hasbro has informed us that it has revised manufacturing and sourcing strategy and told us they will stop raising POS with us. While this decision was unexpected, it will not impact the overall growth of the business.
Dinesh Iyer, our Chief Financial Officer, has informed us of his decision to step down at the end of June 2026 for personal reasons.

quarters.summary: Q1 FY27 was operationally intense with customer qualification, capacity expansion, and acquisition execution progressing in parallel across four scale-up vectors: new Indian manufacturing capacity (Sangli/Stanley), Turkey expansion (NDOX PCS facility), expanding qualification with global OEMs/utilities (HVDC/FACTS/power products), and inorganic growth (Win-Win/WS insulators). Management guided revenue from new capacity to meaningfully show up from Q3-Q4 FY27, reiterated ~20% EBITDA margin modeling and ~20% FY27 growth guidance, flagged a temporary margin moderation particularly in Q3 from commissioning overheads and an aluminium cost pass-through lag, and indicated intent to raise capital (ceiling "less than ₹500cr") for the WS acquisition, US market entry, and next-gen tech projects.

subsections.label: Sangli new facility (Stanley)
points: Machinery installation progressing; management cited minor last mile issues around sequencing, utilities, and statutory interfaces, none of them structural.
Trial production targeted during the current month, subject to remaining approvals.

Commercial ramp constraint is qualifications, not machines: products are regulated and customer-approved-facility dependent, so the company cannot start producing everything overnight because customers want it only from an approved facility.

Approvals/audits path: must obtain local statutory clearances (pollution, factory inspector, building completion certificate, etc.), then ISO audits (9000/14000/OHSAS) taking about a month, then approximately 60 customer audits.
Guidance reiterated: approximately 6 months from opening the facility for audits to fully shift volumes.
Audit prioritization is project-driven: first focus is approvals for executing HVDC orders (Hitachi global approvals first, then Adani/PGCIL audits).
Revenue meaningfully shows up from Q3, with Q4 the point of turnaround; Q2 may see only small 'trickling' revenue.
Implied near-term risk: margin/throughput volatility due to commissioning overheads plus time-consuming customer qualification sequencing.

subsections.label: HV CTC magnet wire facility (new product line)
points: Machinery installation commencing; machines are already on.
New-to-company product expects 3-5 months stabilization.
Full production expected by Q4 this year.

subsections.label: NDOX Turkey — PCS (Power Conversion Systems) facility
points: Civil construction complete; operations expected to begin during Q3 this year.
Capacity context: a four gigawatt facility in Turkey, with almost one gigawatt already ordered.
Facility economics framed as light capex for high-tech manufacturing: entire facility costing about $2 million, good enough for at least $70-80 million peak revenue potential (timing not committed).

subsections.label: Commissioning overhead warning (cross-referenced)
points: New Sangli capacity brings fixed costs (depreciation, manpower, power, overhead) before utilization fully ramps up, causing expected temporary margin moderation particularly in Q3, normalizing as absorption improves over ~15 months.

subsections.label: International expansion thinking (Nehru exports; Europe vs US localization)
points: Nehru already supplying inside the Denmark grid, with more from the Swedish grid very soon.
Europe is described as inward looking in tender policies; management believes it would definitely need a facility somewhere in the European peninsula to scale there.
US seen as more open: US can be catered out of India.

subsections.label: Operating model shifts: group resource management and procurement integration
points: Management moving away from siloed company teams, increasingly looking at management as a common group resource rather than individual company teams.
Cross-deployment of leaders across NDOX/Nehru/others to scale integration capacity.
Appointed a Chief Procurement Officer to consolidate group purchasing, aggregate volumes, rationalize suppliers, and standardize common specifications.
Engineering/manufacturing/testing protocols being standardized across facilities to reduce qualification friction and improve scalability.

subsections.label: Competitive landscape note (China-linked bidders in India)
points: Management downplayed impact, arguing referenced entities are India-based operations with domestic sourcing constraints and are currently not meaningfully operational.
Quality Power supplies some components to such players (e.g., via Sukrut) and expects to supply developed GIS components as well.

subsections.label: Status / process
points: Confirmatory due diligence completed without adverse findings.
Enterprise value of ~₹315cr (per CFO).
Consolidation most probably in Q4 this year; being an SEZ property, the process is bureaucratic.

subsections.label: Why insulators (strategic bottleneck + leverage)
points: Management positioned insulators as a structural constraint in grid build-outs: cannot live without them.
Demand is slowing down growth, and every large multinational is getting stuck because of this.
Very few insulators players in the world; nobody is expanding, making the demand-supply mismatch even more extreme.
Not run as captive backward integration: each division internally buys from the cheapest source, and each division has to sell at the highest margin, even to the internal factory.

subsections.label: Asset base and upside
points: Site advantage: ~40 acres land in an SEZ campus; only ~8 acres currently used by the plant.
Run-rate potential of at least ₹300-400cr per year initially (management).
Later characterization: without capex ₹250-300cr, with capex ₹450-500cr peak contribution (investor Q&A).
Planned capex of ₹50cr proposed for enhancing capacity at that location, plus adding capabilities (not only volume) including composites used for bushings.

subsections.label: What happened historically (newsworthy detail)
points: WS ('Wetching House') is American-origin, a legacy exporter, shifted from Chennai to Vizag SEZ.
Disruptions from labor issues plus cyclone Hudhud; almost ₹240cr written off; plant idle for six to seven years.
Later investors renovated with about ₹150cr but got hit by the gas crisis, losing about ₹2cr a day as gas became expensive or unavailable, prompting the need for a larger balance sheet.
Plant has meaningful technical credentials: approved in over 15 countries, supplying 765 kV-class insulators into the US via white-labeling (to be stopped).

subsections.label: Margin profile expectation
points: Current observed range anywhere between 15% and 25%.
Margin profile expected to stabilize in about four quarters from the date of acquisition.

subsections.label: Qualification/approval sequencing risk
points: Products are regulated and customer-approved-facility dependent, limiting the pace at which new Sangli capacity can be commercially utilized despite machinery being ready.

subsections.label: Commissioning overhead / margin volatility
points: New Sangli capacity brings fixed costs before utilization ramps, expected to cause temporary margin moderation particularly in Q3.

subsections.label: Raw material pass-through lag
points: Aluminium price spike in Q1 expected to hit the P&L about six months later, with potential impact flagged for Q3.

subsections.label: Insulator supply-demand mismatch
points: Insulator demand is slowing growth for the industry broadly; very few insulator suppliers exist worldwide and none are expanding, making the mismatch more extreme.

subsections.label: IGBT bottleneck
points: Key bottleneck for PCS/BESS execution flagged as IGBTs across the world.

subsections.label: Europe market access constraint
points: Europe described as inward looking in tender policies, constraining ability to scale there without a local facility.

subsections.label: Turkey non-cash accounting drag
points: Turkey hyperinflation (IAS 29) accounting created a ₹7.82cr non-cash monetary loss impacting reported EBITDA in the quarter.

subsections.label: Historical insulator plant disruptions (context)
points: Historical labor issues, cyclone Hudhud, and a gas crisis caused significant write-offs and idle periods at the WS Vizag SEZ plant being acquired.

subsections.label: Forward posture: growth and margin
points: Management stuck to ~20% growth guidance for FY27, refusing to commit to higher numbers despite order book strength, citing it being very early in the year and preferring to err in caution.
Margin guidance: investors asked to model the company at 20% EBITDA margin, with management saying it will try to do better.

subsections.label: Fundraise
points: Intent indicated to raise capital (not fully quantified) primarily for (1) WS acquisition plus capex, (2) US market entry (sales office/team), and (3) next-gen tech projects.
Rough ceiling mentioned: less than ₹500cr.
Timing: attempt this month, before the AGM, with roadshows from around the 20th.

subsections.label: Long-term vision
points: Aspiration to be the alternative to Hitachi from India, not competing with them but complementing them.
Focus on high-technology grid segments (BESS/PCS, automation, HVDC/FACTS/power quality) and recycling free cash flow into further complementary acquisitions.

subsections.label: Capacity timing guidance recap
points: Sangli trial production targeted during the current month; revenue meaningfully shows up from Q3, turnaround visible by Q4; Q2 may see only small trickling revenue.
HV CTC magnet wire facility targeted for full production by Q4 this year.

subsections.label: Hyperinflationary accounting (Ind AS 29) - Endoks
points: Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin appears lower (19.1% vs 27.9% in Q3) and PBT margin lower (17.3% vs 26.1% in Q3) due to Ind AS 29 restatement, not underlying business deterioration.

Turkish subsidiary Endoks operates in a hyperinflationary economy per Ind AS 29; non-monetary items (PPE, inventories, equity) are restated using a general price index; monetary items (cash, receivables, payables) are not restated but lose purchasing power, and this loss is recognized in P&L under 'other expense'.
Q4 FY26 net monetary loss from this restatement was approximately INR 25.7 crores.
This is a purely accounting-driven, non-monetary, non-cash adjustment mandated by Ind AS 29; it does not flow into operating cash flow, working capital, or business performance.
Treatment is symmetric across quarters - earlier quarters had net monetary gains recognized under the same head, so QoQ optics fluctuate on index movements, not business reality.
Endoks underlying operating margins remain north of 25%, and business continues to deliver on commercial milestones including the new PCS facility at Nigde.
Normalized for the Ind AS 29 charge, consolidated PAT for FY26 would have crossed INR 210 crores.
Analysts encouraged to model Endoks on an Ind AS 29 normalized basis, treating monetary loss/gain entries as below-the-line non-operating items.
Endoks EBITDA margin on stable currency terms (excluding net monetary gain/loss/forex) was 32.01% last year and 32.13% this year despite 150% revenue growth, showing stability at the operating level.

subsections.label: Q4 one-time items
points: Q4 figures absorb one-time provisions related to new Indian Labour Codes across Indian operations and subsidiaries.

Other expenses increase also attributable to freight outward of INR 12 crores and LD (liquidated damages) of INR 5 crores; LD was a pre-acquisition item from Mehru subsidiary that has since been curtailed.

subsections.label: Mehru integration performance
points: Mehru delivered around 20% EBITDA margin in Q4 and 15% annualized within just one year of acquisition, supported by revenue stream expansion and deeper market penetration.

subsections.label: Capital allocation and cash preservation
points: Promoters and management have collectively decided to forgo any incremental salary for the second consecutive year and to forgo their share of dividend again this year, to preserve cash, strengthen balance sheet and minimize future dilution ahead of proposed fundraising.
Board recommended final dividend of INR 1 per share, with promoters voluntarily waiving entitlement.

Board approved enabling authorization to raise up to USD 75 million across permissible modes as strategic dry powder for international expansion, acquisitions and technology investments; funds will be called as and when required, not necessarily immediately.
Enabling fundraising resolution could support North America-related growth initiatives or acquisitions, subject to business plan and market comfort at appropriate time.
Company operates as an essentially debt-light enterprise with healthy interest coverage; almost 80% of factory has been completed without any debt from promoters, using current cash flow.

Cash in hand (~INR 250 crores) is earmarked partly for organic expansion and cash flow needs; some acquisitions under evaluation by BDNA committee are larger in value than current cash on hand, hence fundraising provision.

subsections.label: Other income and expense drivers

Cash-generated interest income expected to continue given large cash balance.

subsections.label: Order book composition and growth
points: Group order book exceeds INR 1,400 crores, about 1.4x last year's revenue.
Quality Power order book exceeding INR 520 crores; Mehru ~INR 430 crores; Endoks ~INR 450 crores.

During last quarter alone, added over INR 870 crores of fresh orders (corrected figure), reflecting increasing customer confidence and strong market demand; executed INR 300 crores of orders in the same quarter.

subsections.label: Pipeline and demand drivers
points: Business pipeline exceeds INR 1,100 crores for QP alone, including strong opportunities in FACTS systems, renewables and data center infrastructure.
Demand visibility robust across Middle East, Europe, United States and Australia, particularly in grid modernization, renewable integration, STATCOM applications and power quality solutions.

Data center demand: started with Microsoft in Finland last year; recently bagged an order from one of the 'big three' in the US (~INR 49 crores); expect a couple more projects in next few quarters; company already booked out on deliveries for HVDC and other projects, north of INR 500 crores current order book; new facility needed to take more orders.
BESS order book target of US$60-80 million for the year would make company the largest PCS manufacturer in the country by scale.

TAM sizing: largest competitor Trench Electric Limited (formerly Siemens-owned, now PE-owned) had EUR 1.5 billion pending order book as of last December; nearest competitor to Mehru in instrument transformers, Arteche (Spain), had revenues north of INR 3,500 crores - management believes opportunity size/TAM is not a constraint, execution is the challenge.

subsections.label: Order intake constraints and strategy
points: Order book growth is capped by execution capacity; company is not aggressively taking new orders in Sangli and Delhi facilities as order intake for next quarter is almost closed - only strategic orders are being pulled in.
Insulator component deliveries are running 18-24 months, hurting some projects; cable supply issues have been mitigated via vertical integration (own cable manufacturing).
Company targeting INR 1,500-1,800 crores order book before start of next year, but cautions this depends on execution capability given 12-month order book cycles and component constraints.
Order pipeline will pick up more in Q2/Q3 to support new capacities coming online.

Renewable vs conventional order book split difficult to quantify precisely as HVDC, energy storage, and data centers all connect to or are fed by renewable generation; roughly could be considered 50-50 given ~50% of India's generation is renewable, but company frames itself as grid-interconnection agnostic to source.

subsections.label: Segment strategy - growth vs margin trade-off
points: Company does not run as independent businesses each chasing own numbers; runs as a team with strategy where one business carries margin in a year while the other carries growth, and roles can flip.

This year, given raw material environment in the high voltage product business, company chose to chase growth in power electronics business, accepting some margin sacrifice; window to build scale and customer references in power electronics is now.

As power electronics scales, margins expected to follow; as energy storage ambition is pursued, component prices should ease with increased order volume, making future entry into Indian storage market more viable as electronic component costs approach Chinese price levels at volume.
High voltage product portfolio holds the margin line for the group meanwhile.

subsections.label: BESS/PCS business model and economics
points: BESS is a high voltage, high power inverter business similar to SVC/STATCOM products already built in Turkey (medium voltage).

Value chain has four components: battery (company does not intend to enter, as it's chemistry), power electronic inverter (manufactured in-house), software/EMS connecting BESS to grid, and transformer (in-house product).

Currently selling to developers of large renewable energy projects in Europe (not India yet, ACME/Avaada-type counterparts avoided; talking to European counterparts) due to better price realization in Turkey vs India; scaling in Europe first to build semiconductor volume/pricing before launching in India.
India BESS tenders are primarily O&M-oriented; company positions itself purely as a manufacturer, not O&M operator.
Data center BESS use case differs: battery component <1% with much larger converter share, used like a UPS for contingency backup alongside 50MW steam turbines.
Currently giving entire BESS container (software, hardware, integrated batteries) but open to selling converters standalone as company is a manufacturing entity.
Battery prices (a commodity) expected to at least halve in the next 2 years, meaning converters will become relatively more expensive than batteries, giving company more margin room.

subsections.label: HVDC/reactor/transformer segment economics
points: A classic 6GW HVDC LCC technology project entails INR 200-300 crores of reactors alone and another INR 50-70 crores of instrument transformers.
IGBT converter at 6GW level not yet operational; estimated coil business opportunity ~INR 70-100 crores.

Company bid on US$80-100 million of transformers in the US market this quarter but lost most bids; uncertain on scaling transformer business given global capacity build-out and lower margins versus current operations - not prioritizing low-margin transformer orders.
Company is engaged in multiple bids for transformers for data centers currently but treats this as non-priority given lower margins.

subsections.label: Quality Power vs Mehru vs Endoks focus areas
points: Quality Power currently focused on data centers with order book of about INR 520 crores; expects to execute first US data center order this year with more possibly completing this year or next.
Endoks (Turkish subsidiary) not focused on data centers; focused on renewable energy integration and large steel factories.
Mehru focused on GIS, high voltage, and AC substations - different customer base from Quality Power and Endoks.

subsections.label: Endoks revenue growth drivers
points: Endoks revenue growth (from prior years) driven by increased demand for power electronics support in grid integration for steel factories and renewables - fundamentally a demand-supply dynamic rather than a single new project or product.

subsections.label: In-house R&D and new product development
points: PCS (power conversion system) for grid-scale energy storage developed in-house by own R&D and engineering team, result of multi-year investments in power electronics design, testing capability and engineering depth.
1,725 KW PCS inverter design underway, expected to reach market over next few quarters (also referenced as within next two quarters at Endoks).
GIS (gas-insulated switchgear) is another patiently-invested category expected to deliver compounding contribution over time similar to earlier R&D-led products.
At Mehru, development of 765 kV product category is described as a clear signal that technology improvement is embedded in company culture.
Underlying habit across product lines: investing in capability ahead of demand, trusting in-house R&D, and moving the technology bar step by step.
Technology earns the company the right to participate in the most demanding tenders, while scale earns the right to win them - both considered primary competitive advantages.

subsections.label: PCS technical description
points: PCS is the power converter required to connect stored battery energy (DC) to the grid (AC), converting high power DC to high power AC via large power electronics base.
Software interface manages charge/discharge based on load demand forecast and exchange pricing plan rather than simple on/off like a home inverter.

Software connects to the main grid, creating data security/software security considerations where Chinese vendors are typically restricted, giving competitive advantage in US, European, and recently Indian markets (India recently mandated domestic software interconnection).

subsections.label: Semiconductor sourcing economics
points: Indian semiconductor market still evolving with few players and limited high-power capability; largest semiconductors sourced from European, Japanese or Chinese players.
Volume-based discount differential between $100,000 and $10 million order sizes can be as high as 40-50%, meaning scaling purchase volume directly drives margin improvement - a key competitive moat.

subsections.label: Capacity expansion projects
points: New Sangli factory expected to commence operations around July-August 2026, alongside commissioning of a new high-voltage test laboratory to enhance testing and execution capabilities; project managers internally still targeting December-January start but customer pressure pushing for faster delivery, with trial production and some deliveries targeted by end of year.
Sangli plant faced delays due to gas shortages and operating problems 'during the start of the conflict' but is now at full swing anticipating trial production.
At Mehru, additional oven capacity being added post-September 2026, along with development of GIS manufacturing and testing infrastructure.

Endoks setting up a new BESS manufacturing facility based on in-house developed technology at Nigde, targeted for December 2026, funded with about US$2 million given existing land banks in Turkey; construction expected to be fast.
Sangli plant capacity peak revenue potential is about INR 1,500 crores, subject to completing CTC cable expansion and resolving insulator supply problems.

Mehru plant can scale another 20-35% (last quarter did about INR 320 crores) before the plant saturates at current capacity; a new greenfield expansion is being explored in Turkey (not India), with more details expected next quarter.

Capital work-in-progress of INR 73 crores reflects active deployment across Sangli global coil manufacturing facility, HVDC/PCS/CTC magnet wire facility (on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning), Mehru's GIS and high-voltage testing equipment capex, and the new Endoks PCS facility at Nigde.

subsections.label: Vision and organizational building
points: Vision meet conducted at Panhala Fort involving nearly 95 senior and middle management members across the Quality Power Group to align on common long-term vision, mission and growth roadmap.
Deepening engagement with academia and bringing in regular training from renowned external trainers and institutions to build next layer of managers and engineers.
Company plans to add another 500-1,000 employees across business segments this year while building out facilities.

subsections.label: Geographic focus by entity
points: Turkish operations (Endoks) cater primarily to global/European load, while India (Quality Power/Mehru) focuses on India and near countries.
Company exports to Europe, Middle East, Australia, Southeast Asia, and is delivering HVDC in Australia and India.
Demand visibility robust across Middle East, Europe, United States and Australia.

Turkey positioned as manufacturing hub for Europe with land border to Germany (4 days by road) and only 11 days by sea to the US, providing freight/speed competitive advantage; raw material prices in Turkey similar to or lower than India for key inputs; labor costs about 4x India but not a major cost driver in this business.

Company has operated in Turkey for 16 years, receiving 'best R&D company of the year' recognition from the Turkish government/Prime Minister over the last 10 years; other Indian multinationals (Tata, Mahindra, JSPL, Birla) also have plants in Turkey.

subsections.label: Supply chain constraints and mitigation
points: Facing execution challenges related to insulators and winding conductors; mitigation initiatives underway including own cable manufacturing to improve supply reliability.
Geopolitical tensions, logistics disruptions, commodity volatility and supply chain constraints continue to impact industries globally; managed through vertical integration.
Global shifts accelerating movement towards diversified and resilient sourcing strategies, positioning India as a preferred global manufacturing and engineering destination.

Cable supply chain problems have been addressed through vertical integration (own cable manufacturing); insulators remain a critical bottleneck being explored for potential inorganic solution ('board is deciding something on the insulator side').

Logistics/container shortages during the quarter constrained revenue recognition (revenue would have been higher had logistics cleared up), resulting in increased inventories; expected better logistics-driven performance in Q1 next year as a result.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning - BESS
points: BESS market dominated by Chinese players globally; software and service support helps keep Chinese vendors out of Europe, US and Australia.
In India, only EMS currently needs domestic supply; power electronics still lacks large domestic manufacturing base and is largely imported.

GE identified as a large competitor but priced at a very high level; company not yet competing with GE in this product line as an 'upstart' in the market; primary competition viewed as Chinese players.

subsections.label: Competitive positioning - HV products
points: Largest competitor in coil/reactor products is Trench Electric Limited (formerly Siemens-owned, now PE-owned).
Nearest competitor to Mehru in instrument transformers is Arteche (Spain), a listed company.

Company generally does not compete with Hitachi, Siemens or GE; these are customers or partners in different markets - company creates/develops/buys products these majors do not manufacture in order to complement rather than compete with them.
For coil products, Hitachi and Siemens do not manufacture this product; GE has only a small factory in Brazil - for Indian subcontinent, Asia and Europe, these majors buy from Quality Power.
For high voltage instrument transformers, Hitachi, Siemens and GE reportedly buy more from Quality Power in India than from their own facilities due to volume and scale.
In battery energy storage, majors are described as far more expensive and not operating in the markets the company targets.

subsections.label: Customer strategy
points: BESS customer targeting focused on renewable energy developers in Europe rather than large Indian developers like ACME or Avaada, to leverage better European pricing and build volume before an India launch.
Data center customers include Microsoft (Finland) and one of the US 'big three' for a recent ~INR 49 crores order; demand exists for eco-reactors for large data center build-outs globally.

subsections.label: Fundraising enabling resolution
points: Enabling resolution for fundraising placed before shareholders is a long-term growth capital enabler available as and when required, not necessarily to be drawn immediately.
Could support future expansion opportunities including North America-related growth initiatives or acquisitions, subject to business plan and market comfort at appropriate time.
Board approved enabling authorization to raise up to USD 75 million across permissible modes as strategic dry powder for international expansion, acquisitions and technology investments.
Some acquisitions under evaluation by the BDNA (M&A) committee are larger in value than current cash on hand, necessitating the fundraising provision; cash on hand also needed for organic expansion.

subsections.label: M&A and stake strategy
points: No current plan to increase stake in Endoks; may consider in future.

Strategy focus is on gaining access to critical technologies for development rather than increasing ownership stake for its own sake; internal technology transfer between locations is charged at a 1-2% royalty.
Company prefers investing in newer technology areas for growth over simply increasing EPS via higher ownership stakes.

Company is considering inorganic opportunities in power electronics/battery storage (top priority), high voltage power products (second priority), and insulators (third priority, viewed as a critical bottleneck globally) - though no specific plans confirmed ('all in good time').

subsections.label: Nebeskie/Sukrut acquisition integration
points: Sukrut (Nebeskie) consolidated for about three months post-takeover from Jan 5th; still in technology development phase with small current revenue contribution; expected to scale over next couple of years.
Sukrut has turned around, halving losses versus last year; targeting 70-75% growth this year without losing money while building team and technology; aggressive scale-up planned over next two years.

subsections.label: Supply chain and geopolitical risks
points: Geopolitical conditions across several corridors continue to make an already congested supply chain more difficult; industry-wide realities being managed through vertical integration.
Execution challenges related to insulators and winding conductors continue; insulator delivery lead times running 18-24 months, hurting some projects.

Commodity/raw material price volatility, especially linked to geopolitical conflict and dollar movements, makes margin guidance difficult; company cannot guide precise future margins given volatility, though historically orders have been booked at similar or higher margins.

Raw material cost pass-through to customers occurs with a lag, creating potential short-term margin pressure (management expects Q1/Q2 next year could see a margin dip of a couple of percentage points, though not expected to be very large given 33% margins in some high voltage product lines and continued volume growth).

subsections.label: Accounting/reporting risk
points: Ind AS 29 hyperinflationary accounting for Turkish subsidiary Endoks creates volatile optics on consolidated other expense/EBITDA/PBT margins quarter to quarter due to indexation-driven net monetary gain/loss, though it does not affect underlying cash-generating performance.

subsections.label: Geopolitical risk - Turkey/India relations
points: Analyst raised concern about Middle East crisis and India-Turkey political tensions potentially impacting Turkish operations; management does not see problems given 16-year operating history, government recognition, and presence of other Indian multinationals in Turkey; views geopolitical decisions as more of a P&L consideration than an operational risk given favorable freight/logistics and raw material cost dynamics.

subsections.label: One-time cost items
points: Q4 results include one-time provisions related to new Indian Labour Codes across Indian operations and subsidiaries, which weighed on Q4 profitability.

key_figures.label: Target order book before start of next year
Initial EBITDA margin guidance range (early teens to 20%)

subsections.label: S-curve growth trajectory
points: Company guiding to an 'S-curve' this year - FY27 is a stabilization/team-building/capacity-building year with muted growth guidance of 15-20%, as new factory (Sangli) is not yet ready (audits take 6 months) and Mehru new ovens only arrive around September; most growth currently being delivered from Endoks.
FY28 expected to return to growth north of 50% as new capacities come online.

Confirmed view (in response to analyst question) that FY27 is roughly a 20% growth year, with FY28 seeing more than 50% type growth, following the S-curve journey, with possible near-term margin impact from shortages.

subsections.label: Margin outlook
points: Traditional high-voltage product line margins expected to hold with maybe a couple of points of variability due to conflict-related price increases; company happy with current margin levels in this segment.

BESS/power electronics margins currently 10-12% at converter/bid level, expected to scale to 17-18% as volume increases and semiconductor purchasing scale improves; battery pass-through margin only 2-3% since batteries are passed through the balance sheet as part of integrated containers.

Gross margin (46-47.7% range in Q4) sustainability uncertain due to geopolitical volatility and dollar impact on raw material costs; management cannot guide precise numbers but notes orders were booked at similar or higher margins; expects possible couple of percentage point dip in Q1/Q2 next year as a short-term impact, not a large one.

subsections.label: Prior guidance track record
points: At start of FY26, company had guided to a revenue band of roughly INR 800 crores with EBITDA margins between early teens and 20%; later revised upward to INR 900 crores revenue with ~22% EBITDA margin aspiration.
Company closed FY26 above the revised range: INR 1,007 crores revenue and approximately 23.8% (also cited as 23.5%) EBITDA margin, exceeding guidance.

EBITDA margin aspiration of around 22%

Targeting at least INR 1,500 crores to INR 1,800 crores of order book before the start of next year

Believe BESS is a billion-dollar opportunity to be realistic, growing into a billion-dollar opportunity in the next few years
Targeting close to 500 to 600 MW of converter manufacturing this year
Anticipate the 10%-12% converter margin to scale to about 17%-18% for the inverter as volume increases
New Sangli factory expected to commence operations around July-August 2026, alongside new high-voltage test laboratory
Peak revenue from Sangli factory could be about INR 1,500 crores, subject to CTC cable expansion completion and insulator problem resolution
Additional oven capacity being added at Mehru post-September 2026, along with GIS manufacturing and testing infrastructure development
Mehru plant can scale another 20-35% before saturating at current capacity
