risk_register.risk: Geopolitical tensions across corridors making an already congested supply chain more difficult
risk_register.note: Industry-wide reality; being managed through vertical integration.

risk_register.risk: Execution challenges related to insulators and winding conductors
risk_register.note: Insulator delivery lead times running 18-24 months, hurting some projects; own cable manufacturing initiative underway as mitigation; insulator bottleneck remains unresolved and being explored for potential inorganic solution.

risk_register.risk: Raw material/commodity price volatility linked to geopolitical conflict and dollar movements
risk_register.note: Makes forward margin guidance difficult; cost pass-through occurs with a lag; possible couple of percentage point margin dip expected in Q1/Q2 FY27.

risk_register.risk: Hyperinflationary accounting (Ind AS 29) creating optical volatility in reported margins
risk_register.note: Non-cash, indexation-driven; treatment symmetric across quarters (gains and losses); does not affect underlying cash-generating performance.

risk_register.risk: India-Turkey geopolitical tensions / Middle East crisis potentially affecting Turkish operations
risk_register.note: Management does not see problems given 16-year operating history in Turkey, government recognition, and presence of other Indian multinationals there.

risk_register.risk: New Indian Labour Codes compliance costs
risk_register.note: One-time provisions taken in Q4 across Indian operations and subsidiaries, impacting Q4 profitability.
Constrained Q4 revenue and increased inventories; expected to support better Q1 next year performance as backlog clears.

risk_register.risk: Loss of transformer bids in US market
risk_register.note: Lost most of US$80-100 million transformer bids in the US market this quarter; company also uncertain on scaling transformer business given global capacity build-out and lower margins.

Sangli and Delhi facilities have almost closed order intake for next quarter; company only pulling in strategic orders due to inability to deliver more; growth in orders expected to resume once new capacity comes online.

themes.label: Order book strength
themes.note: Group order book crosses INR 1,400 crores (1.4x FY26 revenue), with strong fresh order intake of INR 870 crores last quarter.

themes.label: BESS/PCS scale-up
themes.note: BESS order book at US$31 million targeting US$60-80 million this year, positioning company as largest domestic PCS manufacturer and eyeing a billion-dollar opportunity.

themes.label: Hyperinflationary accounting optics (Ind AS 29)
themes.note: Endoks Turkish subsidiary's Ind AS 29 net monetary loss of INR 25.7 crores distorts quarterly margin optics but is non-cash and does not affect underlying operating performance.

themes.label: Supply chain bottlenecks (insulators/conductors)
themes.note: Insulator lead times of 18-24 months and winding conductor constraints are capping order intake and delivery, partially mitigated via vertical integration into cables.

themes.label: Capacity expansion / S-curve growth
themes.note: New Sangli, Mehru and Endoks facilities coming online through 2026 justify a muted 15-20% FY27 growth guide before an expected >50% growth in FY28.

themes.label: Technology-led moat (GIS, PCS, 765kV)
themes.note: In-house R&D across PCS, GIS and 765kV product categories seen as building a technology moat alongside a scale moat.

themes.label: Cash preservation and fundraising optionality
themes.note: Promoters forgo salary/dividend again and company seeks enabling USD 75 million fundraise authorization as dry powder for M&A/expansion, while remaining debt-light.

key_takeaways: We have crossed for the first time INR 1,000 crores in total revenue with an EBITDA of INR 236 crores, in spite of the write-off adjustment.
Q4 was our highest ever quarter at about INR 310 crores in total revenue.

At the start of the year, we had guided to a revenue band of roughly INR 800 crores with EBITDA in margins between early teens and to 20%. We have closed the year above that range on revenue and at approximately 23.8% margins.
We enter FY27 with an order book of over INR 1,400 crores, about 1.4x last year's revenue.

FY26 has closed comfortably ahead of every guidance milestone we set for ourselves at the start of the year - closed the year at a consolidated revenue of INR 1,007 crores, a growth of nearly 157% YoY, with a full-year EBITDA margin of 23.5%.
Full-year EBITDA stands at INR 236 crores, up by 98%. Profit before tax at INR 216 crores, up by 93%, and PAT at INR 185 crores, up by 85% YoY.
Normalized for this Ind AS 29 charge, our consolidated PAT for FY26 would have crossed INR 210 crores.

The board has also approved an enabling authorization to raise up to USD 75 million across permissible modes, strategic dry powder for international expansion, acquisitions, and technology investments.
The guidance would be, as of now... around 15% and 20% [for FY27], and the next year, I think we should be going north of 50% again.
pressing_questions: Can you shed more light on your fundraising plans? What are the sources through which you are planning to raise, considering the fact that you are having a cash balance of almost INR 250 crores in your books now?
Regarding your INR 1,400 crores order books, can you quantify how much comes from renewable sources?

Regarding your Turkish operations - the Middle East crisis and political situation between India and Turkey is not very good at this point of time - are you apprehending any negative impact due to this?
Can you give the revenue bifurcation for Mehru, Quality Power and Endoks, and the operating margin for each?
If you could provide the details on the order bid pipeline separately for Mehru, Endoks and Quality Power?
Since Turkey's currency is largely stable now, is there any hedging related income that came in this quarter, and what kind of numbers should we assume while forecasting other income?
Since you do not have any kind of price variation clauses, how are you managing the commodity cost inflation, and is there a possibility that Q1 margins can see some kind of dip?

quarters.summary: Management sees the commodity/pig iron downcycle as having turned, with sequential margin improvement expected in Q2/Q3 FY27 as price pass-through concludes (largely done in castings, still under discussion in alloy steel/tubes). Castings demand remains broad-based and strong with Rajpura sold out and Solapur foundry ramping, while tubes remain the key swing factor due to adverse mix, dumping, and subdued oil & gas order flow; capex plans span renewables, foundry expansion, pig iron/steel upgrades and tube capability enhancement, with FY27 capex guided at ₹600-700 cr rising with large project triggers.

subsections.label: Other expenses spike (key explanation)
points: Increase largely from power & fuel: 'the increase is 58 crores… in power and fuel.'

Split between rate vs volume: ~₹28–29 cr from tariff/rate increase; ~₹28 cr from higher consumption/quantity (notably higher casting activity at Rajpura and no Jejuri shutdown like last year): 'casting production and sales in Rajpura has increased… last year we had long shutdown of Jujeri plant, and this time we are running normal full month.'

subsections.label: Structural regulatory hit to power optimization (Maharashtra)
points: Power trading benefit lost: 'We used to get about 10 crores per annum of benefit by power trading… that has stopped.'
Green power usage window curtailed: 'Earlier we were allowed to use the green power for 17 hours, now it is only allowed for eight hours.'
Direct implication: renewable projects still pay back but less: 'instead of getting 100 crore benefit in a year, we may get 80 crores… payback… from three years may go to 3.6 or 3.7 years.'
Management's mitigation path is explicit: battery storage is the workaround—'all that will become possible if we have battery storage.'

key_figures.label: Pig iron external sales growth YoY

subsections.label: Pig iron ('Pigaran')
points: Management attributed lower external sales to higher internal consumption, noting last year's Q1 had 'stoppage of JG plant for a few days', depressing internal consumption then.

Management stated it 'improved sales realization on Pigaran' and later highlighted the downcycle has likely turned: 'continuously falling commodity prices have taken a break… Pigaran prices have gone up.'
Export parity support noted: 'we are also exporting 30,000 metric tons of Pigarin… realization is likely better than domestic prices.'

subsections.label: Castings
points: Realizations held despite broader commodity weakness: 'we could hold the sales realization on castings.'
Management emphasized resilience in prior periods: 'though the commodity prices went down, our casting realization did not go down, rather, we maintained or slightly improved.'

subsections.label: Tubes
points: Realizations were pressured by adverse mix: 'we had to sell more of line types in the absence of high realizing export orders as well as… oil and gas tubes.'
Tubes remain the most explicitly volatile segment, with headwinds from dumping and weaker oil & gas order flow.

key_figures.label: Tube size coverage (current, up to 10 inches)

subsections.label: Renewable power (near-term commissioning; but regulatory headwind)
points: 35 MW solar plant: 'in the stage of commissioning'; expected commissioned Jun–Sep quarter.
12 windmills (2.1 MW each): also targeted for Jun–Sep commissioning.
Management is evaluating MW-scale battery storage to restore/expand benefits under new regulations.

subsections.label: Foundry/castings expansion and forward integration
points: Solapur 'two-part / no-bake' foundry (large castings): capacity 15,000 TPA (management clarified phase structure: 'phase one, phase two, we have plugged together to make it to 15,000… There will be no more on that.').
Commissioning targeted by October.
Ramp expectation: within 1–1.5 years reach 500–600 T/month (vs 1,250 T/month nameplate); full utilization about one more year after that.
Demand visibility: 'One of the customers wants the full capacity.' Management already exploring another large casting foundry.
Rajpura foundry expansion (two phases): Existing ~25k TPA; Phase 1 to 40–50k TPA in ~8 months; Phase 2 to 6,000 T/month (~70k TPA).
Current situation: 'Rajpura Foundry is totally sold out.'
Group casting capacity (post expansions): stated 'realizable' capacity across foundries: ~270,000 TPA.
To reach 300,000 TPA castings: 'in three to four years' (with a potential 7th foundry).

subsections.label: Pig iron upgrades and cost efficiency
points: Blast furnace upgrade to 300 m³; pig iron capacity up to 360,000 TPA.
Efficiency projects: pulverized coal injection (PCI) and other features already in BF1/BF2; further expansion underway.
Oxygen plant + enhanced PCI at blast furnaces: completion expected Feb–Mar (next year implied).

subsections.label: Steel and rolling expansion
points: Rolling capacity at Jejuri ('JD') to 25,000 T/month from 15,000; implies ~300,000 TPA rolling, with ~240,000 TPA saleable external alloy steel.
Koppal steel plant: early-stage; MD stated they are ready and intend to proceed; execution horizon ~2 years.
Converting one BF to steelmaking: 'all the government clearances in place… press the button… commissioned within two years' (land clearance within existing premises still needed).

subsections.label: Tubes: product capability upgrades + premiumization
points: Premium couplings project (Baramati): ordering expected 'in next few weeks' time.'
Expander mill (to make larger seamless tubes up to 18"): build time ~2 years; management expects reaching ~350k TPA tubes 3–4 years out.

Strategic rationale (internal actions to raise oil & gas mix): expand processing capacity to execute project 'windows'; bring premium couplings in-house; expand size range: 'only up to 10 inches… covers only around 60%… if we go up to 18 inches… another 40%.'

subsections.label: Total capex envelope
points: FY27 capex indicated ₹600–700 cr, but expected to rise as large projects trigger.
Medium-term: 'around three to three and a half thousand crores in next four years.'

subsections.label: Weaker/volatile demand
points: Oil & gas tubes—'oil and gas related activity is subdued because of which the volumes are less. Export volumes… got affected.'
No major substitution concern acknowledged: When asked about seamless losing share to welded, management replied: 'This volatility is nothing to do with that.'

risk_register.note: Alloy steel pass-through still under discussion with delay; tubes pass-through is market-driven, not contractual.

risk_register.risk: Forest development fee contingent liability (~₹350 cr)
risk_register.note: Karnataka 2016 levy at 8%; High Court favored industry, state appealed; pending Supreme Court judgment; company continues to provide and disclose as contingent.

risk_register.risk: Commodity price volatility (pig iron, steel, tube)
risk_register.note: Pig iron commodity market has fallen continuously for the last 3 years without substantial fall in raw material prices; management expects the pain is over but realizability of international price gains ($475) into Indian pricing is uncertain.
Dollar has risen to INR95 and coal prices have risen by about $25/ton on average; coking coal has further risen ahead of Q1 FY27, adding cost pressure.

risk_register.risk: Operational stoppages (Hiriyur blast furnace, steel plant)
risk_register.note: Hiriyur blast furnace was stopped for ~3.5 months in FY26 due to unfavorable market conditions causing a 68,000 ton shortfall; one blast furnace also had a 5-day stoppage in Q4; steel plant took two fortnight stoppages for fume extraction system erection.

risk_register.risk: War/geopolitical and macro disruption (tariffs, Middle East war, Hormuz blockage, fuel costs)
risk_register.note: Management cited tariff period, Middle East war, Hormuz blockage, high fuel costs, and disruptions in many areas as headwinds, though demand and growth have been sustained despite them.

risk_register.risk: Regulatory changes affecting green power utilization
risk_register.note: New government regulations in Maharashtra could restrict prime slot solar utilization; some utilization-period regulation changes are currently sub judice, affecting FY26 power benefit realization; company exploring battery storage to mitigate.
Solapur ramp-up is described as 'ticklish' due to core productivity and complexity of casting (complicated blocks and heads), not customer-related, requiring time to stabilize process and output.
ONGC order for seamless tubes has seen a delay; management does not have exact pending order figures currently.

themes.label: Commodity price recovery
themes.note: Management believes the commodity downtrend has reversed: 'continuously falling commodity prices have taken a break,' with pig iron prices up and steel price hikes announced.

themes.label: Input cost inflation
themes.note: Power and fuel costs increased ₹58 crores from both tariff rate hikes and higher consumption/quantity.

themes.label: Casting volume growth & capacity expansion
themes.note: Castings production/sales grew 19%/18% YoY; Rajpura sold out, Solapur foundry commissioning targeted by October, group casting capacity roadmap to 300,000 TPA in 3-4 years.

themes.label: Backward integration & green power
themes.note: 35 MW solar and 12 windmills targeted for Jun-Sep commissioning, but Maharashtra regulatory changes cut green power usage window and trading benefits, prompting battery storage evaluation.

themes.label: Realization mix shift (value-added castings/exports)
themes.note: Casting realizations held/improved despite commodity weakness, while tube realizations were pressured by adverse mix from lower export and oil & gas volumes.

themes.label: Operational disruptions (Hiriyur, steel plant)
themes.note: No Jejuri plant shutdown this year (unlike prior year) contributed to higher casting activity and consumption at Rajpura.

themes.label: Deleveraging & capex discipline
themes.note: FY27 capex guided at ₹600-700 crores, expected to rise as large projects trigger, with medium-term capex of ₹3,000-3,500 crores over next four years.

key_takeaways: Near-term earnings swing factors are (1) power/fuel inflation + regulatory changes in Maharashtra, (2) timing of price pass-through (castings largely done; steel pending), and (3) tubes mix recovery (oil & gas/export normalization).

Management confidence is anchored in: Commodity stabilization + pig iron export support; Strong casting demand and sold-out Rajpura capacity; A clearly staged capex plan (renewables commissioning, large castings, rolling expansion, steelmaking at Koppal, expander mill for tubes).

Most explicit headwind remains tubes: dumping and subdued oil & gas are restraining high-margin mix; management response is capability expansion (premium couplings + expander mill) rather than short-term pricing levers.
pressing_questions: When asked about seamless losing share to welded, management replied: 'This volatility is nothing to do with that.'

quarters.summary: Management expects commodity price recovery (pig iron, steel, tube) to support realizations in FY27, targets ~15% volume growth in casting (production ~1,85,000-1,90,000 MT incl. Oliver), 10-11% volumetric growth in tubes, continued capex of INR600-700 crores/year across pig iron, foundry, steel and tube expansion, and progress on backward integration (mines, beneficiation, pellet plant, green power) while flagging commodity price volatility, cost inflation (coal, dollar) and Hiriyur blast furnace stoppage as key headwinds.

subsections.label: Sales realization pressure
points: Overall top-line growth of 3% (standalone) / 5.1% (including Oliver) was achieved after accounting for drop in sales realizations due to low commodity prices.
Quarter 4 saw pig iron prices and steel prices pick up, partially offsetting the annual realization drop.
Tube realization dropped ~10% for the year; management expects at least half of this drop to be recovered in FY27 as pig iron, steel, power and fuel costs rise.

subsections.label: EBITDA margin trajectory
points: Compared to October, pig iron prices are up INR5,000/ton; compared to December, up INR4,000/ton.
Cost pressures include dollar at INR95 and coal prices up by about $25 per ton, which will factor into costs even as value addition improves.
Management stated current EBITDA is just above 12.5%, and is comfortable only at 15% EBITDA; effort continues across all products for volume growth.

subsections.label: Capital allocation
points: Cash generation is better than the company's ability to invest; borrowings have been reduced substantially.
Company plans to continue investing at INR600-700 crores/year across pig iron, foundry, steel and tube, and hopes to generate cash better than that.
Obligation areas for investment include making mines operational, beneficiation plant, and pellet plant.

subsections.label: Merger update
points: Company is working on merger of Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries, expecting to close in the next couple of months to get merger benefit for FY25-26 itself.

subsections.label: Casting business growth journey
points: Management considers 20-25% growth targets not realistic; targets volumetric growth of ~15% as reasonably good.
Casting production grew from 1,39,000 to 1,62,000 tons, about 23,000 tons more produced and sold.
Company expects to march forward to about 1,90,000 tons due to large number of castings under development moving into serial production.
Demand for casting remains robust from auto sector and tractor sector.
Sixth foundry (large casting foundry) to be commissioned; expected to get good loading given growth in large castings.
Large capacity underutilization exists at Solapur; effort is to take Solapur to 60,000 tons.
Company has started working on creating a seventh foundry to avoid manufacturing capacity shortfall over next 2-3 years.
Feasibility exists for future aspirational volume growth up to 3 lakh metric tons per annum, requiring more foundries with output increasing 10-15% every year.

subsections.label: New customer acquisition in casting
points: 3 new customers added to casting after 6 years of steady 26 customers.
One new customer is a diesel engine manufacturer with facility in India, manufacturing for India (Indian supply for KFIL) and export.

Other 2 customers use engines for stationary application, tractors (TREM V next level); direct export orders booked, starting with small direct exports in earthmoving equipment, with visibility for more exports in earthmoving equipment and tractor industry.
Clear volume growth plan and SOP timelines exist for these customers; visibility for next 3-4 years is volume going up to 3 lakh metric tons per annum.

subsections.label: Realization mix shift
points: Customers increasingly look to KFIL for intricate/difficult castings, blocks and heads rather than conventional tractor housings/crankcases; portfolio of tractor housings has not grown much.
New order bookings are at better pricing than conventional tractor housings/crankcases.
Sales realization remained flattish after giving commodity price reduction to customers (INR10-12/kg reductions).
Machine shops progressing well across all 3 locations; 22 HMCs purchased and absorbed into operation, with more to follow; expected machining value of about INR100 crores within a year.

Combination of better-priced castings, machining value addition, and export casting pricing is sustaining/improving realization; expect realization to exceed INR130/kg within 2 years partly as commodity price increases flow back.

subsections.label: Solapur foundry utilization
points: Minimum expectation from both Solapur lines is at least 6,000 tons/month; actual could be ~5% more.
Actual last quarter was 4,200 tons/month against 6,000 tons target, i.e., about 70% utilization; another 30% capacity utilization improvement expected over next 3-4 quarters.

Solapur ramp is 'ticklish' due to core productivity and complexity of casting (complicated blocks and heads) — not a customer-related issue but a foundry process/complexity issue that takes time to stabilize.

subsections.label: Oliver Engineering ramp-up
points: Oliver produced 13,500 tons last year, but by Jan-Mar reached run rate of 1,700 tons/month.
Effort is to take Oliver production to at least 2,000 tons/month to reach 24,000 tons for the year.

Oliver run rate expected to move from 1,700-1,800 in April to 2,200-2,300 by year-end, averaging ~2,000/month, yielding 24,000-25,000 tons for the year; order bookings and machining setup already in place.
After merger, sourcing that had shifted to Oliver (about 2,000 tons vs earlier 1,700) will appear in Kirloskar Ferrous books.

subsections.label: Combined foundry run-rate (Solapur + Koppal)
points: Company targeting to reach 15,500 tons/month per line, totaling 45,000-46,000 tons/quarter (with Oliver) within a couple of quarters.
Shift of some sourcing to Oliver and effort to produce more blocks and heads at Koppal affects the timeline to reach the 45,000/quarter run rate.

subsections.label: Seamless tube order book / oil & gas
points: Pending orders exist from last tenders; new tender expected this year, and company expects to pick up those orders.
Exports growing; fuel prices high and reconstruction requirement rising support expectation of robust domestic and export orders in oil & gas segment.
Management does not currently have exact figure for pending tube orders.
Debottlenecking and capacity utilization improvement expected to give 10-11% volumetric improvement in tube business.
ONGC order and other high-margin joint orders are pending; ONGC order has seen delay.

subsections.label: Pig iron pricing dynamics
points: Hiriyur did not get full volume in Q4 (start-up spillover from Oct-Dec into January).
One blast furnace took a 5-day stoppage during the quarter causing some production loss.

Pig iron typically runs 15-day order book with 1-2 days stock; committed pricing to regular customers for a month means price increases from January had spillover effect and full benefit did not come into Q4; further fine correction in price increase happened even in April.
Company expects steel and tube prices to also rise given rising international pig iron price ($475) and coal cost pressure.

subsections.label: Blast furnace / pig iron capacity plan
points: Long-term plan is to set up one blast furnace in Koppal for steel, which will result in pig iron sales going down to 5 lakh tons instead of 6-7 lakh tons; blast furnace 2 will go for alloy steel production.
Plan to expand seamless tube plant in Baramati so entire steel blooms go to Baramati.
Opportunity exists at Hiriyur to upgrade the blast furnace to produce close to 3,00,000 tons of pig iron, either continuing as pig iron or moving into spun pipe or steel.
Phase 2 plan is to take both MBFs into steel.

subsections.label: Green power expansion
points: 35 MW solar plant to be commissioned by July-August and 25 MW wind plant by September, equivalent to about 90 MW of combined solar/wind (55+35).
Existing 70 MW plant in Jalna already up and running; will reduce CO2 emissions, positioning Jejuri as a green steel producer.
Preliminary work started on bringing in megawatt-level battery storage system to increase utilization of green power despite new regulations coming in Maharashtra.
Wind generation is stronger in monsoon while solar generation is weaker in monsoon — complementary generation profile.

subsections.label: Rolling mill and steel debottlenecking
points: Plan to debottleneck rolling mill to roll the entire 3 lakh tons; of that, 50,000-60,000 tons to go to Ahilyanagar and remaining 2,40,000 tons (20,000/month) for external (non-KFIL) sales.
Currently at 85,000 tons of external sales last year; effort is to expand external sales and internal consumption ahead of the new steel plant coming online.

subsections.label: Oxygen and PCI improvements
points: 150 TPD oxygen plant to be commissioned towards end of year, enhancing oxygen enrichment from 2.5% to 5%.
PCI level to increase from 130 kg to 160-170 kg, resulting in pig iron output increase and coal consumption reduction — productivity and cost benefit.

subsections.label: Tube mill capacity expansion
points: Capacity expansion in Baramati targets bigger size tubes; immediate next-year focus is capacity utilization improvement.
Basic study, design and source study completed for the biggest tube mill; project expected to complete within next 1.5 years.
Investment for the tube mill project could be 500+ crores, part of overall capex plan of INR600-700 crores per year covering pig iron, foundry, steel and tube projects.

subsections.label: Backward integration
points: Coke requirement fully met from own Coke Oven; 52 MW of waste heat recovery power running from blast furnace and Coke Oven.
Progressing on operationalizing Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines with very good quality iron ore, expected to help produce better quality prime pig iron.
Plans to bring in beneficiation and pellet plant once mines are operationalized, to use all kinds of iron ore and sell some pellet quantity in the market.
Backward integration strategy described as 'mine to machine castings' and 'mine to seamless tubes', with energy management as key to monetizing energy cost into future savings.

subsections.label: Cost inputs
points: Company always holds 3 months of coal; fourth month price will change with market.
Team is working on coal purchase commitments, coke price, production cost and margin impact for Q1 FY27 clarity.
Rising dollar (INR95) and coal price increase (~$25/ton) add cost pressure even as value addition and commodity price increases provide some offset.

key_figures.label: Order book duration for pig iron

subsections.label: Oliver merger
points: Company is working on merging Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries and looks forward to closing it in the next couple of months, so as to get merger benefit for FY25-26 itself.

subsections.label: Backward integration roadmap
points: Roadmap includes bridging the gap from pig iron to blast furnace steel to seamless tube (Baramati) and value-added Jejuri steel sold in market.
Own Coke Oven fully meets coke requirement; 52 MW waste heat recovery power running.

Investment of INR125-150 crores planned in Hiriyur to upgrade blast furnace capacity and bring manufacturing cost in line with Koppal via efficiency improvement/cost reduction, with payback period of less than 2 years.
Operationalizing Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines for better quality prime pig iron, followed by beneficiation and pellet plant investment.
Strategy described as 'mine to machine castings' and 'mine to seamless tubes' with energy management central to monetizing energy costs into future savings.

subsections.label: Alloy steel strategy
points: Long-term plan to convert one blast furnace in Koppal to steel, reducing pig iron sales to 5 lakh tons (from 6-7 lakh tons), with blast furnace 2 dedicated to alloy steel production.
Plan to expand seamless tube plant in Baramati so entire steel blooms go there.

Jejuri alloy steel currently uses ~30% green power; pushing to commission additional 35 MW solar (Jul-Aug) and 25 MW wind (Sep) power, equivalent to ~90 MW combined with existing 70 MW at Jalna, to reduce CO2 emissions and position as green steel producer.
Plans for debottlenecking rolling mill to roll entire 3 lakh tons capacity, splitting between Ahilyanagar (50,000-60,000 tons) and external/non-KFIL sales (2,40,000 tons).

subsections.label: External macro disruptions
points: Tariff period, war in the Middle East, Hormuz blockage, fuel cost increases and disruptions in many areas/places have affected demand and cost conditions.
In spite of these conditions, management remains optimistic about better demand position and continued growth.

subsections.label: Commodity price volatility
points: Pig iron commodity market has been terrible for the last 3 years (not just 1 year), with continuous price falls without a substantial fall in raw material prices.
Management expects that pain is over and prices should improve, though this needs to be watched closely.
International pig iron price at $475 is encouraging, but whether it converts to Indian pig iron price increases needs to be seen and how much of it is realizable is uncertain.

subsections.label: Cost inflation
points: Dollar has risen to INR95 and coal prices have risen by about $25 per ton on average, adding cost pressure even as some value addition offsets it.
Coking coal has further risen, affecting Q1 FY27 spread outlook; management is analyzing coal purchase commitments, coke price, production cost and margin impact.

subsections.label: Operational disruptions
points: Hiriyur blast furnace was stopped for almost 3.5 months during FY26 due to market conditions not being conducive, causing a ~68,000 ton production shortfall for the year.
One blast furnace took a 5-day stoppage during Q4, causing production loss.
Steel plant took two fortnight-long stoppages during the year for erection of primary and secondary fume extraction systems to improve environmental aspects.
Hiriyur did not get full quarter-4 volume due to start-up spillover from Oct-Dec into January.

subsections.label: Regulatory risk
points: New government regulations in Maharashtra could limit prime slot utilization of solar energy, prompting company to explore battery storage systems to improve wind/solar utilization.
Some regulation changes regarding utilization period are currently sub judice (in court), affecting realized power cost benefit calculations for FY26.

subsections.label: Casting volume guidance debate
points: Analyst noted prior aspiration of 1,85,000-1,90,000 MT for FY27 combined (incl. Oliver) may be at risk given commentary on 45,000/quarter run-rate taking a couple of quarters and 15% growth framing.
Management reaffirmed commitment to 1,80,000-1,85,000-1,90,000 MT target for FY26-27: Solapur to reach 60,000 tons, Koppal already over 1,05,000 tons, and Oliver contributing 25,000 tons.
Numbers referenced are production numbers, not exact sales numbers; small difference of 2-3% expected due to foundry stage rejection.
Management highlighted that last year casting production and sales increased by 23,000 tons, and this year the effort is for another ~25,000 ton increase.

subsections.label: FY27 overall growth outlook
points: Reversal of commodity price fall should help sales realization; efforts to increase volume in pig iron, casting, steel and tube continue.
Management looks forward to at least 15% growth once again in FY27, provided commodities do not fall again.

subsections.label: Tube guidance
points: Tube volume was 1,88,700 tons in FY26 vs 1,68,800 tons in FY25; company targets 10-11% volumetric growth from here.
On sales realization, expects to recover 5-6% of the ~10% value decline seen last year in tubes, aligned with NSR of ~1,13,000/ton, as pig iron, steel, power and fuel costs rise.

subsections.label: Pig iron production recovery
points: With a little improvement/positive contribution from Hiriyur, company expects to quickly return to ~7 lakh metric tons or at least 680,000-690,000 tons with current productivity levels.

key_takeaways: Quarter 4 pig iron production quantity was 1,58,152 metric ton compared to quarter 4 last year, 1,62,286 metric ton — lower by 3% compared to the last year.
Casting production is 36,596 metric ton against 32,474 ton, which is 13% higher than the last year.

Total year production last year '25-'26 was 6,23,939 metric tons against last year's 6,31,103 metric tons; major drop to the extent of 68,000 was because of stoppage of Hiriyur blast furnace for almost 3.5 months because of the market conditions not being conducive.
Total sales value for the quarter is INR 1,781 crores; year-end sales were INR6,861 crores against INR6,628 crores last year.
Profit before tax is INR514.43 crores against INR532 crores before exceptional item against INR432 crores, an improvement of about INR100 crores on the PBT.
Overall growth on the top line achieved was 3%, including Oliver about 5.1%, after accounting for the drop in sales realizations because of commodity prices being low.
Company is working for merger of Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries and looks forward to close it in the next couple of months so as to have the benefit of merger for the year '25-'26 itself.
Casting business demand remains robust from auto sector as well as the tractor sector; company expects to march forward to about 1,90,000 tons and is commissioning a sixth foundry.
3 new customers added to casting after 6 years of steady 26 customers, including a diesel engine manufacturer and 2 customers for tractor/earthmoving applications with export visibility.
Company is comfortable only when EBITDA is at 15%; currently just above 12.5%.
